0.worldDesc: Maple World, the land of endlessly unfolding mystery. A realm where countless forms of life and magic coexist. From islands drifting above the clouds to cities in the deep sea, from frozen mountain ranges to burning deserts, each region holds its own history and legends.\r\nFor ages, Maple World has been a stage where light and darkness, order and chaos intertwine. Upon that stage, adventurers write their own stories, as the world continues to await the rise of yet another hero.

0.regionDesc: This is the place where all Explorers begin their adventure in Maple World. To the west stands a legendary maple tree. To the east is a small port with service to Victoria Island.\r\nAll new travelers were once greeted by Heena and Sera, but these two have settled down to lead a quiet life. Sen, who used to keep careful watch over his house, still loves to eat Nina's candy, though he's grown up quite a lot since the old days. Todd and Peter, who used to teach combat lessons, have moved to Victoria Island with Robin and the others. In their absence, the island has slipped into a sleepy, happy rhythm.

0.desc: A small, weak creature native to Maple Island and Victoria Island. They used to be so common that there was a saying: "As common as snails." You don't see them as much these days.\r\nI've got an interesting snail tale. There was once an explorer who dreamed of becoming a star-throwing Thief, but her family was too poor to afford throwing stars. Left with no alternative, she started throwing snail shells instead. It turns out she had a knack for it. In the end, she became a famous adventurer.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: This blue variant of the garden-variety Snail also makes its home on Maple Island and Victoria Island. It's bigger, badder, meaner, and tougher than its small cousin, but it's still about as weak as a monster can be. The real question, however, is...why did it turn blue?\r\nSnail shells used to be a popular weapon back in the day, but you don't see them much anymore. A real shame, that.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
Red Snails are found throughout Maple Island and Victoria Island. Local folklore holds that Blue Snails turn red after they complete a Job Advancement, but nobody has been able to find a Snail Job Trainer to confirm if this is true.
They have incredible speed and strength...relative to other snails. They do provide a good challenge for Beginners, at least.
Note the difference in heft between a blue shell and a red shell. Every avid shell-thrower knows that the Red Snails' shells are the best.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc:
This kindhearted girl makes her home in Amherst. She never hesitates to lend a hand to whoever needs it.
In fact, she even helped me when I was just getting started! She taught me about inventory management, item ownership in hunting grounds, and how to get to Victoria Island.
I really should drop in and say hi...
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: She runs the Amherst general store. Most shopkeepers stay INSIDE the building, but she stands outside. I suppose she's worried Beginners won't know how to open the door.\r\nShe'll spend all day telling you about potions if you let her.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: Amherst's chief. I met him once when I was a Beginner. He asked me if there was anything I needed, and I told him I needed a hundred trillion mesos. He gave me 100 mesos instead.\r\n(I was completely serious, too...)\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: He runs the weapon shop in Amherst, but I hear business isn't going very well. After all, Maple Island is not exactly a dangerous place. Who would have thought that peace could be so bad for business?\r\nThat said, Sid's weapons are well worth the coin. His Razors, in particular, are quite sharp.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
Amherst's only mechanic. As you might imagine, repairing his neighbors' broken appliances and whatnot keeps him extremely busy.
You know, I actually got to know him pretty well back in the day. I gathered scrap for one of his inventions, and as a reward, he used some of it to make me a chair. I still have that chair somewhere...
On an unrelated note, his cousin Bari is doing well after finally finding a job.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
This fierce lady guards the entrance to the Adventurer Training Center. She's dedicated to drilling the fundamentals of adventuring to any young Explorers who cross her path.
Before she took on her current duties, she was a mercenary guard who kept the Explorers of Maple Island safe. Now that Olaf has sent many other mercenaries to tak on that job, she has much more free time on her hand. It doesn't help that the Adventurer Training Center isn't quite as popular as it once was.
Is it just me, or has the training center gotten smaller...?
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: A young resident of Southperry. He often talks about how he will one day sail upon a great ship, but it seems he's yet to achieve this dream.\r\nHe secretly collects snail shells and mushroom caps. Why does he keep it a secret? I can't say! I clearly remember helping him collect them in the past, but if you ask him about it now, he pretends to have no idea what you're talking about.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: Southperry's armor merchant. Well, he calls it armor. All of his wares are just ordinary clothes, as far as I can tell.\r\nHe's not actually native to the town. He arrived here from across the sea at some point and decided to settle down. He can't be making much money with his current business... I wonder what keeps him there.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc: The captain of the Shangri-La, the ship that ferries supplies and people between Maple Island and Victoria Island. He took over this role after Captain Shanks retired.\r\nAs for Shanks, he's happily settled down with Maria. You never see those two apart!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.regionDesc: A peaceful village at the center of Victoria Island. Filled with giant mushrooms and lush green fields, it's famous as a training ground for Bowmen.\r\nWarmth and vitality flow throughout the village. This is the starting point for countless adventurers.

0.desc: These mushroom monsters can be found all over Maple Island and Victoria Island. They bounce from place to place in search for new food to eat.\r\nUnfortunately for them, they're quite delicious, and they often end up as an ingredient in Mushroom Candy and Mushroom Stew.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: This monster may have the same orange cap and spots as the Orange Mushroom, but you can tell it apart by the cynical expression on its face. What twisted thoughts lurk inside its mind?\r\nThese mushrooms have been spotted quite frequently in the forests east of Henesys. How worrying...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
A Green Mushroom monster with a dull cap. It's a mutated form of small poisonous mushrooms and is thus immune to poison.
These were once found around construction sites and outside dungeons, but its habitat seems to have shifted. They can now be found in the vicinity of Henesys.
These mushrooms are highly poisonous. No matter how hungry you are, do not eat them under any circumstance!
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
We have an update in regards to the cooking of Green Mushrooms.
Some Green Mushrooms develop a faint yellow tint. These are said to be edible, but testing indicates that they are still mildly poisonous. Even so, they do have some positive medicinal effects.
Unless you are a mushroom expert, extreme caution is advised when handling any mushroom.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
This mushroom monster's cap is covered with horns, hence the name. These monsters used to dwell primarily underground, but like many of their brethren, they can no be found near Henesys.
It was once believed that Green Mushrooms would lose their poisoin and grow horns if deprived of light for long periods, which is where Horny Mushrooms came from. We now know that this is not the case, as they no longer live in the dark. It is now believed that Green Mushrooms that eat certain herbs lose their poisons and grow horns.
Even if they aren't poisonous, I recommend against eating Horny Mushrooms.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: These gigantic mushrooms were once believed to be the mothers of all other mushroom monsters in Victoria Island. Today, however, the idea that mushrooms originate from Spores has also gained traction, and the two theories are hotly debated.\r\nThis humble chronicler supports Spore theory. Consider the house in Henesys where Mushmoms are commonly discovered, and you find evidence that a Mushmom is merely a mushroom that grew big by eating too much food.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: A mushroom monster with horns growing from its cap. It looks nearly identical to a Horny Mushroom, but exposure to strange energy has given it an erratic temperament.\r\nIt wanders around in a constant state of rage. Caution is advised.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
A mass of animated rock that moves around a central core. These constructs were once found in the forests near dungeons, but over time they've moved south and are now found around Henesys.
There are many theories around what animates Stone Golems, but the scholar Bruce's cutting-edge research suggests that the life force of the primrose blossoming on their heads is what gives them life.
The primrose has the unique ability to absorb the earth's energy and bloom in the light of the moon. This may explain why the golems have migrated from the darkness of the forest canopy out into the open plains.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
A Stone Golem that has been corrupted by evil power. They are feared for leaving the forest in ruins and battle the Stone Golems who protect the temples.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt
Appended are additional research notes from the Magician Association.
There are signs that some of these golems willingly left the temple. Our conjecture is that they recognized the early signs of their corruption and departed before they lost control in order to keep the temple safe.
They made their way to Sleepywood. Over time, as they overcame the evil influence, they returned to resume their duties at the temple.
Their outward appearance has been forever changed, but they still serve as devout guardians to this day.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc:
After the Golem's Temple was overrun by evil, only the Stone Golems, Dark Stone Golems, and Mixed Golems remained.
One day, without warning, golems infused with the power of ice appeared. Bruce speculates that these golems are highly evolved and empowered by the life force of the primrose.
Curiously, the Ice Golem's core is as hot as a furnace. One curious principle of magic is that opposite elements can be combined to draw both to their extremes. Perhaps Ice Golems were created along similar lines.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc:
After the Golem's Temple was overrun by evil, only the Stone Golems, Dark Stone Golems, and Mixed Golems remained.
One day, without warning, golems infused with the power of fire appeared. Bruce speculates that these golems are highly evolved and empowered by the life force of the primrose.
Curiously, the Fire Golem's core is as cold as ice. One curious principle of magic is that opposite elements can be combined to draw both to their extremes. Perhaps Fire Golems were created along similar lines.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc: Formed from the mutated remains of Stone Golems and Dark Stone Golems, these strange constructs have the strength of both. They can be found in dungeons and in the abandoned Golem's Temple. It seems they are still drawn to guard the temples of their predecessors.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc: A mushroom monster with a blue cap. It is the plumpest of the mushroom monsters in its family. Long ago, these mushrooms were fairly rare, but they're one of the more common mushroom monsters these days.\r\nThey aren't poisonous, but they're rarely used in cooking due to their offputting blue coloration. Utterly disgusting. Truly, horrid. I hear that they are used in the cuisine of some nations, which just goes to show that it takes all sorts in this world of ours.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc: These Blue Mushrooms look as though they've been struck around the head. This is simply how their faces look. Nobody knows why these mushrooms appear around Henesys or why they make such an odd expression.\r\nBefore they were well known, grifters would keep them as pets and beg for money to buy medicine for their "poor sick mushrooms."\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc: A truly bizarre Mushmom variant. You would think this was a Blue Mushroom that grew into a Mushmom, but it's actually a Mushmom that turned blue. It's believed this happens when a Mushmom eats garbage.\r\nHenesys tried to stop adventurers from leaving their old food wrappers laying around the forest, but that didn't work. Now they just put a bounty on Blue Mushmoms. It's simpler that way.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc:
A charming young lady in Henesys. She cares deeply for Utah, so much so that she once gave her most prized marble to him for his birthday. She is both kind and shy at the same time--she would prepare meals for the sickly Maya, but then have someone else deliver them because she was too embarrassed.
According to Athena Pierce (who happens to be my mentor), Camila has an interest in cooking. She learned Athena Pierce's recipe for Orange Mushroom Juice and Mrs. Ming Ming's recipe for Salad.
Incidentally, the secret to a good Orange Mushroom Juice is to let it ferment for a full week before serving.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: The wife of Chief Stan, she works tirelessly caring for her fellow townsfolk. She happens to be Henesys's most skilled artisan, talented at clothing, cooking, and medicine preparation. Any time there's an event in Henesys, you can be certain that she'll be involved.\r\nShe happens to be friends with Estelle in Ellinia. They say that their families spent time together while she was traveling with her grandfather, Alloy.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: Roca insists that he isn't suspicious. Doesn't this make him all the more suspicious? Does he truly think that no one can tell he's obviously an informant for the Cygnus Knights? The only person he's fooling is himself.\r\nBut if you ask him directly, he will insist in no uncertain terms that he is absolutely not investigating strange phenomena and the movements of the Black Wings.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: A mushroom research. When the Mushroom Castle was occupied by King Pepe, he created Killer Mushroom Spores, which were a great help in battling the penguin king.\r\nIn fact, these spores were developed through a close collaboration with his close friend, Bruce. Scarrs made a point of giving Bruce equal credit for their invention. What a beautiful friendship, to overcome the hurdle of academic rivalry!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
The chief of Henesys. He may look gruff, but he's a family man at heart. He makes sure Jay takes his eye medicine every day and he gathers ingredients for his wife, who loves to cook.
He's also a big fan of Horny Mushroom Pie. So great is his love for this pie that it's said he married Mrs. Ming Ming because of her mushroom dishes.
Things weren't always so idyllic for Chief Stan and his family. It grew so bad that his son ran away once, but things between them seem to have improved.
A word of advice: if Chief Stan ever asks you to deliver a letter, DO NOT SAY YES. You have been warned. No matter how much he begs, don't accept if you value your life. Do not accept it...!
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
No one knows why Pia dresses the way she does. She has a crush on a boy who is close to Camila, and sometimes she takes her jealousy out on Camilia. As you might have guessed, the boy is Utah. It's best to stay out of conflicts such as this.
Though she lives in Henesys, most of her friends appear to live in Ellinia. Given her history of giving gifts to thieves-in-training, she has a kind heart.
According to Bruce, she knows a great deal about mushrooms and magic. My hypothesis is that she would often be bullied by Blue and Green Mushrooms, and so she learned magic to protect herself.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
A warm-hearted resident of Henesys. She feels grateful towards Athena Pierce, the hero who protected the village during the great war long ago, and often prepares Blue Mushroom Porridge for the ailing Maya.
On nights when the moon is full, Rina sometimes appears at the Golem's Temple. It is said she goes there to gather primrose, as it is the only place near Henesys where they bloom.
Primrose is known for its pleasant fragrance and is used in tea, cosmetics, and soap. Even so, venturing into the Golem's Temple late at night suggests she is braver than she looks.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: A student who came from another world. They say they like this world and have no intention of returning to their homeworld.\r\nOne wonders about the wisdom of this idea. To be honest, it may cause problems for the people they've befriended.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc: A disciple of Grendel the Really Old, the great magician of Ellinia. He's known as the Barrier Master.\r\nHe accidentally created a link between Maple World and another world. As a result, he's in charge of keeping an eye on the closet that connects ours dimensions.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: A disciple of Grendel the Really Old, the great magician of Ellinia. It seems Grendel has quite a few disciples. She is known as the Manipulation Master.\r\nShe's quite talented, but it seems she's always being roped into cleaning up after her brother's messes.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc:
A frail resident of Henesys. She suffers from an incurable illness.
Thankfully, her neighbors do much to help her, and Teo provides her with medicine so that her condition doesn't worsen.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
Maya asked that I add a few additional words on her behalf.
Long ago, an adventurer helped her to acquire some medicine that saved her life. To thank them, she gave that adventurer a bamboo hat that had belonged to her parents.
I asked her if she regretted giving away such a keepsake, and Maya answered that her parents had worn the hat while themselves searching for medicine for her. They would be happy for the adventurer to have it, she said.
Maya concluded our chat with the hope that the adventurer who helped her was doing well.
Afterwards, she gave me a Horny Mushroom Pie. Her mother's recipe, apparently. It warms the heart to see her doing so well.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc:
The instructor at the Henesys Bowman Instructional School. She's taught every Bowman Explorer, including yours truly.
She came with the first refugees when Victoria Island split from Ossyria. As one of the founders of Henesys, she is the hero who saved the village during the war 300 years ago. It is said that Athena Pierce is one of the few elves to escape the Black Mage's curse. Even today she continues her good work, representing Explorers in the Maple Alliance.
Perhaps you have heard of Legor, one of my fellow students under Athena Pierce? When he was younger, she rescued him after he became lost in the forest. That day, she told him the words that would shape him into the Legor we know today: 'Even without sight, if you have true insight, you will always hit your mark.'
As one who walks the path of the Bowman, I too will continue to train diligently under Athena Pierce's guidance until my bow becomes as a storm.
When we meet, I confirm my commitment by repeating to her a deferent phrase: #e'My bow will never waver.'#n
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc:
Mrs. Ming Ming's book-loving son.
He gets along well with his stepfather, Chief Stan, but his relationship with his stepbrother Alex was once strained. Their personalities are as different as night and day, and Alex even ran away from home over the matter once. Over time, however, these two have grown much closer.
He's something of an amateur historian. It also seems that he is acquainted with the King of Ludibrium. How does a young man from a small town like Henesys come to befriend royalty? An intriguing question indeed...
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc: A mini-game enjoyer who spends most of his time in Henesys Park. His motto is "Live for fun!"\r\nThis chronicler also happens to enjoy mini-games. Oh, I used to spend hours playing Omok and Memory with the townsfolk. I've been too busy to play lately, but perhaps I could find time for a match or two in the name of research.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

14.desc: The proprietor of Henesys' storage business. If you've spent any time in Lith Harbor, you've likely run into someone who looks like his twin.\r\nCould they be brothers? They have different surnames, so it seems unlikely. Then what, exactly, is their relationship?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc: He wears overalls. His hat has animal ears. And he sells food that pets can't seem to get enough of.\r\nDriven by my scholarly curiosity, I tried to sneak a bite of this unusually tasty pet food, but he stopped me. Surely I cannot be the only one who wishes to try it? But the man stands ever-vigilant, prepared to intervene should any human palate attempt to taste of his treats.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

16.desc: This pet trainer can be found at the top of the Pet Walkway. When nobody's looking, he's been known to sneak off to play with cats instead of working.\r\nOf course, he also does that when people are looking, so maybe that isn't such a surprise. At least he got into the right line of work for it!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

18.desc: An item maker at the Henesys Market. These days, he only handles item repair. He rarely gets any customers nowadays, and he seems to miss the days when he made equipment himself.\r\nAh, I think fondly back to the times when I came to him for my own item needs. I spent hours gathering branches and firewood, refining ores, and helping him craft each piece by hand... Those were the days...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

19.desc: A street vendor at the Henesys Market. Before he came along, it was hard to find good equipment in Henesys if you weren't a Bowman. Seeing an opportunity, General Mau bought up a variety of goods from other towns and brought them to market here.\r\nIf you need to update your weapons after completing a Job Advancement, it may be worth paying him a visit.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

20.desc: A merchant operating out of the Henesys Market. He sells little pocket items like wallets, pocket watches, house keys, scissors, books, and roses.\r\nThe wares seem to be of a decent quality, but I don't know anyone who's bought anything from him.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

21.desc: A merchant of secondary weapons and emblems at the Henesys Market. Rumor has it he's got an arrangement with General Mau. As a result, they make sure to have no overlap in their inventory so that they don't cut into each other's sales.\r\nYou can't normally acquire an emblem without being affiliated with a given faction. Don't ask me how he acquired his.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

22.desc: A weapon merchant at Henesys' equipment store. He frequently complains that General Mau's presence at the market has hurt his business.\r\nHe also claims to have the cheapest prices in town, though they seem to be quite similar to the street vendor's. It's not surprising he's lost business.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

23.desc: An armor merchant at Henesys' equipment store. His canvas shoes used to be quite popular, but they've recently fallen out of fashion. He's found it harder and harder to compete with General Mau's street stall.\r\nStill, he seems to be doing better than Karl.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

24.desc: The proprietor of the Henesys General Store. She always seems to be dozing, leaving the customers to sort through her inventory on their own. Does she care about sales at all?\r\nUnlike the other shopkeepers in town, she may actually be the owner of her own building. She runs it less like a business and more like a hobby.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

25.desc: As the owner of the Henesys Skin-Care salon, Ms. Tan personally performs the salon treatments herself. Your skin is in good hands with hers.\r\nMost of her business these days is done through in-home services. She seems genuinely delighted when a customer visits her salon in person.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

26.desc: Lauren is the Henesys Hair Salon's android beauty expert.\r\nIf you enjoy dressing up your androids as much as I do, then I highly recommend her services.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

27.desc:
This elegant lady can often be found at the Henesys Hair Salon. If you follow high fashion at all, then you've likely already met her.
She was recently involved in #s#transporting valuables#s#, but she is no longer in that line of work.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

28.desc: One of the hair dressers at the Henesys Hair Salon. True to his name, his got a big head--both literally and figuratively. He will tell you that he's one of the best hairstylists around, and most of his clients agree.\r\nHe also offers in-home services these days. If you want Big Headward's artistic stylings, you can have them anytime.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

30.desc: An assistant hairstylist at the Henesys Hair Salon. She is the daughter of Natalie, the Head Hairstylist. Still in training, she spends most of her time assisting her mother.\r\nInterestingly, even Brittany acknowledges that the best stylist is not Natalie, but Big Headward.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

31.desc: The Head Hairstylist at the Henesys Hair Salon and Brittany's mother. She hired Big Headward some time ago and has long since stepped away from styling herself. It almost feels as if Big Headward is the true owner of the salon now.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

32.desc: The Plastic Surgeon at Henesys Plastic Surgery. He is an artist with a scalpel, but he no longer performs procedures these days. The reason is simple: with the arrival of Plastic Roy, there's no longer a need for him to step in.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt\r\n

33.desc: An unlicensed doctor at Henesys Plastic Surgery. He no longer performs procedures, instead referring any would-be clients to Plastic Roy. Thank goodness! The man is a menace and should not be allowed near anyone's face. I unfortunately speak from personal experience.\r\nEven if he offers to give you a free surgery, under no circumstance should you accept!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

34.desc:
This pet trainer offers his service along the Pet-Walking Road. While he does offer simple walking services, he also trains pets to compete in obstacle courses.
In spite of his stern expression, pets seem to love Bartos and follow him willingly.
He is Frod's brother, though they look nothing alike. There is someone in Ludibrium who looks more like him, but he insists that Frod is his only brother. It's likely just a coincidence...
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

35.desc: The pet master of Henesys Park. He dresses humbly in a straw hat, and is thus easy to overlook. In truth, however, he's a magician who created the magic to bring dolls to life using Water of Life. These living dolls came to be popular as pets, and thus he became Cloy the Pet Master.\r\nIt is thanks to his work that adorable pets now roam Maple World.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

36.desc: A scholar researching monsters at the Golem's Temple. While his close friend Scarrs focuses his research on mushrooms, Bruce studies a wider range of monsters. He has a particular interest in monsters that inhabit relics and ruins. Having published numerous papers on various monsters, he is quite well known in academia.\r\nHe spent a great deal of time searching for his missing daughter. Adventurers helped to reunite them, and the experience is said to have helped him relax quite a bit.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.regionDesc: A port town on the westernmost shore of Victoria Island. Popularly known as the novice adventurer's gateway to other continents. \r\nThough the town may appear quiet, with its endless blue rolling waves, it is filled with sailors and merchants throughout, all of them eager for tales of new adventures.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: This small mushroom monster is often found in grassy areas. Weak by the standards of most monsters, it keeps itself alive with its speed. At first glance, they resemble Orange Mushroom monsters, but their smaller frames and aggressive-looking faces set them apart. \r\nThese creatures spread mushroom spores with abandon, keeping the mushroom population high all throughout Maple World.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc:
The oldest snail in Maple World. His huge body reflects his age, as does his mustache. He enjoys the morning dew, especially on the leaves he eats for breakfast.
If fortunate enough, one can acquire a Rainbow-colored Snail Shell, which is said to grant its owner a wish.
It's even possible to learn the snails' language, through a book titled 'Legend of the Snail.' Alloy, the great-grandfather of Jay and Mrs. Ming Ming, worked hard to write that book over the years.
According to this chronicler's first few lessons, the proper snail greeting translates roughly to 'At your leisure.'
                                      -  Chronicler Ritt

0.desc:
A muscular man often seen in Lith Harbor. They say he's the finest sailor there. He says he's retired and no longer sails, but if you're in need of a seasoned sailor, you may be able to lure him out of retirement with a 'Tropical Fruit Punch.'
Despite his rough and burly appearance, he's a very kindhearted person. A native of Maple Island, he occasionally hires mercenaries to looks after his hometown. He seems to have quite a wide network as well. He appears to be acquainted not only with Lucas and Mai of Maple Island, but also with a horned prince from somewhere...
In fact, this chronicler is also on fairly friendly terms with him, from my early adventuring days, when he would teach me lessons on job advancement.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: One of the wealthiest people in Maple World. He owns several mansions, but he loves the sea so much that he spends much of his time in Lith Harbor. \r\nHe used to run a great many businesses, but recently seems to have scaled things back a bit. Perhaps he is preparing a new venture.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: The man with the most distinctive beard in Lith Harbor. He may look like a bandit at first glance, but he's actually quite friendly. A former Explorer, he once traveled in search of new worlds. Even now, after retiring and settling down as a sailor in Lith Harbor, he's always delighted to meet new Explorers and swap stories. If you happen to be an Explorer, you owe it to yourself to speak with him at least once. \r\nAs an aside, he used to collect snail shells for arthritis medicine. I wonder if he ever managed to gather enough.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: A pale-looking man often seen in Lith Harbor. He was once a sailor, but retired a bit early and now lives as a local fisherman. He seems to suffer quite a bit from arthritis, perhaps an unwanted souvenir from his days at sea.\r\nTeo, a friend of John, finds John's recent behavior suspicious, and questions what's in the wooden box he's been carrying about. However, this chronicler knows the truth. The box holds nothing more sinister than ordinary arthritis medicine.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: A kind-faced old man often found in Lith Harbor. Judging by his unfamiliar attire, he seems to hail from another region. \r\nHe seems to love meeting new people and making friends. After all, he might say, what remains after a journey are memories and the friends with whom you share them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
A girl in Lith Harbor. Between her bunny headband and the rest of her distinctive outfit, she's easy to spot. She originally wanted to be an adventurer, but her father has forbidden it. 
In truth, she seems to have more talent for alchemy than adventuring. Simply by following along with books, she managed to create valuable potions. She even wrote a book based on her talent, titled, 'Jane's Alchemy for Beginners -- So Easy a Monkey Can Do It!' The book is said to be so well known that even Maed, the head of the Alcadno Society in Magatia, is familiar with it. 
How did she manage to write something memorable enough for such an authoritative figure to remember? I couldn't say, but it makes me want to read it myself someday.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: One of the sailors in Lith Harbor. He loves adventure, and often returns from his voyages with treasure chests in his hold. For many years, he dreamed of sailing to the Sea of Storms, and after he gathered the map fragments from the Lord Pirate's lair, he finally managed to do so. \r\nDespite full firsthand knowledge of the sea's many dangers, he braves the waters again and again, an adventurer at heart through and through.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: A man who runs a storage business in Lith Harbor. His outfit and manner of speech are quite distinctive, implying that he hails from another region. \r\nIn a broader sense, as one travels about Victoria Island, one often meets people with similar names and similar jobs. They even look remarkably alike, to the point of confusion. Could he be Mr. Kim's brother, perhaps?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc:
A man in Lith Harbor. He's handsome, and he knows it. 
To elaborate, his confidence goes beyond simple self-assurance and crosses into outright bragging, which likely explains why he's not very popular. He claims he has never received chocolates on Valentine's Day, and honestly, I wouldn't give him any myself. 
According to rumors, someone once took pity on him and asked Chef to give him chocolate, but he got Blackheart Noodles instead. The taste of the Blackheart Noodles was better than expected, but it somehow brought tears to his eyes.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc: An information broker in Lith Harbor. According to rumors, he comes from Rien. He is said to maintain a large database and charge reasonable prices for access, making his services quite useful. Or so this chronicler has heard, at least. He and I have rarely crossed paths, and I have yet to make use of his services.\r\nIncidentally, he seems to have a particular fondness for polearms, as do many heroes in his place of origin. Not to call him heroic, as such.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc: The man who runs the weapon shop in Lith Harbor. One of his legs is a prosthetic, so he uses a crutch. Judging by the tattoos on his arms, he looks to be a former sailor.\r\nThis chronicler often visits Silver's shop, as I have fond memories of the fruit knife I once bought there.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc: Lith Harbor's armor merchant. There are rumors that his considerable facial hair hides a memorable scar. Many of the merchants in Lith Harbor were once sailors, so it wouldn't be surprising if the rumors were true. \r\nWith Lith Harbor being a relatively peaceful place, there are no particularly remarkable items among the armor he sells. However, the Sky-blue Wooden Chair is quite charming, if you have room for it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc: Lith Harbor's general shopkeep. While the store does resemble others of its kind, the Lith Harbor shop does sell one special exclusive treat: Tropical Fruit Punch. It's extracted from the fruits of Florina Beach's palm trees, and when served chilled, it has a distinctly sweet flavor.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.regionDesc: This city is nestled in the shadows of Victoria Island, where dazzling neon signs coexist with dark, gloomy back alleys.\r\nOn the surface, it appears lively, but beneath the city, secret organizations and thieves operate. All manner of rumors and conspiracies swirl about.\r\nThieves who seek true power in darkness hone their skills here.

0.desc: This octopus-like creature possesses almost alien features. The most daring of culinary artists use this bizarre animal to make mushroom meatballs. Some even brew it into medicinal tonics... \r\nThe tentacles do look chewy in an oddly tantalizing way, but something about it still feels deeply...icky.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: This training monster was discovered at the Secret Garden Training Grounds. It is quite large and swings its dual blades simultaneously for a formidable attack.\r\nIt's strange... The whirling blades should be enough to hold anyone's attention. And yet, I find myself transfixed by its belly...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: This training monster was discovered at the Secret Garden Training Grounds. It's small and slender but wields dual blades nearly as effectively as its larger bretheren. Be wary of its charge attacks, for they add power to the thrust of its deadly swords.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: This small green snake is most commonly found in damp swamps. Do not let its diminutive size fool you. It is quite agile and can be a formidable opponent for novice adventurers.\r\nAs for harvestable products, Jr. Necki Skin is durable but supple, putting it in fairly high demand for adventurers' equipment. However, there is very little information available regarding the viability of its meat as a source of protein. Perhaps I should perform some hands on research...?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: This green, crocodile-like monster commonly inhabits swamps. Ligator Skin is tough and durable, making it a highly sought after crafting material for adventurers' equipment.\r\nBecause it stays low and close to the ground, it can be quite the challenge for taller adventurers to dispatch it. Proceed with caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc:
This olive-toned, crocodile-like monster commonly inhabits swamps. It resembles a Ligator, but it is far stronger and faster.
Croco Skin is another prized, durable material that could provide a lucrative side hustle for any adventurers with a more entrepreneurial spirit.
Similar to its smaller bretheren, because it stays low and close to the ground, it can be quite the challenge for taller adventurers to dispatch it. Use extreme caution.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: This mud monster is common in the wetter regions of swamps. It may seem dim-witted, but it is actually quite cunning. Adventurers who underestimate it often become its victims, losing all of their belongings in the process.\r\nThis seemingly unremarkable glob of muck survives by absorbing nutrients from mud and swamp plants. Ew.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: This massive crocodile-like beast prowls the Kerning City swamp regions. It closely resembles a Ligator, but it is significantly larger. As if they weren't formidable enough, this specific mutation appears to be capable of weilding magic.\r\nIt may seem similar to its cousins, but it is much stronger and poses a much greater threat to unwary adventurers. Extreme caution is advised.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: This mud monster is common in the wetter regions of swamps. It is distinguished by a small sprout growing on its head. \r\nIts combative expression keeps all but the bravest of adventurers at bay. This otherwise unremarkable goop survives by absorbing nutrients from mud and swamp plants. Ick.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: This bat-like monster flies around inside the subway, preferring the darkness over sunlight.\r\nIt darts around with such quick, erratic movements that it makes me dizzy just watching them! They often travel in swarms and take advantage of their numbers to overwhelm adventurers and steal their belongings.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: This tiny ghost was born from shadow. It stalks its prey while draped in a pure white tablecloth.\r\nBeware! It may be adorably teensy, but do not underestimate this opponent. Ghosts possess formidable skill.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc: This tiny ghost was born from shadow. It stalks its prey while draped in a pure white tablecloth.\r\nStudies have yet to determine the reason it carries an herbal tonic. I suspect that even ghosts must need a pick-me-up on occasion.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc: This large ghost was born from shadow. Its entire body is pitch black, and its appearance would suggest that it is more powerful than a Wraith.\r\nIt's only speculation at this point, but studies would suggest they despise light nearly as much as they do humans. Perhaps that knowledge may be useful in combat...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: This magician somehow attracts adventurers to the sewer entrance. There are rumors that she is a goddess, but they have so far gone unsubstantiated, since she has proved to be excessively scatterbrained. By all accounts, she has mistakenly thrown Magic Growth Potions into the sewer not once, but twice!\r\nBeyond the obvious problem this creates for monster management, it's worth noting that everything hit with growth accelerant tastes TERRIBLE...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: This is a local item crafter... or so he claims. He's quite well known in the underworld, which suggests not all of his activities are strictly legal. Questionable hobbies aside, he has a reputation for knowing everything happening in Kerning City's back alleys.\r\nBut this information is all second-hand, of course. An honest, moral, and upright Chronicler such as myself would never rub elbows with anyone of ill repute!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: Like most of the storage keepers on Victoria Island, this Kerning City resident wears red clothing. \r\nPerhaps there is a storage keepers' union that decides on a sort of uniform? Regardless, as someone who stores valuable items themselves, it's reassuring to know I can trust this organization to keep my things safe.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: This master lockpicker can easily open the locking mechanisms on treasure chests and padlocks. Of course, it will cost you a pretty penny to benefit from their services. Thieving is a risky business that demands hazard pay.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: This Cygnus Knights informant is investigating strange phenomena occurring throughout Victoria Island.\r\nHe has quite an intimidating presence, considering his height and solid build. But there's no need to be afraid of him. He's a big softie! One time, when I was really hungry and broke, he gave me a boiled Tiguru egg to help me out.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: This intelligence gatherer takes various requests from her clientele and finds adventurers willing to handle them.\r\nShe may appear kind and generous, but she is ruthless when it comes to profit and cost efficiency. In fact, she has a notorious and long-standing rivalry with JM.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: You'll always find Don Giovanni's son wearing a blue hat and daydreaming about soaring through the sky like a bird.\r\nUnfortunately, he looks nothing like his father and constantly worries that maybe he's not Don Giovanni's biological son. Hopefully, his fears are unfounded.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: This boy always looks a little scruffy. Perhaps that's why he pulls his black cap so low over his face.\r\nHe doesn't exactly have the look or demeanor of a Kerning City resident, and rumors suggest he ran away from home during a turbulent phase due to family discord. Poor kid. Why does Kerning City seem to have so many runaways...?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: This mysterious woman can be found at Naora Hospital. She exudes a creepy, otherworldly aura, and if you get too close to her, you can feel an unsettling chill.\r\nWait, did she just look this way?! Ah! I shouldn't make eye contact! Oh, I hope she doesn't try to talk to me!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc:
This is the King of Thieves in Kerning City as well as the Thief job instructor. He can be found at the thieves' hideout, the Jazz Bar.
The title of Dark Lord is proudly handed down from one worthy thief to the next, most recently to the eighth Jin. The latest Dark Lord's core strength is so legendary that he regularly hangs around upside down doing crunches just because he can.
He and Lady Syl, the head of the Secret Garden Training Grounds, have a murky history built on resentment and contrition. One must always demonstrate respect for his devotion by greeting him with the phrase, #e'Now I understand your resolve.'#n.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc:
This is the shrewd owner of the Kerning City Hair Salon and proud father to Shumi and Icarus.
He's a self-possessed indivudual whose bold, spirited personality is reflected in his extravagant fashion choices.
And he's no shrinking violet, either! Rumor has it his skin is so tough that he uses the same moisturizing products common to conditioning crocodile leather pouches. Crocodile leather!
                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc: This is the assistant at the Kerning City Hair Salon. He speaks in a nasally tone that grates on anyone unfortunate enough to hear it, and rumor has it that he's a lifelong bachelor.\r\nHe claims to be a competent stylist, but clients can't help noticing Big Headward always steps in to perform any hair treatments of import. It doesn't exactly inspire confidence, now does it?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc: This is the ore refiner at the Kerning City Repair Shop. As the title suggests, he both refines ore and repairs equipment. Considering he works in a forge right in the middle of town, its clear the house was designed for efficient heat ventilation.\r\nRumor has it that he closely guards a cherished pillow.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc: This weapons dealer in Kerning City has unusual taste for dishes made from Evil Eye Tails--stir-fried Evil Eye Tails, no less! His choice of delicacy may not be popular, but there's no denying that he qualifies as a foodie. Perhaps there's something to it...?\r\n                                      -  Chronicler Harper

15.desc: This armor merchant in Kerning City is a skilled crafter who personally designs and hand makes his pieces.\r\nHe has a favorable reputation in town for a number of reasons, not the least of which is because he charges unbelievably reasonable prices for his wares.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

16.desc:
This individual owns Kerning City's Pharmacy and sells general goods. It took some effort to learn his name.
Despite his advanced age, he possesses quite a childlike palate. As such, he is especially fond of Teddy-shaped jelly, which is limited edition and rather difficult to come by.
He sometimes makes medicine himself and but more often sources his medicinal ingredients from Nella on commission.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

17.desc: This swordsman stands at the entrance to the Secret Garden at Kerning City Back Alley. He used to loiter near the Jazz Bar, but once suspicious rumors about him began to circulate, he deemed it wise to change locations.\r\nIt seems he is on a mission to gather as much information about the Dark Lord as he can...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

18.desc: This girl trains on the lower floor of the Secret Garden. For reasons known only to her, she stands atop an owl. Based on the owl's distinctly ruffled appearance and obvious discomfort, I have to wonder why it allows for such behavior.\r\nShe seems to care deeply for Lady Syl and treats her as one would their own mother, which includes crafting stunning flower bouquets for her.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

19.desc: This owl is located in the basement of the Secret Garden. Surprisingly, it serves as a training instructor who teaches Dual Blades and possesses exceptional skill.\r\nIt uses word cards to communicate with people.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

20.desc: This individual is in charge of training beginner Dual Blades in the basement of the Secret Garden. He takes great pride in his work and affiliation. Despite his large build, I can personally attest that he possesses a warm, approachable demeanor and a kind heart.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

21.desc: This general goods merchant plies his wares in the basement of the Secret Garden. His owl-like hairstyle and stunning eyes are his defining features.\r\nHis potions are known far and wide for their mystical, glittering appearance. But, honestly, nothing is more mystical and glittering than Taeha's eyes.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

22.desc: This weapon and armor merchant has a shop in the basement of the Secret Garden. \r\nIt's the best place to purchase hot-off-the-forge items, since she forges the weapons herself on the massive anvil beside her. She has a reputation for being an extremely skilled craftsperson with wares of the highest quality.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

23.desc: This Dual Blade job instructor is typically at the top of the Secret Garden. Rumor has it that she is the daughter of a former Dark Lord.\r\nThis woman's beauty is almost as stunning as her wit and charisma. And judging by how often Yun presents her with flowers, she must have a fondness for them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

24.desc: This public service worker is stationed at the Subway Ticketing Booth.\r\nHe is a diligent, kind young man, who is surprisingly dedicated to his work--dare I say too dedicated? From what I hear, his shift should have been over a LONG time ago...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

25.desc: You can find this janitor in the Transfer Area. However, he is no ordinary janitor.\r\nRumor has it that this unassuming custodial worker is actually a powerhouse in Kerning City. It seems the messes he cleans up are more...metaphorical. Stay on his good side.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

26.desc: Icarus's older sister has a talent for eye-catching fashion.\r\nShe's a bit scatterbrained and loses things fairly often. Sometimes she's only down there to find something, but the fact that she can spend an entire day in this dark and dreary subway is really a testament to her fortitude.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.regionDesc: A shopping center located on the outskirts of Kerning City. The Kerning Square used to be here as well, but after a renovation, it was replaced with a skyscraper. Kerning Tower is where trends are born, and superstars get their start.

0.desc: This CD, a compilation of the latest hits, was sold at the record shop in Kerning Square.\r\nSince it features the most popular songs of the last three months, everyone seems to want one.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: This CD, a compilation of the greatest oldies, was sold at the record shop in Kerning Square. It is a compilation album featuring classic songs from the past.\r\nTrack 8 on Disc 2 is Chief Stan's favorite. A song with frequent triplets, his taste suggests he has a good sense of rhythm.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: With advances in technology, a walking speaker has finally been made. It's equipped with the latest artificial intelligence and is said to move exactly as people tell it to.\r\nThe downside is that it sometimes doesn't listen. Are they not going to make a walking amplifier to go with it?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: A blue raspberry-flavored jelly drink. The top appears to be whipped cream, but it is in fact vanilla ice cream with chocolate syrup.\r\nThe overwhelmingly sweet taste was not to my liking. It's very cold.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: A massive espresso machine. A demitasse is precariously balanced on top of its head. Take caution of the steam it blasts from its head if approaching.\r\nI say this after getting burned trying to look at its coffee beans. I only wanted to check the roast level...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: A grape-flavored jelly drink. The top appears to be whipped cream, but it is in fact vanilla ice cream with chocolate syrup.\r\nThe overwhelmingly sweet taste was not to my liking. It's very cold.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: A green notebook that can fly. The two loose pages protruding from the cover resemble rabbit's ears. Its expression seems to be challenging someone to try to open it, which does activate my competitive spirit. \r\nI won't let it get away. I'm determined to find out what kind of class these notes were taken in.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: A blue notebook that can fly. The two loose pages protruding from the cover resemble rabbit's ears. Its expression seems to be challenging someone to try to open it, which does activate my competitive spirit. \r\nI won't let it get away. I'm determined to find out what kind of class these notes were taken in.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: Yellow headphones that are leisurely wandering around the record shop. They enjoy playing slow-tempo tracks. \r\nI'd like to try them on, but it's difficult to force a monster to stay on your head. The nerve... I'll leave a review saying the sound quality is terrible.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: Red headphones that are sprinting around the record shop. They enjoy playing fast-tempo tracks.\r\nI'd like to try them on, but it's difficult to force a monster to stay on your head. The nerve... I'll leave a review saying the sound quality is terrible.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: A fanged eyeshadow monster. As its appearance suggests, it's extremely violent and vicious. Still, it's supposedly a high-end cosmetic. That's probably why it behaves so recklessly. \r\nIf you charge in without thinking, you'll end up covered head to toe in bright blue eyeshadow.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc: A cracked and shattered vanity monster. The broken parts have turned into fang-like teeth. As its appearance suggests, it's extremely violent and vicious.\r\nSince it was once a vanity that held high-end cosmetics, you can obtain valuable rewards from it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc: This hair roller monster appears permanently irritated. While it appears to have two small legs, its preferred method of movement is rolling. \r\nThese would be inefficient hair rollers as best, as they would likely either never release your hair, or roll away in rage.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc: A perm machine has turned into a monster, and an angry one at that. It looks as if its only mission is to burn your hair. \r\nIt claims to only use the highest-grade perm solution, but I fail to see the significance. The hostile intent is still quite obvious. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc: According to Blake, this is the Spirit of Rock, and its evil spirit lurks within a guitar. Local legends report that it will appear to novice singers with potential. Does that indicate a bright future for anyone who sees it?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: Blake's hairdresser. His reputation precedes him, and he and Blake have a long working relationship. \r\n A man of many talents, he also works as an MC for a music program. His name is rather well known in the music world as well.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: Blake's makeup artist and stylist. Her work is well known in the industry, and she's worked with Blake for a long time. \r\nHer makeup skills are said to be so good that she can make a face look no bigger than a fist with makeup effects alone.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: A producer at Big Hit Records. In the past, he worked as a public service worker at the Kerning City Subway, but went on to fulfill his dream of becoming a singer. He rose all the way to the top quickly. \r\nThere was a time he felt lost in the hustle and bustle of the popstar life. Now, he has stepped down from the spotlight and works as a producer, searching for a vocalist who can sing the masterpieces he has created.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: A devoted Blake groupie. Apparently, she likes him so much that she even knows Blake's shoe size. From what I hear, she has been a fan for a very long time. \r\nSince his debut, she has never missed a meet and greet or autograph session. The ardor and persistence of her passion is quite impressive.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: A public service worker who served alongside Blake. Although he was older than Blake, they were very close friends.\r\nHe now handles general goods in the Kerning Tower lobby.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: A makeup artist who works at the cosmetics shop in Kerning Tower. A dedicated and skilled perfectionist, he always makes sure his tools are in pristine condition. \r\nIt's a bit difficult to say his name aloud without smacking your lips a little.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc:
She works at the hair salon in Kerning Tower and is very enthusiastic about her own self-promo.
Even so, she takes pride in her work and is considered a master of her craft. 
It's a bit difficult to say her name aloud without smacking your lips a little.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.regionDesc: A village of warriors in the massive rocky mountains located in the northern part of Victoria Island.\r\nFor many years, brave warriors have gathered here to form tribes and live together, undergoing training in a harsh natural environment to become ever stronger fighters.\r\nTowering rocky peaks and ever-burning bonfires represent the village's strength. Adventurers who wish to inherit the warrior spirit often gather here to test their valor.

0.desc: A small, round monster that appears in the South Rocky Mountain. Do not be fooled by its cute appearance -- it casts all kinds of debilitating status spells. It also has sticky fingers, and frequently steals people's belongings.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: A moving tree stump monster found in North Rocky Mountain. The single eyeball embedded in the center of its body is quite unsettling.\r\nIts legs, formed from twisted roots, are very short, making its walking speed slow and awkward. However, it has a sturdy body. Stump-dropped items are put to good use in the daily lives of Perion's residents, making it a fairly useful monster.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: A Stump with a slightly darker hue. Its exterior is thoroughly dried out, but its insides still retain some moisture. Dark Stump leaves can be used as cooking ingredients or medicinal herbs. Unlike regular Stumps, however, they do not seem suitable for use as musical instrument materials.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc:
A Stump with an axe embedded in its head. Its bark is even tougher than that of a regular Stump.
There are many legends surrounding the Axe Stump. One tale says that a woodcutter struck a Stump in the head with an axe to use it as firewood, then left it behind, and that resentment caused it to become a monster.
Another says that a young girl, who witnessed its wounding, pulled the axe from its head and promised to help if such a thing ever happened again. Wanting to see the girl once more, the Stump later embedded an axe into its own head, hoping that would make her come back.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: An Axe Stump with a slightly darker hue. The axe obtained from a Dark Axe Stump is said to be of fairly high quality.\r\nIt can also yield a rare crystal known as a Stump's Teardrop. There are rumors of ones that bloom with flowers, but none have been seen so far. Unlike regular Axe Stumps, they does not seem suitable for use as musical instrument materials.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: A mutated species of Stump. It appears only near excavation sites, suggesting it was influenced by the evil energy emanating from the ruins.\r\nIt's said that if the branch on a Ghost Stump's head is planted in the ground, it will grow into an enormous tree.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: A somewhat strange Ghost Stump. For reasons unknown, it spends the entire day grinning. There are rumors that a mysterious doll made it that way somehow.\r\nAccording to people at the excavation site, its expression somehow makes you want to hit it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc:
A ghostly tree, rumored to have lived since time immemorial. The king of the Stumps. It's said that strips of cloth, stained red with the blood of old spirits, hang from each of its branches.
Stumpy was once a guardian tree, all the way back when Perion was a lush forest, but when humans destroyed that forest, it became a furious monster.
Ironically, it's now draining Perion of its life force, contributing to the land's gradual desolation.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: This Wild Boar looks utterly terrified. There's no confirmed explanation for what could have frightened a Wild Boar, a symbol of toughness, so badly.\r\nDon't assume it's easy prey just because it's frightened. If anything, it's more sensitive and aggressive. How do I know? I tried to get some Wild Boar meat and got rammed head-on.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: Angered by the discrimination between regular pigs and Ribbon Pigs, certain pigs gathered here in Perion.\r\nOver time, in order to survive Perion's harsh environment, they evolved into Wild Boars, with sturdy bodies and powerful tusks.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: A pig clad in steel armor. Even so, it is extremely fast, so be careful. It tends to move in groups, and if you provoke one carelessly, you may face an entire herd of Iron Hogs charging after you.\r\nAmong pigs, this steel armor seems to be a symbol of heroism.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc: A Wild Boar clad snout-to-hoof in extremely tough steel armor, which does nothing to hinder its incredible speed. Should you face one, exercise extreme caution. It appears to be the leader among the Iron Hogs.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc: In adapting to Perion's environment, this Wild Boar gained the ability to ignite flames.\r\nSometimes it burns so intensely that it ends up cooking itself. I should hunt these guys and see how they taste.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

0.desc: A girl living in Perion, though she wasn't born there. The people of Perion took Ayan in when she lost her memory and collapsed.\r\nShe is terribly afraid of Stumps and Orange Mushrooms. As a child, she was attacked by a giant Orange Mushroom, which caused her to lose both her way and her memories. As for Stumps, she says it's simply because their eyes look too scary.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: A storage keeper in Kerning City. He wears red clothing and an eyepatch. Why do all the storage keepers on Victoria Island seem to dress so similarly?\r\nIt almost feels like there's a storage keepers' union. Well, from the perspective of someone storing items, it's reassuring to know things are kept safe.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: Perion's armor seller, known for his fearsome look. He warns people not to steal his goods, but...\r\n...Well, anyone who would still think of stealing after seeing that face must have incredible nerve. He sells sturdy equipment, able to withstand Perion's harsh environment.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: Perion's weapon seller. Not as intimidating as Harry, but he still has a rough-looking face.\r\nFor some reason, his sales pitch is exactly the same as the weapon seller in Lith Harbor. The weapons he sells will not break easily, even in Perion's harsh environment.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc:
A Perion resident carrying a spear. He seems to enjoy playing pranks, though sometimes he goes too far.
Like stuffing a monster into a gift that Boogie gave to Dances with Balrog, or giving Ayan an Orange Mushroom Transformation Potion, which she absolutely hates... It's probably best not to get too close to him.
                                      - Chronicler Harper
This chronicler happened to visit, after a long time away, and heard an amusing story. Blackbull talked about how his cousins, who once lived in Henesys, all tried to move to Perion. There were so many of them that they even took on a request to recover lost land deeds, and went as far as building all the houses themselves.
As for how it ended, all the cousins who'd lived in Henesys did manage to settle in safely. However, it didn't take long before they grew bored with Perion and returned to Henesys.
Well... perhaps that's only natural. There's not much to do in a desolate place like Perion, after all. There are few places on Victoria Island as nice as Henesys.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
Perion's equipment expert. He repairs equipment in need of maintenance. He insists his name has nothing to do with lightning. 
                                      - Chronicler Harper
In the past, he mainly processed raw ores and crafted equipment. He specialized in hard materials like bronze and steel, and many adventurers once sought him out for his skills. 
As time passed and people began refining materials on their own, his customers dwindled. These days, he makes a living by repairing the village's equipment. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: Perion's blacksmith. He works on refining minerals and crafting material items. He appears to be Mr. Thunder's apprentice. Lately, he's been quite busy, too much so for any special requests.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: A mysterious warrior standing at the top of Perion Village. Wearing a straw hat and facing away, he radiates overwhelming presence and charisma that make him difficult to approach. This powerful fighter once battled the Demon King Balrog, and it is said that he still possesses Tristan's sword.\r\nWith only rumors remaining and Tristan long dead, some believe the stories are nothing more than legends. If you have the courage, ask him, #e'Tell me of your fight with Balrog.'#n I can't promise anything, but he might just share the tale of that day.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: A woman who runs a general store. She is well versed in alchemy. Her original dream was to become an alchemist and travel the world, but her mother and uncle opened a general store, leaving her stuck making potions instead.\r\nShe seems to be close to Christopher, often showing concern for him.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc:
Perion's general goods merchant. He sells potions he makes himself. However, there's no noticeable difference in quality compared to potions sold elsewhere. 
Like Harry, he also warns people not to steal, which makes it seem that Perion has more thieves than one might expect.
Arturo also repeatedly warns people not to steal. But judging by the way he grips that staff, asking too many questions about it would probably end badly.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: Perion's Warrior job instructor and chief. He is highly respected among the people of Perion as a true Warrior. He values a healthy body and mind, and his people see him as a strong yet kind-hearted pillar of the community. He has a reserved personality, which may be why there are so few entertaining rumors about him. \r\nBut there are legends, passed down by word of mouth, as well as an anonymous book titled "The Perion Chronicles: Heroes of the Highlands' Records." That book includes the story of how he became the chief. If you want to learn more about his younger days, greet him with respect and say, #e'I pay my respects to the legend.'#n.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc: An archaeologist studying ancient trees and fossils in the Rugged Rocky Zone. As a scholar, he tries to approach and solve every problem through academic analysis.\r\nIf monsters appear, for example, he thoroughly analyzes the cause and works to eliminate the root of the problem. He is said to be Dr. Bruce's mentor.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc:
A member of Perion's excavation team. He has a severe lack of direction, so it takes him ages just to reach the excavation site. He's also incredibly clumsy and frequently loses his belongings. 
In fact, I just came across his lost canteen, and not for the first time. Shuang must be having quite the headache dealing with him.
                                      - Chronicler Harper
It seems his talent as an explorer is utterly nonexistent.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc:
A Perion resident keeping watch around the village in the Armor Pig Land. 
Although once known as a seasoned Explorer and a former Job Instructor, he's returned to Perion after reaching the limits of his abilities.
After hearing that his friends entered Azmoth Chasm, he debated going himself, but was surprised to hear they'd evacuated soon after.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.regionDesc: The ruins of Sharenian, an ancient nation that once ruled all of Victoria Island, still remain here. \r\nOther similar structures can be found scattered throughout Victoria Island.

0.desc: This goblin-like creature, who wears a wooden plank over its face, delights in startling people.\r\nIt's been interfering with excavation work, much to Captain Shawn's concern. Most likely, the construction site's evil ambient magic created this creature.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: This petty thief-like monster wears a stone slab over its face.\r\nIt's been interfering the with excavation work, much to Shawn's concern. Most likely, the construction site's evil ambient magic created this creature.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: A former Sharenian war hound awakened by demonic power. Surprisingly, it does little more than charge, with no other notable attacks. Perhaps because it's an undead monster, it drops no edible loot at all.\r\nAt least to me, it seems to have no real value. Still, it looks like it could make a decent bone broth. Despite what one might assume, they don't actually chew on each other's bones like dog treats.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: A former Sharenian war hound awakened by demonic power. Its entire body is tightly wrapped in bandages. Surprisingly, it does little more than charge, with no other notable attacks.\r\nPerhaps because it is an undead monster, it drops no edible loot at all. At least to me, it seems to have no real value. Still, it looks like it could make a decent bone broth.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: A former Sharenian soldier awakened by demonic power. Presumed to have been a guardsman, it swings its club with great force to strike its enemies.\r\nIt's clearly guarding something, but we have yet to determine what.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: A former Sharenian officer awakened by demonic power. It brings its sword down with crushing force against its enemies.\r\nClearly, it's guarding something, but we have yet to determine what.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: A former Sharenian commander awakened by demonic power. Its horse has risen into undeath as well. \r\nPerhaps due to its high rank as a commander, its eyes gleam with a fierce light. Clearly, it's guarding something, but we have yet to determine what.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

0.desc: The leader of the relic excavation team. He offers rewards to those who deal with the undead monsters impeding his work. There are rumors that he once secretly smuggled artifacts out of unexcavated ruins, but the truth of the matter is unknown.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: A friendly young member of the excavation team at the ruins. It's said she once served as the poster girl for an artifact excavation contest, but since I have no interest in relics you can't even eat, I wouldn't know much about it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: Agent M of Omega Sector, said to be carrying out an important mission. No matter how much food I offer, or what kind, he won't tell me what that mission actually is.\r\nOf course, that's what one would expect from an Omega Sector informant. People like this usually have a weakness you can exploit... Aha. There's a rumor that he enjoys eating fried Evil Eye tails drenched in sauce. That might be the key.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.regionDesc: Located in the deepest reaches of Ellinia, the Mysterious Forest, this is the stronghold of all magicians in Maple World. For countless years, it has served as the central hub for preserving and researching all forms of magic. \r\nGreat Magicians gather here to guide future generations of magicians, and it's said that the secrets of ancient, hidden magic still lie dormant within.

0.desc: This sparrow, from the eastern forest of Ellinia, has become a ferocious monster. It transformed itself into such to protect its nest from the other creatures of Ellinia.\r\nIt carries its nest atop its head, but the eggs inside have already lost any chance of hatching. Even so, it refuses to stop guarding them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

A wolf beastman affiliated with the Magician Association. Originally an ordinary wild wolf, it is said to have taken on its current form through magical training.\r\nNow devoted to magical research at the Magician Association, it is particularly focused on the study of parallel worlds. Outside of magic, it also seems to have an interest in cooking.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A fairy who sells general goods at the Magician Association. She is the older sister of Len, the general goods merchant fairy in Ellinia, and Lyn, the general goods merchant fairy in Ellinel.\r\nUnlike Len, Rana is wary of humans, and therefore makes the Magician Association, instead of Ellinia, her home.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A magical cleaning doll found in the East Forest of Ellinia. It is said to have been created by apprentice magicians to deal with the Evil Eyes in the forest.\r\nIt sometimes sings strange songs, never heard anywhere else in Maple World. It chants those songs' lyrics in a steady rhythm, without a melody as such. Rumors say that in another world, they call this style 'rap.'\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael
