4.desc: A magical cleaning doll found in the East Forest of Ellinia, created alongside Broomy and Broomer. Like Broomy, it delivers groan-worthy wordplay of unknown origin.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: A magical cleaning doll found in the East Forest of Ellinia. Its way of speaking is similar to the other cleaning dolls, but personality-wise, it seems to be the most cynical of the group.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.regionDesc: A mysterious magical village hidden deep within the vast forests of Victoria Island. All manner of mystical creatures and fairies live here in harmony, preserving the history of magic alongside ancient trees. \r\nAn air of enchantment fills the entire village, where powerful magicians gather to pass down their wisdom to future generations. It is said that anyone seeking to learn the power of magic must visit this place at least once.

0.desc:
A monster made of a squishy liquid, which uses its own viscosity to jump around everywhere. 
The Slime's inherent cuteness makes it a beloved monster amongst adventurers, which is why you'll often come across all sorts of Slime paraphernalia, such as hats and earrings. 
When you hunt Slimes, you'll often end up with small pockets of liquid, which have a very pleasant apple scent. The scented liquid can be used in cooking as well! Sometimes, it will give the pompom on its head to adventurers.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: When slimes come to live in dark habitats like Ellinia, they adapt to the darkness, and their bodies undergo changes.\r\nCompared to ordinary slimes, they move faster and have a higher avoidability rate, making them tough opponents for beginners.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A monster that resembles a winged human. It looks fairy-like, but actually comes from a corrupted line of fairies from the Black Mage's heyday. \r\nThis fairy has magic capabilities and can withstand large amounts of magic attacks. It tends to cast magic on its opponent, inflicting Abnormal Status, and then attacking while the opponent is in that condition.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A high-ranking monster of the fairy realm. Its wings and features are even more beautiful than those of other fairies, earning it wide admiration.\r\nIt also wields powerful magic, frequently casting spells that inflict Abnormal Status on its foes, so caution is advised.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc:
A lizard-like monster with a single eye. Is as evil and ill-tempered as it looks, directing all sorts of aggression toward adventurers.
It once lived in packs deep within dungeons, but for reasons unknown, it has since relocated and taken over the North Forest of Ellinia.
If you ever find yourself surrounded by Evil Eyes, do not turn your back and run. Stay calm, keep your eyes on them, and back away slowly.
                                      - Chronicler Ael
This chronicler would like to add further notes.
In the past, Evil Eyes lived in deep caverns or dungeons. However, some theorize that as more drakes developed a taste for Evil Eyes, their habitat was gradually destroyed, forcing them to relocate.
Evil Eyes favor complex terrain. This makes sense, as such environments are more effective for avoiding drakes.
Taking this into account, it is only natural that Evil Eyes leaving the dungeons would migrate to Ellinia.
On a separate note, Evil Eyes are well known across Victoria Island as gourmet ingredients.
Their flavor is generally chewy yet mild, with a particularly satisfying texture that has earned them a dedicated following. It's said that Cutthroat Manny of Kerning City often eats stir-fried Evil Eye tails.
Unfortunately, they are not to everyone's tastes, but with a shift in perception, they could be used in many more dishes. In fact, they are already being used in hamburger patties.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
Evil Eyes that once lived deep underground began moving into swamps, where they needed to hide themselves from predators.
As a result, they evolved camouflage and transformed into green Curse Eyes.
                                      - Chronicler Ael
This chronicler would like to add further notes.
Curse Eyes are also used as cooking ingredients. However, they tend to be even more divisive than even regular Evil Eyes. While Evil Eyes have a chewy-yet-mild flavor, Curse Eyes are known for their bitter taste.
Even so, there are dishes made with Curse Eyes. Some claim to have made grilled eel from them. Grilled eel made from Curse Eyes... That sounds more like alchemy than cooking.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
Even after Evil Eyes moved their main habitat to the surface, some of them instead retreated deep underground.
In places without even a trace of light, their bodies faded and turned white. Exposed to the demonic energy rising from the abyssal depths, they were reborn into a far more powerful form known as Cold Eyes.
These Cold Eyes, with their newly transformed bodies, soon resurfaced in the world.
                                      - Chronicler Ael
This chronicler would like to add further notes.
Cold Eyes are also used as an ingredient, though they feel more like a seasonal delicacy. They are genuinely refreshing, which is why they are often eaten in the summer, more for the cooling sensation than the flavor.
The most representative dish made with Cold Eyes is a strawberry-flavored ice pop. The recipe is said to be simple: prepare a Cold Eye tail and freeze it together with milk.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
Cold Eyes that emerged to the surface later underwent another stage of transformation after exposure to sunlight.
Under the sun, their once-white skin turned black.
Having gone through the greatest number of evolutionary changes amongst all Evil Eyes, they are the strongest of the group, and now dominate the North Forest of Ellinia.
                                      - Chronicler Ael
This chronicler would like to add further notes.
Surgeon Eyes are one of the more well-known ingredients on Victoria Island. Their appearance may be off-putting, but they are said to have a rich, nutty flavor. Their texture, in particular, is highly praised.
If you have no prejudice against unusual ingredients, it might be worth closing your eyes and giving them a try. There are even rumors that Surgeon Eyes are the secret ingredient in Moon Bunny's Rice Cakes, filling in whatever something seems to be missing.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: The daughter of Dr. Betty, a biologist. She seems to enjoy playing by herself, but also appears to be the type who gets lonely easily.\r\nIt's likely because her mother is often too busy with research to give her much attention. Rumor has it that she has taken a liking to a certain fairy. Perhaps she inherited her mother's curiosity.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: An Ellinian magician. One of Grendel the Really Old's disciples, said to be skilled at creating mysterious substances. If not for Grendel's approval, his appearance alone would make him seem suspicious.\r\nHe is said to have raised a mysterious monster in the past, but what he is up to now remains unclear.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc:
A fairy living in Ellinia. A graduate of Ellinel Fairy Academy, who introduces herself as a master of alchemy.
She says she can't remain in contact with humans for long, yet sometimes creates special items for them, or asks them to help recover lost belongings. Perhaps she actually likes humans more than she lets on.
She seems to be long-time friends with Rowen, the two of them having attended Ellinel together.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A fairy living in Ellinia. A graduate of Ellinel Fairy Academy and a classmate of Arwen. She currently assists Grendel the Really Old.\r\nLike Arwen, she seems wary of humans, but she clearly separates personal feelings from duty. Quiet, yet sharp and decisive in nature.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: This man owns the Forest of Endurance near Ellinia. Many rare medicinal herbs grow within the forest.\r\nShane claims he cannot allow just anyone onto his land, but in reality, it seems he will let anyone in for the right price.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: A man who manages the Forest of Endurance. He looks unmistakably like Shane's brother. He tends to casually boast about himself to anyone trying to leave the forest.\r\nStill, unlike Shane, he doesn't ask for money, so he may be fairly conscientious after all.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A fairy who researches pet magic. She helps adventurers with matters related to their pets.\r\nIt's said her magic has created many of the snail pets adventurers like to raise. She also seems to be acquainted with Cloy of Henesys.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: A man in Ellinia who handles storage services for adventurers. According to rumors, storage businesses across Victoria Island are monopolized by a single guild.\r\nIf you dig into it, you might uncover some rather interesting facts.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: A biologist who researches the many creatures of Victoria Island. Always busy with her work, she rarely seems to have time to play with her daughter, Anne.\r\nPlants, animals, fossils, monsters...if it was ever a living thing, she studies it without discrimination. She never speaks of her husband, so it seems she currently lives alone with her daughter. She also appears to visit Winston of Perion frequently.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: This fairy doesn't seem very diligent. Always overwhelmed with homework, she often asks adventurers to do it for her.\r\nShe claims to be far too busy to handle the assignments herself, but no one seems to know what she's actually busy with.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.desc:
An informant of the Cygnus Knights, currently dispatched to Victoria Island on an intelligence-gathering mission. Highly suspicious by nature, he is wary of anyone who approaches.
He seems particularly interested in the herbs that grow in Shane's Forest, though it is unclear what he intends to use them for. According to Shane, Hersha is so suspicious, he might actually be suffering from paranoia.
Still, that level of suspicion seems to help him gather a wide range of information. Even if he appears careless at times, he is still a member of the Cygnus Knights.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

11.desc: This fairy sells weapons at a shop in Ellinia. Most of her stock is for apprentice magicians.\r\nJudging by the forge inside the shop, it seems she makes the weapons personally. Despite appearances, this fairy may be quite skilled with her hands.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

12.desc: A fairy who sells armor at a shop in Ellinia.\r\nShe offers a variety of armor suited for magicians, and is always seen together with Flora.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

13.desc: The owner of the general store in Ellinia. She sells potions and a wide variety of items for adventurers, and is widely known for being kind to customers.\r\nInside the shop is a large teddy bear, suggesting a fondness for cute plush toys. Her older sister and younger sister also run general stores in different locations.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

14.desc:
The Great Magician of Ellinia, the job instructor for all adventurer Magicians, and the leader of the Magician Association. As befits his status as a great Magician, his name is known throughout Maple World.
His exact age is unknown, but considering his connections with Alcaster, the Great Magician of El Nath, and Tatamo, the Chief of Leafre, it's clear that he is no ordinary old man. He currently resides in the Ellinia Magic Library, where he leads countless Magicians.
That said, not all rumors about him are favorable. According to the fairies, he once dabbled in dark magic. However, it seems he has since repented and now lives as a benevolent sage. That said, the fact that he never shows his eyes when speaking is a bit suspicious...
Both then and now, Grendel the Really Old has consistently believed in the pursuit of magic as a field of study. If you ever meet him, try greeting him with #e'The power of magic is quite spectacular.'#n
                                      - Chronicler Ael

15.desc: Somehow, this tree learned to speak. It seems to dislike how people find it fascinating. Like the other trees of Ellinia, it wants to grow tall, but for some reason it hardly grows at all.\r\nSeeing how it wishes other trees could speak like it does, perhaps it's actually lonely. If you're reading this, try talking to it when you pass through the forest path.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

16.desc:
A talking cat who lives in the North Forest of Ellinia. It seems to be treated as a sacred creature, but is said to be Grendel the Really Old's first disciple.
(There is much debate over who Grendel's top disciple truly is. Elwin and Fanzy both claim the title, but the prevailing view is that it is clearly Lily.) 
It is said that the cat was originally human, but transformed in magical accident. At times, its body even turns transparent.
                                      - Chronicler Ael
It's unclear how much of what Fanzy says is true. There are also rumors that it was not a magical accident at all. 
Was it really human to begin with? There are even stories that it was a cat granted magical power by Grendel the Really Old.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.regionDesc: A school for fairies, located deep within the mystical forest of Ellinia. \r\nFor many years, fairies have come here to learn and practice magic, and to nurture their skills at protecting the forest.

0.desc: A monster born from an ordinary slime commonly found across Victoria Island, fused with plant matter.\r\nIt's the result of a slime consuming firefly plants over a long period of time. Although it has lost its soft, squishy body, it now gives off a much stronger and fresher scent.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
A monster born from an ordinary slime commonly found across Victoria Island, fused with a fairy.
How a fairy-type monster and a liquid creature like the Slime came to be combined remains unknown.
Ellinia scholars have proposed several theories, but for the sake of your imagination, I will refrain from recording them here.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A manifestation of the water element. Said to appear often in forests rich with magical energy.\r\nAs a pure element, it poses no harm to humans.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A manifestation of the wood element. It is said to appear often in forests rich with magical energy.\r\nIn the past, such elements were easy to encounter, but now they are said to appear only rarely, deep within fairy forests untouched by human hands.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc:
A forest protector.
At a glance, it resembles a small Fairy, and some theorize that Wisps are the manifested souls of fairies who have accepted the power of darkness.
If not attacked first, it poses no threat to humans.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc:
A monster born from a magic book used at Ellinel Academy, imbued with magical power.
At fairy academies, where magic is frequently handled, objects are often infused with magic and become monsters in this way.
Among them, these magic books are said to be particularly violent, reflecting the feelings of children who would rather avoid studying.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc:
A monster born from a Raging Tome infused with magic.
Because it contains stronger magic than a Grumpy Tome, it's faster and more powerful.
Still, it's at a child's level, so it's far less threatening than ordinary monsters.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: A monster derived from an onion-shaped Mandraky. When approached, its strong onion scent brings tears to the eyes.\r\nAlthough violent, it's often cultivated in large quantities due to its value as a medicinal herb. Mandraky species are said to be grown only by fairies.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: A monster derived from a turnip-shaped Mandraky. While Oniony is used as a medicinal herb, Turnipy is mainly used as food.\r\nIt is commonly used in light soups, and dishes made with Turnipy are considered healthy meals, making them popular among young female fairies.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc:
This mole, living in the Ellinel Forest, ate too many Mandrakies and turned into a monster.
It was originally small, but after adapting to the effects of the Mandrakies, it grew massive and gained greater intelligence.
It kidnapped the Mandrakies of Ellinel and uses them as its underlings. Admiring winged fairies, it dreams of taking a fairy bride.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc:
The headmaster of Ellinel Fairy Academy, a long-established educational institution for fairies. Known among fairies for her gentle smile.
Once wary of humans and unwilling to associate with them, she is said to have since resolved those misunderstandings and chosen a path of harmony with humanity as a whole.
Though somewhat old-fashioned, she is a fine educator, and dearly loves the children of the academy.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
The faculty head of Ellinel Fairy Academy. Despite his intimidating appearance, he is a devoted educator who cares deeply for the children.
Perhaps because of his love for fairy children in particular, he seems wary of outsiders.
There appears to be something about him that differs from other fairies, but it feels best left unspoken.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc:
A magician affiliated with the Ellinia Magician Association. Highly curious, he is always searching for new subjects to research, which has led to misunderstandings and even detentions.
Though constantly absorbed in his studies, he frequently loses his research materials and journals, so his results are said to be less than impressive.
Still, he is a kind-hearted Magician who puts himself at risk to help improve relations between fairies and humans.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A fairy girl currently attending Ellinel Fairy Academy. She always wears a playful smile and enjoys spending time with her friends.\r\nShe seems more interested in playing than studying, at least for now.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A fairy boy currently attending Ellinel Fairy Academy. He seems to admire the heroes who sealed the Black Mage.\r\nHe often feels down, saying that Phiny teases him frequently.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: A fairy girl currently attending Ellinel Fairy Academy. She seems very interested in her appearance.\r\nShe seems to want a boyfriend, but doesn't seem particularly interested in her classmates.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A fairy boy currently attending Ellinel Fairy Academy. He has a strong interest in theater, and practiced a play, right under the teachers' noses, based on the heroes who sealed the Black Mage.\r\nHowever, he now seems completely absorbed in the story of a different hero.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
A fairy boy currently attending Ellinel Fairy Academy. He mistakenly believes that Tracy has a crush on him.
Among the children, he is especially fond of playing pranks.
He often teases Tosh for being close with the girls, but this chronicler knows well that deep down, he does so out of jealousy.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc:
A fairy who sells general goods at Ellinel Fairy Academy.
She is the youngest of three sisters, alongside Len in Ellinia and Rana at the Magician Association.
Like her eldest sister Rana, she's been wary of humans, and even after graduating from Ellinel, she is said to have remained there instead of leaving.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.regionDesc: A silent forest of colossal old-growth trees south of Ellinia. A single Sylph resides here, having left town in search of peace and quiet.

0.desc: A strange creature born of Elodin's Spiney Puff Bush. Was it influenced by the Dim Forest's magic?\r\nIt attacks with the thorns sticking from its body. Handle with care!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: Shimmer Songbirds that have mutated under the influence of the forest's magic. The magic seeps into the egg before it hatches, the chick emerging a monster.\r\nBut why the eggshell upon its head? Cases of high intelligence, like Ruenna's familiar Shula, are extremely rare.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A Forest Howlet transformed from exposure to enchanted moonlight. It's accustomed to darkness and more active at night.\r\nThe eggshell on its head also changed color for reasons unknown.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: Forest hay given life through supernatural means.\r\nFilled with dust and hay. I recommend caution. Disturbing these may provoke the Forest Howlets.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: Formed after a hay bundle was left out to gather an extraordinary amount of dust.\r\nIt's unusually aggressive--is it aggravated by the dust? They blend into the forest shadows, so take care not to step on them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: A Wisp of Elodin Forest. These spirits resemble small fairies. Are these the spirits of fairies who accepted the power of darkness?\r\nThey usually won't harm humans unless attacked first.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A fox monster of the forest. The firefly on its head lights the way at night.\r\nTake care not to touch the firefly, in spite of its cute appearance. When angered, it attacks with electricity.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: An aged Forest Glimmerfox. It can generate a greater charge than an ordinary Forest Glimmerfox.\r\nIt's extraordinarily expressive for an animal. Very popular among fairies.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: Spirit of Elodin Spring. Born from the water element, its body is made entirely of water.\r\nThe forest's magic sometimes makes such spirits appear as human girls. Legends tell of such spirits luring humans into the water to drown them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: A being born when the elemental energy of a Spring Spirit grows especially strong.\r\nIt possesses more potent magic than ordinary Spring Spirits. Caution advised.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc:
A fairy who lives alone in Ellinia's South Forest. Unlike other fairies, she is said to prefer the dark. Hence her residence in the deep forest.
Her friend Arwen notes that she is unusual for a fairy.
She has a gentle appearance, but her eccentricity is well known. Rumors once spread in Ellinia that she is a witch.
All this, simply because she prefers the dark.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: One of Ruenna's familiars. He gathers herbs from the forest for her and even occasionally purchases supplies in town.\r\nEven in the darkness of the South Forest, he never loses its way. The firefly on his head serves as a guide.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: One of Ruenna's familiars. He travels to the outside world to trade goods on Ruenna's behalf, as Ruenna never leaves the forest.\r\nSince he's nocturnal, he never loses his way in the darkness of the South Forest. He still wears the eggshell that he hatched from for reasons unknown.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A mysterious bird that lives deep in the South Forest. She's constantly singing. Her beautiful song keeps peace in that part of the woods.\r\nRecent observations indicate that she is teaching her song to her chick.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A baby bird in Elodin. He's the child of a songbird, but he's astonishingly tone-deaf. His song reportedly sends forest animals into a frenzy.\r\nHe has contentious relationship with Ruenna the Fairy. Still, he works hard to sing in order to protect the forest.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

11.regionDesc: A village of elves with a long and storied history.\r\nOnce the seat of a prosperous society, the entire settlement fell into an unnaturally long slumber after falling under the Black Mage's curse. It is only recently that they have once again rejoined the world.

0.desc: An enchanted target dummy used by the young elves of Elluel for archery practice.\r\nDespite its blank expression, it is moved by elven magic, making it difficult to hit. Is its power contained in the sprout on head?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: An enchanted target dummy used by the young elves of Elluel for archery practice.\r\nThe sprout on its head has bloomed into a flower. Is this related to the dummy's increased agility?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: An enchanted target dummy used by the young elves of Elluel for archery practice.\r\nFlower Dummies are used in elven archery examinations. These are the fastest and strongest among the target dummies. They're recognizable by the flower in full bloom on their heads.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc:
Elluel's Elder of Magic is one of three elders who guide their people under the Ruler of the Elves. He is responsible for matters of magic.
Elven magic is ancient and mysterious. Due to the elves' tendency to remain within Elluel, little is known about it. Philius himself remains a mystery.
Philius serves as a spiritual pillar to the elves second only to Mercedes.
Reports indicate he is also dedicated to maintaining his hairstyle.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
Elluel's Elder of War is responsible for advising the Ruler of the Elves and training young elves in archery.
She sometimes leads her forces in battle personally. Despite her youthful appearance, Cygnus Knight intelligence estimates that she is around 240 years old. When around Mercedes, she tends to act childish.
She's been heard calling herself the weakest Elder of War in history, but her skills are said to rival the Chief Knight of Wind's. Athena Pierce was taught archery by Danika.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: Elluel's Elder of Life. She's said to be the oldest among all the elves in Maple World, though even Mercedes does not know her true age.\r\nShe oversees every aspect of daily life in Elluel, from clothing to food to construction. She also serves as a close adviser to the Ruler of the Elves.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc:
A young elf of Elluel. He looks like a child, but he would be an adult by human standards.
Deet was one of the elves trapped in ice by the Black Mage's curse; before the curse, he is said to have been a peer of Athena Pierce.
In the past, he was a close rival to Athena Pierce in archery.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A young elf of Elluel.\r\nRoa loves reading and is said to have memorized the contents of every book in Elluel's Corridor of Knowledge.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc:
A young elf of Elluel.
He often burst into tears, though this sensitivity is attributed to his pure heart.
He possesses no particular talents compared to his peers and seems to envy Deet and Roa, who each have talents of their own.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: An elf of Elluel. Caretaker of the Corridor of Knowledge and teacher to the younger elves.\r\nAccording to the children, he has absolutely no talent for archery.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
Merchant and master potion maker of Elluel.
He uses the elves' sacred spring to craft his potions, making them particularly effective at healing wounds.
His fondness for money is not usually found in elves.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: Blacksmith and equipment merchant of Elluel. Crafts a wide range of weapons, from practice bows for young elves to Mercedes's famous Dual Bowguns.\r\nAlso forges Mercedes's enchanted bolts. The secret to crafting these has been passed down through his family for generations.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc:
The keeper of Elluel's storehouse. Insists on a peculiar hairstyle that covers his eyes.
He gives off an irresponsible impression, but he has never been observed to shirk in his duties.
Frequently argues with Ethos. Are they best friends?
                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.desc: Cygnus Knight. Captain of the unit dispatched to protect Elluel.\r\nHe appears strict, but has a reputation for kindness. He was once a prominent Knight before the founding of the five divisions. After taking a severe wound in battle, he stepped into his current role as guard captain.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

11.desc:
Cygnus Knight. Dispatched to guard Elluel with Lalich and Vel.
He was originally a Thunder Breaker. Allegedly he requested reassignment after being unable to handle the enthusiasm of Chief Knight Hawkeye.
He seems content with Elluel. Perhaps he's happy to be away from Neinheart's nagging.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

12.desc:
Cygnus Knight. Dispatched to guard Elluel with Lalich and Crusoe.
He was the first to volunteer for the mission. He appears to have a particular interest in elven culture.
Reports indicate that he has a crush on Danika.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

12.regionDesc: A small island off the east coast of Victoria Island, renowned for its beautiful golden sands. Gold Richie built a luxury resort here, and it's now a premier vacation spot.\r\nHowever, there have been recent sighting of Black Slimes on its shores...

0.desc:
A form of Black Slime that is carrying coconuts. Native to Gold Beach.
Slime experts claim that these slimes do not occur in nature. Result of magical research?
Why are they appearing in such large numbers?
Black Slimes known to cling to plants and animals. It's possible that the first things the Coconut Slimes saw upon arriving at Gold Beach were baskets of coconuts.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to a palm tree. Native to Gold Beach.
Lies in wait disguised as a real tree, only occasionally revealing its true form.
The slime replaces the functions of the tree's roots, feeding water and nutrients to its host.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to an emerald clam. Native to Gold Beach.\r\nThe slime itself hides underground, only surfacing when necessary. The clam on its head appears to still be alive.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to a violet clam. Native to Gold Beach.\r\nAdapted to the strategy of an ambush predator, lying in weight until an opportune moment. The clam acts as living camouflage.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A form of Black Slime that has absorbed a seagull. Native to Gold Beach.\r\nHas gained the ability to fly from its host. It has also gained the seagull's temperament and is more aggressive than other slimes.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc:
A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to a red inner tube. Native to Gold Beach.
Slimes such as this will sometimes take an inanimate object as a host. Is this a mistake or some sort of adaptation?
Possibly a mistake, but the slimes seem to enjoy drifting along the waves in their tubes.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to a blue inner tube. Native to Gold Beach.\r\nIt's unusual for slimes to take a non-living host like this. When viewed from afar, a group of these slimes resemble a rolling tide of darkness.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to a shrimp. Native to Gold Beach.
This species of shrimp usually grow to the size of a palm. Has slime somehow enhanced its growth to reach this size?
In spite of health hazard, these overgrown shrimp have become a local delicacy on Gold Beach.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to a flying fish. Native to Gold Beach.\r\nThe weight of the Black Slime keeps the flying fish from gliding over the water. Instead, these slimes run tirelessly along the shore.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc:
A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to a Starfish Octopus. Native to Gold Beach.
Why did these slimes choose hosts that were so much bigger than them? Does this grant some defensive or offensive advantage?
Even if the advantage is significant, the slimes do not look happy...
                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.desc:
A form of Black Slime that has attached itself to a Seashell Octopus. Native to Gold Beach.
The slime appears to be unhappy carrying such a large octopus around everywhere.
Black Slimes are known for infesting plants and animals. This one seems to have chosen its host poorly.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

11.desc:
The progenitor of the Black Slimes of Gold Beach. Its host is a giant mutant octopus.
Possesses a greater intelligence than other Black Slimes and is highly driven to create more of its kind.
Its host octopus is also very powerful, but it is unable to dive to its native waters because of the slime on its head. Unable to swim in shallower water, it rides in an inner tube.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc:
The resort manager at Gold Beach. Known for abrasive demeanor and antagonism towards his employer.
Runs the resort with impressive efficiency in spite of his personality. Gold Richie has entrusted him with several other businesses as well.
Looks down on Little Richie for "riding on his father's coattails."
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: Gold Beach staff member. Well regarded at the resort for his diligence and enthusiasm.\r\nClose surveillance indicates that he had a secret motive for taking this job: so he could work on his tan.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: The son of Gold Richie, world-renowned merchant and billionaire. Spends most of his time at Gold Beach and with his pets.\r\nHe is driven to be a businessman like his father, but seems to lack the necessary talent. Often claims to be busy with work; in actuality, he is usually playing with his pets instead.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A staff member at Gold Beach. Obsessed with the finer things in life.\r\nSeems unreliable, but Gold Beach has thrived with his assistance. He cares deeply for his fiancee, Lois.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A staff member at Gold Beach. Advertised as a native of the island. He's actually just wearing a costume. Pointing this out causes irritation in the other staff and should be avoided.\r\nHe considered leaving Gold Beach once, but those plans changed for unknown reasons.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

13.regionDesc: This massive whale-shaped submarine makes its berth in the strait between Henesys and Ellinia. \r\nIts captain is Kyrin, a quarter-elf who has traveled the world in pursuit of Black Mage. She's recently settled on Victoria Island to train a new generation of Pirates.

0.desc: This pig gets a blue ribbon. Literally. It's got the competition beat in both strength and flavor. Just thinking of those succulent cuts of pork gets my mouth watering!\r\nThe best pork comes from Blue Ribbon Pigs. But don't underestimate them! They're aggressive, reckless, and fast. If you're not careful, your the one who'll end up on the dinner plate.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc:
In the world of pigs, ribbons are not given likely. They are reserved for the strong and the delicious.
Observe the Ribbon Pig. Looks at those powerful leg muscles. Doesn't your mouth just water at the sight?
                                      - Chronicler Harper
After doing some...fact-checking of my esteemed colleague's notes, I must admit that ribbons do seem to hold special significance for the pigs who wear them. Some of Harper's more dubious claims have yet to be reviewed.
                                      -  Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
Plain old pigs. You'll find them on beaches, in pastures, and on pig farms, of course. They move fast and are great at ramming.
They're also edible, which makes them one of my favorite monsters.
Have you ever eat pig head? There's nothing better! They raise pigs on the Nautilus, though those oinkers are as rowdy as the pirates sometimes.
You know what they call a misbehaving pig? Dinner. Heh...
                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc:
Nobody knows where these pigs came from. They just showed up at the farm one day, ribbons all torn up, and started attacking everyone.
Unreasonably strong, those things. And the look of murder in their little piggy eyes... The memory of them makes me shudder! These are no ordinary Ribbon Pigs.
The farmer doesn't what makes a pig go bad like that. All I know is they're causing all kinds of ruckus and have got to be stopped.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

0.desc:
This lively pirate adores Kyrin and has an axe to grind with Sharyl. (Seems to me that Sharyl's got a crush, but that's none of my business.)
She's always picking on Sharyl, but her pranks usually go right over his head. Call it cultural differences between humans and whales.
Even though she's a sailor, she's quick to get seasick. Why join the Nautilus's crew, then? Well, rumor has it she can talk to octopuses. A talent like that's only got so many uses.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc:
The quartermaster of the Nautilus is also in charge of studying strange treasures and other knicknacks the pirates bring aboard.
He's probably most famous for that time he invented an explosive new weapon, then immediately got shipwrecked before he could test it out. Don't tease him too hard about it, mind you. The memories still give him frightful shivers.
Believe it or not, this pirate can't swim! He can be as prim and proper as he likes, but I say it's shameful!
                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc:
A Pirate stationed at the watchtower high above Nautilus Harbor, keeping a weather eye on the horizon for squalls and monsters alike.
Watch duty can be lonely and hard, but he has the Pirates' close allies, the seagulls, there for help and company. Taking care of the seagulls seems to be part of his job.
These seagulls love shiny things, and often steal them for their nests. Because of this, someone's glasses keep going missing.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc:
The Nautilus cleaner in charge of sanitation. Despite her dirty job, she never goes a day without a smile.
Cleaning seems to be her true passion. Perhaps because of that, she's always watching me whenever I carry snacks.
Ever notice how people who carry brooms around are always acting that way?
Since she cares so much about cleanliness, she always keeps one eye on Jack, who supposedly never bathes at all.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc:
A foul-smelling Nautilus crew member. In the ten years he's been on board, he apparently hasn't bathed one single time.
Mrs. Reade has tried everything, but he remains filthy.
It's amazing he hasn't been kicked off the ship yet. Uh-oh. He's coming this way...
                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc:
The Nautilus's armor merchant. Sells sturdy armor, designed with Pirates in mind.
Jack constantly scratches his head while passing by, making him worry about the armor getting coated with dandruff.
You know, it's strange. The Nautilus has a quartermaster, and yet the Pirates seem to buy their armor with their own money...
                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc:
The Nautilus's weapons dealer. Sells weapons for Pirates, and truly loves his job.
For some reason, he also sells mops and handbags. Are those just for Mrs. Reade?
Again, there's supposedly a quartermaster on board, so why are weapons each sold separately?
                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc:
The Nautilus's general goods merchant. An elderly man who looks like he ought to take more breaks.
Word is he's a long-time resident of the Nautilus, and he handles nearly all potion supplies.
He may not be the most fit crewmate, but none of the younger Pirates can match his experience.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc:
The Nautilus's storage keeper, always seen 'puffing' on an empty pipe.
He manages almost everything on board. Though he seems a bit unreliable at first glance, he's actually very capable.
He sometimes stores extremely heavy items. I'm no sailor, but I wonder if that affects the way the ship sits in the water.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc:
This Pirate is usually seen in front of the navigation room, with his eyes covered. He carries himself like a high-ranking officer.
He looks stern and intimidating, but he's actually a really good guy, so don't be afraid of him.
No one knows why he keeps his eyes covered, but apparently, he CAN see. If you spot anything suspicious at sea, Muirhat ought to be the first to know.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc:
This Nautilus crew member keeps to his post on the lower decks, sweeping the deep sea for unusual sounds.
He is so busy that he often skips meals. With hearing that sharp, one would expect him to notice the nearby water leak, or at least feel it, but apparently not.
He seems to be friends with the Nautilus chef, Tangyoon.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc: A crew member plugging a hole in the Nautilus's hull. She needs glue to repair it properly, but cannot find anyone to make the glue, nor the turtle monster required for ingredients.\r\nShe can't keep blocking the hole like this forever, especially not with that shark in such close proximity.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc:
He looks like an ordinary dolphin, but he's actually a prince of the Whale tribe. When his mana runs low, his transformation breaks, and he returns to dolphin form.
If you find Sharyl struggling to keep his form steady, try bringing him a Mana Elixir. If you're lucky, you might then see him transform into a human.
He has feelings for Kyrin, and makes Valerie very jealous. Unusually, he finds Stump's Eyeball cute.\r
                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc:
Who better to be the Pirate Job instructor than the captain of the Nautilus? Kyrin is a dignified beauty, with an aura of bold charisma. Being one quarter elf, she...looks good for her age, let's say.
It was she who led the Nautilus to Victoria Island in pursuit of the Black Mage.
She's suprisingly close with Dr. Kim of the Omega Sector; in fact, he played no small part in the Nautilus's construction. They stay in touch, and if you walk past the navigation monitors, you might see the good doctor's face on them.
Her rallying cry, befitting a pirate, is #e'This voyage will never end.'#n
                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc: Believe it or not, seagulls have a king, who organizes their society and maintains their alliances. The pirates have years of friendly history with the seagulls, and have made an annual tradition of visiting the seagulls' Lord Jonathan.\r\nThere was a time when this noble bird would train experienced captains and teach them new skills. He must have soared to great heights in his younger days.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

15.desc:
The crew of the Nautilus has this panda to thank for their ever-full bellies. A master chef, he uses his culinary wizardry to craft extraordinary dishes from the bits and pieces of monsters.
Adventurers crave the dish that bears his name, and he's said to be working on a fifth version of it now.
When he's not pouring his heart and soul into the kitchen, he manages the ship's cattle.
Yes, there are farm animals on board the Nautilus. Weird, I know, but they're there.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

16.desc:
The Nautilus crew's best trainer, her appearance is as charming as her manner is gentle.
She works out constantly, not to bulk up, but to build practical strength.
Black Bark is always asking her for more training, but she always helps without complaint. She likes lemons and is afraid of mice. Curious adventurers are welcome to stop by her training grounds. Just keep them clean, like she does.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

17.desc: The navigator of the Nautilus, he brings strength and style. A true Pirate at heart, with a love for exploration, adventure, and treasure.\r\nIf an adventurer seems like they might not be up to the task, he often sends them to Shulynch for training. Unrelated, but he once gave Kyrin a dress as a birthday gift.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

18.desc:
Don't be alarmed if you see this monster in the Nautilus generator room. It's tame. Helpful, even!
It watches over the glowing stones, checks for any abnormalities, and manages the pearls that power those stones too.
It's well-respected for its diligence, and its crewmates consider it highly intelligent. It apparently has a similar friend in Mu Lung.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

19.desc: A Nautilus crew member keeping watch along the beach. Occasionally deals with monsters that gather near the shore. Usually sleepy, which gives the impression he's lazy.\r\nDespite that, he's actually very responsible. And being able to sleep peacefully while Ribbon Pigs run wild nearby? That's just impressive. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

20.desc:
A dairy cow from the Large Forest Trail. Lives peacefully with its family. She's a big girl with a big heart.
Her milk is fresh and rich. If I weren't such a law-abiding citizen, I might try to sneak some when no one was looking..
The cows don't have their own barn yet, so she lives with the pigs. They seem to be getting along.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

21.desc:
Utah's father, and the owner of Utah's Pig Farm. He and Utah are always busy with farm chores and management.
He seems a bit forgetful, especially about his lunch boxes.
It's a big farm, and you can't take care of it all on an empty stomach, so I hope he gets better at remembering to eat.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

22.desc:
The dog grew up at the Utah place. For some reason, it really doesn't like Utah.
Utah seems to get particularly nervous whenever the dog is eating.
In fact, the dog is sniffing my pocket for snacks right at this very moment. I should go. 
                                      - Chronicler Harper

23.desc: Gustav's son. He helps his father manage the huge pig farm.\r\nHe and Camila, from Henesys, have been friends since childhood, and the town is always buzzing with 'will they, won't they' gossip about the two of them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

24.desc:
Utah's mother. Skilled with her hands, she always makes delicious-smelling lunchboxes.
She seems to do a full house cleaning every weekend, dragging Utah along each time.
Because of this, Utah sometimes ends up in a tug of war between his household chores and his farm chores.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.regionDesc: An ancient ruin southeast of Henesys. The indigenous inhabitants, called Karuppa, live mainly in a small nearby village.\r\nThe temple sits atop a vast underground complex, said to hold a magnificent artifact of the ancient world.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: A lifeform found in ancient, forested ruins near Henesys. Surprisingly hostile, it bounces on its pistil and stamens to attack its prey. For that, locals know it as a 'Pudgy Flower.' How does it move? Some ancient power, perhaps? I couldn't properly say.\r\nBut I can say this: these flowers carry an oil, which one can extract for many fine uses.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: A lifeform found in ancient, forested ruins near Henesys. Its movements resemble those of the Pudgy Flower, but its petals carry venom inside, earning this species the name Toxiblossom.\r\nLike the Pudgy Flower, one can extract its oil for various uses. Have no fear -- the extraction process causes all the venom to evaporate.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: A monster found in the ancient forested ruins near Henesys. It most closely resembles a rabbit, though it is certainly not one. Scholars are divided as to whether it qualifies as a living creature, with some theorizing that the relic itself is its true body. \r\nIt emits a strange aura, and the glowing flower atop its head can lash out in surprisingly dangerous ways.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: A monster found in the ancient forested ruins near Henesys. It most closely resembles a rabbit, though it is certainly not one. Scholars are divided as to whether it qualifies as a living creature.\r\nIt rides a bird-shaped relic, which may in fact be the physical manifestation of a forest spirit bound to the artifact.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: A monster found in the ancient forested ruins near Henesys. It most closely resembles a rabbit, though scholars believe it to be a plant species instead. It wanders through the woods, using a censer-shaped relic as a mount, from which it appears to be inseparable.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt\r\n

5.desc: A monster found in the ancient forested ruins near Henesys. It most closely resembles a rabbit, though scholars believe it to be a plant species instead. It wanders through the woods, using a pottery-shaped relic as a mount.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: A lifeform found deep within the forested ruins near Henesys. Despite living in the woods, it relies on flames for defense, generating said flames via special trees. Fire-resistant armor is highly recommended.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: A lifeform found deep within the forested ruins near Henesys. Despite living in the woods, it relies on flames for defense, using flint-like stones to generate said flames. The stones could be of use in outdoorsmanship, were an adventurer to acquire them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt\r\n

8.desc: A lifeform found deep within the forested ruins near Henesys. Despite living in the woods, it relies on flames for defense, generating said flames via special trees. Unlike ordinary Log-a-Rhythmic Bugs, this species uses special trees that grow poisonous mushrooms, making it far more dangerous.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: A lifeform found deep within the forested ruins near Henesys. Despite living in the woods, it relies on flames for defense, using flint-like stones to generate said flames. Unlike ordinary Sparkinstone Bugs, it uses special stones that emit green smoke, making it far more dangerous.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc: A strange monster found deep within the ruins of Partem Forest. Wondrously, the ruins themselves seem to have taken on lives of their own. Perhaps they were created in a manner similar to Stone Golems. If you choose to approach them, be mindful of your toes.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc: A strange monster found deep within the ruins of Partem Forest. Wondrously, the ruins themselves seem to have taken on lives of their own. Perhaps they were created in a manner similar to Stone Golems. They are even larger than their cousins, and a careless step could mean a broken bone or worse. Always watch your footing inside the ruins.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc: A strange being found deep within the ruins of Partem Forest. This species resembles the Ruins Sentinel, but gives off a faintly sinister aura.\r\nHeavy chains with weights are attached to its body, possibly meant to restrain it from moving.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc: A strange being found deep within the ruins of Partem Forest. This species resembles the Ruins Guardian, but carries a brazier on its back, blazing with blue flames. The flames radiate a sinister aura, which seems to sharpen the creature's vision somehow.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

14.desc: A strange being found deep within the ruins of Partem Forest. This species resembles the Ruins Sentinel, but its body is completely stained in deep darkness, with shards of red light leaking through.\r\nThe root of this sinister energy seems to be the plant growing on the creature's head.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc: A strange being found deep within the ruins of Partem Forest. This species resembles the Ruins Guardian, but its eyes burn with dark fury. When agitated, it swings its chains in a recoiling motion.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc:
A resident of Karuppa Village. While others believe in legends, he claims that he does not.r

Despite his words, he seems to show considerable interest in ruins tied to particularly ominous legends.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: The chief of Karuppa Village. He treats outsiders with respect and is willing to speak with them, withholding judgment until he can see their character.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: Residents of Karuppa Village. They are generally gentle in nature, and give off a warm glow. They often appear to be resting, drawing nourishment from sunlight.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: One of the residents of Karuppa Village. More cautious of outsiders than the others -- not out of hostility, but because they admire brave people and consider themselves timid. Try approaching slowly and keeping a respectful distance.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: This general goods merchant works in Karuppa Village, selling items much like those found in other villages. Given the nearby ancient ruins, one might expect something special, but surprisingly, that does not seem to be the case.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: The storage keeper of Karuppa Village. At a glance, the small boxes made of leaves do not seem capable of holding much, but surprisingly, they store a large number of items. They seem potentially useful in situations where storage might be needed in a hurry.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: The only Partem resident who lievs outside the village itself. This...odd fellow observes the ruins from the village outskirts. He is said to collect strange objects, and seems far more curious than the other locals.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

15.regionDesc: One of the most mysterious hot springs in the Maple World, this is a special place where cute and quirky slimes gather and live together.\r\nAll around the hot springs, slimes can be seen playing in the bubbles and foam. The warm waters here are said to restore energy to weary adventurers.

0.desc:
A massive slime found in the lowest depths of the Ramuramu Hot Springs. According to the Chief Slime, the Slime God's angels descended long ago to personally carry cute slimes to the world beyond. Could that truly be?
Based on the reports from its initial discovery, and stories told by other slimes, the Guardian Angel Slime appears to be the very slime that its god once deemed most adorable.
As a side note, this chronicler suspects that the Slime God's standards for cuteness are based on size, color, and natural appearance. When compared to other slimes, the type that experience sudden growth through a Growth Potion, this one is clearly cuter.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

Baby Slime Kkyu, from the Ramuramu Hot Springs. One of a slime trio, who move about in a small group and are often seen sticking together. This slime ends nearly every sentence with 'kkyu,' but it's hard to tell whether that is just an act to seem cute, since it sometimes speaks normally as well.\r\nUnlike the other slightly transparent slimes, this one has a rich, dense color. It somehow looks as if it would taste like soda.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: Baby Slime Myu, from the Ramuramu Hot Springs. One of a slime trio, who move about in a small group and are often seen sticking together. This slime ends nearly every sentence with 'myu,' but it's hard to tell whether that is just an act to seem cute, since it sometimes speaks normally as well.\r\nAmong the three baby slimes, this one is the largest and has a more mature personality, making it seem like the eldest.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: Baby Slime Q, from the Ramuramu Hot Springs. One of a slime trio, who move about in a small group and are often seen sticking together. This slime ends nearly every sentence with 'Q.'\r\nThe smallest of the trio, it looks like a tiny snack. With its strawberry milk color, it seems like it would taste like a candy bar. Or maybe more like jelly, since it's a slime. Unfortunately, it just noticed me salivating. This is awkward.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: The chief of the Ramuramu Hot Springs. He sports a beard several times longer than his own body, but it's actually fake. He is still quite young, and wears it to look older.\r\nOddly, his personality seems to change depending on whether he has the beard on or not. With the beard, he acts like a dignified village chief. Without it, he is gentle and soft hearted, much like the baby slimes.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: Despite its shyness, this slime has an EXTREMELY LOUD voice. It's not particularly small either, so its presence is hard to miss.\r\nBecause it's so shy, it always needs someone else to relay messages on its behalf. Most of the time, the yellow baby slime does the talking.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc:
A slime that tries to look as cute as possible by puffing itself up. It takes a deep breath and does everything it can to make its body appear larger.
However, something will invariably make it laugh and, consequently, deflate. Still, it seems to enjoy even that, bursting into giggles and rolling around on the ground.
Sometimes it laughs so much it's almost unsettling. That said, when it STOPS laughing, you know things have gotten serious. Diet-wise, it's willing to try just about anything.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: A slime that tries to look as cute as possible by puffing itself up. It takes a deep breath and does everything it can to make its body appear larger.\r\nIt wears a flower decoration on its head, which matches its body color quite well. It seems to have a good sense of color. Among the three gluttons, this one feels the thickest and most solid.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: A slime that tries to look as cute as possible by puffing itself up. It takes a deep breath and does everything it can to make its body appear larger.\r\nIt attempts this constantly. Judging by how long it can hold its breath, its lung capacity seems impressive, and when it finally exhales, you can feel the force of its breath. Maybe it'd be a good singer.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: A slime that wears glasses and considers itself intelligent. I suppose 'intelligent' doesn't always equate to 'well-spoken.' It speaks with a kind of slur, drawing out vowels, and no one seems to know if that's intentional or not.\r\nDespite its appearance, it's soft hearted and sensitive.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: A slime enjoying a hot spring bath while drinking orange juice...and by that, I mean 'holding an orange with a straw stuck in it.'\r\nIs it really drinking anything? It's been holding the straw in its mouth for quite a while. Also, leaving an orange soaking in hot spring water like that would probably broil it. Then again, that might be a treat in its own way...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: Baby slimes from the Ramuramu Hot Springs. They seem enjoy speaking in cute little voices, befitting their age, and also enjoy soaking in the shallow waters of the hot springs.\r\nOne should note that the green one, in the wool hat is not actually submerged in water. Still, they seem to be having fun.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc:
The slime we're all most familiar with. It seems to be something of a liaison for its people, and has a bit of a mischievous side.
Surprisingly, it possesses a great deal of scientific knowledge, rivaling even the Smart Slime. And I know this because it wouldn't stop talking about it...
In any case, don't let your guard down around it. Its body slam packs far more power than one might imagine.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc: Apparently, soaking in the Ramuramu Hot Springs can make you cuter, or so this slime believes. Surprisingly skilled at floating and drifting.\r\nIts skin is smooth and slick, probably from bathing so often. It's got a kind of tangerine color to it, which...makes me wonder what it would taste like if I licked it. Maybe I can get away with trying it once...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc: Apparently, soaking in the Ramuramu Hot Springs can make you cuter, or so this slime believes.\r\nRather than a slime, it looks more like a gourd, especially when it's floating in water. On an unrelated note, it has a habit of adding an 's' sound to the end of its sentences.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc: It has a habit of adding an 's' sound to the end of its sentences.\r\nIt has a habit of ending its sentences in a casual, drawn out way, almost like a yawn -- which goes along well with its generally sleepy look. This slime has a strawberry milk color, like an almost-ripe strawberry. Maybe just a quick lick...?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

15.desc: Don't say the words 'Defiled Tree Sap' around this species, or the slimes will be all over you. Verbally, I mean.\r\nThis slime is softhearted and extremely fragile, its past dreams of cuteness having ended in tragedy. It's now training at the hot springs in hopes of returning to its original form.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

16.desc: A slime that enjoys bathing in the hot springs while sitting in a basket. It resembles the Mascot Slime. The basket fits the slime's shape perfectly, making it quite pleasant to look at.\r\nDoes it still count as soaking in the hot springs if it's just sitting in a little boat on the surface? Maybe it just likes the feel of the steam.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

16.regionDesc: A castle of mushrooms, accessible from Singing Mushroom Forest southwest of Henesys. The kingdom is inhabited by mushrooms, whose intelligence is comparable to that of humans. \r\nRumor has it their princess is an exquisite beauty.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: A mushroom found in Mushroom Castle, with a chandelier perched on its head. \r\nWhy a chandelier? I have no idea. Sometimes, mushrooms only make sense to mushrooms.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: A mushroom found in Mushroom Castle, clad in heavy iron armor. So completely armored, in fact, that its mushroom form is no longer visible. It might not even be a mushroom anymore. Of course, that's not particularly important.\r\nWhen facing an opponent this heavily armored, it's best to swing blunt weapons, or thrust sharp ones where the armor isn't. Archers may find such armor somewhat difficult to deal with, but with enough training, it shouldn't be impossible to aim for the gaps in the helmet.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: A soldier seagull under the command of the Black Viking that invaded Mushroom Castle. Judging by the dark circles hanging under its eyes, it seems to be in need of sleep.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: A soldier seagull under the command of the Black Viking that invaded Mushroom Castle. Its eyes are heavy with exhaustion. Perhaps it's low in rank and burdened with menial tasks.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: A soldier seagull under the command of the Black Viking that invaded Mushroom Castle. Others call it the 'Warm Viking,' so this chronicler has followed suit, though it's hard to say whether that description truly fits. One can't help but wonder how it manages to fly with a body like that.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: A soldier seagull under the command of the Black Viking that invaded Mushroom Castle. It differs little from the Warm Viking, except that it wears an eyepatch over one eye. \r\nWas it already injured in another battle? If so, one would think it would be best not to send it into combat again.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: A soldier seagull under the command of the Black Viking that invaded Mushroom Castle. Unlike the other soldiers, it looks quite stern. Compared to the Vikings who forego weapons, this species' upright posture and axe in hand give it quite a formidable appearance.\r\nThat said, the axe itself seems poorly maintained, as its blade is chipped.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: A soldier seagull under the command of the Black Viking that invaded Mushroom Castle. Unlike the other soldiers, it looks quite serious. It carries a blunt weapon in one hand. The helmet is pulled down so low that it makes one wonder whether it can see properly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc: A soldier squid under the command of the Black Viking that invaded Mushroom Castle. It oversees the prison slaves. \r\nHow a squid ended up working alongside seagulls is unclear, but its loyalty to Black Viking's forces is unquestionable.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: The one who led the invasion of Mushroom Castle. Between the pink helmet with its wings and heart-shaped ornament, the cute ribbon in its braided hair, and the pink bunny slippers, this one clearly has very strong personal tastes. \r\nTricked by the Prime Minister's nonsense, it attacked Mushroom Castle, but must have regretted it after seeing Violetta.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: The king who rules Mushroom Castle. He once lost his kingdom to King Pepe, but with the help of many others, he defeated the true culprit, the Prime Minister, and managed to reclaim his land. Surely, he will not lose the royal seal again. \r\nThese days, he hopes to see a grandchild who closely resembles his daughter, Violetta.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: The daughter of Mushking, and the only princess of the Mushroom Castle. If beauty were a crime, they say, she'd never leave the dungeon. For the sake of others, she has no choice but to conceal her lovely face.\r\nThis chronicler HAS seen Violetta's face once, and in that moment, I found myself frozen like a stone.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: The Mushroom Castle's captain of the guard. He protects the castle responsibly and well. His younger brother also serves as a guard, and is growing into the role nicely.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: The prime minister of Mushroom Castle. He once betrayed the castle, but now claims to have renewed his vows of loyalty. \r\nThat said, he doesn't exactly give off a trustworthy impression.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: The sole general goods merchant in Mushroom Castle. Despite the location, which some might find exotic, the merchant sells nothing particularly special. Most items there are the same ordinary goods one would find in any other town. \r\nIt seems the mushrooms' everyday lives are as mundane as most others.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: A resident of Mushroom Castle. A passionate fan of Princess Violetta, who loves even the princess's cold demeanor and never misses a meeting of the fan club.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: A mushroom who somewhat resembles a legendary hero. Heroic tales have been growing in popularity recently, with one academy even putting on a hero-themed school performance, so perhaps this mushroom is simply following the trend. \r\nThat said, if you listen closely to what Ghostie says, he might just look like a butter-grilled mushroom.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
This mushroom seems to resemble a pair of twins from somewhere. It's especially fascinating how the cap has been carved to create that hairstyle. 
Their voice has a distinctive musical quality to it, certainly worth listening to at least once.
...I shouldn't be the only one to suffer.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

17.regionDesc: A region located at the center of Victoria Island. Centered around a massive tree, it connects to six villages via branching paths, which is why it's called Six Path Crossway.

0.desc:
A guard stationed at the entrance to Sleepywood, though his reputation is not particularly good. He often asks for ingredients, saying he needs to cook nourishing food for his mother, or alcohol, claiming he and his mother have run out. 
While his devotion to his mother is admirable, he dozes off far too often to be trustworthy. Does he even deliver the gifts properly? You may need to press him by asking, #e'Did you deliver the gift to your mother?'#n
As an aside, Luke once remarked that he wanted to go on an adventure, and in exchange for someone helping him gather the necessary supplies, he gave away a family heirloom. That heirloom turned out to be none other than the 'Old Bronze Nordic Helm.'
Even though I walk the path of a Marksman myself, I still believe the Gold Nordic Helm is the finest Nordic Helm there is.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: A pilot and flight instructor from Edelstein. In the past, he earned great fame in Edelstein for his exceptional skills. Though he has since retired and now works as an instructor, it seems he could return to active duty at any time, were Edelstein to call upon him. If you find yourself in danger in the skies, perhaps a heartfelt prayer will bring him to your aid.\r\nHe does offer flight lessons, but this chronicler personally believes that riding in a passenger plane, with one's fellow adventurers, is all part of the joy of adventuring in general.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: A guide at the station to Orbis. In the past, travelers had to pay Mesos to buy tickets and wait for the ship, but now, alchemists from Magatia have developed mana-saving floating stones, allowing airships to operate for free. \r\nDespite this added convenience, fewer and fewer people are using the airships, and Joel seems disappointed by the decline.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: A Stewardess at the station to Orbis. In the past, travelers would wait for the airship while listening to Sterwardess Cherry talk, but these days, ships come and go so frequently that there's no time for chatting. One could say some of the romance has faded.\r\nOh, and if you've purchased a private airplane through Irvin, be sure to take it out for a flight at least once so it doesn't go to waste. Stewardess Cherry will assist you with the boarding process.\r\n                                      -  Chronicler Ritt

18.regionDesc: A village, located in the deepest reaches of Victoria Island, where massive caves intertwine with a silent forest. The atmosphere is always dim and heavy with moisture -- and with ancient magic, as if the land itself were in a cursed sleep. \r\nThough dangerous monsters roam their hunting grounds, the hidden dungeons' long histories and mysterious treasures draw brave adventurers, ready to challenge them time and again.

0.desc:
This dragonkin was driven out of Sleepywood's underground dungeon. Apparently, its brethren exiled it for being the weakest and least intelligent.
However, while it is weak by draconic standards, it's still fast and strong enough compared to other monsters.
It mainly inhabits the areas around Sleepywood's swamps.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
A mushroom monster revived by attaching a Charm of the Undead to mushrooms that adventurers defeated prior.
Opinions vary on who revived these mushrooms and for what purpose. The most widely accepted theory is that it was the work of a magician researching dark magic.
Because it's dead, and being held together with magic, it will collapse if the dark charm is removed.
However, due to its zombie nature, it continues to charge forward even when injured, making it difficult to deal unless one exploits that weakness.
Their nest can be found in the Ant Tunnel near Sleepywood.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: An undead mushroom monster, revived with a the Charm of the Undead.\r\nThese mushrooms' distinctive facial expression makes them look like they are under much duress.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc:
An undead variant of the enormous Mushmom species. Some initially believed that this creature was simply larger Zombie Mushrooms, but rather, it appears that someone revived a dead Mushmom with a Charm of the Undead.
The Zombie Mushmom inhabits the Ant Tunnel, and charges at any adventurer it sees.
Its jumping attacks are even more dangerous, unexpectedly so. Should you encounter one, stay calm, hang onto a rope, and observe the situation before you engage in combat.
If you succeed in defeating the Zombie Mushmom, you can obtain the mushroom that was parasitizing it. Despite any hopes to the contrary, it's not edible, and is every bit as poisonous as it looks. It's best to take it to a mushroom researcher.
                                      - Chronicler Summer

0.desc: A master equipment craftsman. He even forged the Gladius for Tristan, the hero who sealed away Balrog.\r\nHe is the brother of Sabitrama, and together they are said to have arrived in Sleepywood to eliminate the dangers of the Cursed Temple and seek the truth. To other adventurers, he serves as a guide to the Cursed Temple.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: A master herbalist, and the younger brother of Chrishrama. He is said to enjoy traveling the world to collect a wide variety of herbs.\r\nUnlike Chrishrama, he shows no particular interest in pursuing the truth.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc:
An unidentified statue. It gives off a mysterious aura, and it would be unwise to touch it carelessly.
If you place your hand on the statue, a strange light envelops your body and transports you somewhere else.
In that 'somewhere else,' you can obtain rare flowers, but unless you're a highly skilled adventurer, escaping will not be easy.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A man in charge of storage room operations in the Sleepywood region. Despite it being the most dangerous area on Victoria Island, he carries out his duties without a second thought.\r\nOne can't help but wonder what kind of connection he might have with the other men who manage storage rooms in towns across Victoria Island.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc:
The middle sibling between Manji and Ilji, this wandering warrior travels across Maple World.
Unlike his older brother Manji, he is quite talkative and enjoys telling stories, particularly stories about Manji himself. The younger brother seems less than pleased at that, as he feels those stories are neither heroic nor particularly impressive.
He always stands as if he might draw his sword at any moment, but no one has ever actually seen him do so. Some say it's because his draw technique is too fast to see, while others claim it's simply because he has never drawn his sword at all.
Among adventurers, opinions on Chun Ji's true skill remain sharply divided.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: A monk undergoing rigorous training to temper the soul. It's said he can heal souls tainted by darkness.
