For some reason, he feels difficult to approach.\r\nHe usually remains deep in meditation, but when an adventurer with potential appears, he seems willing to help train their soul as well as his own.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: The younger brother of Manji and Chun Ji. Theirs has been a family of warriors for generations now, but unlike his brothers, Ilji appears rather timid.\r\nHe is currently traveling across Victoria Island as part of his training, though it seems he often ends up relying on help from adventurers.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
One of Victoria Island's dedicated sentries, he keeps watch over Sleepywood.
Before becoming a guard, he studied the geography of Victoria Island. He appears to be highly knowledgeable about rare materials and various forms of magic.
Like Luke, who stands guard on the opposite side, he often dozes off while on duty. However, despite his calm, sedate exterior, one suspects he may be hiding great strength within.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc:
The sauna manager of the Sleepywood Hotel. He says his son, Ronnie, is always getting into trouble and causing him constant worry.
The only thing he treasures as much as his son is a certain book.
Strangely enough, he looks nothing like Ronnie. There's a rumor that Mr. Wetbottom had blonde hair, as Ronnie does, in his younger days, but his years of work at the sauna, and frequent after-hours lingering inside it, have left him looking the way he does now.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc:
The receptionist of the Sleepywood Hotel. She helps run the hotel alongside the two brothers, Mr. Wetbottom and Mr. Sweatbottom.
She is kind and courteous, but is known for keeping a clear professional distance from adventurers. Some adventurers even visit the hotel and use the sauna every day just to learn her name, making her surprisingly popular among a small group of devoted fans.
She looks so much like Rina from Henesys that some suspect the two might be sisters.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.desc:
The sauna manager of the Sleepywood Hotel, and the twin brother of Mr. Wetbottom.
It's impossible to tell the brothers apart by appearance alone. Usually, the older brother, Mr. Sweatbottom, is said to manage the general sauna.
Like Mr. Wetbottom, there are rumors that he was blond and handsome in his youth.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

11.desc:
The son of Mr. Wetbottom, the sauna manager of the Sleepywood Hotel.
Living in Sleepywood, one of the most remote places on Victoria Island, he doesn't have many toys to play with, so he's made a hobby out of drake-watching.
It sounds quite dangerous, but perhaps that's what it takes to survive in Sleepywood.
Lately, instead of watching drakes, his new pastime is sneaking looks at his father's treasured books.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

19.regionDesc: A giant tree that rises at the center of Victoria Island. Tainted with dark magic, its leaves have dried up, and its branches are grotesquely deformed.

0.desc: An unidentified dark-purple sap that emerged from the lower reaches of the Dark World Tree. It appears to have been tainted by the power of a cursed blade. Upon spotting a person, it rushes in quickly and slams down with heavy punches.\r\nWhen they swarm together in a group, the sight is extremely threatening. Even I would hesitate to try tasting them...though I imagine they might taste like grapes.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: This unidentified dark blue-black sap appears in the lower reaches of the Dark World Tree. The cursed blade seems to have caused it to decay.\r\nStories, possibly related, claim that an ordinary slime turned into Defiled Tree Sap simply by coming into contact with the Dark World Tree. The cursed blade's power appears to be that lethal to living beings. Even I would hesitate to try tasting something like this...although, if I had to guess, I'd say it probably tastes like soda.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc:
Soldiers who fought on the front lines alongside Alchetto. Among the demons, they were said to be the finest warriors. However, the power of the cursed blade has driven their pride and dignity into the mud.
They seem to retain more reason than the demon swordmasters do, but still shows a blind devotion to the 'law of strength.'
Carefully gather the demons' blades and bring them to Alchetto. In doing so, you can help preserve the honor of the demon warriors who fought to the very end.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc:
Dark demon swordsmen, twisted through evil magic into even stronger, more deadly forms. Their dark auras are unsettling enough, but their eyes...somehow both unfocused and obsessive. Creepy as hell, literally.
Whatever the cursed blade did to them, it left them mad with resentment and beyond all reason, turning them into rampaging beasts.
Carefully collect the demons' swords and bring them to Alchetto. In doing so, you can help preserve the honor of the demon warriors who fought to the very end.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc:
Dark demon axemen, twisted through evil magic into even stronger, more deadly forms. Their dark auras are unsettling enough, but their eyes...somehow both unfocused and obsessive. Creepy as hell, literally.
Whatever the cursed blade did to them, it left them mad with resentment and beyond all reason, turning them into rampaging beasts.
Carefully collect the demons' axes and bring them to Alchetto. In doing so, you can help preserve the honor of the demon warriors who fought to the very end.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: Soldiers who fought on the front lines alongside Alchetto. Among the demons, they were said to be the finest warriors. However, the power of the cursed blade has driven their pride and dignity into the mud.\r\nCarefully gather the demons' axes and bring them to Alchetto. In doing so, you can help preserve the honor of the demon warriors who fought to the very end.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: Once the elite of the demon army, these warriors terrified their enemies and bolstered their comrades. Now, however, they've fallen into disgrace, corrupted by the power of the cursed blade.\r\nCarefully collect these demons' shields and bring them to Alchetto. In doing so, you can help preserve the honor of the demon warriors who fought to the very end.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc:
Dark demon shieldbearers, twisted through evil magic into even stronger, more deadly forms. Their dark auras are unsettling enough, but their eyes...somehow both unfocused and obsessive. Creepy as hell, literally.
Whatever the cursed blade did to them, it left them mad with resentment and beyond all reason, turning them into rampaging beasts.
Carefully collect the demons' shields and bring them to Alchetto. In doing so, you can help preserve the honor of the demon warriors who fought to the very end.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc:
Once the elite of the demon army, these warriors terrified their enemies and bolstered their comrades. Now, however, they've fallen into disgrace, corrupted by the power of the cursed blade.
The same seems true of the wolves they ride, as all reason has burned away from their eyes. They do occasionally show hints of some recollection, but still seem to act on instinct, driven solely by the 'rule of strength.'
Carefully collect the demon wolves' fangs and bring them to Alchetto. In doing so, you can help preserve the honor of the demon warriors who fought to the very end..
                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc:
Dark demon swordsmen, twisted through evil magic into even stronger, more deadly forms. Their dark auras are unsettling enough, but their eyes...somehow both unfocused and obsessive. Creepy as hell, literally.
Whatever the cursed blade did to them, it left them mad with resentment and beyond all reason, turning them into rampaging beasts, as feral as the wolves they ride. Such rampages have even turned their bodies a dark crimson.
Carefully collect the demon wolves' fangs and bring them to Alchetto. In doing so, you can help preserve the honor of the demon warriors who fought to the very end.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: This dark, eagle-mounted demon appears in the middle and upper tiers of the World Tree. Both mount and rider to have been cursed by the infernal blade. There's not a trace of reason left in their eyes now.\r\nBeware the creature's massive wings and long claws. It swoops faster than one might expect, raking its opponents time and again before there's even time to drink a potion.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc:
This corrupted imp appears on the bottom tier of the World Tree. Even the demons' minions seem unable to escape the influence of the cursed blade.
It looks less threatening than the imps of Root Abyss, but remember, never judge by appearances.
It swoops in at incredible speed from who-knows-where and swings a razor-sharp scythe. Good luck drinking a potion in the time it gives you.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc:
A commander of the Black Mage's army. Among the mixed-blood demons, he was once frail and weak, but after making some kind of deal with the Black Mage, he became exponentially stronger.
It is said that he devoured the World Tree Alicia and briefly gained the power of the Transcendent of Life. In addition, the World Tree itself fell victim to the corrupting power of his cursed blade.
Most times, such overwhelming power leads only to ruin, even for the one who wields it. But who can say whether he'll share the same fate?
                                      - Chronicler Harper

0.desc:
A half-blood demon who remained at the encampment with Alchetto. He serves as the quartermaster, and is one of only two demon officers left at the abandoned camp, the other one being Alchetto himself.
He exchanges spirit stones, marked with the demon brand, for Stigma Coins. Since this crisis was caused by half-blood demons like himself, he wishes to resolve it with his own hands.
However, because those he must face were once comrades, he cannot bring himself to strike them down. Instead, he turns to other adventurers for help, offering the Stigma Coins as payment for that request.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: A half-blood demon soldier who remained at the encampment with Alchetto. He works mainly in logistics, though his old blade suggests he's seen a swordfight or two.\r\nHe exchanges Stigma Coins for AbsoLab weapons. Supposedly, these weapons were made for the demon army, but they seem much more powerful and distinctive than standard-issue military equipment, making their original purpose unclear.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: A high-ranking officer of the half-blood demon forces. It's said that he ranked just below Damien. He cares deeply for his men, and has a strong sense of responsibility to them. That's why he feels so guilty. He thinks his last rallying speech accidentally led them to corruption rather than victory. \r\nFor that reason, he chose not to return to his homeland of Tynerum, and instead remains at the Dark World Tree. From what I understand, he wants his old comrades, warped as they are now, to die honorably as demons should.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: A mixed-blood Demon who remained at the camp with Alchetto. Works in storage, and judging by his weapon, he appears to have been a former shieldbearer.\r\nWhen it comes to protection, he appears exceptionally capable. After all, he served as the storage seeker for Damien's personal unit, where security was paramount.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

20.regionDesc: North of Sleepywood, in the center of Victoria Island, is a large cavity beneath the roots of a giant tree. Originally filled with life, it is now tinged with darkness and exudes an eerie aura.\r\nHere lies a blond girl, trapped and unable to move beneath the enormous roots. The girl is, in fact, the World Tree itself. It's said that a demon wearing an eyepatch sealed her away in Root Abyss.

0.desc: An imp found in the Neglected Garden, a place with a gloomy, menacing aura and, clearly, some significance to imp-kind.\r\nA subordinate of the Seal Guardians, this fearsome imp has a devilish appearance. Even if his body is destroyed, it's said that the flame on his tail will go on blazing until it finally crumbles to ash.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: An imp found in the Neglected Garden, a place with a gloomy, menacing aura and, clearly, some significance to imp-kind.\r\nA subordinate of the Seal Guardians, this fearsome creature has a devilish appearance and wields a sharp spear. His tail is extremely sharp as well, so keep your eyes on both his ends.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: A fearsome imp with a devilish appearance, serving as a subordinate of the Seal Guardians. Even if his body is destroyed, the flames on his tail continue to burn fiercely.\r\nBecause of this trait, the remains of a Fire Imp often burn themselves to ashes. One more reason to be careful around fire, I suppose.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: A subordinate of the Seal Guardians, and the strongest among them, serving under Vellum. A fearsome imp with a devilish appearance and a long spear.\r\nCompared to Blazing Imps, he seems to possess greater intelligence, having learned to use weapons. Like others of his kind, his tail is just as sharp as the spear he carries, so should you face him in combat, be prepared.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: The Guardian of the Western Seal, tasked with protecting the seal of the World Tree. He hosts a massive tea party in the West Garden, waiting for guests. Hmm, a tea party... That does sound intriguing.\r\nI'm curious about what treats might be there, but it would be wiser to keep my distance for now. You never know, I could end up being one of those treats! This guardian is said to be the third strongest among the four of them. Rumor has it that he wears a strange hat and performs bizarre tricks. Some even say Pierre appears as two figures at once somehow. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: The Guardian of the Eastern Seal, tasked with protecting the seal of the World Tree. He is also a time mage, who has stopped time in the East Garden. His time magic appears to function in the form of hypnosis. Impressive as all that might sound, he seems to be the weakest among the four guardians.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc:
The Guardian of the Southern Seal, tasked with protecting the World Tree's seal. She quietly resides within the South Garden castle.
The Crimson Queen is an utterly grotesque being with an enormous body and three faces, with each visage housing its own distinct personality. She has a heart as cold as frost, and will dispose of her subordinates without hesitation if they dare to disappoint her.
She is said to be the second strongest of the three guardians. She despises uninvited guests, especially rude ones. Take it from me, you'd best be on your best behavior!
                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc:
The Guardian of the Northern Seal, tasked with protecting the seal of the World Tree. As Damien's closest confidant, he is the strongest among the four guardians.
He holds absolute loyalty toward Damien, and despite being draconic in nature, he seems to consider himself a kind of honorary demon.
They say he captures and devours his own followers from the lizard tribe, though I hope those are just rumors.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

0.desc: A traveling merchant. I have no idea how he even found his way to this place. Whether out of entrepreneurial spirit or just dogged stubbornness, he's running a shop even here. But hey, I'm not complaining.\r\nCarrying that heavy bundle all the way here must have taken real effort. To honor that dedication, I bought a watermelon.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

21.regionDesc: An ancient temple slumbering deep within Sleepywood, in the heart of Victoria Island. Forgotten for countless years, it has been tainted by dark energy, and a powerful curse now lingers within.

0.desc: Many adventurers have fallen prey to this fearsome draconic beast. That said, it's a creature of low intelligence, which arguably disqualifies it from being a proper dragon.\r\nIndividually, they can be outwitted, but a pack of them can swarm an adventurer, then drag them off straight to the dinner table.\r\n                                      -  Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
Like other Drakes, it is weaker and less intelligent than true dragons.
It currently nests in the Sleepy Dungeon, but in the past it lived amongst the clutches in the Perion Plateau. There, it adapted to the intense heat of the sun, so much so that it learned to throw long-range fireballs.
Not many adventurers can penetrate a Red Drake's tough hide, nor survive its roaring flames. That said, if an adventurer still wishes to try, ice-based attacks are certainly the way to go.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: This draconic creature inhabits the depths of the dungeon. Weaker and less intelligent than its more respected kin, it nonetheless is well adapted to its frozen lair\r\nIt can freeze its prey's very bones solid, transforming them into a pillar of ice. Should you tread anywhere near its lair, be on your guard.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A dragon that inhabits the inner areas of the dungeon. \r\nTainted by dark power from the Cursed Temple, it developed a hard, blackened hide. It wears the darkness like a sleeve, and slips through it effortlessly.\r\n                                      -  Chronicler Ael

4.desc: Somewhere within the Sleepywood Underground Dungeon is a famous Mobile Store. However, even deeper inside, an unidentified Snack Bar is said to open from time to time. \r\nStrangely enough, not a single person has ever actually managed to buy anything there. The moment you approach, the owner starts to bristle at you. It seems the dungeon's mobile store owner doesn't take kindly to the appearance of a new competitor.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc:
Some say this creature was the ancient demon Balrog's loyal pet cat, or that it was once an abandoned house cat who wandered into a dungeon and mutated somehow. 
However, according to a certain scholar's research, Wild Kargo is not a cat at all, but a reptile. That said, its eyes do look feline in nature, so one would suggest further study. 
Whatever its origins, this beast one of the most powerful anywhere near the Temple Entrance.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: This monster guards the temple deep within the Sleepywood Dungeon, at the center of Victoria Island. With the head of a bull and the body of a human, it wields a massive crescent-shaped spear, summoning lightning and laying waste to everything around it.\r\nIt is violent by nature, extremely fast, and its lightning strikes are devastatingly powerful. It stands watch at the entrance to prevent travelers from entering the Cursed Temple. There are rumors that it was assigned the role of gatekeeper as punishment for past sins. What those sins might have been is a mystery at present.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
A monster that guards the temple deep within the Sleepywood Dungeon at the center of Victoria Island. Rushing through the darkness with a massive spear, Taurospear is a fearsome creature that combines formidable defense and overwhelming attack power. 
Some adventurers consider it even more of a threat than Jr. Balrog. There are rumors that it was assigned the role of gatekeeper as punishment for past sins. What those sins may have been remains a mystery.
                                      - Chronicler Ael
Taurospear is one of the most significant monsters in the history of adventurers.
Veteran adventurers across Maple World recall the first time they beheld it, bearing down on them with its heavy spear.
However, a great enemy can also be a great teacher. Those adventurers carefully studied Taurospear's movements, and eventually learned how to perform his rushing techniques themselves.
Today, those techniques have evolved into many different skills with countless variations, but it's worth remembering that the origin of the charge began with Taurospear.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc:
An ancient demon with massive wings and razor-sharp claws. Particularly bold and 'lucky' adventurers sometimes spot it within the Cursed Temple of the Sleepywood Dungeon, at the center of Victoria Island. 
Why, and by whom, such a dangerous creature was left in the depths of the temple remains a mystery. Its physical attacks are powerful enough, but the destructive force of its magic is beyond imagination. 
In particular, the Balrog's meteor magic, where it spreads its enormous wings and summons a flaming hailstorm from above, is nearly impossible to survive.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: A Dark Demon King sealed deep within the Central Dungeon of Victoria. Decades ago, he was sealed away by the former Dark Lord 'Sung', the warrior 'Manji', and the hero 'Tristan', and gradually faded from everyone's memory.\r\nNow, however, he is slowly regaining his strength, revealing his ambition to break the seal and rise again.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc:
A wandering spirit without a physical body. Stories say he died long ago, but was unable to find peace, and remains in the mortal world. 
Those same stories suggest that the monsters of the temple are the reasons he continues to linger. In his efforts to suppress the temple's evil energy, so it's said, he repeated his ascetic practices until only his soul remained. 
He calls himself the 'Insignificant Being,' but nomenclature notwithstanding, it may not be possible to hold back the Cursed Temple's monsters without him.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: An adventurer investigating the Sleepywood Underground Temple, keeping watch over the dark entities slumbering within. In the past, he gained fame by exploring all across Victoria Island. \r\nHe often winds up injured, but always grits his teeth and carries on.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A general goods merchant who sells almost anything you could ask for. No one knows how he managed to come in this far, but to adventurers exploring the Underground Temple, he is always a ray of hope.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc:
This unidentified man does business with adventurers along the passage leading to Balrog's Temple. 
His name and origins are unknown, but his items, which he crafts in exchange for spoils from the Balrog, are certainly first-rate.
He seems bound by Balrog's chains, which raises many questions. He may be connected to the Balrog's resurrection, but for now, he seems benign enough.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A warrior and disciple of Manji. He remains in the Cursed Temple to stop Balrog, and wears the same outfit and straw hat as Manji out of admiration for his master. \r\nThough he often sighs and wears a lazy expression, he is surprisingly responsible and well-mannered.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc:
A demon from another world who introduces himself as a scholar studying souls. He spreads otherworldly magical weapons, known as 'Soul Weapons,' to adventurers. 
His speech is casual yet terrifying, sometimes remarking on the scents or tastes or various souls, or promising that he doesn't eat people he can speak with. He is said to be a friend and distant relative of the demon 'Ergoth,' who once brought about the fall of the great Sharenian Empire. 
How beings like Murgoth and Ergoth came to Maple World, or where they might have come from, remains unknown. What is certain, however, is that their realm does exist, and that it poses a definite threat to Maple World.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A warrior who once stood alongside the former Dark Lord 'Sung' and the swordsman 'Manji' to stop Lord Balrog. \r\nAs the wielder of the legendary Gladius, he was renowned for his bravery across Maple World. Now, with only his soul remaining, he watches over the evil energy of Lord Balrog, seemingly waiting for a powerful warrior who can carry on his will.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

22.regionDesc: A small island, covered in snow and ice, off the southern coast of Victoria Island. \r\nIt was once inhabited by humans, but most of them have left. Now, only a single human girl remains, living among the penguins.

0.desc: A special monster that can only be seen in Rien.\r\nA member of the of the Muru species, featuring unusually thick lips.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: A special monster that can only be seen in Rien.\r\nIt looks fully grown, even aged, but is really only a teenager in Muru years.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A special monster that can only be seen in Rien.\r\nNotable for the Baby Muru on its head.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A special monster that can only be seen in Rien.\r\nCovered in white fur, as if made out of snow. Looks as if direct sunlight could melt it away.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc:
A special monster that can only be seen in Rien.
Only a select few adult Muru grow to be like this.
Has a horn on its head, and sports a relatively powerful attack for a Muru.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc:
The last human girl remaining on the island of Rien, known for ice, penguins, and very little else. A member of the Rien Clan, she has long awaited the return of a hero.
With her blue eyes and hair, she gives off an air of mystery. True to her lineage, as a descendant of a clan that once stood against the Black Mage, she is highly capable in many fields. In particular, her skill at deciphering codes is said to be unmatched in Maple World.
She is known to have a somewhat cold and distant side, but considering who her older brother is, that may not be so surprising.
That brother, of course, is Neinheart, the strategist of Empress Cygnus, who is widely known for his formal personality.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
This penguin lives on the island of Rien, making a living by dealing in weapons and armor.
Despite his lack of opposable thumbs, he's quite the craftsman, and makes many types of goods from scratch (though as far as weapons go, he only seems to make polearms).
One would think a penguin would be used to the cold, but he nonetheless wears a full hat.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc:
A general goods merchant penguin in Rien. Since herbs don't grow on the island, he sources ingredients from the mainland to make potions.
His primary ingredients are giant bellflowers, which he imports from Mu Lung.
However, because they invariably arrive frozen solid, he has to spend hours and hours thawing them out, often with his own body heat, before he can use them.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: This penguin serves as the storage keeper of Rien, guarding the island's treasure vault.\r\nThe vault also holds emergency rations for the penguins, and the keeper is troubled by the number of penguins trying to sneak in and take them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc:
The spirit of a boy, apparently, who resides within a certain polearm wielded by the hero Aran. It's said that spirit-imbued weapons resonate with their wielder, allowing them to harness new levels of power.
However, such weapons do not accept a new wielder easily. Only those who pass the spirit's trials can earn the right to join such weapons in battle.
Maha, of course, is no exception. At present, it accepts no wielder other than Aran, and even Aran would tell you that the weapon can be stubborn at times.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: A penguin living in Rien. As a hobby, he takes in and raises baby huskies. Apparently, there are times when he mistakes wolf pups for huskies and raises them anyway.\r\nHe is said to enjoy taking the baby huskies out on sleigh rides.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: The oarsman penguin of Rien, who sails the straits near the island. He uses his pet whale as a boat.\r\nThe two of them enjoy going fishing together.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
A master of the penguin martial arts and trainer of penguin warriors.
By studying techniques that a hero of the past left behind, he is said to have developed a polearm-based fighting style, optimized for penguins' builds and capabilities.
That said, his polearm practice often leaves him with an aching back.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: A penguin of Rien. A warrior training in penguin martial arts, he manages the Rien Training Center together with Puo.\r\nAs Rien's finest warrior, he dreams of someday testing his strength against Aran.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: One of the wolf species living on the icy plains of Rien. Such wolves were once wanderers of the world, but now seem to have settled on the island.\r\nThey appear to be at odds with the area's native penguin population. As for their attitude toward humans, while they are wary at first, there are rumors that those who pass the Wolves' Test may receive the blessing of their chieftain.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

23.regionDesc: A strait south of Victoria Island, near Rien. \r\nRecently, the water temperatures have been rising, a phenomenon that has caught the locals' attention.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc: An ammonite fossil monster with another ammonite fossil embedded in its forehead.\r\nAs rising temperatures caused the permafrost to melt, the underlying rock layers were influenced by magical minerals, giving rise to this monster.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: A fish fossil monster with another fossilized fish embedded in its forehead.\r\nAs rising temperatures caused the permafrost to melt, the underlying rock layers were affected by magical minerals, giving rise to this monster.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A monster born from pollution. It gives off an overwhelming stench.\r\nA byproduct of mechanical development, which came into being after being influenced by magical minerals.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A monster born from discarded waste. It gives off an overwhelming stench.\r\nIt came into being when byproducts of mechanical development were influenced by magical minerals.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: At first glance, this individual looks like a seal monster, but it's actually a Black Wing lackey wearing a seal costume.\r\nThe seal doll on his head is a high-quality prop with a moving tail. Judging by the face paint, he seems to have prepared this disguise quite thoroughly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: At first glance, this individual looks like a walrus monster, but it's actually a Black Wing lackey wearing a walrus costume.\r\nThe walrus doll on his head is a high-quality prop with a moving tail. Judging by the face paint, he seems to have prepared this disguise quite thoroughly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A Warmer Bot deployed by the Black Wings to melt the glaciers of Rien. It operates by spewing waste, and is the cause of rising sea levels around the area.\r\nIt appears to have been built using the mechanical technology of Edelstein.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: A shaver bot designed to transport ice melted by the warmer bot. It looks to have been carrying ice from Rien to an unknown destination.\r\nIts mechanical style suggests it was built in Edelstein.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: A tank-type incineration machine created by the Black Wings to melt the glaciers of the Riena Strait. A Black Wings lackey sits in the driver's seat.\r\nUsing its tank treads, it moves swiftly across the icy terrain, using its mounted flamethrower and ice drill to attack glaciers and enemies alike.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc: A native penguin of Rien. He is the younger sibling of Puri Puri, who runs a general goods shop in Rien proper.\r\nTo serve the peoples of the Riena Strait, he operates a general store at the Glacial Observatory.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: A native Malamute of Rien. She is the younger sister of Alvesh, who is in charge of Ice Station 2.\r\nTrue to her Malamute nature, she has a keen sense of smell. Perhaps for that reason, she can't stand the scent of penguins. Personality-wise, she carries herself with diligence and dislikes laziness.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A native seal of Rien. Unlike many of Rien's indigenous inhabitants, who tend to dislike one another, Dachi seems to harbor no ill feelings toward the others.\r\nA peace-loving seal who enjoys the sea and sailing.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc:
A native penguin of Rien. Evng among the penguins, Putan seems especially hostile toward the other indigenous peoples.
Putan considers the Malamutes to be antisocial and the seals to be frivolous.
He takes great pride in being a penguin.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A native seal of Rien. He serves as the helmsman on a ship traveling through the Riena Strait. Despite being a seal, he's a poor swimmer, which is why he learned how to pilot ships instead.\r\nHe's a friendly, easygoing fellow with a fondness for jokes.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc:
An archaeologist who studies sites all over Maple World. Has a strong interest in permafrost and glacial regions, which led to a research project in Rien.
Considers the work paramount, despite being deathly afraid of monsters.
Hails from Henesys, and doesn't handle Rien's cold very well.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A penguin researcher, and Rien native, he monitors the climate of the Riena Strait from Ice Station 1.\r\nHe is always busy running around the station, and constantly focused on observing the area's short-term weather and long-term trends.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
A native Malamute of Rien and Alviola's older brother, he runs Riena Strait Ice Station 2.
Usually calm and well-mannered, but having never left the Rien region, he also has a naïve side and knows little about the outside world.
Like other Malamutes, he has an extremely keen sense of smell, which often gets him into awkward situations.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc:
A native seal of Rien. He is in charge of Riena Strait Ice Station 3, and guards the underwater cave.
Well known for his kind heart, he hopes that all the natives of Rien can learn to get along peacefully.
All that said, it seems he absolutely cannot tolerate being mocked or called stupid.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc:
An old woman living in the Riena Strait, known as the 'Frostwitch' (though, by all accounts, that's only a nickname, and she's not an actual witch).
After rising sea levels left young native children with nowhere to go, she took them in, and has been raising them until they can stand on their own.
Her mannerisms are brusque, but her heart is warm as cocoa.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

24.regionDesc: A mysterious city in the sky, floating high above against a backdrop of clouds and stars. A pure, noble energy flows through the entire city, and visiting adventurers prepare for their next journeys amid its breathtaking scenery. \r\nShips departing from the city's port are said to open routes to other continents, playing an important role in expanding access to new realms ripe for adventure.

0.desc: One of the fairies who lives in Orbis. A nymph with feathered wings, she usually flutters around in the sky, unless there's something strange happening.\r\nLike a lot of fairies, she seems not to like humans, but that seems like it's mostly just talk. Actually, from what I can see, she gets along with humans pretty well.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc:
A stray dog wandering around Orbis. With no owner to see to his grooming, his overgrown fur hangs messily over his eyes.
In spite of this, the residents of Orbis make sure he's regularly fed, so he doesn't seem to be in any danger of going hungry. Maybe if I had a Fairy's Horn Flute, I could understand what Moppie is saying...
                                      - Chronicler Q
Since one of mankind's highest purposes is petting puppies, I went ahead and gave him plenty of scritches behind the ears.
Apparently, he's very intelligent; he's been waiting for his owner for over 30 years. He's surprisingly spry for a dog of such advanced age.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: One of the residents of Orbis. Although Lisa's got birdlike wings, she can't fly, since she's half human and half fairy. \r\nShe's had to deal with some discrimination because of her mixed heritage, but since she understands where humans AND fairies are comin' from, she plays an important role in Orbis Village mediating between the two.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc:
The storage keeper of Orbis. 
Though she does have those birdlike wings, her wings are unusually small, so she can't fly very high--she just manages to hover a little above the ground. 
Items you leave in her care are stored in sturdy boxes and locked up with large keys.
                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: The armor merchant of Orbis. She's a nymph with birdlike wings on her back and a curious, cheerful personality \r\nShe's always interested in humans and stocks a selection of armor sized to fit human buyers.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: The weapon merchant of Orbis. She's a nymph with birdlike wings on her back but, unlike Nuri, she doesn't much like humans. \r\nShe's friends with Rowen, a fairy from Ellinia, though they haven't seen each other in a long time.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: The general goods merchant of Orbis. \r\nShe's a nymph with birdlike wings on her back who works hard to gather all the necessary ingredients to brew quality potions. Every now and then, she travels to Ellinia to collect ingredients for her potions.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: One of the staff members at the Orbis Station. She stands at the station's entrance and provides information on all of the facilities you can find there. \r\nAccording to Agatha, Orbis Station has flights connecting it to Victoria Island, Ludibrium, Leafre, Mu Lung, Ariant, Ereve, and Edelstein.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: One of the staff members at Orbis Station. She stands at the station entrance and provides information about each of the platforms. \r\nIsa is quick to point out that Orbis Station is quite large and the platforms look very similar, so visitors end up getting lost or at the wrong platform every day.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: One of the staff members at the Orbis Station. She assists passengers boarding the airship bound for Victoria Island. \r\nThe route between Orbis and Victoria Island is heavily traveled, so the flights there and back are always crowded.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: One of the staff members working at Orbis Station, assisting passengers boarding the airship bound for Ludibrium. She's the twin sister of Ramini, a stewardess who works aboard the airship to Leafre.\r\nThe question is, which is the older sister? When I asked, they both insisted that THEY are the elder sister, making it impossible to tell which of them is actually older...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: One of the staff members working at Orbis Station, helping passengers boarding the airship bound for Leafre.\r\nShe's the twin sister of Sunny, a stewardess aboard the airship to Ludibrium. Since Leafre is known to be a dangerous place filled with dragons, she always warns passengers that only well-prepared adventurers ought to be making the journey.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: A crew member at Orbis Station who assists passengers bound for Ariant.\r\nAs you might guess from his clothes, he's actually from Ariant originally. Since many visitors are unfamiliar with Ariant's culture and style, he's been sent to Orbis to provide guidance.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc: One of the fairies living in Orbis. Although he's a nymph with birdlike wings on his back, he is actually incapable of flight. Apparently, his body is a bit too heavy to lift, so flapping his wings doesn't accomplish much more than tiring him out. \r\nHe absolutely adores cats and can't stop bragging about his own feline companion, Nero. It seems he also has an older sister living in another region.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

14.desc: One of the fairies living in Orbis. She works as a housekeeper and people often tell her that she could totally pass as a human. Thing is, that seems to be a source of stress for her. Some speculate that there may have been a human ancestor somewhere in her lineage. \r\nShe's a distant relative of Neve, the glove maker. Unfortunately, the homeowner up and disappeared, so she's not even getting paid for her work right now. ...Are fairies eligible for unemployment?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

15.desc: An Omega Sector soldier who crash-landed in Orbis.\r\nHe started a small business with Staff Sergeant Charlie, hoping to raise enough money for the return trip home. Once Corporal Wilson started selling pet food, he seemed to really take to the job, to the point he might not be all that concerned with going back anymore.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

16.desc: A glove maker from Orbis. He's a nymph with bird-like wings on his back, and he sources the leather he uses to make his gloves from zipping around in the sky hunting.  \r\nUnfortunately, business seems to have been slow lately, so he mainly keeps food on the table by doing repair work. He's distantly related to Elma the Housekeeper.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

17.desc: An Omega Sector soldier who crash-landed in Orbis.\r\nTogether with Corporal Wilson, he started a business in the hopes of raising enough money to return home. He trades loot he found in the El Nath Mountains for other goods. Unlike Corporal Wilson, who totally embraced the merchant life, he doesn't seem all that well-suited to running a business.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

18.desc: An artist who has made his name in the field of plastic surgery, renowned by his seniors, juniors, and especially his customers (judging by all the five-star reviews). \r\nHe'll basically show up anytime, anywhere to help people change their appearances as long as someone has a coupon. Looks like the famous Plastic Roy was in Orbis all along!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

19.desc: An assistant doctor who works at Orbis Plastic Surgery. She's being trained by the famous Plastic Roy, putting her all into learning the fine art of physician-assisted beauty.  \r\nShe's got the fundamentals down pat, but doesn't seem to have the same innate aesthetic sensibilities Roy does, so she hasn't yet risen to the same level of renown as her mentor. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

20.desc: The director of the Orbis Plastic Surgery clinic. \r\nAlthough he runs the whole operation, he rarely performs surgeries himself--not since he hired the renowned Plastic Roy. Say what you want; the guy knows how to delegate.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

21.desc: The Lead Hairstylist of the Orbis Hair Salon. He's the one who gets to do all the hairstyles for the fairies in Orbis, who definitely know a thing or two about beauty. \r\nThey must really like his work, 'cause all the fairies in Orbis still seek out Mino instead of going to Big Headward.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

22.desc: An assistant at the Orbis Hair Salon. \r\nShe used to admire the owner, Mino, but lately she's been considering moving to a different hair salon. It might have something to do with the fact that the only clients the Orbis Hair Salon gets are fairies, but it sounds like she wants to try honing her craft under Big Headward instead.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

23.desc: A dermatologist at the Orbis Skin-Care clinic. \r\nShe's always trying to sell the fairies of Orbis on the merits of a good tan, but no one really shows any interest, which I think has kinda bummed her out. Have you ever seen a tan fairy, though...?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

24.desc: An archaeologist most often seen at the Orbis Guild Base, in the Hall of Heroes. He's so absorbed in archaeology that he even dresses like a historical figure. \r\nHe has discovered a passage leading to the underground waterways of the long fallen Sharenian Kingdom and is always trying to get adventurers to investigate it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

25.desc: A staff member at the Orbis Guild Base, in the Hall of Heroes. \r\nShe's in charge of guild unions, which are large coalitions made up of multiple guilds. The leaders of the guilds all have to agree to the union for it to be recognized.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

26.desc: A staff member at the Orbis Guild Base, in the Hall of Heroes. She's in charge of making sure the Banner of Plenty is ready every Thursday. \r\nIf you're part of a guild, make sure you visit Deia and get those freebies.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

27.desc: A guild leader who mostly hangs out at the Orbis Guild Base, in the Hall of Heroes. \r\nGuilds are groups made up of like-minded people who share the same ideals or goals, and by registering their group with Heracle, it'll become an officially-recognized guild.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

28.desc: Once a member of the prestigious knights, he is now the loyal caretaker of the Guild Castle. His neatly-groomed white hair and mustache, along with his impeccable posture, reflect the dignity and decorum of his glory days as a knight. \r\nHe knows the history and secrets of the castle better than anyone, and is dedicated to rebuilding the estate.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

29.desc: The kindhearted employee running the Guild Shop. She always greets guild members with a bright smile, all while meticulously managing the shop and providing all the items a guild could possibly need. \r\nShe and Oliver are fraternal twins, but Susan claims she's older.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

30.desc: A craftsman in charge of fashioning decorations for the Guild Castle. The pieces of art born from his mighty hands have surely made the Guild Castle a truly unique and even special space. \r\nHe and Susan are fraternal twins, but Oliver claims he's older.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

25.regionDesc: A massive tower that stretches into the sky, connecting the floating city of Orbis to the land below. \r\nIt's said to have been built by adventurers in ancient times to open a path to the skies.

0.desc: One of the monsters commonly seen in the Orbis Tower. They look like round stones and float in midair. \r\nThey doesn't appear to be natural; signs point to them having been artificially created, but even the fairies of Orbis have no idea who might have first made such a creature. The prevailing belief is that they were made to serve as sentries for the tower.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: One of the monsters commonly seen in the Orbis Tower. They resemble a Jr. Sentinel, but are much larger, about the size of a human head. \r\nThey're made of solid stone, and when they attack, their bodies momentarily split apart to fire lasers from some hidden mechanism. It's clear that they're some sort of artificial construct, but who made them and for what purpose remains a mystery.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: One of the monsters commonly seen in the Orbis Tower. Though similar in size and appearance to regular Sentinels, they've been imbued with the power of fire. \r\nAccording to Huckle, who's been studying Sentinels for a long time, it doesn't have a "core" or any sort of concentrated energy source. Instead, a faint fire-aspected energy permeates its entire stone body.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: One of the monsters commonly seen in the Orbis Tower. Though similar in size and appearance to regular Sentinels, they've been imbued with the power of ice. \r\nAccording to Huckle, who's been studying Sentinels for a long time, it doesn't have a "core" or any sort of concentrated energy source. Instead, a faint ice-aspected energy permeates its entire stone body.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: One of the monsters commonly seen on the lower floors of the Orbis Tower. \r\nAs a spirit born from the snow of El Nath, where the Orbis Tower stands, it looks at first glance like a clump of white fur. It's light enough to float easily on the currents of El Nath's cold winds, drifting along almost weightlessly with the chilly gusts.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: One of the monsters commonly seen on the lower floors of the Orbis Tower. \r\nThough born from the snow of El Nath, where the Orbis Tower stands, it's been stained black because of all the dust that's accumulated in the tower over the years. In areas where Dark Leattys gather, adventurers find themselves far more prone to sneezing. However, loud noises tend to attract even more of them, so...maybe wear a mask or something.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc: One of the residents of Orbis. He came to Orbis Tower and just sort of...made himself at home. Now he's been there for 30 years, collecting and researching magical materials. His research mainly focuses on the Sentinels, though it seems he's yet to fully uncover their secrets. \r\nHe doesn't look particularly well-off at first glance, but he actually owns a house in Orbis Village and even has a pet waiting for him there.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: A statue erected on the 8th floor of the Orbis Tower. It has been sculpted in the form of a beautiful woman with long, flowing hair and birdlike wings on her back. \r\nMost scholars presume the statue's design was based on the nymphs, but no one knows who built it or why. Maybe they just wanted to look at an attractive piece of rock.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A scientist and inventor you can meet in the basement of the Orbis Tower. With his eccentric personality, he seems to prefer living in seclusion to actually interacting with other people. \r\nHe's more confident than anyone when it comes to creating things by combining magic and science (he said so himself!). He appears to be rather fond of seals.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

26.regionDesc: A vast park shaped from massive clouds, located high above the floating city of Orbis. \r\nIn this mysterious place created by the fairies of Orbis, visitors are able to walk upon the clouds and feel the energy of the skies.

0.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. Cute spirits that float through the air wearing red hats, people believe they were born from the clouds of Orbis that have been touched by starlight. \r\nThough it looks insubstantial--understandable, what with it being a cloud and all--it's actually much heavier than you'd expect.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. Cute spirits that float through the air wearing purple hats, people believe they were born from the clouds of Orbis that have been touched by moonlight.\r\nWhen attacked, they whip out a magic wand from...somewhere and counterattack using lunar energy.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. Cute spirits that float through the air wearing black hats, people believe they were born from the clouds of Orbis that have been touched by sunlight. \r\nCloud Park, where the Luster Pixies tend to dwell, is the sunniest place in Orbis.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. These carnivorous plants, large enough to even prey on animals, are thankfully rooted to the ground. They do attack anything that enters their reach, though, so caution is advised. \r\nTheir immobile nature is capitalized upon by canny adventurers, who make use of ranged attacks to turn the fearsome foliage into salad. The seeds are popular as an ingredient for juices.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. They look almost identical to Nependeaths, but are easy to distinguish by the inky black shade of their flowers. \r\nWhile ordinary Nependeaths are poisonous, Dark Nependeaths possess even stronger toxins, requiring special processing before their seeds can be consumed.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. They resemble lion cubs, the notable difference being the small horn that grows from their forehead. \r\nHaving not yet grown to maturity, they have yet to learn how to make use of their horn. Instead, they resort to more physical attacks, charging and ramming foes with their bodies. Their white fur with golden tips looks incredibly soft, but those who touch it will find themselves on the receiving end of an electric shock that leaves one's fingertips tingling.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. They resemble lion cubs, the notable difference being the small horn that grows from their forehead. \r\nHaving not yet grown to maturity, they have yet to learn how to make use of their horn. Instead, they resort to more physical attacks, charging and ramming foes with their bodies. Their white fur with purple tips looks incredibly soft, but those who touch it will find themselves on the receiving end of a bracing chill that leaves one's hand icy cold.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. They resemble lion cubs, the notable difference being the small horn that grows from their forehead. \r\nHaving not yet grown to maturity, they have yet to learn how to make use of their horn. Instead, they resort to more physical attacks, charging and ramming foes with their bodies. Their white fur with reddish tips looks incredibly soft, but those who touch it will quickly pull their hand away, as though they had touched a hot kettle.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. The fully grown form of the Jr. Lioner, they can gather the power of lightning in the horn on their forehead to attack. \r\nMaturation has only increased the power of the electric current flowing through their fur, which now packs enough of a shock to leave one's entire arm numb. If you're planning to pass through Cloud Park, caution is advised.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. The fully grown form of the Jr. Grupin, the tips of their furry coat that were purple as juveniles turn a bluer hue as they mature.  \r\nThey can gather the power of ice in the horn on their forehead to attack, so caution is advised if you're planning on passing through Cloud Park.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. The fully grown form of the Jr. Cellion, it can gather fiery energy in the horn on its forehead to attack. \r\nCellion fur is said to be fire resistant, and because of that, it's in high demand for use in flame-retardant textiles and other such applications.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. Like Jr. Lioner, Jr. Grupin, and Jr. Cellion, they bear a resemblance to lion cubs. \r\nUnlike those species, however, they have no horn, their ears resemble wings, and the tip of their tail is pointed. They're also known to be particularly aggressive, which sadly makes them impossible to pet.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: One of the monsters that inhabits Cloud Park. The fully grown form of Jr. Lucida, their growth is accompanied by an increase in their ferocity. \r\nStatues of Lucida can be found throughout the Stairway to the Sky, suggesting that the ancient people of Orbis may have admired or even worshiped the creatures...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc: An ancient creature that had long lay in slumber within the Orbis Cloud Park. The legends say it was once the goddess's beloved pet, given charge over Orbis. \r\nHowever, while Eliza was asleep, the Pixies kidnapped the goddess, leaving Eliza consumed by rage. It is known to love music, and will fall asleep if it hears beautiful music being played.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc: One of the fairies living in Orbis. The ringlike ornament on her head once caused her to be mistaken for something else, but she's an ordinary nymph with birdlike wings. \r\nShe loves tasty food, and especially enjoys a cup of fresh-squeezed Nependeath juice.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: One of the residents of Orbis. \r\nA skilled magician and prophetess with an eccentric personality, she doesn't especially enjoy socializing with others. In order to live her ideal life of seclusion, she left the village and built a small house in the middle of Cloud Park. She does appear to have one assistant living there with her, though.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc:
One of the residents of Orbis. 
She serves as Spiruna's assistant, diligently training in magic by her side. She has vowed to remain there, not returning home until her skills have improved. 
(As she has declined to reveal her name, I've been forced to list her as simply '???'.)
                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: One of the Omega Sector soldiers who crash-landed in Orbis by accident. \r\nSeparated from his fellow soldiers by a great distance, he seems to be searching for them. Given his optimistic personality, he doesn't appear overly worried.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

27.regionDesc: A village built atop the eternal frost of the El Nath mountain range, where the land is encrusted in snow and ice year-round. \r\nIt has become a haven for the adventurers and hunters who endure the harsh cold and blizzards, and a resilient vitality seems to hold sway throughout the village.

0.desc: Small penguins that appear in and around El Nath. When one encounters Jr. Pepes, one can safely assume one is fairly close to El Nath. \r\nThey are highly adaptable to different conditions, although appropriate temperature and climate is a must. They seem to have adapted particularly well to the icy terrain of the El Nath Snowfield and move quickly even on slippery ground, making them difficult to avoid.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: Small yeti often spotted in the snowfield near El Nath. Having lived their lives in cold climates, they are highly resistant to Ice-Type Attacks and, correspondingly, more vulnerable to Fire-Type Attacks. \r\nTheir small frames and slow movement make them an easy target, but one should beware, as these cute little creatures are capable of packing quite a punch. They're also capable of transforming into giant yeti, and if they do so, I would recommend a tactical retreat.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: Yeti often spotted in the canyons of El Nath. It's said that the Dark Jr. Yeti are a more 'evil' form of the 'good' Jr. Yeti. \r\nThey are much faster than Jr. Yeti, boasting greater strength both offensively and defensively. Their alignment is completely different as well, making them particularly vulnerable to forces of Sanctity.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
Penguin monsters occasionally found in the snowfield of El Nath. 
Able to move quickly and nimbly even on the icy snowfields, they are easily recognized by the golden crown perched upon their head. They're able to move more quickly than most other monsters in the snowfields, so beware if you see one of them acting aggressively toward you. Their speedy dash attacks make a hostile Pepe difficult to avoid. 
Pepes often form close relationships with Yeti, another monster common in the snowfields. This explains why Yeti are occasionally found with a Pepe riding on their heads, although no one has discovered what gave rise to this strange phenomenon.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: Penguin monsters often spotted in the canyons far from El Nath. These transformed Pepes have been endowed with evil powers. \r\nThese challenging monsters boast powerful attacks and defenses, especially compared to normal Pepes. One characteristic they share with normal Pepes is their speed. Of note is that Dark Pepes are vulnerable to forces of Sanctity.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: Wolf monsters that appear near El Nath. They're a popular target amongst hunters, who seek to harvest the thick pelts that allow Hectors to survive in the icy climate of El Nath. \r\nWhen attacked, Hectors retaliate with a powerful attack infused with magic, so it's recommended that you take a quick step back if you find yourself in a dangerous encounter with this monster.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
An unidentified witch of the Snowy Mountains. 
Among the hunters of El Nath, there is a legend that the Snow Witch is the true ruler of the El Nath mountain range, and that any who wish to hunt there must first receive her permission. 
However, that legend fails to account for the witch's background. Other sources maintain that a magician unwelcome in El Nath was driven out of the village, fleeing deep into the forest where she was consumed by resentment, eventually becoming the Snow Witch. 
Were the misunderstandings to be resolved and the Snow Witch to let go of her longstanding resentment, it's possible she might disappear entirely.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: Wolf monsters that appear near El Nath. They're a popular target amongst hunters, who seek to harvest the thick pelts that allow White Fangs to survive in the icy climate of El Nath. \r\nTheir white fur blends in with the snowy surroundings, making these monsters more difficult for hunters to spot than Hectors. In addition, their aggressiveness, power, and resistance to ice-elemental attacks make them a troublesome creature to tangle with.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: A boy found in the El Nath region. He has been studying the region's geography for a long time, and his diligent nature shows in his acknowledgement that there is still much he doesn't know and his insistence that he must work harder. \r\nRecently, he has been searching for a close friend. Based on what I've heard, Jade's friend seems to be a descendant of the author of an ancient book.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: A renowned hunter from El Nath. Having lived there a long time, he is well versed regarding its monsters and the legends surrounding them. \r\nAlthough at first glance he appears rough and intimidating, there's a reason behind his behavior. In the past, a monster that emerged from an abandoned mine claimed the life of his wife, Lia. Eventually even his son Nick, who vowed revenge, left him.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
The Chief of El Nath. It may surprise one to know that he is incredibly old, having lived for hundreds of years. In that time, he has made connections with many figures and accumulated a remarkable amount of knowledge. 
There are so many tales involving Alcaster that some sound more like myth than reality. He is said to have known the adventurer Sayram from hundreds of years ago, and in Magatia, he's regarded as a renowned alchemist and an authority on inverse attribute experiments. In my role gathering information for the archive, I was unable to verify whether all of these claims are true.
In the present day, the method by which All Cure Potions are made is widely known, but there was a time at which only Alcaster knew how to brew them. Speaking from experience, this chronicler has managed to recover from several dicey situations thanks to All Cure Potions received from Alcaster. Although it has been a number of years since I last made such a request, I still keenly feel a sense of gratitude toward him.
His most cherished memory is of the childhood he spent with his mentor, Aurelia, who fell in battle during a war long ago. Grieved that he never had the chance to say a proper farewell to one who meant so much to him, the traces left behind by his mentor have always been a source of pain and longing for him. 
If you ever happen upon a bottle of #e'Aurelia's Elixir#n, be sure to show it to him. He may share with you stories of the warmth of El Nath's mountains as he vividly remembers them.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
The 3rd job instructor for Warriors. 
Though he now lives quietly in El Nath as a job instructor, it's said that in years past, he was particularly famous--being, on one occasion, caught up in an abduction plot by the Crimson Balrog and Lycanthropes while out on a mission. There were many who threatened his life, lending credibility to the rumors regarding his reputation. 
Witnessing how strong he remains even now, one might wonder if Tylus himself belongs to the realm of legends. 
When you respectfully offer your regards by saying #e'I will carry on your adventure.'#n, he may be inclined to tell you old stories about the job instructors.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
The 3rd job instructor for Bowmen. 
While she's less well known than Athena Pierce or Legor, any Bowman worth their salt is well aware that Rene is no less formidable an archer than those other two. 
She is said to have once been Athena Pierce's disciple, though the reason they parted ways is no longer clear. Still, the fact that they continue to exchange letters suggests their relationship is not a bad one, and that she is clearly respected.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
The 3rd job instructor for Thieves. 
There is a fascinating story about Arec's handling of a certain task that involved illegally smuggling an artifact to sate a client's personal greed, which served to spark a raging debate over whether it's acceptable to engage in morally questionable actions undertaken as part of a contractual request. When questioned about his actions, Arec is said to have replied, 'If I was interested in just doing things by the books, I would've joined the knighthood.' 
As to the truth of this colorful anecdote, this chronicler remains uncertain, with too little evidence to certify its legitimacy. However, Thieves seem to accept it as true, and perhaps for them, that is enough...
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
The 3rd job instructor for Magicians.
Alongside Grendel the Really Old of Ellinia and Alcaster here in El Nath, she is one of the most renowned magicians, widely known for her strict nature. Among those magicians in pursuit of truth who study powerful magic, there are and will likely always be a few who cross lines that should not be crossed, but Robeira holds no forgiveness in her heart for such individuals. Of course, Robeira herself is ever careful to maintain those proper boundaries. 
It is rumored that Robeira once personally sealed away a magician who crossed that line, and that she still keeps a close watch over that magician even now. This chronicler cannot help but wonder who that individual might be...
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: The 3rd job instructor for Pirates. \r\nPedro joined later than the other chiefs, so there's little we know about him, and not a great deal that can be conclusively verified. There is little doubt his skills are on par with Kyrin's, but the lack of tales about regarding his past is conspicuous. One cannot help but wonder if such stories were intentionally suppressed, or even erased.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc:
A Hoblin named Shammos imprisoned in the basement of the Chief's Residence. 
One may be surprised to learn that he was originally a magician--a very promising one, at that. However, he fell into the study of dark magic and strayed down the wrong path, ultimately sacrificing many lives. As punishment for his sins, his body was transformed into that of a Hoblin, leaving him in his current form. 
Even so, his efforts to create great magic met with success--it is believed that Genesis, Blizzard, and Meteor Shower were born from his work.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: A storage keeper in the El Nath Market. Wrapped in cloth from head to toe, one must admit he seems like a rather suspicious character. He does not seem to be a native of El Nath. \r\nThalj claims that the warehouse is safe and that any and all items can be entrusted to his care, but his reassurances impart little trust. In truth, he seems like someone better avoided; this chronicler has never felt safe entrusting any sort of item to Mr. Thalj. Personal biases aside, there have been no reports of Mr. Thalj actually causing any problems.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc: A master cobbler in the El Nath Market who hand-crafted shoes in El Nath for over 50 years, although it seems he has retired from the trade. In the past, few shipments of goods made it to the region due to the heavy snowfall, but in more recent years, there have been more than enough supplies to go around. \r\nHe seems to have been a mentor to Moren, an item maker from Magatia. Though he was once thought to have secret shoe-making techniques he hid from even his apprentice, he recently revealed that it was all thanks to the Magic Iron.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc: A refining expert in the El Nath Market. In years gone by, he was constantly busy refining ores and gemstones brought to him, but now that many people have become skilled in specialized professions, he no longer offers his services.\r\nAmong craftsmen, he was particularly known for his skill in handling Dark Crystals, perhaps thanks to the famous Holy Stone of El Nath.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc: A weapon seller at the El Nath Weapon and Armor Shop. He claims to deal only in equipment of the highest quality, and does in fact sell equipment superior to what can be found on Victoria Island. \r\nThat said, there's nothing exceptionally special about any of the gear on offer, so it's best to avoid making any impulse purchases.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc: An armor seller at the El Nath Weapon and Armor Shop. She warns that venturing outside without proper armor can lead to serious trouble, which seems entirely accurate given El Nath's harsh weather. \r\nRumi sells a special piece of equipment not found in other towns: Snowshoes. If you're worried about slipping on El Nath's icy paths, this chronicler recommends purchasing and equipping a pair.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

14.desc: A general goods merchant at the El Nath General Store. She calls herself the greatest alchemist in El Nath, but everyone knows that the greatest alchemist is Alcaster. While it can be argued that Alcaster stepped away from practicing the alchemical arts long ago, surpassing him is still no easy feat. \r\nThe items she sells aren't much different from those found in other towns, but if you're struggling to adjust to El Nath's cold climate, she's quick to recommended buying a bowl of Red Bean Porridge.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc: The commander of the Alpha Platoon's Network of Communication, said to have crash-landed in El Nath after an airship malfunction while on an important mission. \r\nCuriously, he seems unaffected by the cold. As it turns out, this isn't due to his sheer grit, but the effect of an enchanted cloak given to him by a kind old man.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

16.desc: One of the members of the Alpha Platoon, said to have crash-landed in El Nath after an airship malfunction while on an important mission. Despite the crash, El Nath appears to have been the destination to which the platoon was traveling. \r\nOne wonders whether he and his fellows managed to complete their mission.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

17.desc: A dungeon guide stationed at Ice Valley to warns travelers looking to enter the Deepwoods. He always advises caution before proceeding any further, explaining that unlike the enemies they may have faced so far, the area beyond is crawling with fast and ferocious creatures. \r\nBetween guarding the entrance, the scars over his eyes, and his distinctive cloak, one cannot help but wonder if he might truly be a warrior of exceptional skill and experience.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

18.desc: A merchant located in Ice Valley who serves as the last supply point for travelers before entering the Deepwoods.\r\nThough he claims his place is rather modest compared to what's on offer in the village, this chronicler is of the opinion that the food here is just as nutritious as what can be found in town, and tastes better. Perhaps it's the effect of relishing a warm meal when one is half-frozen...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

28.regionDesc: Deep in the El Nath Mountains, this lonely castle sits atop a rocky peak. It was once home to a hearty people who thrived even amidst the bone-chilling cold, but its once-grand halls now lie in ruin. \r\nOnly the Lion King, a man who has lost everything, remains in the gloom-filled audience chamber.

0.desc: The first type of monster one is likely to encounter in the Lion King's Castle, possessing a crocodilian appearance. \r\nThey are characterized by their massive swords and iron helmets, and the shockwave created by the downward chop of their great blade is, needless to say, extremely dangerous.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: Monsters found in the Lion King's Castle whose appearance resembles that of a reindeer. They are further distinguished by the sharp spear they carry.\r\nThe strength generated by their well-developed trapezius muscles amplifies the power and recoil of their spear thrusts. If you ever face a Reindeer in battle, it is recommended to keep a healthy distance between yourself and the creature.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: Monsters found in the Lion King's Castle whose appearance resembles that of a reindeer. While similar to ordinary Reindeer, their crimson fur has led them to be dubbed Blood Reindeer. It is said those who come within close proximity of the creatures will even catch the scent of blood. \r\nIf you ever find yourself fighting a Blood Reindeer, keeping out of range of its attacks is highly advised.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
Monsters found in the Lion King's Castle that resemble eagles. The piercing and sweeping attacks they make with the halberds they carry make them a foe not to be underestimated. 
With powerful wings that render them capable of swift flight, one ought to be wary of surprise attacks while in their territory.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: Monsters with a unique form found in the Lion King's Castle. These bears clad in their iron helmets, wielding iron clubs, and sitting astride their wolf mounts make for a truly bizarre sight. The working hypothesis is that the wolf covers the front while the bear handles the rear, allowing the pair to stay alert at all times without any blind spots. \r\nDespite the strange partnership, the bear's strength far surpasses a human's, and the wolf's fangs make it a dangerous foe, so we would recommend not getting too close if your combat style allows for a ranged offensive.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: Golems formed from sections of castle walls and iron, found in Lion King's Castle. Resembling small fortresses, these hulking constructs have rightfully earned the name 'Castle Golems'.
