Their massive weight causes the castle itself to shudder, as if each attack holds the potential to cause it all to collapse. \r\nAs their appearance might suggest, they boast extremely high defense. If you are not confident in the power of your weapon, aim for areas that look comparatively weaker and avoid the brick sections.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: Prison guards found in the jail area of the Lion King's Castle. Possessing a turtle-like form, the extreme hardness of their shells leaves little choice but to confront them head-on. \r\nThey exhibit impressive combat skills, including the ability to swing massive weapons and leaping high to throw opponents off balance. Of a size considerably larger than other monsters, one must take care not to be captured while fighting.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: Monsters with a roselike form found in the Abandoned Garden. These monsters are believed to have come into being when the dark energy emanating from the Lion King's Castle was absorbed by the garden's roses. \r\nParts of its body are frozen, and it is able to launch ice at foes, so remain on your guard.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc: Monsters found in Soul's Rest. They resemble rhinoceroses in appearance and oversee young ghosts, keeping watch to ensure they do not escape. \r\nAlthough at first glance one would assume they attack with their clubs, they instead use bizarre throwing attacks, showing once again that first impressions aren't everything.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: Small golems found along the edges of the castle walls. Much smaller than Castle Golems, they are wrapped in rose vines. \r\nThough to many they seem initially less threatening due to their smaller size, their reduced mass grants them increased speed. These golems employ this speed in straight charges intended to ram their targets, making them dangerous and difficult to avoid.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc:
The master who rules the Lion King's Castle. At first glance, he appears to be a strong man with red hair, but once the battle begins, he is said to transform into a massive lion with a crimson mane. 
This power stems from the fact that he is a commander in the Black Mage's army. Despite this, he does not appear to be active; instead, he remains alone in his castle, which has long since fallen into ruin.
Legend has it that he was once the king who ruled the harsh realm of El Nath. For what reason did he sell his soul to the Black Mage and become a commander? We are still gathering whatever information we can find related to this matter.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc: Golden-hued bees occasionally spotted in the Rose Garden. Since they often appear in swarms, it is likely they've built a hive somewhere in the garden. \r\nSome naturalists have speculated they may have grown stronger by feeding on honey distilled from the garden's roses.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc: Massive golems uncommonly spotted in the Rose Garden. Far larger than Castle Golems, their prodigious size renders their ground-smashing attacks even more dangerous. \r\nThey employ unorthodox attack strategies, such as ambushing enemies by bursting out of the ground or throwing structures, so knowing what they're capable of is recommended before facing one.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: Ghosts found in the Lion King's Castle. They appear to have once been treasure hunters. \r\nCursed by the Lion King and turned into specters, they continue to linger here in the world of the living, suggesting that there may still be bound by their insatiable search for treasure.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc:
A lovely young ghost named Cecilia found in the Gardener's area.
She is said to have once been charged with tending the Rose Garden. Judging by how beautiful the roses remain even now, it would seem Cecilia spared no effort in her devotion to their care.
Historical sources tell us she was close to Ifia, the queen of the Lion King, Von Leon.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

29.regionDesc: This abandoned mineshaft burrows deep into the El Nath Mountains. \r\nIt was once the lifeblood of the local town's economy. Now all that's left is a shell of its former glory, a ghost town haunted by the echoes of its former inhabitants tortured by Zakum's undead thrall.

0.desc: Gigantic creatures that appear in the snowfield of El Nath. Although seemingly sluggish, they are capable of striking the ground with both of their fists, dealing considerable damage to any unfortunate enough to find themselves between the ground and said fists. Their thick coats allow them to thrive in the cold, but they're unable to stand much heat. \r\nThese fundamentally mild-mannered monsters roam around with a Pepe on their backs, as the two species readily form friendships. They're in popular demand as pets, as they've been found to be loyal and obedient when raise by humans from a young age.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: Gigantic creatures that appear in the snowfield of El Nath. \r\nThese mutant Yeti, corrupted by an evil force, are stronger and more dangerous than the usually mild-natured Yeti in every aspect. Like the normal Yeti, they can also deal major damage with their fists, making them all the more dangerous. With the shift in their natural attributes, they have become vulnerable to holy energy.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
This fairly odd couple roams the snowfield of El Nath with total disregard for their unconventional appearance. This leaves even the most serious adventurers bemused by the pairing. 
Many researchers have studied the pair for years, but as yet, they have not uncovered the origins of this phenomenon. The pair remain an amusing anomaly in an otherwise solemn environment.
Their existence has had quite the impact on the locals, even inspiring the phrase 'as close as Yeti and Pepe.'
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
Legend has it that this creature is an unusual combination of human and Snow Spirit. 
It may look like a monster, but it possesses the soul of a human. So the pain of being ostracized by its fellow humans is that much more acute. Seeing its pain, the Snow Spirit took pity on Nyalmo and froze the entire El Nath mountain range just for them. 
The gentle giant Nyalmo avoids humans these days, choosing to flee rather than fight. However, he will ruthlessly defend the Snow Spirit against anyone who threatens it.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: This unusual pairing roams the snowfield of El Nath. \r\nHowever, unlike their paler cousins, this Yeti and Pepe have been consumed by evil and suffer a dark cast to their appearance as a consequence. Beware, for their malevolent leanings grant them stronger attack, defense, and speed than their regular Yeti and Pepe counterparts.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: This monster takes the form of a wolf in the deepest end of the snowfield's valley. It prowls along on two feet like a human and unsheathes wicked claws to attack any traveler unfortunate enough to cross its path. \r\nBut most disturbing is the rumor that anyone it bites is, themselves, transformed into a vicious Werewolf.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
This monster takes the form of a wolf in the deepest end of the snowfield's valley. It prowls along on two feet like a human and unsheathes wicked claws to attack any traveler unfortunate enough to cross its path.
When it senses a battle is no longer in its favor, this so-called king of Werewolves summons its fellows. Its physical and magical defenses are exceptionally high, and it is resistant to cold, making it a formidable opponent. However, it is weak against fire-based attacks, so be sure to use those when hunting Lycanthropes.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt
Note: 
-Since they're members of the canine family, you might think these creatures would be fun to pet. They're really not! Whatever you do, DON'T pet them!
-For some reason, other Werewolves rarely respond to this creature's call for backup anymore. Maybe they're on strike? Or maybe there aren't as many as there used to be because their habitat shrank... Who's to say?
                                       - Chronicler Harper

7.desc:
These undead monsters haunt the Forest of Dead Trees in El Nath. 
When the Lich's tomb formed the Forest of Dead Trees, it bewitched these lifeless beings, creating zombies. Now forced to spend their afterlife defending the forest, these miserable creatures express nothing but hostility toward humans. r

Beware! These monsters may limp along slower than snails, but the potent poison they spray can be deadly.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc:
There once lived a revered priest who possessed incredible power. But as he aged, his fear of death overcame his reason. So he betrayed his faith and sought the power of the demons, drawing the ire of the god he had once worshipped. 
Upon this fallen priest's death, his loyal followers buried him in the Forest of Dead Trees...but his afterlife was far from peaceful. Soon, the forest was overrun with zombies spurred into undeath by the evil in the priest's soul. In the time since, many heroic adventurers have braved the forest and thinned the zombies' numbers. But it only served to anger the fallen priest, who rose from the grave as a horrifying Lich to defend his zombies.
Today, this undead monster rules the Forest of Dead Trees with powerful magic and elimination skills. As a former priest, he is highly resistant to attacks based in the sanctity attribute.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: These undead beasts roam the Forest of Dead Trees in El Nath. When dark magic radiating from the Lich's tomb gave rise to the Forest of Dead Trees, it forced many lifeless beings into undeath, doomed to roam the forest as zombies. \r\nIt remains unclear whether the Miner Zombies' severe limp and nearly blind eyes are due to a pre-death accident or an undead mutation.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc: Bat monsters that dwell in the abandoned mine in El Nath. Over countless generations, they degenerated into one-eyed creatures with huge wings due to spending their entire lives caverns almost entirely devoid of light. They fly throughout the mine's tunnels, ready and able to attack visitors at any time.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc: Bain pups born from lava. When fully mature, they transform into terrifying monsters, but at this stage, they're cute enough that one feels some measure of guilt about taking up arms against them. As juveniles, they lack immunity and are vulnerable to poison attacks.\r\nIt is theorized that somewhere hidden within the lava fields, there is a colony where Jr. Cerebes live together. \r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc: Monsters born in an ocean of lava deep within a cave system. With their reddish eyes, monstrous teeth, and spiky collars, Cerebes present an imposing threat, although they are limited to close-range attacks. \r\nWhen a Cerebes grows older, it will become a Bain, which is capable of using powerful fire-attribute attacks.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc: This beast takes the form of a fireball and dwells in the Lava Dungeon of El Nath. As its appearance suggests, it is resistant to fire attacks but weak against ice. \r\nWhile the circumstances behind its existence remain a mystery, one thing is certain. When threatened, it self-destructs, leading some researchers to believe that it may be descended from Zakum. \r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

14.desc: This fearsome creature was born in a subterranean lake of lava and began life as a Cerebes. However, extended contact with the lava imbued it with a mysterious energy, slowly morphing it into its current form. \r\nFire is its greatest strength. This king of lava decimates its victims with blazing flame.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc:
For countless years, the spirit of the Zakum Tree lay dormant and formless. But as it absorbed the energies of the lava region's inhabitants, it slowly began to take shape. 
The nearby settlement was brimming with dark energy born of the residents' selfish desires. Amid the darkness, flames, and scorching heat, that dark energy fueled Zakum's growth and twisted its spirit. 
Zakum may have started as nothing more than a wretched tree, but the energy it absorbed over centuries gave it power that surpassed that of the humans. Eventually, it used that power to manipulate the inhabitants of the lava region into crafting stone statues it could inhabit, and Zakum rules over them to this very day.
                                       - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: This hunter is out in the snowfield. Whatever he is investigating in the Forest of Dead Trees, it's likely related to the zombies there. \r\nJudging by the Werewolf lying defeated beside him, he no doubt has the considerable skill required to survive alone in such an unforgiving place.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: This gatekeeper to Zakum's lair stands firm, muttering constantly about how his once-peaceful village was overrun by monsters. He is very likely a former resident of the now-abandoned mining town. \r\nThe man seems solely focused on preventing any more victims from passing through the gates. As such, he instists that all those who enter must prove that they are highly qualified to survive on their own before he will allow them to pass.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: This man can be found at the Breath of Lava. Once you have gathered the materials to summon Zakum in the Unknown Dead Mine, then here, at the Breath of Lava, you must prove that you are worthy to fight Zakum. If you wish to give up at any time, speak with Amon.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: This woman can be found in the Unknown Dead Mine. She was once the most reliable crafter of Eye of Fire if you brought her Fire Ore and paper. But now that there is an ample supply of Eyes of Fire, there's no real need for Aura's services.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: This woman is located at the Breath of Lava. Once you have prepared the necessary materials to summon Zakum in the Unknown Dead Mine, you must prove your worthiness to fight. Only those who reach the bitter end may meet Lyra. \r\nIt has yet to be confirmed, however it appears she is Aura's sister.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: You will find this man in the Room of Tragedy. It has yet to be confirmed, however it appears he is Amon's brother.\r\nIf you wish to abandon the trial, you must speak with him.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

30.regionDesc: This city under the sea is home to countless marine creatures who peacefully co-exist. Its extraordinary sights and mysterious atmosphere make this city a must-visit destination for adventurers and marine researchers alike.\r\nAquarium is also an essential stop for any adventurers headed to the deeper underwater world.

0.desc: These baby seal monsters are popular amongst adventurers in Aqua Road. Their sparkling eyes and tiny little flippers are just about as adorable as it gets!\r\nThe only trouble is, they don't stay cute baby seals forever. Eventually, they turn into Freezers and Sparkers when they mature. How sad...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: You can find this Pepe around Aqua Road. While Pepes are usually limited to the El Nath territory, this type in particular seems to have found its way into a tunnel beneath Orbis Tower and popped out at the entrance to Aqua Road.\r\nCompared to ordinary Pepes, it's smaller, but it's also more clever and agile.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc:
This fish inhabits the Crystal Gorge in the western waters of Aqua Road. 
It can only survive in fresh water, which means the Poopa is a great way to gauge the quality of a body of water. If you see a Poopa, it's a sure sign of excellent quality. 
When it feels threatened or when it is attacked, it abruptly inflates its body to scare off enemies.
                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: This fish inhabits the Red Coral Forest in the western waters of Aqua Road. \r\nIt looks like a Poopa apart from one interesting feature. The surrounding coral seems to have turned it purple! But that's not the only thing the coral imparted to this fearsome predator. Be wary of its spines, since they are full of a dangerous toxin.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc:
This is what a Jr. Seal looks like when it's all grown up! Females are Freezers, and males are Sparkers.
When a Freezer reaches adulthood, an ice-shaped emblem appears on her chest to signify that she has embraced the cold power of El Nath. This penchant for cold means that they prefer the chilly waters of the deep sea.
Oh! And they carry their young atop their head. Isn't that adorable?
                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: This is what a Jr. Seal looks like when it's all grown up! Females are Freezers, and males are Sparkers.\r\nUnlike Freezers, no one seems to know how Sparkers came into existence. What is certain, however, is that their hide is so thick with blubber that they have impressive resistance to cold, even to that of a Freezer's cold!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: This fish that inhabits the eastern waters of Aqua Road and has a very unique feature: the black markings around its eyes make it look like a little aquatic bandit! \r\nIt's very large and has especially hard scales covering its belly, which make it quite a formidable opponenet. However, it has a gentle temperament, so as long as you're polite, you probably have nothing to worry about.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: This shrimp hops around the eastern waters of Aqua Road with its arms crossed as if it's angry at the world. \r\nWhile it gets along well with other marine creatures, it's... not so fond of warm-blooded land dwellers. I suppose that's reasonable, considering how many land creatures have tried to eat them over the years...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: This giant clam is very shy and does its best to stay out of sight. However, they love a flashy outfit and can't resist adorning their shells with pretty starfish. \r\nDisturbing a resting Seruf has both an up and down side. On the one hand, it will pelt you with pearls. On the other hand, those pearls are worth a pretty penny. Just ask Tae Gong. He used them to make a stunning necklace for Grandma Yeon!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: This unique fish brightens the eastern waters of Aqua Road by way of a single, colorful flower on its head.\r\nIt's actually a fin, but that didn't stop people from calling it the 'Flower Fish'. Anyway, it makes for ingenious camouflage against predators, since the creature can skim the ocean floor and blend in with the aquatic flora.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: This fish inhabits the eastern waters of Aqua Road.\r\nIt's a fascinating little creature whose body is so completely transparent that it looks like an air bubble. Legends say this magnificent creature might even have been borne of the sea foam! Origins aside, its excellent camouflage makes it a tough catch for predators.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: This fish inhabits the eastern waters of Aqua Road. \r\nIts vivid crimson and white stripes are striking, but its most unique feature is the horn growing from its head! Scientists of the past theorized that it was related to whales, but sadly, that theory was later disproven.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: This sea creature inhabits the eastern waters of Aqua Road. \r\nIts tail curls backward, and a fascinating, crown-like horn grows from its head. This underwater royalty expects nothing less than perfection, and as such, only lives in clean, unpolluted seas.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc:
This sea creature inhabits the eastern waters of Aqua Road.
Its tail curls forward, and a helmet-like fin grows from its head. A head butt from this creature will make you see stars!
It's a close relative of Cico, sharing nearly identical hunting habits and behavior patterns.
                                      - Chronicler Q

14.desc: This sea creature inhabits the eastern waters of Aqua Road. \r\nIts entire body is densely covered in black spines it can tuck away. Most of the time, it lies still on the ocean floor, looking like nothing more than a black stone at first glance.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

15.desc: This ghost fish can be found in Aqua Road's deep sea. \r\nConsidering it's nothing but a skeleton, it's difficult to tell what kind of fish it once was. What we do know is that it's a source of terror for deep-sea travelers! Its sharp dorsal fin bones and teeth make it a force to be reckoned with. The witch Carta speculates that the darkness of the deep sea gave rise to such ghosts.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

16.desc: When exploring Aqua Road's deep sea, take care to disturb as little as possible, including piles of sediment. There's no telling what kind of creature might be lurking in the dark.\r\nCarefully inspect the holes in the sediment, and you might just see the glowing eyes of a Goby shining in the darkness, staring right back at you.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

17.desc: This fish inhabits Aqua Road's deep sea. These creatures are timid by nature and usually hide inside a Goby den made from packed sediment.\r\nBeware! They may be docile, but if you make the mistake of disturbing their home, they attack as a swarm. Compared to their Bone Fish cousins, they are harder to catch and even more dangerous. Use caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

18.desc: This sea creature inhabits Aqua Road's deep sea and looks like a fascinating cross between an Ammonite and an Octopus.\r\nIt attacks by spraying poisonous ink at its enemies that's difficult to outswim, making it an extremely dangerous opponent. Be careful not to ingest the ink-tainted seawater.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

19.desc: This sea creature inhabits Aqua Road's deep sea and looks almost identical to a Squid, but it does not spray ink. Rather, it raises its two tentacles, builds up an electrical charge, and unleashes an attack that's positively shocking. \r\nA Risell Squid's attack will paralyze its victims, making it difficult to swim. Avoid provoking it at all costs.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

20.desc:
This fish inhabits the Aqua Road's deep sea and has a distinctly dazed look about it. 
Beware! Its lackadaisical appearance belies an extremely volatile temperament. It attacks deep-sea travelers with its sharp teeth at the slightest provocation. 
Travelers collect Shark Teeth to show off their strength and skill, but they're rarely worth the deep lacerations.
                                      - Chronicler Q

21.desc:
This fish inhabits Aqua Road's deep sea.
It's related to the Shark, but it is vastly more intelligent and wields the cold energy of the deep sea when threatened. If possible, it is even more dangerous and fearsome than a Shark. 
Likely due to how difficult it is to defeat, Cold Shark dorsal fin is a popular delicacy and only the bravest adventurers harvest it.
                                      - Chronicler Q

22.desc: This powerful monster dwells in the deepest cave of Aqua Road's deep sea. It snugs itself into a cozy hole in the cave where you can only see its head. Because of that, there's no telling how big they are, but any size is too big if you ask me! \r\nAs the king of the deep sea, it unleashes devastating attacks by firing beams straight from its mouth. So it's best to just avoid caves altogether.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc: This storage keeper has set up shop in the Aquarium General Store.\r\nHe wears a whimsically wonderful marine creature costume to welcome visitors. Of course, all those legs must make it quite difficult to move around... Maybe that's why Gerrard spends most of his working hours sitting down.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: This is the general goods merchant for the Aquarium General Store.\r\nLike his General Store counterparts, Oannes wears a marine creature costume to make visitors feel more welcome. He makes for a wonderfully jovial starfish! Though, I've heard his facepaint is so difficult to remove that he had to craft a special potion to wash up at the end of the day.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: This weapons merchant conducts his business in the Aquarium General Store.\r\nLike many in the Aquarium, Calypso wears a marine creature costume to welcome visitors. In this chronicler's opinion, his Longnose Sawshark outfit suits his sharp features perfectly. And it seems he is well aware, since he accepts compliments with an air of quiet confidence.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: This armor merchant has a thriving business in the Aquarium General Store.\r\nMelias, too, dons a marine creature costume to welcome visitors. His turtle hat was especially whimsical, and I couldn't resist touching it. It was softer than I expected and seemed quite comfortable, if a bit warm. Lucky for him, the Aquarium is on the cooler side.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: This friendly Aquarium zookeeper studies both land- and sea-dwelling creatures, making her extremely knowledgeable. If anyone can answer your creature questions, it's Kenta! So, fire away... metaphorically, of course.\r\nThe only trouble is, her fees are quite expensive, probably to help cover the Aquarium Zoo's steep overhead.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc:
This Aquarium zookeeper wears a marine creature costume to help visitors feel welcome.
Muse is among the most capable and trusted zookeepers and is responsible for the Balrog's care. I've never seen her fight, but she must be really strong to handle that job...
She spends each day pining after her boyfriend, Gail, who disappeared while on a mission into the deep sea for research.
                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: This dolphin operates the Dolphin Taxi in the Aquarium and takes you to such exotic destinations as the Sharp Unknown or Herb Town. \r\nRiding the Dolphin Taxi is an exhilarating experience and would likely make for a popular tourist attraction.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: You can find this girl on Snowy Whale's Island.\r\nShe lives a solitary but fulfilling life raising three huskies in an igloo on a whale's back. Life is anything but boring when you live with three huskies! She truly does seem happy.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: You can find this man of mysterious origins at Two Palm Trees.\r\nHe has no idea how or why he ended up at Aqua Road, and he seems entirely unconcerned about it. As for leaving? He claims he can swim but fears what lurks beneath the surface of the water. So he stays put, hoping to be rescued.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: This fisherman leisurely casts his line from a small boat floating on Aqua Road. However the quarry he seeks is far grander than simple fish... He seeks time itself. \r\nI highly suspect that this is Tae Gong, Grandma Yeon's husband from Korean Folk Town. Hopefully, he can at least bring home a decent catch.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: This witch lurks in the deepest, darkest caverns of Aqua Road's deep sea.\r\nIf the rumors are to be believed, then she can see the future. Carta herself denies this, claiming that no one can truly see the future. But she's unnaturally talented at predicting things before they happen, so... who really knows? Not this chronicler!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: You'll find this seafarer at the Aqua Road Deep Sea shipwreck. \r\nHe once captained a special expedition to investigate strange activity in the deep sea. However his role quickly shifted to that of search and rescue when his entire crew disappeared. Sadly, he's spent many years searching high and low for them to no avail.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

31.regionDesc: This secret research facility is hidden deep below the sea, where the Resistance's most advanced scientific technologies are concentrated.\r\nIt was built in the depths of the ocean to secure the safest possible location, beyond the reach of the Black Mage's power and the watchful eyes of his lieutenants, the Black Wings.

0.desc: This biologist is affiliated with Veritas, Aqua Road's secret research institute. He believes science is the guiding light that reveals the truth of the world and that scientists are duty-bound to pursue it.\r\nSadly, he reports that some of his former colleagues have strayed down a darker path.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: This is the mascot of Veritas, Aqua Road's secret research institute. This mechanical wonder rides a strange floating device, and locals believe it's a robot the researchers made.\r\nThanks to its long ears, no one can decide whether it looks more like a fox or a cat. Either way, we can all agree its adorable!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: This physicist is affiliated with Veritas, Aqua Road's secret research institute.\r\nHe studies the strange phenomena occurring throughout Maple World and specializes in theoretical physics. He tried to explain what theoretical physics is, but honestly, I couldn't understand a single word of it...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: This general goods merchant and alchemist is affiliated with Veritas, Aqua Road's secret research institute.\r\nShe hails from Magatia and uses its latest technology to develop new, more effective potions. Unfortunately, none of her creations are allowed to be taken off the premises, so she can't sell them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

32.regionDesc: A toy city, floating above Ludus Lake, on the continent of Ossyria.\nThe bright and cheery city, with buildings made of toy blocks and toy figurines for inhabitants, is filled with childlike joy. However, the entire city remains frozen in the very moment it was created, the moment Rhinne halted time. Deep within its Clocktower lays the Dimensional Crack, caused by the distortion in time, where monsters from other dimensions come and go as they please.

0.desc:
This cuddly, brown, wind-up teddy was manufactured at the Ludibrium Toy Factory.
The creepy thing is, it can move without anyone winding it. It seems a dimensional crack has not only brought the toys of the Ludibrium Clocktower to life, but it's given them a sort of bloodlust. Use extreme caution.
These things give me the heebie jeebies.
                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc:
This snuggly, pink, wind-up teddy was manufactured at the Ludibrium Toy Factory.
Beware. That yellow ribbon belies a thirst for carnage. Defending myself from the creature revealed it was full of nothing but ordinary stuffing. 
Clearly, like the other toys in Ludibrium Clocktower, it is powered by some dark force from the dimensional crack.
                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc:
This adorable wind-up panda was manufactured at the Ludibrium Toy Factory.
The toy was most likely modeled after the panda tribe of Mu Lung, and the wide array of styles suggest these dolls were especially popular in their heyday. 
It's shockingly durable while attacking its victims, but it quickly reverts to its soft and cuddly state once you manage to defeat it and the influence of the dimensional crack fades. Dispatch them quickly.
                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc:
This little duck family toy was manufactured at the Ludibrium Toy Factory.
Like the other toys in the Clocktower, it has been magically animated by energy from the dimensional crack.
The sight of a mother duck shepherding her ducklings would be adorable... if they weren't so vicious. Maybe a kind adventurer will give me one they've defeated...?
                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc:
This Toy Trojan was manufactured at the Ludibrium Toy Factory.
Like the other toys in the Clocktower, it has been magically animated by energy from the dimensional crack.
It appears to be modeled after a knight but bears no resemblance to the actual Cygnus Knights. Regardless, this little toy horse and rider make for a formidable jousting opponent, dealing heavy damage on impact thanks to its charge attack. Caution is advised.
                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc:
This Toy Robot was manufactured at the Ludibrium Toy Factory.
Like the other toys in the Clocktower, it has been magically animated by energy from the dimensional crack.
It probably wasn't designed for combat, but it looks menacing nonetheless. I suppose it's all the more reason to be nice to your electronics...
                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc:
This advanced Toy Robot was manufactured at the Ludibrium Toy Factory.
Like the other toys in the Clocktower, it has been magically animated by energy from the dimensional crack.
According to its design schematics, it's possible to use the Master Robo to command all of the Robos. Of course, it's likely only the bravest of scientists from Edelstein could verify that.
                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc:
If you continue your descent into Ludibrium Clocktower, you will eventually reach a Subspace Crevasse that is otherwise inaccessible.
One of the many monsters that dwells within is Tick, which resembles a bug adorned with a small clock.
The leading theories about this creature suggest it's growth is fueld by consuming time itself, though I could not definitively prove the hypothesis. True or not, there's no guarantee I would comprehend what I was seeing anyway.
                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc:
This monster drifts along in the Subspace Crevasse within Ludibrium Clocktower.
Some scholars claim that Tick-Tock is the evolved form of Tick. I must admit the two do look quite similar.
However, it's unclear whether creatures existing in a chaotic tangle of time and space would evolve in the same way as ordinary lifeforms.
                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: According to Ludibrium records, Chronos did not begin life as a monster, but rather, as an ordinary grandfather clock.\r\nHowever, when time in Ludibrium came to a halt, clocks became useless, and the grandfather clock was discarded. As it sat forgotten in the darkness and eveloped by strange energy, it began to transform into something else. Dark, trans-dimensional energy warped it into something almost unrecognizable, and it awoke as Chronos.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc:
This Chronos is more powerful than average.
You'll know it when you see it, because apart from being massive, this ghost turns the air frigid wherever it goes. Its skills and behavior suggest this evil spirit is supercharged by extradimensional energy.
Deal enough damage to it, and this chillingly fearsome creature will let out a shriek that will rattle your bones.
                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: This Chronos is very much like a Platoon Chronos, apart from one big difference. It has bells attached to its hat like a clown.\r\nLike a Platoon Chronos, it radiates a powerful chill, and dispatching it is much the same process. However, its death rattle is quite unique. Perhaps defeating this terrifying monster is better left in the capable hands of a Bishop.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: This monster drifts through the Subspace Crevasse deep inside Ludibrium Clocktower.\r\nIt appears to be yet another toy produced by the Toy Factory in the shape of a large owl clock. However, Manager Karl insists the Ludibrium Toy Factory has never made anything like it. If that's the case, where are they coming from? Have they emerged from the Subspace Crevasse, like Tick-Tock or Tick? Or do they perhaps hatch from eggs... Speculation among the scientific community is rampant.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc: This assistant apparently commands the Toy Trojans of Ludibrium Castle and distinguishes themselves by wearing a large, impressive hat and riding a starry rocking horse. \r\nHowever, the strange, extra-dimensional energy has driven most of the Toy Trojans into an uncontrollable frenzy. Assistant Cheng is desperately trying to resolve the situation, but has so far been unsuccessful.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: The manager who oversees the Ludibrium Toy Factory. He has a safety-first attitude, and, despite all of the dangerous machinery they use, the workers have a perfect, zero-accident record! That said, he says the real thorn in his side is the toys always running amok... \r\nHe has a daughter in Ludibrium village named Nemi.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A weapon creator. Works in the Apparatus Room of the Ludibrium Toy Factory. \r\nWhen I found out he no longer accepts commissions... What's a stronger word than 'disappointed'? He only does repairs now, just like Pi, Ludibrium's refining expert. I had really hoped to see him in action one day.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: A passionate assembly worker at the Ludibrium Toy Factory. \r\nHans comes second to none when it comes to assembling toys. But he might be a little TOO passionate because he finds his factory work too dull to keep him stimulated. He finds his creative outlet in assembling his own...experimental toys.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A repairman at the Ludibrium Toy Factory. \r\nHe's such a diligent guy, I can tell he really cares about his job. Everyone's got their limits, though, and he's running himself ragged with how often these machines break down. It's all because of that Dimensional Crack... \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: A mechanic at the Ludibrium Toy Factory. \r\nNot only does he keep the production machines running as smooth as silk, he's also the one who drafts the blueprints for all of them! It seems Master Robo is constantly stealing his maintenance documents, though... Maybe he should start keeping them somewhere a little safer? \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: An adventurer who guards the Crossroad of Time. \r\nHe apparently belongs to an anonymous organization, shrouded in mystery, but he doesn't seem dangerous. After all, someone who fights off monsters in the Clocktower with a yo-yo probably wouldn't end up being a bad guy...right? \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: A grandfather clock, who was last seen inspecting the Tower at Lost Time. \r\nWhy did they send such an old clock to the Clocktower to repair the Dimensional Crack? The Chronos lurking in the area seem to be tormenting him with nightmares and preventing him from completing his job. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

33.regionDesc: A place located atop the vast Ludus Lake in the center of the continent of Ossyria. The flow of time here has been frozen by Rhinne, the Transcendent of Time. Ludibrium remains forever locked in its present.

0.desc: A direct advisor for the King of Ludibrium himself. Well, 'advisor' is a bit of a loose term. Since the King has never revealed himself, Tigun can be considered as an 'acting' king of sorts. \r\nBefore becoming the king's advisor, he was a brave and renowned adventurer. It's strange, though. He's very tight lipped about his past. Mayhap someone else can take up the challenge, look him in the eye, and ask him, #e'Were you really an adventurer?'#n \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: Ludibrium's Buddy List Admin. \r\nOnce upon a time, there was a line out the door to talk to him. After all, there was no one else you could go to expand your Friends List. Apparently, it used to cost 50,000 Mesos for just five extra slots. I thought that seemed a little pricey, but he was always running one sale or another, and he ended up penniless and jobless. Maybe the original prices were more justified than I thought...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A storage keeper in Ludibrium. \r\nShe drives around a bright red car, which she apparently uses to transport goods to a nearby storage. I originally thought she just threw everyone's things in the trunk, but she laughed at me when I asked her about it! \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: Head Security Officer of Ludibrium. \r\nMarcel is a busy man, overseeing security for the castle, Eos Tower, AND Helios Tower. Not only that, he acts as a guide for tourists, pointing people to all the best sights in Ludibrium. For such a public figure, he sure did get embarrassed when I complimented his voice! \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A seemingly young girl who lives in Ludibrium. \r\nDon't be fooled by her pigtails and general childish demeanor (like I was)! The blame might lie with me for trying to guess someone's age in a town where time doesn't move. She is very interested in mysterious, preferably ancient, documents. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: A pet food merchant in Ludibrium. \r\nShe looks just like the snuggly Teddies they make at the Ludibrium Toy Factory! I really want to ask her if they were related, but I tried to 'think before I act,' like people always tell me to do, and I ended up keeping my question to myself. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: A Ludibrium weapon seller. His eyes light up whenever he talks about weapons. \r\nIs he a toy soldier, or is he just dressed like one? Well, that's a mighty cool sword he has, if he is just pretending. I really wanted one of my own, but apparently the hilt is made specifically for Ludibrium resident hands to hold...? \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: An armor seller in Ludibrium. \r\nThis one, I'm SURE is not an actual solider. Apparently, since his clientele is mostly soldiers, he likes to wear his items and show them off in action.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: A general goods merchant in Ludibrium. \r\nWhen I went to visit her store, at first, she was busy manning a potion manufacturing machine. I wasn't sure if she'd heard me when I called out, but then, her head turned around in a FULL CIRCLE, and she responded to me! The world sure is full of mysterious, terrifying things.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: A physician assistant at Ludibrium Plastic Surgery.\r\nHe's a bit of a jerk! He told me my face was a mess! A mess! Can you believe it? I had one or two things I wanted to say about HIS face, but since I'm a dignified knight, I stomped out of there instead.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: A plastic surgeon in Ludibrium. \r\n While I'm sure she had a bigger clientele back in the day, her clinic has grown quiet as of late. It must be because Plastic Roy, another reputable surgeon in the area, has gotten so popular. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: The owner of the Ludibrium Hair Salon. \r\nShe's very into unique hairstyles and modern trends, and she even offered to give me a makeover. But considering everyone in Ludibrium seems to be sporting a strange, helmet head, I very politely declined. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: An assistant at the Ludibrium Hair Salon. \r\nI'm particular about my hair, so I was a little hesitant to get a cut from a trainee. I went with a shampoo and blow dry instead, and she blew it out of the park! I hope she achieves her dreams of opening her own hair salon one day. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc:
A dermatologist in Ludibrium. 
I've never seen anyone so tall in my life! I still have a crick in my neck from looking up at her and her red hat. She did pull off that hat very well... 
I heard that the stewardess who works at the Ludibrium Station, Tian, and the armor seller, Miru, visit Gina regularly. Where was my invite...?
                                      - Chronicler Q

14.desc: A pet trainer who works at the Ludibrium Pet Walkway. \r\nHe and his younger brother, Neru, help train pets at the Walkway. Their obstacle course is straightforward and simple: deliver Weaver's letter to his brother at the end of the course. Whether it was 'easy' was a different matter completely... \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

15.desc: A pet trainer who works at the Ludibrium Pet Walkway. \r\nHe is also the younger brother of another trainer on the walkway, Weaver. According to Weaver, he doesn't look much like him, but I can't say for sure. I failed the obstacle course and never managed to meet Neru. The difficulty of the walkway is far too high. He and his older brother, Weaver, help train pets at the Walkway. Weaver informed me that he and Neru look nothing alike. However, I'll just have to take his word for it, because I never did finish that obstacle course. Personally, it likely wasn't just me, and they should consider lowering the difficulty. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

16.desc: A guide who works at Ludibrium Station. She's usually around the front gate. \r\nThese days, there must not be too much to do. While they used to collect ticket fees, the Magatia alchemists developing magic stones made it so everyone flies free now. Maybe that's why she always seems so grumpy? \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

17.desc: A stewardess stationed at Ludibrium Station. \r\nI was having trouble finding the right platform for Orbis, and she helped point me in the right direction. We had a nice conversation, and she told me about her dreams of traveling the world by train. It seems to me that she's working at the wrong place for that... \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

18.desc: Also goes by the Master of MiniGame in Ludibrium. \r\nChico taught me how to play Omok and Memory, and he even helped me create my own Omok set. He must have been a real expert because I just couldn't beat him! I can't wait to teach the other knights how to play when I return. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

19.desc: The one to go to for all things refining in Ludibrium. At least, he used to be. He's not in the market for refining right now and only does repairs. I heard he was very good, so I can't help but wonder why he stopped. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

20.desc: A young girl from Ludibrium Village and Karl's daughter. \r\nShe makes her father a lunchbox to take to his job, managing the Ludibrium Toy Factory, every day! The two of them must have a great relationship. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

21.desc:
A young resident of Ludibrium who went missing for ten months. It hasn't been long since they found her. 
She doesn't seem to have any memories from those months, which could be considered a good thing too. I don't know what happened to her, but at least she's been regaining her sense of normalcy.  
                                      - Chronicler Q
  Addendum for clarification. We are, in fact, quite aware of the events of Korin's 'missing' ten months. 
Korin was abducted by aliens, who then extracted her memories. An agent, who will remain anonymous for security reasons, reported that, although they successfully recovered Korin's memories, it would be detrimental to her recovery process to reimplement them. Doctors also judged this to be the correct choice, as these were traumatic memories that had already been experimented on. 
While her missing months do cause increased anxiety for Korin, however, the Omega Sector reports incidents of this nature frequently enough that the agent's word can likely be trusted. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

22.desc: A glove maker in Ludibrium. \r\nShe makes gloves with her sewing machine and has a whole rainbow of different threads and fabrics. But, like Tara, I guess she's only open for repairs these days... \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

23.desc: A shoe maker in Ludibrium. \r\nTara only does repairs now, just like Sarah. I really wanted a pair of custom shoes, but I had to settle for some stock ones she had...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

24.desc:
A teeny tiny fairy that hangs around the entrance to Eos Tower. 
When I say that Wisp isn't like other fairies, I mean it! Unlike the other prideful fairies, who can hardly deign to look at other races, she has a real and true love for pets. So when Mar the Fairy called, she answered! That's how she ended up in Ludibrium, helping humans with their pet needs. #s#However, she emits an unusually bright light even compared to other fairies, making it difficult to clearly discern her form. Wisp shines even brighter than other fairies, so it's hard to even see what she looks like.#s# 
Wisp learned how to control her light! And she's...so adorable! I swear she's a little taller too, but she said that was my imagination...
                                      - Chronicler Q

34.regionDesc: A particularly strange place in Ludibrium, and a side effect of the town's stopped time. Otherworldly invaders now enter through the Crack in Time to wreak havoc.

0.desc: According to records from the Helios Tower Library, they were originally benign spirits, born from the darkness of the Ludibrium Clocktower.\r\nHowever, due to the dimensional crack, their once gentle nature was corrupted, and they began attacking people by wielding the tangled Power of Time drifting deep within the Clocktower.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: According to records from the Helios Tower Library, they were originally benign spirits born from the darkness of the Ludibrium Clocktower. \r\nDue to the dimensional crack, their nature became corrupted, and among them, the spirit that grew especially ferocious is known as Lazy Buffy. It never stops running about, attacking everything around it with the Power of Time. Their proximity to the Dimensional Crack slowly corrupted them, and those of especially ferocious natured warped into Lazy Buffy. It's a serious menace with its Power of Time. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: According to records from the Helios Tower Library, they were originally workers assigned to the Clocktower Generator Room. \r\nThe darkness that flowed from the Dimensional Crack slowly corrupted their souls, until they became the jesters of time. The grandfather clocks they would once meticulously set the Clocktower's time with are now just weapons in their hands. Don't get lost in the Clocktower, or you might find yourself at the wrong end of their clocks.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: According to records from the Helios Tower Library, they were originally workers assigned to the Clocktower Generator Room. \r\nThe darkness that flowed from the Dimensional Crack slowly corrupted their souls, until they became the jesters of time. Each time Deep Buffoon swings its grandfather clock, it damages the Clocktower's time, which in turn exacerbates the Dimensional Crack. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: Another monster like Tick-Tock and Tick, it's sailed into our world from the Subspace Crevasse.\r\nAccording to records from the Helios Tower Library, they are pirates who roam the Sea of Infinity, plundering travelers who have lost their way. To avoid becoming lost themselves, they sail through the air aboard ships fitted with massive clocks.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: Like Tick-Tock and Tick, it is a being that emerged from a Subspace Crevasse. \r\nAccording to records from the Helios Tower Library, they are pirates who roam the Sea of Infinity, plundering travelers who have lost their way. They fly through the air aboard ships equipped with powerful engines capable of piercing weakened cracks in time in a single burst.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: Like Tick-Tock and Tick, it is a being from a Subspace Crevasse. \r\nAccording to records from the Helios Tower Library, they were sailing the Sea of Infinity when they lost their way and drifted into the Clocktower. Desiring to return to their original world, they indiscriminately attack any being that interferes with the flow of time.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: Like Tick-Tock and Tick, it is a being from a Subspace Crevasse. \r\nAccording to records from the Helios Tower Library, they were sailing the Sea of Infinity when they lost their way and drifted into the Clocktower. The lantern hanging from their flag appears to have been attached to help locate separated companions.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: A powerful gatekeeper summoned by Papulatus to guard the entrance to the Clocktower Generator Room. \r\nThough it appears to be clad in massive armor, a closer look reveals that the armor itself is alive. Although, most would prefer to avoid getting that close to its terrifying visage to begin with. \r\n                                           - Chronicler Q

9.desc: Once, it was an ordinary teddy doll from the Toy Factory; now, it's a sad, abandoned thing. \r\nAbandoned deep inside the Clocktower, an evil spirit from the Dimensional Crack took advantage of its neglected soul. It possessed the bear and sapped the last of the fuzziness from Fuzzy Wuzzy. All that remains of a once-cherished childhood toy is a raging vortex of resentment toward humans.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: Like Tick-Tock and Tick, Klock is a sentient clock that emerged from the Subspace Crevasse. \r\nIn the past, it was believed to be a corrupted Ludibrium clock, like Chronos, but recent research has revealed that it is an entirely different being. They spread false time to sow confusion among people, and live by feeding on that confusion. People once believed that it was, like Chronos, a result of Ludibrium's corruption. Recent research shows that it's something else entirely, though! They feed on confusion, so they like to mess with people's watches and clocks, to sow as much confusion and chaos as possible.   \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: Like Tick-Tock and Tick, this being emerged from the Subspace Crevasse. \r\nAs you could guess, it's Klock, but stronger. They spread false time to plunge people into confusion and live by feeding on that confusion.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: Previously: an ordinary teddy bear from the Ludibrium Toy Factory. Now: a teddy ghost? \r\nThese poor teddy bears, once cherished and loved, were abandoned somewhere inside the Clocktower. Evil spirits from the Dimensional Crack possessed them, and they're now cursed to haunt the Clocktower as the spirits slowly drain their essence. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc: Previously: an ordinary teddy bear from the Ludibrium Toy Factory. Now: a teddy ghost? They became what they are after evil spirits from the Dimensional Crack found them, abandoned in the Clocktower, and possessed them. \r\nAccording to records from the Helios Tower Library, when the chains that bind the teddy and spirit turn gold, the teddy has been fully absorbed, mind, spirit, and soul. It'll wander the Clocktower, lost to time, for eternity. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

14.desc: Long ago, the King of Ludibrium imposed a horrific punishment upon a criminal. The sinner was sealed inside a clock, forced to repent for the rest of eternity. \r\nBut with the Dimensional Crack opening and the Subspace Crevasse forming, reality was twisted. The sinner's soul awakened into what we now call Phantom Watch. It's still doomed to its punishment, chained to a watch as it drifts aimlessly around, but the curse is clearly weakening. At the very least, the strength of its icy blasts seem to suggest as much. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

15.desc:
Long ago, the King of Ludibrium imposed a horrific punishment upon a criminal. The sinner was sealed inside a clock, forced to repent for the rest of eternity. 
But with the Dimensional Crack opening and the Subspace Crevasse forming, reality was twisted. The sinner's soul awakened into what we now call Grim Phantom Watch. Unlike its counterpart, its soul festered in its hatred, refusing to repent. It seems hellbent on revenge against all of Ludibrium.
The prison clock still binds the soul, but its hold is extremely weak.
                                      - Chronicler Q

16.desc: Summoned by Papulatus, its only reason for existence is to guard the Clocktower Generator Room. \r\nIt's believed to be a mage that crossed over from another dimension. Maybe it was a side effect of traveling through the Dimensional Crack, but it's difficult to tell if it's even a living being anymore.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

17.desc: A monster who found its way to our world through the Dimensional Crack. \r\nIt may have numerous personalities, but all of those personalities are uniformly evil. After all, Papulatus is the one responsbile for warping the innocent toys of Ludibrium into monsters AND the growth of the Dimensional Crack. It seems like the bigger the Dimensional Crack gets, the more power Papulatus is able to siphon from other worlds. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

18.desc:
A ghost of teddy bears past. 
In a tale as old as time, the teddy bear couldn't bear being neglected and abandoned in the Clocktower. Attracted by the toy's resentment, an evil spirit fed on the last of its warmth. All that remained of the teddy bear was its hatred of humans.
Master Soul Teddy resentment raged and warped out of control, giving birth to a superior evil spirit. 
                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc: A man dressed as a clown, but not a clown. He can be found in the Path of Time, on the bottom floor of the Clocktower. \r\nHeHe's investigating an incident he witnessed where he saw a bright light falling into the Crack in Time. Was it just me, or did things seem a little tense between him and Ghosthunter Bob? \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: A ghost hunter who also resides in the Path of Time, on the bottom floor of the Clocktower.\r\nHe was dispatched by the Spirit Hunter Association to deal with evil spirits that emerged from the Dimensional Crack. He seems a lot more interested in eating burgers, though.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: The Path of Time seems like an interesting place for a merchant to set up shop. \r\nConsidering the unsettling frequency of rabid toy attacks and the Dimensional Crack, and the fact that he even makes the potions himself, he sure is a diligent guy.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: A man dressed as a clown, but not a clown. He can be found in the Path of Time, on the bottom floor of the Clocktower. \r\nI thought it was reasonable of me to ask if he was related to Mr. Bouffon in some way, all things considered. But he seemed a little affronted, emphatically stating that there was no relation and, in fact, that they weren't even close at all! \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A local bird of Ludibrium, who likes to perch up at the Warped Path of Time on the bottom floor of the Clocktower. \r\nHe looks like a bird, smells like a bird, and talks like...a very peculiar tropical bird. Apparently he likes being in the Clocktower, because there's all sorts of bits and ends for him to collect. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

35.regionDesc: A massive Clocktower in the city of time, Ludibrium, that leads to the future. At the bottom of its endless floors, a gateway opens to the Omega Sector, a secret military base that stands staunchly against the alien threat.

0.desc: A golem made of blocks.\r\nAccording to Tigun the Advisor, it was created using leftover materials from Eos Tower's construction. Once a staunch guardian of the tower, the Dimensional Crack made it lose itself and forget its mission. Now, the golem wanders about, attacking all who dare travel the tower.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: A golem made of kingly blocks. \r\nThis lonesome king was once just like its yellow counterparts. But when the Dimensional Crack ripped through time and space, the golem was sucked into it, and its color turned back when it returned. Now, the King Golem wanders about, attacking all who dare travel the tower. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A bird wearing goggles and a helmet that flies around Eos Tower. \r\nConsidering this is a bona-fide, real-life bird, and not a toy, it can't be from around Ludibrium. For a visitor, it sure is grumpy, though. Don't even consider going near its nest; it'll attack you on sight! \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: A light blue toy plane that flies around the outer area of Eos Tower. \r\nIt's the largest and heaviest of its kind. Maybe its weight isn't evenly distributed across its wingspan, but this aerial toy is always accidentally crashing into people.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A yellow toy helicopter that flies around the outer area of Eos Tower. \r\nTry as it might, the little guy's propellors just aren't strong enough to withstand the strong winds around the tower. It's suffered more than one scratch as it gets buffeted about like a paper airplane. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: A pink toy plane that flies around the outer area of Eos Tower. \r\nSomeone needs to check the batteries in this pink menace, because it seems far too overpowered. In fact, it often loses control of its engine entirely! \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: A toy block that resembles an octopus. \r\nAccording to the latest research from Omega Sector, Bloctopus is mostly likely just a mutated version of Octopus, another side effect of the Clocktower. With its excellent jumping ability, Bloctopus is a little too good at navigating its way up and down the tower as it chases people down. They say adventurers and travelers should consider it a 'high-risk threat,' but it's just so cute... \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: This regal Bloctopus found a crown somewhere and declared himself king! \r\nNo one can really figure out why its so much stronger than regular Bloctopus. Its crown really is just a toy crown, and The only thing differentiating King Bloctopus is its crown, which really is just an ordinary, toy crown. Maybe it's a confidence thing? \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: A bunny doll toy that lives in Eos Tower. \r\nIt beats its drum nonstop without rest. Strangely enough, although it should be powered by batteries, there's nothing inside it at all. How on earth is it moving?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: A bird wearing goggles and a helmet that flies around Eos Tower. \r\nConsidering this is a bona-fide, real-life bird, and not a toy, it can't be from around Ludibrium. It's a big difficult to \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: A spider that's made a webby home for itself inside Eos Tower. \r\nThis dark, musty, and oversized tower must have seemed like the perfect place for a spider to settle in. They may have settled in a little too well, seeing as I kept getting tangled in their webs! I had just gotten my hair done too... \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: A spider that's made a webby nest for itself inside Eos Tower. \r\nWhile its abnormal green body and red stripes are menacing, it's luckily not venomous. Why 'luckily'? Because I tested it out on myself!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: If this toy rat moves on its own, what does the wind-up mechanism on its back do...? \r\nThis rat was designed to catch mice, which is probably why it looks so disturbingly realistic? The intent was for it to camouflage with the rodents so as to not alarm them. Now that it moves on its own, there's very little to differentiate them from the real thing... \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc: If this toy rat moves on its own, what does the wind-up mechanism on its back do...? \r\nIt was originally created to help catch mice. After discovering a population of black mice in the tower, Black Ratz was created to imitate them as well.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

14.desc:
The strange symbiotic relationship that is Rombot caused Dr. Kim of Omega Sector to question everything he thought he ever knew between aliens and Bloctopuses... and for me too... 
It looks like the teeny tiny alien Bloctopus is the brains of this operation, while the armored golem is the brawns. 
                                            - Chronicler Q

0.desc: A toy soldier guarding a door on the 100th floor of Eos Tower. \r\nIt's been standing in the exact same spot for so long that it's bored out of his mind. The diligent soldier tries its best to hide its sleepiness by keeping its eyes peeled, but that just makes him look incredibly stern and serious.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: A toy soldier guarding a door on the 100th floor of Eos Tower. \r\nHe seems pretty worried, seeing as a monster stole the Ludibrium Clocktower's pendulum and fled into the room beyond the door.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: This little roly poly worker is very diligent. \r\nHe used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. It's hard work they're doing here, especially with the endless flow of monsters here.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: This little roly poly worker is a bit grumpy. \r\nHe used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. Ratz keep stealing his lunchbox, so I don't exactly blame him for his bad mood.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: This little roly poly worker seems to be sulking. \r\nHe used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. He needs something sticky to do his repairs, stat!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: This little roly poly worker has a bright smile. \r\nHe used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. His upbeat, can-do attitude and concern for worker safety is just like a knight! He was looking for ideas to make it easier for roly poly workers to communicate with each other.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: This little roly poly worker always has a misleading scowl.\r\nHe used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. While his permanent frown might give off the wrong impression, he really cares about his job.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: This little roly poly worker just loves life! \r\nHe used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. The little dude really is the definition of, 'If you love your work, you'll never work a day in your life.' Working in a big tower is one of his childhood dreams. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: This little roly poly worker is wearing an eyepatch. \r\nHe used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. No matter what he says, his eyepatch is from being wounded on the job.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: This little roly poly worker has a mustache. \r\nHe used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. Now that he mentions it, I think I skipped breakfast too...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: A roly poly worker with clear, bright eyes. \r\nIt used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. It might be the youngest of the ten workers sent on the job, but there's no question that it's the most enthusiastic.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: A roly poly worker with a stern expression. \r\nIt used to work at the Ludibrium Toy Factory but was temporarily dispatched to Eos Tower to help with repairs once news of the damage broke. It seems pretty eager to finish the job and return home.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: A toy soldier who got lost while wandering the vast Eos Tower. \r\nIts original assignment was to guard the 59th floor of Eos Tower but somehow ended up all the way on the 92nd floor. I do have a sneaking suspicion that it just doesn't want to go back to his post.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc: A sign that's posted on the 101st floor of Eos Tower. \r\nIt's been recruiting brave individuals to help close the Dimensional Crack that has formed in Ludibrium. If you wish to defeat Alishar and aid Ludibrium in its time of crisis...you're supposed to talk to the sign. I've only ever met one other talking sign.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

14.desc: A gumball machine on the 66th floor of Eos Tower. \r\nInsert a coin and turn the handle to receive potions or pills. I wanted to get a gumball myself, but, despite its name, it didn't have any...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

36.regionDesc: Another massive Clocktower rising in the city of time, Ludibrium. Unlike its counterpart, this tower leads to the path. A mysterious power flows through it, as if a clock's spring was being wound in reverse.\r\n

0.desc: A librarian who manages the Helios Tower Library. \r\nAt one point, that whole Dimensional Crack mess turned the library's storybooks into a hopeless, mixed-up disaster, but most of it's been sorted out by now. That said, a few of those stories still haven't found their endings...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: This sharp scientist works in Ludibrium's time control room.\r\nWith Rhinne's permission, she uses the time controller to keep time frozen in Ludibrium. But the Dimensional Crack damaged it, and now you can use it to travel back into the past. You'll need Karen's approval to use the time controller.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

37.regionDesc: A theme park located northeast of Ludibrium. Its mascots are Targa the bear and Scarboss the lion. The puppet show the two put on is considered the park's best attraction.

0.desc: One of the mascots of Fantasy Theme World, Creeper Scarlion. \r\nIt hangs out over at Funky Station in Fantasy Theme World. Even though it looks like a lion, it doesn't exactly strike anyone as the 'brave' type. If anything, its slightly timid face gives it a pretty friendly and approachable charm.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: One of the mascots of Fantasy Theme World, Ratacula. \r\nIt hangs out over at Funky Station in Fantasy Theme World. It looks like it's modeled after a bear, though. A little bit of stuffing is poking out of its ear, but it's by design!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A ghostly character that lives in Fantasy Theme World. \r\nLooking pretty dejected and bitter, it seems to be talking to itself as it floats around. It's definitely just a character, right? It isn't an actual ghost... right?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: Canterbear is a pair that lives in Fantasy Theme World. \r\nAt first glance, it looks like a rider on horseback, but the mount is actually just a rocking horse scavenged from a carousel. The horse seems to move by hopping around on its metal spring. It seems to be enjoying the ride so much, that even falling off doesn't cause its ear-splitting grin to fade.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A well-balanced character that lives in Fantasy Theme World. \r\nDecked out in a clown hat and face paint, this lion's barrel-balancing, balloon-holding circus act is impressive. It does look a little overwhelmed, though. It is JUGGLING a lot of things at once!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: A hydrated bear that lives in Fantasy Theme World. \r\nStrapped with a massive barrel on its back, it's always ready to spray a refreshing grape-flavored soda through its giant straw the moment an order comes in. The only issue is that the carbonation can be so intense that it occasionally sends customers flying...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: A pilot lion that lives in Fantasy Theme World. \r\nIt seems to always be flying pretty low to the ground, which might be because of its damaged wing. Medical care can't be easy to access around here, so all it has right now is a poorly-applied bandage on the injury.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: A little bus that drives around Fantasy Theme World.\r\nIts decorated with cute Creeper Scarlion and Ratacula dolls on the roof. While I could definitely beat it in a race, it goes at the perfect pace for sightseeing. It's not exactly a pleasant experience, though, as the little thing gets jostled by every little bump and pothole in the road.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: A Viking character that lives in Fantasy Theme World. \r\nA Viking is truly nothing without a ship, and this one simply won't put theirs down. I'd like to know the workout routine of whoever is inside this costume; it must be the heaviest one in the park!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc:
A giant bear found over at the Crittertorium in Fantasy Theme World. 
Apparently live animals was out of budget for them, so this is just a very, very large teddy bear mascot. I say apparently, because its just as aggressive as the real thing, and it's always trying to attack the audience. Where did this thing pick up martial arts skills?! 
If any elderly visitors are stopping by Fantasy Theme World, it's probably for the best that they steer clear of the Crittertorium altogether.
                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: A giant lion found over at the Crittertorium in Fantasy Theme World. \r\nIt's not actually a real lion, of course; it's just a massive mascot character. It looks like there's someone stuffed inside, manually moving the thing around. Wearing a costume that huge must make it nearly impossible to see and unbearably hot...but they do it all to put on the best show they can.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc: A young boy, sporting squirrel ears and a tail, who hangs out at Fantasy Theme World. I asked, and he said the secret to his silky soft fur was premium acorn seed oil. I'll have to try some. \r\nHe's intent on professing his feelings for someone, but more importantly... are his ears and tail real? It's just a headband and a clip...right?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: A young girl, sporting squirrel ears and tail, who hangs out at Fantasy Theme World. \r\nThis poor girl thought that this was park was the perfect place to go on a date, not a house of horrors. To make matters worse, she scares really easily. Really, really easily.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A merchant at the main entrance of Fantasy Theme World who only stocks general goods. \r\nI had my wallet open and ready to get some souvenirs, but I walked away empty handed. Just take my money already!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: A guide for Fantasy Theme World. \r\nIs it just me or does he look...exactly like Halsted, the merchant at the main entrance? I wanted to ask if they were related, but he was so busy, I couldn't even get his attention.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A guide for Fantasy Theme World. \r\nHalsted the merchant, Oliver the guide, and this guide, could seriously be triplets, right? There's just something about the way they do their hair... They must be siblings. They have to be.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

38.regionDesc: A land of the past dwelling in the shade of Helios Tower. The small village of hanok houses is home to a group of dark-haired, dark-eyed humans. Looking closely, they seem strangely familiar...

0.desc: A white bunny that makes its home in Korean Folk Town. \r\nOnce upon a time, these little guys used to live on the moon, making rice cakes, hence the wooden mallet it carries around.
