The only thing I've seen on the receiving end of it isn't rice cake, however, but adventurers. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: Dark Axe Stump is regional to Korean Folk Town. \r\nAccording to legend, a tree cutter lodged his axe in its trunk. When he never returned to retrieve the axe, Dark Axe Stump, filled with resentment, became what it is today. I may not be the smartest tool in the shed, but even I know that Dark Axe Stump is probably just the result of its environment!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A baby tiger that lives around Korean Folk Town. \r\nThe way it tumbles and plays is incredibly adorable. If you can get close enough to rub its paw pads, you'll find them to still be baby soft. I wouldn't recommend it, though. A predator is still a predator, after all.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: Definitely no longer a baby, Hogul protects its home in Korean Folk Town. \r\nHodori is all grown up now! Despite that massive build and solid muscles, it's actually pretty timid and always moves about with caution. Local villagers will sometimes give it rice cakes, Hogul's favorite snack.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A three-tailed fox that's been spotted near Korean Folk Town. \r\nThis young fox may only have three tails for now, but one day it'll blossom into an elegant nine-tailed fox. Its tails are covered in luxuriously soft fur, which sometimes attracts the wrong type. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: This little blue ball that floats around Korean Folk Town at first seems to be made of goblin fire. \r\nIt doesn't take much poking and prodding to undo its transformation, though. I was a little disappointed to find that it was just an old brick. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc:
A goblin that's often stomping around Korean Folk Town. 
Unless travelers enjoy its favorite past time, wrestling, I would STRONGLY advise against traveling through its mountainous territory. Not only does it let out clouds of stinky, poisonous fumes every it goes, it challenges everyone who encounters it to a wrestling match. 
According to records from the Helios Tower Library, it's fond of buckwheat jelly. 
                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc:
A clumsy blue goblin often seen around Korean Folk Town. 
He might be a goblin, but the way he's always losing and forgetting things is actually a bit endearing. In the past, he even lost one of his favorite caps. 
It tends to use its large goblin bat like a fan, blasting out icy air in a circle around it. According to records from the Helios Tower Library, it's fond of rice wine, which might explain why it's always dropping things. 
                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc:
A fiery goblin that lights up Korean Folk Town. 
All it takes is one swing of its bat to engulf its surroundings in fire. Some Yellow King Goblins get along well with Nine-Tailed Fox, and I can see why. 
According to records from the Helios Tower Library, it loves a good pork dish. 
                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc: A talking toad that lives in Korean Folk Town. \r\nIt's a friend of Kong Ji, another resident of Korean Folk Town and helps her with her work whenever it can.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: A talking cow that calls Korean Folk Town home. \r\nIt is a friend of Kong Ji, a resident of Korean Folk Town, and works together with Toad to give her a hoof when she needs.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A master potter who lives in Korean Folk Town. \r\n Her reputation precedes her: they say that Grandma Yeon's jars will make your food last forever. Grandma Yeon lives a peaceful life making pottery while she waits for her husband, Tae Gong, to return from his deep sea fishing trip.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc:
The son of the rice cake shop owner in Korean Folk Town. 
It seems contradictory, but he actually doesn't like rice cakes. Growing up having eaten it all the time, he'd grown tired of it. 
On another note, he was very shifty eyed the entire time we were talking.
                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A young girl in Korean Folk Town who works tirelessly for her family. \r\nFortunately, her friends, Toad and Cow, help her out a lot, so she gets by one way or another. She's been friends with the Magistrate since she was young.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: One of the residents of Korean Folk Town. \r\nHe is Chil Nam's older brother, and the two are known to be close and affectionate siblings. He's more timid than he looks.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: An older, blind gentleman who lives in Korean Folk Town. \r\nHe's developed a very keen hearing over the years, and he can identify people by just the sound of their footsteps. Could he secretly be a martial arts master...?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: An armor seller in Korean Folk Town. He also crafts the armor himself. \r\nHis most prized tool is a pair of scissors, a family heirloom that's been passed down for generations. I was excited to try a pair on for myself, but he flatly refused and kicked me out on the spot.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: A storage keeper in Korean Folk Town. Mr. Noh is well-known for keeping very meticulous records of every single item that comes under his care. \r\nThe real reason is because he's a little scatterbrained, so he wants to make sure he doesn't lose anything. It's admirable either way!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: The only noble of Korean Folk Town. He is the elder of the village and respected by all. \r\nHe once worked for the government but has since retired to his hometown of Korean Folk Town.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: A general goods merchant who lives in Korean Folk Town. \r\nShe sells potions and other goods at her tavern, and Seolie helps her sell clothes. Her ventures have really paid off, and there isn't anyone in Korean Folk Town who doesn't know Bung's Mama. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: A resident of Korean Folk Town and Chil Sung's younger brother. Not only do they look alike, but their personalities mirror each other too! Everyone in the village attests to the close sibling bond they have. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: A weapon seller in Korean Folk Town, known for crafting sturdy, high quality weapons. \r\nMaybe it's because forging weapons is so exhausting, but he says he always gets hungry very quickly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc: One of the residents of Korean Folk Town. The hardships of growing up poor has done nothing to mar this jewel of the town. \r\nShe makes a living selling clothes at Bung's Mama's tavern and does a little merchanting on the side herself.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

14.desc: God of Mountains lives at the small well on Black Mountain.\r\n I pointed out the huge lump on his head, and he told me a logger dropped an axe into the well and hit him one day! It looked like it hurt. Maybe someone should suggest some logging regulations in the area...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

15.desc: This sturdy tree cutter does most of his work out in Tiger Forest. Thanks to his impressive strength, he makes a good living for himself. He's well known for his deep filial piety.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

16.desc: A merchant who sells around Tiger Ridge. \r\nHe's said to have come from a foreign land, far away from Korean Folk Town. That must be why his clothes and accent were a little different from the locals. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

17.desc: A very rich resident of Korean Folk Town. If his piles and piles of treasure and giant mansion are anything to go by, he must be well off. \r\nI did point out an axe wedged into his front gate, and he mumbled something vague about brotherly quarrels.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

18.desc: One of the residents of Korean Folk Town. \r\nBelieve it or not, Hongbu is Nolbu's little brother. They obviously don't resemble each other much, in more ways than one. He seems mild mannered and kind, but people say he's terrifying when he gets mad.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

19.desc: A rice cake seller in Korean Folk Town. \r\nAt first glance, the glossy, appetizing rice cakes she had for sale immediately caught my eye. She no doubt makes a comfortable living with how popular her rice cakes are, and I was disappointed I didn't have the time to try one. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

20.desc:
An oarsman who can be found at Deep Waters.
He and his brother, the Qing Merchant, look alike in almost every way. There's just one big difference. And that difference is...
That difference is...
Well, just see below...

He doesn't have a mole on his face.
                                      - Chronicler Q

39.regionDesc: When the time controller of the Helios Tower was broken, it opened up a path to the Victoria Island of the past. A proper town has yet to be built in this time, so the people live in a makeshift encampment and are led by an elf named Athena Pierce.

0.desc: These mysterious tree monsters can only be found in Ellin Forest. They are somewhat similar to Stumps in that they, too, resemble a tree stump; however, they are not dead, dry trees, but rather tree monster that are very much alive and can grow flowers and berries. Although they sometimes attack small animals, they generally feed on nutrients they absorb through their roots.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: A strange insect that inhabits Ellin Forest. It weaves its way through rocky crevices and survives mostly on moss. \r\nThe people of Altaire Camp say that Stone Bug only recently began to grow moss on its body, most likely due to the high amount of it in their diet.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A boar that inhabits Ellin Forest. Boasting notably thick coats of fur and tough hides, these monsters don't easily incur damage, even when attacked with a spear. I figured my bow and arrow would only irritate it, so I decided to take a detour around it. I'm curious if it'll grow into a Wild Boar one day.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: A particularly ferocious variant of the primitive boars that inhabit Ellin Forest. \r\nThey look no different from ordinary Primitive Boars, but no one can seem to figure out where their innate aggression comes from. Maybe it was natural selection, or maybe the cave life just wasn't for them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: An ancient snail that can be found in Ellin Forest. Not only is it much bigger than its blue and red counterparts, this edition of snail also comes with razor-sharp teeth. \r\nIt'll lay silently in one spot for as long as they need to as they wait for their prey. It has to be a LONG time for moss to start to grow...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: This giant mushroom found in Ellin Forest towers over Orange and Blue Mushroom in stature. \r\nIt looks something like Horny Mushroom. But with moss, instead of horns. To make matters worse, they're carnivorous, so steer clear if you see one.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: This fairy glistens and sparkles as it flies through Ellin Forest. Just like other fairies, it views other races with a hostile eye. \r\nAccording to Destonen, although fairies were always cautious by nature, it was only recently that they began turning into monsters. I thought Wisp was the odd one out, but maybe not all fairies were always like this.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: Ancient Fairy is protective of its home in Ellin Forest and tend to be much more violent and ferocious than Shining Fairy. \r\nAccording to Ellin, this is because Ancient Fairies are probably the ones closest to Ephenia the Fairy Queen. What made Ephenia turn her back on the world?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc:
Queen of the fairies in Ellin Forest. 
Ephenia is the picture of beauty. Her braided red hair adorned with wooden vines; the way her wings, larger than any I'd ever seen, flutter out behind her... Ephenia is the very picture of beauty and grace. 
No one is sure what made her turn her wrath upon on the sylphs of Ellin Forest, especially since the two groups had always enjoyed friendly relations.
                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc: The chief magician of Altaire Camp. A man of a serious disposition, he does everything he can to secure the camp's safety. \r\nHe erected a magical barrier using stone barriers and maintains it with his magic to prevent monsters from attacking.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: The medic of Altaire Camp. \r\nWhat Loha lacks in combat ability, and social skills, she makes up for tenfold with her medical knowledge. She works tirelessly to treat the injured and keep supplies stocked.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A temporary storage keeper at Altaire Camp. \r\nHe was originally a warrior who took part in settling the area, but after being injured in the leg by a wild boar, he took what work he could on the campground instead. Once his injury recovers, he plans to pass the storage keeper duties on to someone else and return to the settlement efforts.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: A general goods merchant at Altaire Camp. \r\nSince supplies are scarce within the camp, Mayoren is very careful to manage his inventory, so that people will always have access to their basic needs. It's obvious he has a good heart and cares about his job, as he will give anyone injured during an expedition their goods at half price. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A young woman who lives at Altaire Camp. \r\nShe nearly lost her life to a monster, but was saved by the parents of Crawls with Balrog. In return, she now cares for Crawls with Balrog in their place.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc: Crawls with Balrog lost his parents at birth, and so everyone in Altaire Camp looks after him in their place. \r\nThe child's unique name was given to him by his parents when they were alive. In their tribe, names are chosen with the hope that the child will be born with the spirit of a strong warrior. There are some who call him the Child of Destiny.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: The expedition leader of Altaire Camp. To think she would be here, of all places... \r\nShe obviously looks a lot younger, but there's no doubt that it's Athena Pierce, the Bowman Instructor of Henesys. I never thought I'd see a glimpse of Athena's past in a place like this.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc: The thief representative of Altaire Camp. He keeps watch over the desolate land to the west of the camp. \r\nIt's a harsh and dangerous area, unsuitable for building a settlement, but he claims its the best place a thief could ask for.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc:
While Ellin currently resides in the Forest of Poison Haze, Ellin Forest was originally her territory.
However, after the Black Mage split Victoria Island apart, she gave up the forest to refugees who had escaped with nothing but their lives. 
If it were not for this kind fairy, Victoria Island may never have become what it is today. When I tried to thank her for her service, she scoffed and shooed me away.
                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc:
Sion tends to this child, who appears to be even younger than Crawls with Balrog, in the Tent House. 
The energetic bundle of joy seems to be intent on throwing herself out of her bed, so Kyrin needs constant supervision. 
Come to think of it, doesn't Instructor Kyrin also have orange hair?
                                      - Chronicler Q

40.regionDesc: Located at the base of Eos Tower is Maple World's base to defend against alien invaders. The M-Force deploys from here with futuristic gadgets like Mesodizers and Mesotron to combat the otherworldly threat.

0.desc:
This foot soldier is the lowest rank of the Mateons who came from outer space to conquer Earth. What they lack in firepower they make up for in number. 
Allied with the Grays, they intend to take over Omega Sector by combining their teamwork with the Grays' strength. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
Additional information has been appended following a report from the Omega Sector.
Unlike the Grays, whose extraterrestrial origin is clear, the Metons are a mystery. 
Interestingly, their structure is very similar to Ludibrium's Bloctopus and Kerning City's Octopus, proven through Dr. Kim's research paper. 
Dr. Kim claims that the Mateons did not come from outer space, but is rather a lifeform that originated here in Maple World. 
They do all look quite similar... but could the Mateons really be native to the Maple World? I need more proof. 
And it's not because I hold a grudge against Dr. Kim. It really is not.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc:
Mid-ranking soldiers of the Mateons, who came from outer space to conquer Earth. Soldiers in this rank move much more quickly than those in the lower one. 
Allied with the Grays, they intend to take over Omega Sector by combining their teamwork with the Grays' strength. 
Riding small ships, they move swiftly and boast high mobility, launching unexpected attacks instantaneously. Because of this, Omega Sector must remain on high alert at all times.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
One of the Grays who came to conquer Earth. 
Among the Grays, this one holds a relatively low rank and is relatively weaker. However, its psychic powers and cunning are formidable weapons in themselves. 
Allied with the Mateons, the Grays offer their strength in their efforts to attack Omega Sector. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
Additional details have been appended following a report from Omega Sector. 
According to the Omega Sector' battle records, there had been previous encounters with a wider variety of Grays, such as Chief Grays, Zeta Grays, and Zenos. However, Grays maintain their species through replication-based regeneration. Since they have focused on replicating on Barnard Grays and Ultra Grays, which are relatively easy to replicate and possess high combat power, it is presumed that is why other Gray variants have vanished.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
These Grays are unique in that they were created here on Maple World. They are the product of Grays who cloned themselves in the hopes of enhancing their combat abilities. \The strongest of Grays, the Ultra Gray have been implementing their supernatural powers to attack Dr. Kim of Omega Sector. He reports he has made contact with the extraterrestrials and claims they are aloof and condescending. 
Allied with the Mateons, the Grays offer their strength in their efforts to attack Omega Sector. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
Bernard Gray aboard a small saucer. This appears to be one of the methods used to compensate for the Grays' physical weakness. 
It seems only Barnard Grays deemed worth and capable are assigned airships. 
According to the Omega Sector investigation, Mateon technology was used in the construction of the airships.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
Ultra Grays riding in a small airship. Even Ultra Gray is only enhanced psychically, and uses an airship to account for its physical weakness. 
Like the Barnard Grays, it seems only Ultra Grays deemed worth and capable are assigned airships. 
According to Omega Sector's investigation, Mateon technology was used in the construction of the airships.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
A Mateon wearing mechanized armor and was among those that infiltrated Omega Sector. Likely part of some sort of special forces unit. 
Still unsure of the full scope of the suit's capabilities, but Dr. Kim has suggested that the armor may even allow communication with their home planet.
In other words, the Mateons may be receiving direct orders from the planet of the Grays.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: A powerful weapon secretly built by the Mateon aliens to attack the earth. It's been designed to support the small and weak Mateons and is equipped with multitudes of explosive missiles. \r\nThe Omega Sector has sent over a special troop to fight against MT-09.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc:
A saucer sent out from the Mothership. There appears to be someone, or something, driving it. 
Judging by the dimensions, neither a Barnard nor an Ultra Gray could fit in the drone. There must be a very small, different variant Gray inside.r
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
Additional details have been appended following a report from Omega Sector. 
The drone's pilot turned out to be a small Mateon. Interestingly, it seems the drone itself is fueled by the Gray's psychic ability. 
Dr. Kim believes this drone to be the result of the Grays' special abilities and the Mateons' advanced technology coming together. He's developing an upgraded ultrasonic decoder to collect more data. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: A saucer sent out from the Mothership. There appears to be someone, or something, driving it. \r\nAside from being made of black metal, it is no different from White Robosaucer.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: A soldier of Omega Sector. Although deployed to the Omega Sector, he serves as a gate guard and is not sent into combat. \r\nSeeing as he complains incessantly that he wishes to join the glorious battle, he must be quite confident in his skills. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc:
The chief engineer of Omega Sector. With a heavy workload and no assistants, she's constantly busy. Maintaining machinery is her responsibility, and despite how demanding it is, she carries out her duties with dedication. 
Kay has a boyfriend, though his whereabouts are unknown. The ship her boyfriend was aboard was forced to make an emergency landing when it was attacked by aliens.
 It was a top-secret mission, and his survival has still not been confirmed. Still, a letter he left for her gives Kay hope that he's alive, and she continues to wait.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: A general goods merchant that operates out of the Omega Sector hangar. Most of the items for sale are similar to those found in other areas, but there is one notable exception: pain relievers. \r\nAre those particularly necessary for fighting aliens?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: An armor seller who operates out of Omega Sector hangar. His marketing bit is simple: you need sturdy armor when fighting aliens. \r\nI had hoped to purchase the M-Forcer outfit he had on display, but it was just that. For display.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: A weapon seller who operates out of Omega Sector hangar. He often complains that with the increase in monsters, materials for crafting weapons have grown scarce. His wares are no different from those found in other areas. \r\nIt seems that equipment for soldiers of the Omega Sector are actually provided separately.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: The newest member of the M-Force who, succeeding the previous M-Forcer, Minnie. \r\nShe has a neat ponytail which suits her outfit. Her fearsome strength is almost alien in itself.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: A kind-looking middle-aged storage keeper at the Omega Sector hangar. He says the storage is sturdy, and the containers behind him give no reason to doubt him. In fact, the advanced technology implemented here means your items will be much more secure than in any other town.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
This middle-aged doctor is leading the efforts at the Omega Sector and can most easily be found in the command center. He may possess a sharp, reliable look, he's sloppy with his work and documentation. Don't trust him too much. Or at all.
Long ago, a few adventurers came all the way to the Omega Sector at the request of Chief Stan to meet Dr. Kim. He handed them a mere 7,500 Mesos and barely even acknowledged the weary adventurers, completely dismissing the arduous journey they'd undertook to make it to him. He didn't even think them worth a Return School.
Yes. And this chronicler has now returned to the place where it all began. My revenge will be sweet.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc:
Another researcher who works at the Omega Sector's command center. He had an awful cold the last I saw him, but his condition has improved. 
He's a tad nondescript, so there's not much to say about him. Ah. Once, an adventurer once retrieved Rombot's memory card at Porter's request, only for Porter to accidentaly destroy it and send the poor soul all the way back for another one.
 If Porter ever asks you to fetch something, bring back more than one.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: One of the Gray aliens residing in the Mothership above Omega Sector. His name is Nolyfe. It does sound quite alien.\r\n Interestingly, there is a rumor that he is a fan of the M-Force, especially Pink.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc: Dr. Zindelblarp resides in the Mothership Pilothouse above Omega Sector. One of the main culprits of damaging the Mesotron by piloting the giant robot OMNI-CLN. \r\nDespite his title, he doesn't actually hold a doctoral degree.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

41.regionDesc: An ancient village nestled deep within Minar Forest, Leafre is a sacred land where dragons and Halflingers coexist. The air here is filled with the breath of ancient dragons, and the sky still bears traces of massive nests and dragons long past. The Halflingers live alongside dragons while tending to the forest, passing down their wisdom and way of life from generation to generation. This region is a blend of mountains, forests, and ancient dragon ruins. Hunting grounds, such as Dragon Canyon, are home to a wide variety of dragon monsters.

0.desc: A big beetle that lives in Minar Forest, where trees and leaves are abundant. It is protected by a thick outer layer that minimizes the external impact, and the sizable horn it sports on its head can to toss any threatening enemy far away. \r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: A big beetle that lives in Minar Forest which acquired a steel-like firm, silver outer layer when it underwent ecdysis. It threatens its enemies with even more powerful attack than a regular Beetle.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

2.desc: A fuzzy spirit that lives only in Minar Forest. It cannot be found elsewhere, as it only lives in an area where no signs of contamination can be seen. Many adventurers are fooled by its fuzzy fur and adorable appearance, but it is covered in dust which has anesthetic effects.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: A fuzzy spirit that lives only in Minar Forest. Unlike Rash, the creature from which the Dark Rash has evolved, it can be found in contaminated areas as well. The Dark Rash is even more harmful and dangerous than the regular Rash, as its body is covered in dust that has damning effects.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

4.desc: A group of spirits that live in Minar Forest. Unlike their rugged appearance, their personality is rather bubbly and cheerful. They have the ability to out-jump a human by about 1.5 times, which allows them to distract the adventurers by bouncing around. Although they are said to have different colored eye on each side, it is hard to tell by their tiny pupils. \r\nThey cannot carry a tune even if their lives depended on it, so when you hear Hankie screaming, you will undergo a temporary stun status.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: A dwarf spirit that lives in Minar Forest. It has an ugly face but even an uglier personality, so you must be cautious when approaching this monster. It steals from people, but cannot figure out how or for what the belongings are used. It is always in raggedy clothes, and an unconfirmed rumor has it that Hobi was banished from the town after committing a crime that turned this monster into a useless, heinous creature. Once a Halflinger, the Hobis are not particularly fond of the Halflingers.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A dwarf spirit that lives in Minar Forest. As the lead warrior of the Hobis, the Green Hobi is in a more fashionable attire, though not by much. Although it displays battle prowess, handling objects isn't a forte for this monster, much like a regular Hobi. The Halflingers despise this monster, for it likes to attack their town and steal whatever it can get its hands on.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: A bird-like monster with a long tail. It has a ravishing blue tail and a lovely voice that complements its beauty; however, it seduces people in order to lower their Accuracy, putting them in danger.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: A bird-like monster with a long tail. It has a ravishing reddish tail and a lovely voice that complements its beauty; \r\nhowever, it seduces people in order to lower their Accuracy, putting them in danger.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: A monster that has big coiled horns which closely resemble those of a sheep. However, it has a black tail and a small pair of black wings, though no one has seen it fly. While it chews on grass and remains carefree, it becomes furious when attacked, persistently chasing after the enemy. Although it looks like a mammal, some speculate that it is a species of its own.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: A monster that resembles a sheep with huge horns. Contrary to its physical appearance, it has a pair of small reddish wings and a reddish tail. Some claim that it is of the same family as Lucida for said reasons, but such claim has not been confirmed. Something about this monster makes one question whether it really is just an animal monster.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: What was once a sheep has evolved into this devil-like monster. Its burning horns and wings give it a chilling aura. Given that the Azmoth Chasm has opened nearby, there is speculation that it's long been influenced by Tynerum.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: An evil monster of the dragon family that lives in Manon Forest. It is considered a high-ranking dragon, boasting various magic skills as well as high level of intelligence. Its physical strength also contributes to the challenge for adventurers battling against this monster, as it is covered by a firm outer layer and has a breath that can melt even the toughest metals. It can also fly using its small wings. \r\nThe Manons had an amicable relationship with the Halflingers, but for an unknown reason, they have become hostile towards one another.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: A strange race of creatures that live in Griffey Forest. They have a body of a unicorn, eagle's wings, and the tail of a lion. They rival the strength of the dignified dragons, and they have set their nests in Leafre, which is considered to be the land of the dragons. As a race of high intelligence level and respect, the Griffeys, according to a legend, are said to be loyal to heroes.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: A spirit that has the torso of a human and the lower body of a horse. It wears a helmet that has horns sticking out on each side, resembling a Trojan warrior on a horse. It belongs to a group of warriors that have fought against each other for a long time just to prove their strength. It possesses the power of fire attribute and fears attacks of coldness attribute. The Black Kentaurus has the force of darkness, which explains its fear of attacks of sanctity attribute.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: A spirit that has the torso of a human and the lower body of a horse. It wears a helmet adorned with a red plume, resembling a Trojan warrior on a horse. It belongs to a group of warriors that have fought against each other for a long time just to prove their strength. It possesses the power of fire attribute and fears attacks of coldness attribute. It has the force of fire, which explains its fear of attacks of ice attribute.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

16.desc: A spirit that has the torso of a human and the lower body of a horse. It wears a helmet adorned with a blue plume, resembling a Trojan warrior on a horse. It belongs to a group of warriors that have fought against each other for a long time just to prove their strength. It possesses the power of fire attribute and fears attacks of coldness attribute. It has the force of ice, which explains its fear of attacks of fire attribute.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

17.desc: A dragon monster that can be found in the Dragon Forest. While it belongs to the family of dragons, it falls under the category of lower ranking dragons despite its hard shell that render this monster formidable. It is quick to bow down to anyone of superior power, which explains its role as the loyal servant to Horntail. It is a monster of ice attribute; hence, it is vulnerable to attacks of fire attribute. \r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

18.desc: A dragon monster that can be found in the Dragon Forest. While it belongs to the family of dragons, it falls under the category of lower ranking dragons despite its hard shell that render this monster formidable. It is quick to bow down to anyone of superior power, which explains its role as the loyal servant to Horntail. It is a monster of fire attribute; hence, it is vulnerable to attacks of ice attribute. \r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

19.desc: A ferocious dragon that lives in the Dragon Canyon. It is of the middle rank in the family of dragons, and its notable traits include high intelligence level and useful limbs that can freely move. With its threatening horn and soft skin, as well as long legs, this monster is physically strong; however, its flexibility and adaptability in using human tools to attack is one of the unique characteristics that render this monster a formidable enemy to defeat. It is considered the warriors of Cornians.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

20.desc: An evil dragon that lives in the Dragon Canyon. It is of the middle rank in the family of dragons, and its notable traits include high intelligence level and useful limbs that can freely move. \r\nWith its threatening horn and soft skin, as well as long legs, this monster is physically strong; however, its flexibility and adaptability in using human tools to attack is one of the unique characteristics that render this monster a formidable enemy to defeat. People claim that Green Cornians resemble humans the most.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

21.desc: A dragon monster that can be found in the Dragon Forest. It is considered one of the stronger dragons, but has relatively low intelligence; hence, it is controlled by an unidentifiable creature that hides inside the egg, which many people have suspected to be Horntail. Compared to its well-developed hind legs, its front legs are pitifully weak.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

22.desc: A dragon monster that can be found in the Dragon Forest. It is considered one of the stronger dragons, but has relatively low intelligence; hence, it is controlled by an unidentifiable creature that hides inside the egg, which many people have suspected to be Horntail. \r\nIt has frightening horns and is more ferocious than Rexton.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

23.desc: A ferocious dragon that lives in the Dragon Canyon. It has a huge pair of reddish wings but no front legs. It builds its nest in between the valleys and is known to be intelligence. Fast and strong, it flaps its long wings to create swirling gusts. Look in its mouth when it unhinges its jaw, and one would witness the origins of hell itself, just before being burned to a crisp by its flames.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

24.desc: A ferocious dragon that lives in the Dragon Canyon. It has a huge pair of blue wings but no front legs. It builds its nest in between the valleys and is known to be intelligence. Fast and strong, it flaps its long wings to create swirling gusts. It can emit freezing breath from its mouth.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

25.desc: A ferocious, evil dragon that lives in the Dragon Canyon. It has a huge pair of black wings but no front legs. \r\nIt builds its nest in between the valleys and is known to be intelligence. Fast and strong, it flaps its long wings to create swirling gusts. The blasts from its mouth are said to deliver the power of damnation itself.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

26.desc: A group of young dragons that live in the nest. Ever since their amicable relationship with the Halflingers came to an end, they have been left unattended without the protection that Halflingers once supplied. The Jr. Newties cannot leave their nests, but they have the power to attack using a sound wave at a distance. When the Jr. Newties are attacked, a messenger of the nest that protect the Jr. Newties appears.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

27.desc: A golem that guards the nest of a dragon. It has made a deal with the evil dragons to guard their eggs. This monster carries around the nest on top of its head to protect the Jr. Newtie.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

28.desc: A group of skeletons that belong to the dragon family. Skelegons can be found roaming around the dragon nests, unaware that they have died and have become Undeads. They are the reincarnation of dead dragons who were killed during the Dragon War, and will attack anything that comes near regardless of whether the approaching enemy is a human, a dragon, or any other forms of life.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

29.desc: A group of skeletons that belong to the dragon family. The Skelegons can be found roaming around the dragon nests, unaware that they have died and have become Undeads. \r\nThey are the reincarnation of dead dragons who were killed during the Dragon War, and will attack anything that comes near regardless of whether the approaching enemy is a human, a dragon, or any other forms of life. Looking at the cane that they hold in one hand, they are suspected to have been a group of old veteran dragons.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

30.desc: Master of the Dragon Canyon, the Leviathan is the loyal servant of the Horntail. Born from a glowing silver egg, it has grown to become the protector and ruler of the Wyverns in the Canyon. Leviathan attacks adventurers that approach the Cave of Life while silently hovering over the canyon skies, flying around with its silky smooth skin and wings. It is a much-feared creature in the canyon.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

31.desc:
The first dragon that's ever stood up against the dragon chief, Nine Spirit, who was the former ruler over Minar. Horntail assembled an army of evil dragons to create an evil force that instigated the Dragon War. Horntail's forces seemed to be more powerful at the beginning, but Nine Spirit's longstanding experience and wisdom as a leader seemed to overpower Horntail's inexperience. 
In the end, Horntail broke the Pact between the dragons and Halflingers and attacked the Halflingers' village, stealing the egg of Nine Spirit which they were protecting. This was a crime that no dragon known as the guardian of order should have committed. 
Ultimately, Horntail overthrew the reign of Nine Spirit, and the forest was conquered by the demonic servants of Horntail. Since then, no traces of true, honorable dragons could be found in the forest. Horntail, who has three heads and, subsequently, three different minds, is currently hiding in a cave to heal his wounds, and plotting to rule the regions even past Leafre using the egg of Nine Spirit.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc: The chief of Leafre. Judging by his long beard and his friendship with Grendel the Really Old, the great sage of Ellinia, he has weathered many, many years. He strives to maintain balance between the Halflingers and dragons, to preserve peace in the village. And, I found this rather amusing, Tatamo's long beard can easily be repurposed as a rope to climb up and down.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: A weapon technician in Leafre. He appears to be short of work these days. His primary tool of choice is a wooden hammer. In his hands, its impact is stronger that even that of a steel hammer.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: The armor seller of Leafre. It would be safe to assume that he is related to Mos, but nobody has ever thought to ask. He seems quite proud of his impressive beard and hopes to grow one like Tatamo's someday.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: The pet food merchant of Leafre. He also serves as a caretaker himself. Brown cats are not normally found in the forests of Leafre, but Moodie adopted his cat when it lost its owner to an evil dragon.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: The storage keeper of Leafre. He uses eggshells he foraged as storage containers. He himself is unsure what kind of eggs they could be. \r\nAs for all of the snorting and other mannerisms... I can only theorize. Perhaps he has a cold? \r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc:
A Halflinger guarding an egg that is about to hatch in Leafre. 
The young Halflingers of Leafre are each trying their own methods to hatch dragon eggs, and Kumo has chosen to maintain the proper temperature using heated lava stones. 
Perhaps because Raul the Knight once saved him from monsters, he's very friendly toward humans.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A young Halflinger who wants to play music for the eggs. She is singing, but stops shyly if you get too close. \r\nIn addition to singing, she is quite handy. She can play several instruments, make herbal ointments, and many other things.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: A Halflinger hugging an egg tightly to keep it warm. Using lava stones like Kumo might be more effective, but Ito says he wants to hold the egg himself. \r\nGiven his small size, it hardly seems sufficient, but the gesture is heartwarming nonetheless.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc:
A Halflinger diligently polishing an egg in preparation for the baby dragon's birth. 
I couldn't help but wonder if there was any point to the polishing, seeing as the egg was destined to break upon the dragon's hatching regardless. However, seeing his earnest scrubbing, I did keep myself from wondering this aloud. 
When not cleaning the egg, he spends his time decorating the nest. He has a strong interest in interior design.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: The general goods merchant of Leafre. While he sells a variety of the standard items, the most popular is Leafre's specialty, Baby Dragon Food. Originally meant for baby dragons, it also gives humans a brief surge of strength when consumed. The dragon wings attached to the bottle are suspicious, but it does have the intended effect.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: A Halflinger who works as a guide at the entrance to Leafre Station. He looks just like his brother Tommie, but many are surprised to hear that he is the younger of the two. He offers some intriguing information about Corba.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: A Halflinger attendant who guides boarding at Leafre Station. He looks exactly like Mue, but is absolutely a different individual, so take care not to confuse them.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: A Halflinger who passes the time atop Leafre Station. This extraordinary, wizened Halflinger is unique and can even levitate with only the use of his beard. Above all, he is capable of casting a dragon transformation, a technique once thought lost to history. I inquired if his ability was associated to his time as a dragon tamer, but he was not forthcoming. Perhaps his hearing ability has simply diminished...\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: A Halflinger at the Minar Forest Crossroad. His older brother is Max, the armor seller in Leafre. He considered defense of utmost importance and was well known for admonishing those who handled their shield incorrectly.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc:
One of five, Harmonia is the former Warrior Job Advancement Priest, who live in seclusions in the Forest of the Priest. Judging by his ears, he is clearly an elf, but he remains tight-lipped about his origins and past. His ears tell of his elven origins, but his past remains shrouded in myster.
With the long lifespan of his kind, his achievements in the distant past must have been truly remarkable. All across Maple World, people tell tales and sing ballads of him, filled with respect and admiration.
I do believe Harmonia has relaxed slightly. Just the other day, I asked #e'How have you been?'#n and I was rather shocked when he responded. There may even have been a slight smile upon his lips.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc:
The former Magician Job Advancement Priest. A blue orb floats above her head, following her everywhere she goes. Gritto will shut down entirely or ignore anyone who questions her on it.
Even amongst legends, Gritto is considered a league apart. Some even say, 'Much of the modern system of magical studies was organized through Gritto.' While the veracity of that statement cannot be proven, her silence only seems to fuel such the fire.
Once, Gritto and I were discussing the weather. She gave a faint smile and replied, 'Not even a magician can control the whims of weather.' That was the closest she had ever felt to a normal human to me.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

16.desc: One amongst five, Legor is the Bowman Job Advancement Priest. Some ponder whether he even has eyes beneath his blindfold, but it matters not. For whenever Legor looses an arrow, all of Maple World knows it will hit its mark.\r\nThe swiftness of elves gave rise to legendary hunting tales, and even now, whispers of 'he who reached the pinnacle of archery' rustle through the forest. Legor himself, however, brushes off such praises without comment. At times, he can be seen carefully tending to a small potted plant instead of holding a bow. 'You can't live by shooting arrows alone.' That single remark seemed to suggest that even a priest needs their small comforts in life.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

17.desc:
A figure hidden in a dark cloak, with sharp, piercing eyes. Hellin is one among five Job Advancement Priests, the Thief. It's hard to see where his shadow ends and he begins.
He is known for his 'blade which slices shadows,' and nothing else is known about him. While rumors run rampant through Maple World, not a single detail of his past has ever been discovered.
Surprisingly, Hellin is said to be very fond of cats; although, he would deny it if asked directly. I simply cannot help but think that if he did not want the cats in the Forest of the Priest to circle him and yowl, he is not the type of man to allow it to happen.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

18.desc:
Embracing his sea-loving soul, the free-spirited Samuel is one of the five Job Advancement Priests. His rough silver hair, eyepatch, and light footsteps all add up to the perfect pirate. 
Samuel's long career on the sea is shrouded in mystery, but his name lies heavy on the tongue of every pirate who takes to the open waters. 
'Staying on land too long makes me restless,' he once told me, rather absentmindedly. Though he now resides in the Forest of the Priest, his gaze always seems fixed beyond, towards the horizon.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

19.desc: The fallen Dragon Squad Leader, found in Wyvern Canyon. He once saved Kumo, a resident of Leafre, from monsters. Later, it's thanks to Kumo's efforts that an adventurer finds him. \r\nRaul was originally a member of the Dragon Squad that aided the Nine Spirit in protecting the Minar Forest. However, when the evil dragon Horntail kidnapped the Nine Spirit's egg and threatened the peace of the forest, Raul stepped up to his role as squad leader and fought with everything he had. In the end, he suffered severe injuries and was brought down.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

20.desc: A brave human magician found in front of the Cave of Life, deep within Minar Forest. She was a member of the Dragon Squad, a secret organization formed between dragons and humans to aid Nine Spirit, the leader of the dragons. After losing her comrades to the evil dragon Horntail, she is now imprisoned in the dungeon of Keroben, the cave's gatekeeper.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

21.desc: Nix, a half-dragon, was exiled from the dragons' settlement and now lives alone in a remote area of Minar Forest. He seems to have taken the risk of settling between Manon's Forest and Griffey Forest, all in the name of pursuing his research. He conducts various studies related to dragons. He doesn't appear to be on good terms with Tatamo, the chief of Leafre. Despite appearances, he has a rather cantankerous side, so it's best not to enter his home without permission.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

42.regionDesc: South of Minar Forest, a stone colossus has risen from the dense forest beyond. Adventurous Halflingers have organized an expedition to investigate and are actively scouting the area.

0.desc: A mantis that lives west of the expedition site... but it's somehow far too large. While it doesn't present aggressively, it's rarely keen on letting travelers simply pass..\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: Unlike the original, this ferocious mantis is clearly raring for a fight. Its fierce glare paired with its sharp, spiky claws all serve to intimidate its prey. \r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc:
A violet mantis that inhabits the deepest forest west of the expedition site. Its color alone is unsettling, but its lack of pupils is downright frightening. 
Not only is it the fastest monster found near the expedition site, its claws are also equipped with poison.
 
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: Found to the east of the expedition site, this flower has flammable seeds that it ignites to launch fire attacks. \r\nIn other words, to experienced adventurers, it's a very convenient source of fuel.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: Found to the east of the expedition site, this purple flower has flammable seeds that it ignites to launch fire attacks. In this area, purple seems to be a symbol of strength.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: These hornets swarm together and flit about Colossus Road. Rather than stingers, they seemed to be armed with a deadly spearhead. I do wonder if they can still be classified as 'hornets.' \r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: These purple hornets swarm together and flit about Colossus Road. Their angry scowls suggest that diplomacy may not be a viable route with them. True to their name, they possess large poison glands and should not be taken lightly.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: These ferocious hornets swarm together and flit about Colossus Road. Living up to their name, they wear armor-like shells and have ornate spearheads attached to their rears. It really is QUITE clear, I believe, that the classification of these monsters should be reassigned from mere hornets.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: Corrupted Tree Spirit drifts aimlessly about the Stone Colossus Torso. \r\nThese once gentle spirits of the wild once lived hidden deep in the forest, untouched by human influence. However, the same dark influence affecting the Stone Colossus has corrupted them as well.                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: Corrupted Tree Spirit drifts aimlessly about the Stone Colossus Torso. \r\nThese once gentle spirits of the wild once lived hidden deep in the forest, untouched by human influence. However, the same dark influence affecting the Stone Colossus has corrupted them as well.                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: Polluted Rock Spirit drifts about inside the Stone Colossus. The same dark influence affecting the Stone Colossus has corrupted them as well. Ordinarily, Rock Spirits are said to be timid creatures that live hidden inside rocks.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: Corrupted Rock Spirit drifts about inside the Stone Colossus. The same dark influence affecting the Stone Colossus has corrupted them as well. Ordinarily, Rock Spirits are said to be timid creatures that live hidden inside rocks.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: A spider monster that attacked the Stone Colossus's heart. At a glance, it resembles the Big Spider from Verne Mine. But it's unfortunately much larger, and much stronger. Researchers are still unsure what the suspicious rock-like mechanism on its back is for.\r\nGuwaru was so drained from protecting the Stone Colossus' heart from Tarantulus' attacks that he had no strength left to fight off the darkness. It uses webs, as well as a variety of other skills, to attack intruders, so proceed with caution.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc: A general goods merchant at the Expedition Base who is always dozing off. While he hasn't said it outright, he seems to be Mumu's brother. I think.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: Lavi's assistant and an expedition member, she aims to become a legendary explorer someday. While her boundless curiosity does tend to land her in trouble, she simply loves to see and observe new things. There's absolutely no debate that she's this adorable ball of energy is an excellent addition to our expedition.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: The expedition leader in charge of the Halflinger expedition team. His dedication to his job and expeditions is something to be admired. Compared to the other Halflingers, who tend to remain in Leafre, he has quite the outdoorsy aura to him.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: A dashing Halflinger who races around on a mount, which was custom built by the expedition team. \r\nIt costs around 100 million Mesos for a single copy of his autograph, but no one has ordered one yet.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: Chino the Sniper takes her job seriously and is stationed to guard the platform for the expedition. Lately, the swarms of bees have been giving her quite a headache.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A general goods merchant working out of Chino's Station. Since few people come all the way here to shop, he's always dozing off. Still, he wakes up and gets his business done when he needs to, so I see no issue.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: A colossal lifeform born from the gathering of earth spirits. Countless small spirits are said to have accumulated over time to form this massive being. Its so large that, from a distance, it appears to simply be a rocky mountain. \r\nIts enormous size naturally incited fear, and people viewed it as a threat. However, this child of nature has a gentle and kind heart.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

43.regionDesc: A cursed region of Tynerum, another dimension that overlaps with the Maple World. A dangerous place where traces of the unholy experiments once conducted by demons still linger.

0.desc:
A veteran Bowman Explorer and former Job Instructor who was part of the advance party that traveled to Azmoth Chasm.
#s#The shock must have been severe, as she collapsed and is struggling with her speech. She claims that, in addition to their own group, she saw other beings roaming the chasm.#s#
She has since regained her usual confident demeanor. 
Together with Luvar and Ryndon, she guards the Azmoth Boundary, preventing those blinded by greed from entering the chasm. 
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
A veteran Magician Explorer and former Job Instructor who was part of the advance party that traveled to Azmoth Chasm.
#s#Of the three, he is in the best condition. While escaping, he made a snap decision and managed to seize a magic orb from a magical defense tower and return with it. Perhaps his training as a magician has better steeled him to endure whatever they faced.#s#
Together with Dahlia and Ryndon, he guards the Azmoth Boundary, preventing those blinded by greed from entering the chasm. 
Meanwhile, he's working hard to hone his magic skills and is determined to visit Tynerum someday. 
                                           - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc:
A veteran Thief Explorer and former Job Instructor who was part of the advance party that traveled to Azmoth Chasm. He is a veteran adventurer who is said to have once worked as a former Job Instructor. 
#s#The shock appears to have been severe, as he rambles incoherently and spout things that make little sense. He seems to be in urgent need of intensive treatment for post-traumatic stress. #s#
He seems to be doing better recently, as together with Dahlia and Luvar, he guards the Azmoth Boundary, preventing those blinded by greed from entering the chasm. 
Though, considering he still jumps at the slightest things, he clearly hasn't fully recovered yet. 
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

44.regionDesc: A magical kingdom located in the southern part of the Minar Forest. It vanished hundreds of years ago and has only recently been seen again. For some reason, its inhabitants are unaware of the passage of time.

0.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in its frozen blade is unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in these frozen dual blades are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this frozen war hammer are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this frozen bow are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this frozen magic staff are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this fiery blade are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in these fiery dual blades... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this fiery warhammer are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this fiery bow are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this fiery staff are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in its dark blade is unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in these dark dual blades are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                         - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in these dark war hammers are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                              - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this dark bow are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                  - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: The traces of consciousness lingering in this dark magic staff are unsettling... The rumors say that these monsters were once standard-issue weapons carried by the assault troops of the Kritias Kingdom.\r\n                                        - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: A low-ranking royal magician of Kritias who wanders Kingdom Road. They were members of the personal guard that once served King Hekaton, who was a powerful magician himself. Regardless of rank, royal magicians were nearly all graduates of the Ranheim Academy, proud elites of Kritias. How they ended up like this is unknown.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

16.desc: Mid-ranking royal magicians of Kritias who wander Kingdom Road. They were members of the personal guard that once served King Hekaton, who was a powerful magician himself. Regardless of rank, royal magicians were nearly all graduates of the Ranheim Academy, proud elites of Kritias. How they ended up like this is unknown.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

17.desc: High-ranking royal magicians of Kritias who wander Kingdom Road. They were members of the personal guard that once served King Hekaton, who was a powerful magician himself. Regardless of rank, royal magicians were nearly all graduates of the Ranheim Academy, proud elites of Kritias. How they ended up like this is unknown.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc: A researcher studying anti-magic stones in Kritias. Levian may look like an ordinary researcher, but she clearly knows more than she is letting on. There's more to her than meets the eye.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: A professor at Kritias Magic School. True to her stern appearance, she takes an evidence-based approach and analysis that leaves no room for nonsense. As a magician herself, she has a keen interest in the series of events that have unfolded in the kingdom as of late.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: This soldier stands his post guarding Kritias against the chaos. All the while, they're still trying to make sense of the situation themselves.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: A female student attending Kritias Magic School. Naturally calm by nature, Bianca never imagined her light weapon would ever see much action. However, her combat instincts awaken during the chaos of the occupation, and she finds herself jumping into battle. Her prowess on the fields makes her wonder if the military was her fated path all along.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A male student attending Kritias Magic School. His hometown being far away, he had nowhere to go when the school unexpectedly shut down. Prone to delusions of grandeur, Chen believes that his fervent wish that the 'school would disappear forever' combined with his awesome magical talent is what caused the current crisis. Perhaps it is best to leave him to his daydreams of being the 'Chosen One.'\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: A chef for the royal court. Plump and refined in temperament, he speaks in an avant-garde manner. Since coming to town, he has been struggling to procure the ingredients he needs.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A young and rigid knight tasked with protecting the princess. Since the princess is in hiding, he does his best to hide his identity with a large hood when they are out. However, it's caused some awkward misunderstandings that he's a dangerous stalker.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: Supposedly a bard from the royal palace, but one cannot help but feel that he is hiding much underneath his charismatic exterior. It's impossible to discern what he's thinking under his strange mask.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: An armor seller of Kritias. She sells armor in place of her father, the blacksmith Dostov, who is away guarding the western gate.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: A merchant who refuses to abandon the spirit of trade, even during Kritias' fall. The sack he always carries with him seems to be his entire fortune, which he somehow managed to pack and bring with him during the evacuation. I imagine this man would walk through hell as if it was a light summer day.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: A timid general goods merchant of Kritias. He has an unrequited crush on Nita, the weapon seller, and is always gazing over in her direction. Sometimes, it can be to the point that he forgets about his own customers. He even performs little magic tracks, like pulling hearts out of a hat, in hopes that Nita will notice. She hasn't yet, however.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: A diligent young servant boy who is very good at running errands... or so he seems, but he conducts himself rather suspiciously. He is usually friendly and polite but will lash out if anyone so much as touches his hood.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: An elegantly dressed young girl, who seems rather out of place. This is due to the fact that she is, in fact, not the princess, but a maid who acts as a substitute in the case of emergencies. Naturally shy and quiet, it's not easy for her to suddenly pretend to be a princess.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: A strict head maid. She says that a maid's duty is to protect the princess, but she's actually keeping her eye on the princess's substitute.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: The clerk who handles administrative paperwork at the Town Hall. He laments the closure of the university library, blaming it on his own incurable book addiction. No administrative matters in the kingdom gets processed without first going through him.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: A commander in charge of the defense of the eastern gate. What he lacks in experience, he makes up for in entitlement and elitism. He won't hesitate to crawl on the backs of others to reach the top, so it'd be best not to fall under his command.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

16.desc: A volunteer captain in charge of the defense of the western gate. Originally the village blacksmith, he now helps protect both his daughter and the town from their enemies. Nita, his daughter, works down at the market.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

17.desc: A general in charge of the defense of both the northern gate and the entirety of Kritias. He holds the Volunteer Captain in high regard and is himself a widely respected soldier.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

45.regionDesc: Many adventurers train in this village, located among the high mountain ranges and clouds of eastern Ossyria. With its clear bamboo forests and sky gardens, this place has long been a center of discipline for those who pursue the paths of martial arts.\r\nThose who train here learn to cast aside worldly worries and achieve peace of mind. Adventurers seeking a challenge can climb the Mu Lung Dojo to test themselves.

0.desc: A straw dummy that Do Gong made to help train those in Mu Lung who wished to become virtuous masters. Trainees should spend every waking moment practicing on the dummy to achieve mastery. \r\nNo one will claim responsibility for drawing on the dummy's face, but the most probable suspects are the students.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: A wooden dummy that Do Gong made to help train those in Mu Lung who wished to become virtuous masters. Compared to the straw dummy, it's sturdier and does not break easily. \r\nThe arrows protruding from its head and body are a testament to the hard work the trainees put in. Perhaps its a figment of my imagination, but it does seem to have a rather aggressive temperament, compared to its straw variant.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A type of chipmunk that can only be found in Sky Forest. Much smarter and stronger than the average chimpunk. \r\nIt likes to balance upon an acorn to move about, as this eventually makes the acorn easier to crack. This gentle rodent will do no harm, unless a hapless traveler happens to try to pet it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A type of porcupine that can only be found in Sky Forest. A group of porcupines traveling the underground of Maple World settled here, exponentially expanding their population and battling against the chipmunks over acorns.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A type of porcupine that can only be found in Sky Forest. Black Porkies share the same physical features as Red Porkies. \r\nHowever, they are stronger than the Red Porkies, which explains their notable contribution in the battle against the chipmunks. Calling them a family of warrior porcupines would not be an overstatement.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc:
A type of Necki that can only be found in Sky Forest. It is as big as a regular Necki, but has vibrant colors and no poison.
It wears a swim cap that is covered in flowers, but no one knows why the Blue Flower Serpent wears it in the forest.
Neckis cannot swim in water, but it is yet to be discovered whether these swim-cap-wearing Blue Flower Serpents are an exception.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A type of bear that lives near Mu Lung. This bear's heartfelt desire to become a virtuous master is pure, and it devotes nearly all of its energy to training. \r\nWhile it diligently trains in its practice uniform, it sometimes fails to suppress its animalistic instinct and attacks passing travelers, becoming a problem in the area.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: A type of bear that lives near Mu Lung. This bear's heartfelt desire to become a virtuous master is pure, which is why it never takes off its training uniform! \r\nIt has features similar to those of humans, but no one knows whether that is because it is close to becoming a virtuous master or because that's just one of this monster's special traits.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: An apprentice of Mu Lung who had once trained to become a virtuous master, until it harmed a lot of people under the magic spell of the Priest Cat.\r\nIt has, since then, chosen the path of penance, although it still occasionally harms people due to the lingering spell. Its physique of a trainee and its magic render this monster a difficult enemy to defeat.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: A type of Necki that can only be found in Sky Forest. It is as big as a regular Necki, but has vibrant colors and no poison. The Red Flower Serpents like to travel with the Blue Flower Serpents.\r\nThe flowers on their head is known to have miraculous substance that can cure arthritis and MP shortages. The flowers are also used as medicinal herbs.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.desc: A monkey that feeds on peaches at the Peach Farm. Peach Monkeys have pink coat of fur due to the effects of their diet, but these monkeys rival, if not surpass, the intelligence level of humans. \r\nAt first, the Peach Monkeys helped spread the seeds to expand the Peach Farm, but because of the gradual growth of their population, they have actually begun to harm the farm.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

11.desc: A deer that feeds on peaches at the Peach Farm. Due to the effects of its diet, Reindeer boasts high intelligence which allows it the luxury to use powerful magic. \r\nThere is a rumor that a Reindeer's antler in perfect condition can enhance one's ascetical powers, but it's not easy to acquire an antler from a Reindeer without breaking it off.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

12.desc:
A precious document that reveals the principles of nature and universe written by an ascetic of the olden times.
The Book Ghost was brought to life by a mysterious force originating from the profound truth and the ascetic's magic embodied in the book.
Some say that becoming an adept in this book can grant one power and strength, but the Book Ghost will attack anyone who is not qualified to be its master.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

13.desc: A cat that somehow got its hands on a magic book and, having mastered the books' skills, claims to be a Sage Cat.\r\nBecause it did not go through the proper, extensive training of becoming a virtuous master, it is rather antagonistic and violent by nature. Beware of this catty monster, which has the tendency to scratch at enemies, as it now has access to powerful magic attacks.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

14.desc: A wicked monster that lives in the Goblin Forest. It was a cat before it secretly mastered the magic that Mu Lung's trainees were studying in order to become virtuous masters. \r\nIt considers Mu Lung's swordsmith, who instructs mental training, as its arch-nemesis. It dazzles the humans with its eloquence while riding a giant cloud, but remember that this Priest Cat is but a goblin inside.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

15.desc: A training dummy that is occasionally seen at the Advanced Training Center. It will only reveal itself to those whose potential to become a master it acknowledges.\r\nChallenge the Master Dummy to prove that you have honed your skills diligently and consistently. Defeating the Master Dummy will earn you a Proof of Training.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Summer

0.desc: Mu Lung's storage keeper.\r\nHe speaks with a distinctive dialect. His habit of wearing his glasses low on his nose is a trademark of his now.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: Mu Lung's weapon seller. He is the younger brother of the armor seller, Bidiwon.\r\nA highly capable merchant, he brings in and sells a wide variety of weapons from all across the continent of Ossyria.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: Mu Lung's armor seller. People often think he's in a bad mood because of his droopy eyes. He and his brother, Gong Gong the weapon seller, run a trading business importing foreign goods.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael
