3.desc: Mu Lung's pet food merchant. She keeps a white tiger as a pet, and her hobby is training it and performing tricks together. \r\nTheir most popular one is their plate-spinning act.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: This beautiful panda is passionate about skincare and takes her job as Mu Lung's dermatologist seriously. Noma, who works next door, can't seem to do anything to catch her eye, and he has certainly tried.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: Mu Lung's resident plastic surgeon. He runs a clinic that operates in a tent, and the '30% Discount' sign hanging precariously on top doesn't foster a lot of trust. Neither does his appearance, or lack thereof, as his entire face is covered with glasses and a mask. He is skilled at what he does, however.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: An assistant at Mu Lung Plastic Surgery. He trains diligently, but it seems he still has a long way to go before escaping the role of an assistant.\r\nHis dream is to open his own clinic someday. He has a secret crush on Naran, who runs the skincare shop next door.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
A self-proclaimed genius potion maker. He speaks in a distinctive dialect.
He often forgets things and becomes flustered, but his crafting skill is said to rank among the best in Mu Lung. He produces not only potions, but also various medicines and scrolls.
He is the top disciple of Tae Sang, a master of potion making. In his younger days, he is said to have learned a wide range of techniques outside Mu Lung.
Surprisingly, some say that he once studied abroad to learn alchemy, specifically. Though, I've never been so bold to approach him and direct ask #e'Have you ever studied alchemy?#n
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: This artist is never seen without a scroll and a brush in his hands. As Mu Lung's finest painter, it's said that he can restore anything depicted on a scroll.\r\nA long-time friend of Mr. Do, he often grumbles about Mr. Do's requests, but never says no to them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: Mu Lung's greatest pharmacist. Mr. Do's mentor, and the finest medicine maker on the continent. It's said that he can brew the Mastery Medicine, which brings one close to becoming a sage simply by drinking it.\r\nAccording to Mr. Do, he is rigid in temperament and refuses to accept any research outside of herbal studies. He is also the owner of the Peach Farm.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.desc: Mu Lung's general goods merchant. Tae Sang's disciple, she brews various medicines using herbs from Herb Town.\r\nUnlike Mr. Do, she has a meticulous personality, and it is said that she quietly cleans up after all his mistakes.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

11.desc: The owner of the Mu Lung Hair Salon. The faded scissors he always uses prove that Grandpa Luo has reached the level of a master craftsman.\r\nHowever, he's been receiving terrible reviews from the adventurers who have come to his salon. It turns out he hasn't been cutting human hair for very long, having previously only worked on pandas. He's recently stopped taking human customers altogether, claiming old age.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

12.desc: An assistant at the Mu Lung Hair Salon. Grandpa Luo's granddaughter, she effectively runs the salon.\r\nUnlike her grandfather, Lilishu is quite adept at cutting and styling human hair. She dreams of inheriting the salon when Grandpa Luo retires and one day expanding across the entire continent.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

13.desc: One of the masters of the Mu Lung Temple. He became a master after reaching the pinnacle of martial arts. Naturally, as a Mu Lung master, he has many disciples. \r\nHe values perseverance as a core virtue, and accepts anyone with the desire as a disciple. Very few have made it to the end of his grueling training regime.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

14.desc: One of the masters of the Mu Lung Temple. He became a master after reaching the pinnacle of martial arts. As Mu Lung's foremost scholar, he has many disciples.\r\nHe enjoys playing omok as a meditative practice. He seeks to guide those who aspire to become masters onto the proper path. He's identified King Sage Cat, who has been threatening Mu Lung, to be a troublesome nuisance.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

15.desc: He guards the Peach Tree outside Mu Lung, which is a full time job, as attackers often seek to steal the tree's famed mystical powers. However, nothing can bring down this determined guardian. It is entirely possible that Peach Monkeys are simply enjoying bothering Tae Soo.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

16.desc:
A disciple of Mu Gong who manages the Mu Lung Dojo.
While he does say that only the qualified can challenge Mu Gong on the dojo's top floor, it's common knowledge that it only costs 100 Bellflower Roots to convince him to open the back door.
Despite being Mu Gong's disciple, no one is sure how strong So Gong really is.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

17.desc: A panda who manages the Mu Lung Dojo alongside So Gong, and one of Mu Gong's disciples.\r\nUnlike the somewhat clumsy So Gong, he emphasizes the importance of hard work and encourages adventurers who challenge the dojo.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

18.desc:
The owner of the Mu Lung Dojo, and one of Mu Lung's Masters.
A martial arts master regarded as one of the finest, not only in Mu Lung, but across the continent of Ossyria.
He waits at the top of the Mu Lung Dojo to test the worthiness of those who pursue the title of Master.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

46.regionDesc: A town floating atop the lake of Mu Lung Garden. It is surrounded by vast herb gardens, where a wide variety of medicinal plants are cultivated. The gardens are divided into tiers of 10-year, 50-year, 80-year, and 100-year-old herb gardens, and as its name suggests, it's a paradise of countless herbs.\r\nThis place, where herb gathering and research are part of everyday life, is also a central hub for herbal scholars and alchemists.

0.desc: Once used to store medicinal herbs, this jar was brought to life when an unknown monster entered inside. No one has been able to determine more than that.\r\nCaptain Hwang of Herb Town has been working hard to defeat this monster, but he has yet to succeed. The Jar can be found in the field near Herb Town.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
A jar storing aged ginseng.
It was originally created to decoct the ginseng, but the supposedly sentient ginseng convinced the jar to skip town, after which the jar encountered a mysterious force that turned it into a monster.
Or so the rumors go.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A plant that closely resembles a ginseng. Although Bellflower Roots are generally considered inferior to ginseng medicinally, this Sr. Bellflower Root can be even more effective than ginseng at times.\r\nIt may look weak and weary, making you feel guilty about hunting this monster, but its uses as a medicinal herb are undeniable. Remember, it's only a Bellflower Root.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc:
A plant that closely resembles ginseng, although its medicinal effects are considerably less potent.
A group of Bellflower Roots keep encroaching on the ginseng field and absorbing all of the nutrients in the soil, which upsets Mr. Ku of the Herb Town..
The Bellflower Roots discovered Mr. Ku's ginseng field when they were looking for a new habitat, after the abduction of their prince, Wu Yang.
Since then, the Bellflower Roots have settled into the field quite comfortably, and Mr. Ku isn't likely to be rid of them anytime soon.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: This rare Bellflower Root grows exceptionally large.\r\nOne might wonder how potent its medicinal effects would be if it allowed to age for a long time, but that's unlikely to happen. It's as naturally ferocious as it is large, and so it inevitably meets an early end.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: This monster alligator lives in the swampy regions near the Herb Town. It enjoys the company of small plants and animals, so it is often seen carrying a little bird on its head and a baby Bellflower Root on its back.\r\nIt does not attack unless provoked. Do not provoke it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: An unknown figure who serves Lord Pirate. They have accompanied Lord Pirate on many lucrative journeys, but now they mainly pester the Bellflower Roots, under Lord Pirate's command.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc:
An unidentifiable monster who serves Lord Pirate.
It seems to be one rank above Kru, and contributes to the crew's plundering at sea.
When not doing so, it spends most of its energy pestering the Bellflower Roots, on Lord Pirate's orders.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc:
If you gather herbs in the 80-Year-Old Herb Garden, you might see this creature emerge from the water.
A hundred-year-old centipede, this enormous insect is capable of speaking human language.
Of course, a very large caterpillar is still a caterpillar, and it doesn't pose much of a challenge to seasoned adventurers. Ordinary herbalists, however, had best steer clear.
                                      - Chronicler Summer

9.desc:
You might encounter this warrior in the 60-Year-Old Herb Garden. Despite his appearance, he is quite cowardly, and always carries a mystical scroll to hide himself from stronger enemies.
When the Bamboo Warrior holds up the scroll, anything behind it becomes transparent, theoretically camouflaging him. However, since he is larger than the scroll itself, it doesn't seem particularly effective. 
If he spots an easy mark, he'll dramatically 'reveal' himself and attack.
                                      - Chronicler Summer

0.desc: An elderly man with a stern appearance who lives in Herb Town. He owns the herb garden.\r\nHe is especially close with Tae Sang of Mu Lung. He waters his garden carefully, and with herb thievery on the rise, he keeps a very sharp eye out.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: An old man who makes herb-storing jars. All of the jars you see around Herb Town are his work.\r\nLately, however, the jars have started wandering around. He's been worried about that.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: This crane can fly you to Mu Lung.\r\nAt some point, it seems to have realized that creatures without wings get tired of walking, and has monetized its own wings accordingly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc:
The captain of a trade ship, he helps export the town's ginseng for sale.
As his rugged appearance suggests, he once possessed considerable combat skills, though age seems to have slowed him down.
Still, should the town ever need protection from pirates, he stands ready to do his part.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: Herb Town's general goods merchant. As befits a town that cultivates ginseng, he sells tonics.\r\nHe extols the tonics' effectiveness, insisting that nothing is better for a weak body.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: Herb Town's weapons dealer. A young and spirited blacksmith.\r\nHe originally specialized in farming tools, but after a series of Pirate raids, he took to weaponsmithing instead. He takes great pride in the weapons he creates.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: Herb Town's armor seller. To help fend off pirates who raid the village for its herbs, he sells a limited selection of basic armor.\r\nHis name and appearance give me a strange sense of familiarity, as if I've seen him somewhere before, but I can't quite remember where.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: Herb Town's warehouse keeper, known for his distinctive way of speaking.\r\nThough he has a somewhat scatterbrained look, he is surprisingly famous for guarding entrusted items with absolute care.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: A loyal retainer and devoted servant of Wu Yang, King of the Bellflower Roots. He asks adventurers to rescue Wu Yang, who was kidnapped by Lord Pirate.\r\nThe Bellflower Root he carries on his back appears to be their prince, but this has not been confirmed.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

47.regionDesc: A temple where monks gather to practice. It is decorated with colorful tiles and golden ornaments, making it a popular tourist attraction. \r\nHowever, the deeper you go, the deeper the secrets...

0.desc: This ferocious monkey lives in the Forest of Training.\r\nSome speculate that Ravana the Demon's influence is what's driving its ferocity, but my experience is that it's always been this way.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: A ferocious Mama Monkey who lives in the Forest of Training.\r\nYou might think becoming a mother would have made her somewhat gentler, but no, not at all.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: This White Mama Monkey lives in the Forest of Training. Apparently, the baby on her shoulder just tattled to her.\r\nI'm not sure who exactly upset the baby, but for your sake, I hope it wasn't you.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: This White Baby Monkey lives in the Forest of Training.\r\nDo not be fooled by its gentle appearance. If you provoke it, it WILL call its mother on you.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc:
The leader of the White Monkeys, which are regarded as creatures that bring good fortune.
It resembles the White Mama Monkey, but does not carry a baby on its shoulder, and has thick fur around its neck like a lion's mane.
The fruit appears to be worn purely as decoration, suggesting a unique sense of style.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: A creature of the abandoned temple, who awakened alongside the demon Ravana. It guards the western side of the temple.\r\nAs servants of Ravana, such creatures must never be allowed to escape into the outside world.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A creature of the abandoned temple, who awakened alongside the demon Ravana. It guards the eastern side of the temple.\r\nAs servants of Ravana, such creatures must never be allowed to escape into the outside world.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: A creature of the abandoned temple, who awakened alongside the demon Ravana. It guards the lower western side of the temple.\r\nAs servants of Ravana, such creatures must never be allowed to escape into the outside world.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: A creature of the abandoned temple, who awakened alongside the demon Ravana. It guards the lower eastern side of the temple.\r\nAs servants of Ravana, such creatures must never be allowed to escape into the outside world.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: This creature awakened in the abandoned temple, alongside the demon Ravana. It guards the entrance to Ravana's altar.\r\nA vicious demon bearing the form of an elephant.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.desc: A demon said to have awakened after countless years. The Golden Temple was originally a barrier meant to seal Ravana, but over time it was forgotten, and as tourists came and went, the seal gradually weakened.\r\nHe is said to have appeared in a critically wounded state, after being driven into a corner by the Golden Temple monks' desperate resistance. His appearance was identical to the statue at the center of the abandoned temple.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc: A young monk of the Golden Temple. Due to recent events there, all the other monks have gone into the forest, leaving him alone.\r\nHe has asked you to find Somchai.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: A girl running a shop at the Golden Temple. Due to the recent incident at the temple, business has not been going well.\r\nAs befits a merchant at a tourist destination, she sells hot dogs, pizza, and the like, so be sure to give them a try if you visit.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: This Golden Temple monk ventured into the forest to search for his teacher, Master Loong.\r\nHe claims to have found his master's robe hem, only to have it snatched away by a monkey on the spot, much to the frustration of anyone watching.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A tour guide of the Golden Temple. With the temple declared a dangerous area, he must take the tourists back, but one of them has gone missing, putting his job at risk.\r\nHis professional dedication is impressive, as is his self-promotional skill.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: A local guide to the Golden Temple. While trying to bring back a missing tourist, she was attacked by SnowFro the Fruitnificent.\r\nShe responded as she seems to respond to all other problems, with prayer.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: Mr. Yoo and Tthaya have been desperately searching for this tourist. Completely at ease, she says she can't leave yet because she lost her camera.\r\nIt doesn't seem like her trip to the Golden Temple was all that enjoyable.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: He guards a restricted area of the Golden Temple.\r\nAlthough he appears dutiful, he's been known to bend the rules a bit, in a charming sort of way, and let visitors pass under the proper circumstances.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: Noi and Somchai's master, this senior monk is highly respected.\r\nWhen the demon Ravana awakened, he led the monks of the Golden Temple to the Abandoned Temple to put the demon back down.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: A general goods merchant with a familiar name. Despite rumors that the demon Ravana has awakened, he hauled a cart full of goods all the way here to do business.\r\nA friendly fellow, he might remark on how impressive it is that you made it so far. Truly an extraordinary individual.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: This Golden Temple monk is still young, but possesses remarkable inner strength.\r\nHe works desperately to prevent Ravana from escaping into the outside world.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

48.regionDesc: A town built around an oasis in the middle of the desert. With its Arabic-style architecture and desert atmosphere, it serves as a hub of trade, while behind the royal palace loom the shadows of wealth disparity and rebellion.\r\nBeneath red sands and a blazing sun, desert rabbits and cactus monsters roam. To the north, Sunset Road leads to Magatia, the city of alchemists.

0.desc: A type of cactus plant that lives only in the desert. This seedling is young enough that it still has its nappy.\r\nBefore you decide to hold this cute, waddling monster, remember that it IS a cactus, and as small as it is, its needles are still sharp.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: A cactus that lives only in the desert. As the two bumps on its head indicate, it's a full-grown Jr. Cactus. \r\nThis monster's apron indicates its preoccupation with chores and taking care of smaller Jr. Cacti, a role many of its species choose for themselves. You may come across a clothesline in between cacti, with clean laundry hanging.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: A cactus that lives only in the desert. As the two bumps on its head indicate, this Cactus is a full-grown Jr. Cactus. \r\nThis is one of the forms that a fully grown Jr. Cactus can take, although it still sometimes acts immature, and often ends up getting yelled at.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: A female Desert Rabbit found, as the name implies, in deserts. Has a characteristically small pair of ears and a round body. \r\nIts staple foods are the clovers and carrots that grow around oases. Because of that, these Desert Rabbits tend to be naturally good at finding food and water, even in the deepest wastelands. Desert nomads of old used to raise them as beloved pets.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A male Desert Rabbit found, as the name implies, in deserts. Has a characteristically small pair of ears and a round body. \r\nIts staple foods are the clovers and carrots that grow around oases. Because of that, these Desert Rabbits tend to be naturally good at finding food and water, even in the deepest wastelands. Desert nomads of old used to raise them as beloved pets.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: A type of Necki that lives only in the desert. Not only can it see across great distances, with its two huge eyes, \r\nbut the jingling bell around its neck can mislead and lure unlucky adventurers. That said, have no fear! This monster is not venomous.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: This type of lizard lives only in the desert. Although it always looks weary in the hot weather, it wears furry and raggedy earmuffs. \r\nIt does not have the presence or aura of a monster, and this becomes even more evident when it scurries around the desert looking fatigued.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: This type of lizard lives only in the desert. Why this monster wears a scarf around its neck in a blazing hot desert remains a mystery. \r\nRegardless, this monster can be found aimlessly scampering around due to the thin skin on its feet, which can easily incur a burn from the scorching sand if and when stationary.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: An ancient cactus with its actual age undetermined. Its surface looks dead and dry, but when it spots a person with water, it rushes straight at them \r\nOften found in desert sandstorms, which one would think would dry these cacti out faster.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: This type of meerkat lives only in the desert. It has the tendency to whip out its telescope whenever it hears a noise.\r\nAlthough it looks nothing like a cat, it drops Cat's Eyes, as if it is trying to prove its feline heritage. Not that its eyes actually look like those of a cat or anything.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: A type of eagle that lives only in the desert. Perhaps due to the sun's strong rays, its crown feathers have gaps, somewhat resembling a baldheaded old man.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: A type of mole that lives only in the desert. It hunts for food under the sand.\r\nIt has a good rapport with the Sand Dwarves, partly because it often gives them rides on its head.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: A type of scorpion that lives only in the desert. Although its tail has a poisonous stinger, the creature almost never uses it. \r\nRussellon, who lost an eye to this species of scorpion, is a very rare case.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: A desert-dwelling dwarf. It is obsessed with jewels. \r\nWherever it goes, it carries a large sack, in which it drags any Lidium it digs up in the sand.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: A dwarf who lives only in the desert. Looks just like the Desert Dwarf, only darker. \r\nInfamous for its ferocity, as well as its notable ability to discover jewels. It carries around the flames of desert, in a sense.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: A creature that lives only in the desert. It is composed of sand, and has a hobby of passing itself off as an oasis, then scaring whoever comes close. \r\nThat said, apparently the Desert Giants do actually transform into oases occasionally. Keep that in mind when you fight them, for the sake of the desert's ecology.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc:
She runs a skincare salon, which uses Ariant's intense sunlight to provide tanning services.
She has her own shop near the royal palace, and because Queen Areda, known for her greed, is a regular customer, she has a reputation for being somewhat arrogant.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.r

1.desc:
An enthusiastic designer who emphasizes the importance of one's hairstyle, even to the desert folk who wear veils and turbans. 
Beneath his turban hangs a cascade of curly hair, showcases his own sense of style. He also sports a long, impressive mustache.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: A plastic surgeon in Ariant who secretly performs cosmetic surgeries. \r\nHer main clients are Ariant's nobles and the queen. She is known for her love of money and prickly temperament. Judging by Areda's condition, she may not be as competent as she puts forth.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc:
A cultural scholar from another region. He wears safari-style clothing and a turban, and harbors the ambitious goal of learning about every culture in the world. 
It would be nice if he were more willing to get his own hands dirty, but disappointingly, he only ever commissions other people to do his research for him.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A girl working as an apprentice at Mazra's Hair Salon. She started the job to help support her struggling family, but she enjoys the work and has nimble hands, often creating impressive hairstyles. However, she still lacks confidence.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

5.desc:
A young man working as a resident under Vard. However, he's had few opportunities for hands-on training, which frustrates him. 
As a result, he sometimes performs risky cosmetic procedures for those who could not otherwise afford them.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A general goods merchant in Ariant. Instead of a camel, which one would expect in the desert, this extraordinary individual keeps a very thirsty elephant. In any case, the goods he sells are reliable, so there's no need to worry.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

7.desc: An armor seller in Ariant wearing a long veil. She charms her customers with pretty smiles, and claims to offer substantial discounts, but her prices are just about the same as anywhere else. Don't be swayed.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

8.desc:
An Ariant weapon seller with a fierce, shirtless appearance. His intimidating look doesn't seem to do much for business. 
With few customers visiting his shop, he has come outside to actively call out to passersby, but it seems to be having the opposite effect.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc:
A stern storage keeper, always tapping away at a calculator. 
He keeps his eyes closed at all times, which makes you wonder whether he's doing his job right. Fortunately, no one has reported any stolen goods so far.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc:
A guard at the palace gates. For some reason, he handles the palace security alone, and also seems to run personal errands for the queen. 
Judging by the fact that he sells Entry Passes to the Palace for money, he appears to be earning some pocket change on the side.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc:
A storyteller who was taken to the royal palace to entertain the sultan and the queen. She tells stories every day, but having run out of material, she wants to borrow books from Wiz the librarian.
Her dream is to escape from Areda, leave Ariant, and see the wider world. She also says she would love to meet Wiz, the librarian of Helios Tower, in person. 
When that day comes, I should ask her, #e'How have you been lately?'#n
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc:
This greedy queen claims to have once been a fairy from Orbis. Wearing heavy makeup, she lounges against cushions, lavishly adorned with all kinds of jewels. 
She purchases enormous quantities of gemstones with tax money and invests heavily in cosmetics, but it doesn't seem to do much to improve her beauty.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc:
An ineffectual sultan, known for indifference and lethargy. Some say he was once sharp-minded, but was cursed by his queen. 
Lounging on the sofa day in and day out, he often yawns, making it hard to hold a meaningful conversation.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc:
Muhammad the item maker is the only man Ariant trusts to forge swords.
His skill is unquestionable, but he's said to be as rigid and stubborn as his strongest metals.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: A member of the Sand Bandits, dressed in black and wearing a turban, standing on a rooftop with a bow slung on his back. He resists the tyrannical queen with all his heart, as do his fellow Sand Bandits.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

16.desc: Ariant's finest dancer, her graceful movements obscure her dangerous mysteries. \r\nIf you help her, you may uncover the truth about Ariant.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

17.desc: A heavyset member of the Sand Bandits, with a black mask over his face. He wields a mace in battle. Like his brethren, he opposes the queen with great fervor.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

18.desc: A member of the Sand Bandits, veiled in black clothing, often seen dramatically standing on a rooftop. Harbors a fervent, deep-seated hatred for the queen.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

19.desc: A young child from the village. He is the younger brother of Schegerazade, who was taken to the royal palace to tell stories to the sultan and the queen. He worries about his sister.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.\r\n

20.desc:
The leader of the Sand Bandits. He hides in a run-down, abandoned house filled with countless traps. Sejan is actually guarding Jano's hideout. 
He gathered the people of Ariant, who were enraged by the queen's atrocities, and formed the secret Sand Bandit organization to resist her. 
He hopes that one day, the queen will be driven out, and peace will return to Ariant. Unfortunately, that goal still seems far off.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

21.desc:
He works as a ticket agent at the Ariant Station, selling tickets bound for Orbis. He fumes that Karcasa is running an illegal business. 
However, judging by his appearance, he doesn't seem particularly likable either.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

22.desc: An Ariant crew member known to be somewhat hard of hearing. He helps passengers board the Lamp Genie bound for Orbis. \r\nOne would think a genie would have more efficient modes of transportation. Perhaps someone wished for the genie to remain a taxi forever.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

23.desc:
An exhausted child, resting in the desert. He doesn't dress like he comes from Ariant.
There's a vacant air about him, with a sense of mystery, as if he came from some distant star. Perhaps he came here because he needed a friend.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

24.desc:
A man who calls himself a member of the Sand Bandits. As his name suggests, his face practically screams 'villain,' easily marking him as a liar. 
There are rumors of petty criminals known as the Red Scorpions in the area, but his connection to them has not been confirmed.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

25.desc:
A shrewd businessman who trades all kinds of goods from the troupe tent. He even supplies silk to the queen of Ariant. 
He claims to offer a special route back to Victoria Island, but it sounds about as reliable as hitchhiking, with no telling where you might end up.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

27.desc: A camel taxi of the desert. It's unclear whether it has an owner, but it operates as a taxi on its own. \r\nFor just 1,500 Mesos, it carries passengers between Ariant and Magatia. To hire the camel, simply place the money into the pouch hanging from its neck.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

49.regionDesc: A city of souls slumbering under the dominion of the ancient magician Hilla. \r\nOnce the glorious home of a great magical civilization, it was destroyed by an unknown force. Now, all that's left is a ruin, haunted by ghosts and other restless spirits.

0.desc: One of Hilla's summoned minions. An ironclad hyena-like monster, brandishing a massive axe. Though it stands on two legs, it has no humanity, and exists to carry out Hilla's merciless orders. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: One of Hilla's summoned minions. Hilla created this skeletal spearman herself, using the souls of warriors from ancient Azwan. Individually, they are not very strong, but if you let your guard down, you may find yourself swarmed.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael\r\n

2.desc:
The head shamaness of the fallen nation of Azwan -- which fell because of her -- and one of the Black Mage's commanders.
In the past, she was renowned as the most gifted among Azwan's shamanesses. Loved by many for both her talent and beauty, Hilla believed that her beauty would last forever. 
But time was not on her side. Longing for eternal youth, Hilla ultimately sacrificed the souls of Azwan's people to refresh her youth, which led to her becoming a commander of the Black Mage.
Today, Hilla remains in hiding, supposedly planning to resurrect her master. 
                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc: A Cygnus Knight dispatched to investigate Azwan. True to his stern appearance, he will not tolerate disorder in the Storage Room.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: A Cygnus Knight dispatched to investigate Azwan. He seems troubled by the local grave robbers and their search for the supposed 'Elixir of Everlasting Youth.'\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: A Cygnus Knight dispatched to investigate Azwan. He is highly capable, managing to secure supplies even in the middle of the desert.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: The former Secretary of Foreign Affairs from the fallen nation of Azwan. By his own admission, Azwan was a very closed-off country. Did that make his job easier or harder?\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A traveling merchant left behind in the fallen land of Azwan as a ghost. It seems he met his death as his nation did, having been there at the moment of its destruction. \r\nThough he is always smiling, he laments his ghostly fate. \r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: The Prime Minister of the fallen nation of Azwan. He was King Iason's mentor, and blames himself for the king's foolish choices, as well as the stubbornness and arrogance that continued even after the king's death.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A shamaness of the fallen nation of Azwan. It's said she used to be one of Hilla's favorites. She was the first to notice and report Hilla's betrayal, but was unable to prevent the nation's destruction.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: The king of the fallen nation of Azwan. He doted on Hilla to the point of giving her the Shamaness Marble, which no one should have ever been entrusted to her. Ultimately, that brought about the nation's destruction. Even now, he shows no remorse or repentance for his grave mistake, the very image of a tyrant.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: The fallen nation of Azwan's Secretary of Domestic Affairs. All his gold, silver, and jewels hold no meaning in death, and he seems to have fallen into emptiness and lethargy.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

50.regionDesc: A desert town whose culture revolves around the study of alchemy. Two alchemist societies, Zenumist and Alcadno, are in conflict there.

0.desc: Old alchemist bachelors in Magatia, who devote their entire lives to research without setting any personal time aside, become this type of monster in the afterlife. \r\nThey are known to be irritable, and have a tendency to fling beakers at anyone they see.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: Magatian alchemists created this slime. Mainly composed of gelatin, it bounces around to show off its elasticity. \r\nAlthough some say this pink monster resembles a delicious strawberry jelly, that doesn't mean you ought to try eating it.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: An organism created by Magatia's alchemists. It uses a cylinder to move itself into attack position.\r\nAlthough it appears in the form of a plant, it does not display any graceful qualities that most plants embody. That said, it is dangerous, and could become more so if it grows any further.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: An organism created by Magatian alchemists. This monster, known as a Triple Rumo, has become exponentially more powerful than a single Rumo. \r\nConsidering that, it seems highly unlikely that the Rumo leaves are as rare and hard to find as people claim.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc:
A bizarre creature created by alchemists from the Zenumist Society through experimentation on Rumo. Its original leaves were completely dissolved by experimental solution, and the liquid itself became a living being. 
The two specimens always stick together, whispering to each other and frequently causing trouble. Eventually growing fed up, the Zenumists simply left this failed Rumo confined within the laboratory, unable to leave, and abandoned it there.
It's hard to call that a responsible decision, but at least they didn't take it out and dump it someplace else.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: A mechanical apparatus built by Magatian alchemists. \r\nIt is mainly composed of steel, and serves as the foundational structure of all the Alcadno alchemists' mechanical apparatuses. Building an Iron Mutae is the first step for all novice alchemists.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A mechanical apparatus built by Magatian alchemists. Alcadno alchemists would call this modified Iron Mutae a novice's project.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: This machinery, composed of mithril instead of steel, offers many functions. \r\nThe president of Alcadno, Maed, first discovered the process of manufacturing such things. Thanks to his experiments and research, many alchemists are now able to easily master the metalwork process.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: A form of Mithril, enhanced by mixing other metals. Through this special enhancement technique, its strength surpasses normal Mithril Mutae and rivals even Orihalcon.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: Neither mammal nor plant, this strange form of beaker-born life is muggy gray, perhaps because it was created with a mixture of chemicals. \r\nIt likes to roam around with a beaker over its head.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: Neither mammal nor plant, these strange life forms co-exist. Unlike other such pairings, such as that of a crocodile and plover bird, these two creatures are independent of each other. Researchers seemed to have paired these creatures up to study their partnership's development.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc:
A strange form of life created in a beaker, which has eventually become independently mobile. 
The project hoped to harness nature's power and create a soil-based life form, but an accidental drop of blood resulted in this mysterious, unidentifiable creature. 
While it began life as one creatures, it has now bifurcated into two.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: A robot built by Magatian alchemists. Don't let its size deceive you, as its tiny intricate components work together to boost its power greatly.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc:
A mechanical apparatus built to restrict trespassers from entering the 'lab affiliates only' area.
This robot, resembling a huge box, floats around the lab, scanning everyone in sight.
It will attack as soon as it detects an intruder. A console controls it remotely.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: A robot built by Magatian alchemists. Don't let its size deceive you, as its tiny intricate components work together to boost its power greatly.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc:
The 'D' in 'D. Roy' does not stand for Doctor, but rather a name given to the modified version of a pre-existing mechanical apparatus. Since building the Neo Huroid, the alchemists of Alcadno have built an improved Roid, with a self-charging feature. r

It is more independent, as the alchemists had wished, but now they seem to be struggling with a new problem; the D. Roy is hard to control, which makes its maintenance and repair that much more difficult.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc: A beautiful fairy with a pale face and long hair. She appears to have a very quiet personality, always with a hint of sadness on her face. Since her husband, Dr. De Lang, went missing, she has been seeking the truth about his disappearance.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: A banker handling financial transactions. As a member of the Alchemists' Association, he carries a large safe they custom made.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: An outsider to Magatia. A highly capable broker, he keeps his face hidden beneath a black hood, though the tattoos below it remain visible. \r\nJudging by his ability to procure almost anything for the right price, he is an exceptionally skilled broker.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: Phyllia's daughter, a cheerful young fairy. She is a half-nymph, half-human. She looks unhealthy, as she's suffering from an illness.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A robot made to closely resemble a human. Though it's clearly not human, its expressions are strikingly lifelike. \r\nWith wistful blue eyes and a gentle expression, it harbors feelings of affection for Keeny and Phyllia, even if it does not fully understand what feelings are.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: A Magatian general goods merchant. He sells potions you can't find anywhere else. \r\nThe only resident who belongs to neither society, he always wears a smile, but it's impossible to know what he is really thinking.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A Magatian craftsman with a penchant for perfectionism. Dealing with him may test your patience.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: An item maker of Magatia. He once taught others how to create Monster Crystals with his sharp craftsmanship. \r\nThough he stutters heavily when he speaks, if you speak with him yourself, you may end up wishing he would stutter more.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: A Magatian craftsman. After years of research, he is said to have mastered a new technique that relies solely on alchemy, without using forging skills. He is unquestionably a master, but he is very strict about his prices and fees.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: The head of the Zenumist Society. He believes that alchemy should be studied only within the bounds of natural law.\r\nHe appears to be a conscientious figure who refuses to cross the line, yet his attitude toward the missing alchemist gives off an unsettling sense that he knows more than he lets on.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc:
The head of the Alcadno Society. He carries a dark, free-spirited attitude and regards the rival Alchemists Association as narrow-minded and blind to the wider world. 
He believes that life alchemy is dangerous, but that the benefits gained from it outweigh the risks. 
Even so, he is concerned about some association members who have grown overly extreme. He may appear strict, but once you speak with him, you'll see he's not as closed-minded as he seems.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: An alchemist, formerly of the Zenumists and currently of the Alcadno Society. He researches life alchemy so as to treat illnesses and increase resistance to abnormal statuses. \r\nHe believes that the positive aspects of life alchemy should be considered over its harmful effects.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: A Zenumist Society alchemist, responsible for the production of magic stones. He is eager to uncover clues about the missing alchemist. He is on very bad terms with Alcadno.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: A ghost alchemist dressed like a researcher. Despite his solemn appearance, he has a somewhat frivolous personality. \r\nIt's said that he spent his entire life researching alchemy, then came back as a ghost just to do it more. Ironically, his greatest fear is other ghosts.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: A wandering alchemist who travels all across Maple World. Though he claims to be in training, his skills are already quite solid. \r\nIn the past, magicians often sought out wandering alchemists to create Magic Rock and Summoning Rocks. Possibly related, it's said that he was close with a Magatian alchemist named Dr. De Lang...\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc:
A young alchemist from the Zenumist Society. He is in love with Juliet of the Alcadno Society. 
Because they belong to opposing factions, their love cannot be fulfilled. For that reason, and for Juliet's sake, Romeo is working to resolve the conflict between Alcadno and the Zenumists. 
As he rarely gets to see Juliet, he always seems worried about her safety. 
                                      - Chronicler Ael

16.desc:
A young alchemist from the Alcadno Society. She is in love with Romeo of the Zenumist Society. 
Because they belong to opposing factions, their love cannot be fulfilled. For that reason, and for Romeo's sake, Juliet is working to resolve the conflict between Alcadno and the Zenumists.
She is always lost in sadness due to both societies refusing to understand their love.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

51.regionDesc: This mysterious temple, where worshippers gather to honor Rhinne, the Transcendent of Time, floats above the Minar Forest. The past, present, and future all converge here, and one can visit them through three special doors.

0.desc: A traveler lost this hourglass while traveling through the Path of Time.  It's cracked and doesn't work, but after spending so long in the temple, it seems to have gained the ability to awaken a mysterious being. \r\nWhen it meets a temple visitor, it follows them around, thinking they might be its owner. Because its power comes from the temple itself, it turns into a regular hourglass if you take it outside the temple.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: Within the Temple of Time, and beyond the Gate of the Past, the Memory Monks stand upon Memory Lane. They serve Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. They wear smiley masks, suggesting happy memories, but no one knows their true feelings.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: Within the Temple of Time, and beyond the Gate of the Past, the Memory Monks stand upon Memory Lane. They serve Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. They wear smiley masks, suggesting happy memories, but no one knows their true feelings.\r\nThey are a level above monk trainees, and often have a trainee following them on each side. Monk trainees have gray masks, not being skilled enough to wear the smiley masks.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: Within the Temple of Time, beyond the Gate of the Past, the chief of the Memory Guardians stands at Memory Lane. Its sole purpose is to protect Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. Compared to other guardians, its armor seems more sturdy, not to mention brilliantly decorated.\r\nIt was once a human knight, but throughout the many years of protecting the goddess inside the temple, it has shed its humanity. Now it only exists to serve the goddess. The only remnant of its former human life is its heart, which contains beautiful memories.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: Within the Temple of Time, beyond the Gate of the Past, the chief of the Memory Guardians stands at Memory Lane. Its sole purpose is to protect Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. Compared to other guardians, its armor seems more sturdy, not to mention brilliantly decorated.\r\nIt was once a human knight, but throughout the many years of protecting the goddess inside the temple, it has shed its humanity. Now it only exists to serve the goddess. The only remnant of its former human life is its heart, which contains beautiful memories.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc:
A very rare giant whale that only lives inside the Temple of Time. With its thick fins, it swims through air instead of the water, eating pieces of memory that float around. 
It is said that it only eats happy memories, so it's always in a good mood. It often gives the Temple Keeper a headache, because it even eats the memories of those visiting the Temple of Time, 
but because it's an endangered species, there's nothing they can do about it.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: Within the Temple of Time, beyond the Gate of the Past, the Qualm Monks stand at the Road of Regrets. They serve Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. To keep their own hearts clear of regrets, they wear special blank-faced masks, which suppress all emotions. That said, no one knows these monks' true feelings.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: Within the Temple of Time, beyond the Gate of the Past, the Qualm Monks stand at the Road of Regrets. They serve Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. To keep their own hearts clear of regrets, they wear special blank-faced masks, which suppress all emotions. That said, no one knows these monks' true feelings.\r\nThey are a level above monk trainees, and often have a trainee following them on each side. Monk trainees have gray masks, because they are not yet skilled enough to wear the neutral masks.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: Within the Temple of Time, beyond the Gate of the Past, the chief of the Qualm Guardians stands at the Road of Regrets.\r\nIts sole purpose is to protect Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. Compared to other guardians, its armor seems more sturdy, not to mention brilliantly decorated. It once was a human knight, but throughout the many years of protecting the goddess inside the temple, it has shed its humanity. Now it only exists to serve the goddess. The only evidence left of its lost humanity is its hardened heart, which contains all its bitter memories.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: Within the Temple of Time, beyond the Gate of the Past, the chief of the Qualm Guardians stands at the Road of Regrets.\r\nIts sole purpose is to protect Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. Compared to other guardians, its armor seems more sturdy, not to mention brilliantly decorated. It once was a human knight, but throughout the many years of protecting the goddess inside the temple, it has shed its humanity. Now it only exists to serve the goddess. The only evidence left of its lost humanity is its hardened heart, which contains all its bitter memories.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc:
They say he was a well known and respected human knight in the past. He couldn't find a lord he wanted to serve, so he decided to offer his services to Goddess Rhinne and live his life outside of the flow of time. 
As he was positioned to guard the Road of Regrets, he chiseled the regrets out of his own heart. He eventually lost his humanity and became the Ice Knight. 
He is known to be too strict and too serious, even attacking approved visitors, saying that they will disturb the Goddess' sleep. He doesn't get along with the Temple Keeper because of that.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: The Oblivion Monks stand, appropriately enough, upon the Road to Oblivion. They serve Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. Because they have lost all their memories of the past, they wear frowny masks. However, no one knows if the monks are even aware they have forgotten their past, nor if they experience sadness because of it.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: The Oblivion Monks stand, appropriately enough, at the Road to Oblivion. They serve Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. Because they have lost all of their memories of the past, they wear a frowny mask. Are they aware that they've forgotten their past? Do they feel sadness because of it? No one knows. \r\nThey are a level above monk trainees, and often have a trainee following them on each side. Monk trainees have gray masks, because they have not yet earned the right to wear the frowny mask.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: The chief of the Oblivion Guardians stands, as one might expect, upon the Road to Oblivion, beyond the Gate of the Past, inside the Temple of Time. \r\nIts sole purpose is to protect Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. Compared to other guardians, its armor seems more sturdy, not to mention brilliantly decorated. It once was a human knight, but throughout the many years of protecting the goddess inside the temple, it has lost its humanity bit by bit. Now it only exists to serve the goddess. All that remains of what it once was is a shriveled heart, an empty shell of lost memories.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: The chief of the Oblivion Guardians stands, as one might expect, upon the Road to Oblivion, beyond the Gate of the Past, inside the Temple of Time. \r\nIts sole purpose is to protect Rhinne, the Goddess of Time. Compared to other guardians, its armor seems more sturdy, not to mention brilliantly decorated. It once was a human knight, but throughout the many years of protecting the goddess inside the temple, it has lost its humanity bit by bit. Now it only exists to serve the goddess. All that remains of what it once was is a shriveled heart, an empty shell of lost memories.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: A prisoner of the Temple of Time, locked up there after committing a terrible atrocity. The crime itself warranted a much more severe punishment; however, Goddess Rhinne considred that Lyka was born evil and thus not fully responsible. \r\nSo instead, Rhinne decided to lock it up inside the Road to Oblivion so that the flame of oblivion could burn away its evil heart. However, even after all these years, Lyka's vile nature still remains, making the Temple Keeper tremble in constant fear.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

16.desc:
A mysterious man named Kirston used the Mirror of the Goddess to summon this monster. Well, he used it to summon A monster. He likely didn't intend to summon Pink Bean specifically. 
Cute as this little creature is, its power is beyond imagination. It is a very dangerous monster, and should be approached with caution. 
Among other amazing powers, it can revive a dead god. Its world of origin remains a mystery.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

17.desc:
A forgotten god revived by Pink Bean. While it may have been mighty in the distant past, it has now lost both its true power and its true name.
The statue slumbering in the Dusk Temple is not the god's true body either. In fact, the 'Ariel' that Pink Bean revived is only a temporary manifestation of divine power that once bore that name.
Despite not being fully restored, it wields powerful ancient magic, making it as dangerous as Pink Bean. 
The reason these ancient gods were forgotten remains unknown, and there is no guarantee that they will not awaken again in the future.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

18.desc:
A forgotten god revived by Pink Bean. While it may have been mighty in the distant past, it has now lost both its true power and its true name.
The statue slumbering in the Dusk Temple is not the god's true body either. In fact, the 'Solomon' that Pink Bean revived is only a temporary manifestation of divine power that once bore that name.
Wielding a massive spear and a spellbook, it uses lightning-based magic from a long-forgotten time. 
                                     - Chronicler Ael

19.desc:
A forgotten god revived by Pink Bean. While it may have been mighty in the distant past, it has now lost both its true power and its true name.
The statue slumbering in the Dusk Temple is not the god's true body either. In fact, the 'Rex' that Pink Bean revived is only a temporary manifestation of divine power that once bore that name.
Wielding a massive spear and a spellbook, it uses lightning-based magic from a long-forgotten time. 
                                      - Chronicler Ael

20.desc:
A forgotten god revived by Pink Bean. While it may have been mighty in the distant past, it has now lost both its true power and its true name.
The statue slumbering in the Dusk Temple is not the god's true body either. In fact, the 'Hugin' that Pink Bean revived is only a temporary manifestation of divine power that once bore that name.
A god in the form of an eagle, it uses a wide range of ancient magic, including summoning spells. Because Hugin's magic is fire-based, ice-based attacks may prove effective. 
Of course, if this were the god's true form, landing an effective blow would have been nearly impossible.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

21.desc:
A forgotten god revived by Pink Bean. While it may have been mighty in the distant past, it has now lost both its true power and its true name.
The statue slumbering in the Dusk Temple is not the god's true body either. In fact, the 'Munin' that Pink Bean revived is only a temporary manifestation of divine power that once bore that name.
A god in the form of an eagle, it uses a wide range of ancient magic, including summoning spells. Because Munin's magic is ice-based, fire-based attacks may prove effective. 
Of course, if this were the god's true form, landing an effective blow would have been nearly impossible.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

22.desc:
Arkarium was a highly capable high priest who once served at the Temple of Time. Though priests were meant to act as humble guides in service to Rhinne, accounts describe him as exceptionally dangerous, even in his youth as an apprentice priest.
One day, after witnessing a future in which Rhinne would be sealed by the Black Mage, Arkarium betrayed the goddess and joined the Black Mage as one of his commanders. From that moment on, he personally planned and carried out countless acts of evil.
A scholar of remarkable intellect and keen insight, Arkarium's ambition ultimately grew into a desire to stand above time itself. He sought to rule over time, and in doing so, went from a guardian of order to a force of destruction.
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc: An informant of the Cygnus Knights. When rumors spread that Empress Cygnus had been corrupted and was attacking Maple World, she was dispatched to the Temple of Time to uncover the truth. \r\nIt seems she traveled through the Gate to the Future, and is said to have narrowly escaped death on multiple occasions.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: The caretaker of the Temple of Time. He is responsible for managing the entire temple, and is said to be far older than his appearance suggests. The position of caretaker is passed down to a successor when it becomes vacant, and in principle, one is appointed from among the priests. \r\nAt present, he serves as the sole caretaker, with no suitable successor in sight, leaving him unsure how long he must continue in this role. On top of that, a number of incidents have been occurring lately, leaving him with little peace of mind.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: A Guardian of Time and the temple's general goods merchant. No matter how removed from the mortal world the temple may be, it still requires funds to operate, so she earns income by selling goods to visiting adventurers. \r\nShe has proposed selling Temple of Time specialty items, but the strict caretaker refuses to allow it.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A strange old man with his eyes covered, peering through a telescope held up to his beard. It's said that he has spent his entire life observing Erda. \r\nTrue to his name, he knows a great many things and offers valuable advice. However, he rarely involves himself in worldly affairs.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: A strange old man holding a quill with his beard, writing upon parchment that floats in midair. It's said that he records all of Maple World's history, forever. The only things he doesn't know are events that have yet to occur. \r\nHowever, he is bound by a restriction that forbids him from revealing history, as well as one that compels him to speak only the truth. As a result, any question posed to him is answered with nothing but riddles.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A sorcerer said to be capable of brewing any potion. While that claim may be true, he is notoriously obsessed with money. Put another way, if you have enough money to solve a problem, he is the perfect person to turn to. \r\nHe claims he hoards wealth for the sake of a special potion he ultimately wishes to create. What exactly is he trying to make?\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: A Temple Keeper who watches over the Forgotten Twilight. He stood there for so long that he eventually turned to stone. Even the current Temple Keeper seems to know nothing of him, nor does anyone in the Temple of Time recognize his existence. \r\nAs I write this, I feel as if I too might forget, or be forgotten. I should leave the Forgotten Twilight at once. Who was I writing about again?\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

52.regionDesc: A door that should have been kept tightly shut has been opened. In Maple World's not-too-distant future, Henesys has been devastated, its people exhausted from a seemingly never-ending war. \r\nWhat befell the world here?

0.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Henesys. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. It appears as a blue snail riding atop an enlarged red snail.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Henesys. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. Its once cute expression is gone, replaced by horns sprouting from its cap. \r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Henesys. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. It's difficult to determine which type of slime it originally was.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Henesys. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. As a result of that, it now walks on two legs.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: Tino, transformed under the influence of the Black Mage after Ereve fell to the ground. Arguably not as cute as it used to be.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: This specimen of Tiru has been transformed under the influence of the Black Mage, after Ereve fell to the ground. It has undergone rapid aging and now resembles a bald eagle, but with deep dark circles under its eyes. Its angry expression remains unchanged.\r\n                                        - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: This specimen of Tiguru has been transformed under the influence of the Black Mage, after Ereve fell to the ground. It has undergone rapid aging and now resembles a bald eagle, but with deep dark circles under its eyes. Its angry expression remains unchanged.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. The arrows embedded in its body are remnants of fallen Perion warriors.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. The arrows embedded in its body are remnants of fallen Perion warriors.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. The axe embedded in its body is an artifact from a fallen Perion warrior.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: This monster, Stumpy the Tree Monster, dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. Its size and strength have increased dramatically.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. As a result of that, it now walks on two legs.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. As a result of that, it now walks on two legs.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. As a result of that, it now walks on two legs.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. It has grown larger and lost all traces of its former cheerfulness.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: This monster dwells near the ruins of Future Twilight Perion. The Black Mage's influence has twisted both its form and demeanor. It has grown larger and lost all traces of its former cheerfulness.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

16.desc: This monster inhabits the area near the fallen Future Twilight Perion. Said to have been inspired by the sight of an Iron Hog.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

17.desc: A monster born from the restless spirit of a fallen Perion warrior. Formed from the black stone of Perion itself, it has lost all reason, leaving behind only the obsession to protect Perion. For that reason, it attacks anyone who approaches without. discrimination.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

18.desc: A monster born from the restless spirit of a fallen Perion warrior. Formed from the black stone of Perion itself, it has lost all reason, leaving behind only the obsession to protect Perion. For that reason, it attacks anyone who approaches without. discrimination.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

19.desc: A monster born from the restless spirit of a fallen Perion warrior. Formed from the black stone of Perion itself, it has lost all reason, leaving behind only the obsession to protect Perion. For that reason, it attacks anyone who approaches without. discrimination.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

20.desc: A spirit of light. Its essence provides power to the Cygnus Knights and the Dawn Warriors. These spirits once had another purpose here, but it's no longer known. Something clearly happened, but the truth has been lost.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

21.desc: A spirit of fire. Its essence provides power to the Cygnus Knights and the Blaze Wizards. These spirits once had another purpose here, but it's no longer known. Something clearly happened, but the truth has been lost.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

22.desc: A spirit of wind. Its essence provides power to the Cygnus Knights and the Wind Archers. These spirits once had another purpose here, but it's no longer known. Something clearly happened, but the truth has been lost.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

23.desc: A spirit of darkness. Its essence provides power to the Cygnus Knights and the Night Walkers. These spirits once had another purpose here, but it's no longer known. Something clearly happened, but the truth has been lost.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

24.desc: A spirit of lightning. Its essence provides power to the Cygnus Knights and the Thunder Breakers. There was once a clear reason these spirits were here, but it's no longer known. Something definitely happened, but the truth has been lost.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

25.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. They bear little resemblance to the Night Walkers of the present day.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

26.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. \r\nThey look nothing like the Blaze Wizards of the present day. Strangely, they are said to carry books about humor, though what that is meant to signify remains unclear.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

27.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. \r\nThey look nothing like the Thunder Breakers of the present day. A particularly vile group, they even stole a letter Stan had written for Alex.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

28.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. They look nothing like the Wind Archers of the present day.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

29.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. They bear little resemblance to the Dawn Warriors of the present day.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

30.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. They are dressed similarly to Eckhart, the Chief Knight of Darkness.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

31.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. They are dressed similarly to Oz, the Chief Knight of Fire.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

32.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. They are dressed similarly to Hawkeye, the Chief Knight of Lightning.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

33.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. They are dressed similarly to Irena, the Chief Knight of Wind.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

34.desc: The future Cygnus Knights who attacked Henesys alongside the Fallen Cygnus. Once Shinsoo's power, meant to protect the Empress, was warped into a force that robbed the knights of their will, they became a merciless force of destruction. They are dressed similarly to Mihile, the Chief Knight of Light.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

35.desc:
A fallen version of Cygnus from an alternate future world. Influenced by the Black Mage's power, she wields dark forces. Aside from the circlet on her head, she feels markedly different from the true Empress Cygnus.
After sending Ereve down to the ground, she waited in her garden for intruders who dared to oppose the Black Mage.
The idea of Empress Cygnus standing on the side of the Black Mage... It could never truly happen, but even imagining it is a terrifying thought.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc: The first person to greet you upon arriving at the Henesys Ruins. His oversized head remains the same, but he has clearly grown much older. Instead of scissors, he now carries a spear and shield. \r\nGiven the times, he took up weapons to lend his strength, but it seems he cannot deny his true calling. He is troubled by the sight of his own untrimmed hair, which he can no longer tend to.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: He lost his life alongside his wife, Mrs. Ming Ming, during the Cygnus Knights' invasion. Though a grave and statue were erected in his honor in the village, he himself became a ghost and has yet to leave Henesys. \r\nEven in death, he continues to worry about the village, and regrets not having spent more time with his son, Alex.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: In the barren Henesys Ruins, bereft of sustenance, she struggles tirelessly to feed the people however she can.\r\nShe is married to her childhood friend, Utah. When Utah finally returned home after a long time away, she immediately prepared a nourishing meal for him. Her devotion is truly commendable.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: The general goods merchant of Henesys Ruins. Where before she spent her days indoors, plagued by a persistent cough, she has finally stepped outside and taken a more active role. \r\nHowever, she still suffers from her cough and frequent headaches. There are rumors that her grandmother was an elf, but this has never been confirmed.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: The son of Chief Stan and Mrs. Ming Ming. He lost his parents during the Cygnus Knights' invasion. Believing that their deaths were the result of his own weakness, he became a Dark Master. \r\nAfter enduring many hardships, he has grown noticeably more somber and withdrawn. One can only hope he does not stray too far down the wrong path.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: Putting behind him the days of conflict with his father, he became the Chief of Henesys after Stan's death. As a chief in a time of war, he is not particularly warm or accommodating. \r\nA strong leader who actively works to turn the tide of battle while restoring the village. In his heart, he harbors many regrets about not having talked with his father more.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: As one would expect of an elf, she alone remains unchanged while everyone around her has grown old. \r\nHer reaction upon seeing the Dream Fragment was curious indeed. Is she really the same Athena Pierce as before?\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: Evan's older brother, who is Camila's husband.
