He's searching for the glass marble Camila gave him as a gift when they were young, which he somehow lost. \r\nHis dedication to this task paints him as a real romantic, though it would've saved him a great deal of trouble if he'd never misplaced something that important to him in the first place.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: The daughter of Dr. Betty of Ellinia. Growing up as an archer in Henesys, over the years, her personality become rougher--some might even venture to say abrasive. She wages her own guerrilla warfare campaign against the mutated creatures and the Cygnus Knights. \r\nShe and Jay fight side by side as comrades, driven by the same wish: to drive Cygnus and her knights out.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: The niece of Arturo, who once ran a general store. Given the circumstances, it is believed that Arturo has already perished. \r\nAmid forced labor bereft of all hope, she struggles desperately to provide meals for the villagers.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: This dog sells the potions Sophia makes. She took it in as a stray when Perion was invaded by the Black Mage, after the death of Arturo left her in despair. \r\nFor some reason, it still remains by Sophia's side, watching over her. It carries potions back and forth between Perion and the refuge to support the Perion's displaced people.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: Harry, once an armor seller of Perion. His body is worn down by hard labor, and his face etched with worry, as befits the harsh land of Perion. Though he gnashes his teeth at the sight of the Resistance who betrayed them, there is nothing he can do about it.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: A white-bearded man who once sold weapons in Perion. He shivers in the cold, too worn down to even dream anymore.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: A corrupted member of the Resistance. The moment he speaks of 'the great Black Mage,' anyone listening is bound to feel a chill. \r\nThe fact that he seems unable to clearly remember Edelstein offers some small comfort, as it suggests he's a fake who doesn't truly reflect the real person.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: The corrupted leader of the Resistance. It's said that when the Black Mage came to rule Maple World, this leader withdrew from the Alliance and sided with the Black Mage instead. He styles himself as a pioneer of a new age. \r\nApparently, he plans to turn Perion into a tourist destination. He has become a despicable figure, who casually mocks Perion as a village of foul-smelling brawlers.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: A descendant of Dances with Balrog. After the Resistance took control of Perion, the Hall of Warriors was shut down first, leaving him cast out onto the streets. Now, simply remaining alive feels like a disgrace to him.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

16.desc: Christopher, an explorer who once roamed Perion. He used to call himself a genius explorer. Now, in Twilight Perion, he carries a pack frame instead of an adventurer's bag, and toils in forced labor. The hardship has clearly taken its toll, and has aged him many years.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

17.desc: Once a formidable Perion warrior known as Stands with Bulls, he is now an elderly man suffering from a lung disease. As punishment for resisting until the very end, he was forced into hard labor in Twilight Perion. He has a granddaughter named Hard as Stone.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

18.desc: She has taken the weaker villagers of Perion, those unable to endure forced labor, and fled with them to a refuge. With great effort, they've tried to barricade the area, but the situation remains far from secure.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

19.desc: The granddaughter of Stands with Bulls. It seems he used to tell her stories about the great warriors of Perion every night before she fell asleep. She says she wants to hear how those stories end, but...is that truly what this child desires?\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

20.desc: Now elderly, he resides in the Tribal Refugee Camp. He loudly insists that he was once a renowned warrior, which leads others to wonder whether he's grown delusional in his old age. \r\nThe contrast between his boasts and his frail figure, leaning on a spear as if it were a cane, stirs in the hearts of many who meet him an unspoken sense of sadness.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

21.desc: He stands guard over a refuge without wooden barricades in the Spirit Zone. His tattered straw hat and thinning hair hint at the countless trials and brushes with death he has endured. \r\nHe is a true warrior who knows exactly what must be done when evil threatens to swallow the world.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

22.desc: An informant planted within the Cygnus Knights by Alex. A master of disguise, he blends in perfectly wish those around him. \r\nHis presence represents a bold gamble on the part of Alex; the first step toward turning the tide of the conflict within the Henesys Ruins.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

23.desc: Once, he served as the Cygnus Knights' tactician. However, in a future where Empress Cygnus was corrupted, he alone refused to side with evil and was thus imprisoned behind iron bars. \r\nNow so enervated that even standing presents a struggle, his appearance stands in stark contrast to the Neinheart of the present. Despite enduring humiliations beyond counting, his conviction to protect the peace of Maple World appears as unshakeable as ever.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

24.desc:
From Behind the Dream, he was aware that he himself was a resident of that dream. 
When asked how such a phenomenon came to be, he explained that it was the manifestation of unconscious thoughts flowing in from the outside. Could it be because one who regularly remembers reality, in so doing, trains their very soul? 
Whatever the reason, the fact that he is able to perceive the boundary between reality and dreams makes him one clearly warranting closer observation.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

25.desc:
Rina, who has somehow survived in Henesys Ruins.
Much-afflicted by the passage of years, she appears to be in poor health, coughing constantly even as she is sustained by the IV drip connected to her arm.
With no sources from which she might hear news from other towns, her thoughts and worries often turn to Ronnie in Sleepywood. Indeed, it bears wondering--what might Ronnie be like in this world?
                                          - Chronicler J.K.

53.regionDesc: An industrial city located in the northeast of Maple World. \r\nOriginally a prosperous city that utilized Rue Ore as a source of energy, in recent times the Black Wings have occupied the city, filling it with an atmosphere of oppression.

0.desc: Potted Sprouts that wander around Edelstein Park. It appears that, after tremendous effort, they have grown legs, gaining the ability to move about. Yet, in spite of their hard-won ambulatory capacity, they never leave Edelstein Park. It's unclear whether they're simply content having the ability to move. \r\nAlthough their thin legs may not appear impressive, they afford the Sprouts a surprisingly strong jump.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: Potted Morning Glories that wander around Edelstein Park. It appears that, after tremendous effort, they have grown legs, gaining the ability to move about. Like the Potted Sprouts, they never leave Edelstein Park, though the reason why remains unknown. \r\nCompared to the Potted Sprouts, their legs are thicker and sturdier, allowing them to quickly flee from those who try to pluck their blossoms. Indeed, I discovered this firsthand. Such a shame... I'm fond of the fragrance of morning glories, and I thought I might try using the fragrance as a spice.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: Discarded bottles of grape juice. There's a rumor they once dreamed of holding the most prestigious vintages, but after that dream was crushed, they became empty husks of their once-noble aspirations. \r\nSince those who have encountered them confirm that they have no scent at all, the rumor seems likely to be true. With so many monsters like these roaming the park, one can only imagine the vintner must have been an incredibly stubborn individual. At some point, one would think they would have simply given up, but look at all the bottles... Was this a case of too-grape expectations?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: Strange Signs found along the Edelstein Strolling Path. True to their name, they're very odd signpost, and are believed to have confused countless people in Edelstein. The way they simply stand there, with crossed arms and a crooked posture as though they've done nothing wrong, is anything but ordinary. \r\nIf they were truly without fault, then tell us, dear signs, who wrote those inaccurate directions? Who would go that far to mislead and inconvenience people?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: Snakes that appear in a corner of the Edelstein Strolling Path. With their plump bodies and glossy, well-kept scales, none would doubt them to be serpents of outstanding quality, each part possessing value. \r\nAs a result, they are often hunted to make leather bags or nutritious snake-steaks. Just why such specimens have a thriving population within Edelstein's urban zone remains unknown.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc:
The culprits behind the theft of water in Edelstein. Surl, in particular, is said to be plagued by these monsters. It has been suggested that they are using the stolen water to make something in secret. 
Some even believe that the water is a gift for a loved one, though who exactly these thieves love remains a mystery.
While quick and nimble, they have very little stamina, so once caught, the stolen water can easily be recovered. However, these creatures are quite crafty and are said to sometimes smash the bottles on the spot rather than let their stolen water be reclaimed.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: Monsters found along the Edelstein Strolling Path whose bellies are filled with dust and black bags. Perhaps because of that, they exhibit a deeply rooted fear of fire.\r\nSeemingly made up of trash people carelessly crammed into them, caution is advised when hunting these monsters. One wrong move could see an unfortunate adventurer plastered in old garbage. It does lead one to wonder why anyone would go through the trouble of hunting these creatures in the first place.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: Streetlight-esque monsters that appear along Edelstein Streetlight Row. While mankind devised streetlights as a means to help people navigate darkened paths, for reasons unknown some of them became monsters and now obstruct the same byways they were meant to guide people down. Fortunately, there are many who come to this area seeking replacement streetlight bulbs, so their numbers are regularly culled. \r\nI once spent several days observing these creatures, hoping I might make a meal of the Bluebird eggs that crown the poles, but people kept running through to collect more bulbs--everyone from Edelstein citizens to the Black Wings. After a while, I almost began to feel sorry for the poor things.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: Floating robots patrolling the Edelstein Strolling Path; one of several types of creature responsible for maintaining public order in Edelstein. The memory chips of the patrol robots that roam the city have been found to contain an astonishing variety of recorded video footage.\r\nAt this point, it feels uncomfortably close to illegal surveillance, but the Black Wings over there are glaring at me, so I'll leave it to our readers to employ their own critical faculties to the evidence. Actually...wait a minute, does that mean those things also recorded that time I took a three-hour "bathroom break" while I stuffed myself with grilled snake skewers and then took a big nap? Ack! U-unacceptable!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc:
The second type of monster that must be defeated as part of an Educational Program for Resistance recruits. Often used for drills intended to improve reflexes.
Due to their ability to turn invisible, it is extremely important to spot and attack them while they can be seen.
These barrel-shaped robots can be encountered in Training Room A, and walk with an admittedly comical gait.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc:
The second type of monster that must be defeated as part of an Educational Program for Resistance recruits. Often used for drills intended to strengthen attack power.
Because it possesses the ability to self-destruct, it must be defeated quickly before it explodes. Delivering powerful attacks within the brief 10-second window after spotting the monster is crucial.
It can be encountered in Training Room B. Essentially a walking bomb of a robot, its manner of walking is rather comical.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc:
The last type of monster that must be defeated as part of an Educational Program for Resistance recruits.
While not particularly strong, it's quite resilient and has a large pool of HP, requiring steady, persistent attacks.
It can be encountered in Training Room C. Even as a robot, its appearance is hard to describe, yet like some of the other constructs, it has a rather comical way of walking.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc: A monster that must be defeated during the Final Training Course after Resistance recruits complete the entire Educational Program curriculum. Only those with quick reflexes, strong attacks, and patience will be able to take one down.\r\nThey can be encountered in Training Room D. For some reason, they aren't called 'Training Robot D' but 'Training Robot 0'. Of the robots used for training, it's the only model capable of flight.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc: Floating robots that patrol beyond Edelstein and as far as Outside the Mine. Judging by their somewhat distinctive appearance, they appear to be enhanced versions of standard patrol robot.\r\nPatrol Robot S memory chips are said to contain an astonishing variety of recorded voices. It feels disturbingly close to illegal surveillance, but with the Black Wings occupying the area, nothing about anything going on is likely to be considered illegal.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc:
Monsters that issue safety warnings near the mines. Observers will notice one head and one body, but in truth, they are actually two creatures. Are they monsters? Miners? Two adventurers in the proverbial trenchcoat? It's unclear whose safety it is trying to protect.
There are rumors that due to their threatening behavior, Ulrika, who had run away from home, was startled and dropped her photograph.
For some reason, they carry Rue Batteries. Items related to Rue are known to sell for quite a high price, so there are some who regularly hunt Safety First just to obtain their Rue Batteries.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

15.desc: Baby Boulder Munchers that live around Rocky Road. Their name seems to come from the fact that they eat rocks, but who exactly came up with a name that's so oddly straightforward? Perhaps due to its youth, it can't break and eat larger or harder rocks.\r\nIf it stubbornly tries to eat a hard stone and can't manage it, it'll be in a gloomy mood all day. It really is such a cute little creature. I can't help but wonder whether they get tartar on their teeth too. The idea of a rock eater getting a buildup of stone plaque is oddly amusing.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

16.desc: Big Boulder Munchers that live around Ore Trail. Their name seems to come from the fact that they eat rocks, but who exactly came up with a name that's so oddly straightforward? Having grown stronger with age, their teeth are now powerful enough to easily crush even hard rocks.\r\nDo these creatures get some kind of mineral-tartar on their teeth too? The idea of a rock eater getting a buildup of stone plaque is oddly amusing. I've pondered whether Boulder Muncher teeth might make the perfect guitar picks, but decided against trying it, since it might ruin the strings.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

0.desc: A police officer serving the community of Edelstein. Her sense of responsibility to protect the citizens of Edelstein is second to none. However, she is extremely timid, especially when confronted with insects. Even a tiny ladybug can startle her so badly that she freezes up like a statue.\r\nJust one look at the silkworm pupa I was munching on caused her to go pale, demanding that I throw it away immediately. Does she even know how tasty those are? Being told to toss it away like it was some kind of gross, goopy bug felt like a bit of an overreaction...though ultimately, it IS an insect. In any case, while she may be prone to that specific fright, as long as there are no insects around, she's a dependable and trustworthy officer.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc:
The principal in Edelstein, known for his kind and gentle demeanor toward all. The fact that he welcomed me to Edelstein by giving me Rue Ore Chocolate serves as proof of his inherent goodness.
It is widely accepted as indisputable fact that no one who gives you food can be a bad person. He's a wonderful teacher who guides children down the right path, helping them grow into fine adults.
He also seems to hold special classes from time to time, and is an authority figure the people of Edelstein trust and follow. If you have any doubts, go pay him a visit and talk things over. At the time of writing this entry, I've just returned from a deep discussion with him on whether the milk or tea should be poured first when making milk tea.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc:
Edelstein's kindergarten teacher. Despite his bulky build and intimidating appearance, he has a gentle and delicate heart.
Although he's the kindergarten's sole teacher, the children don't seem to like him all that much. Then again, it's not as though they dislike him, either. By all accounts, he is a warm-hearted young man who genuinely loves the children.
He seems to have fallen for Leonore, a Black Wings Watchman, but whether she will accept Elex's feelings remains uncertain.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: A streetsweeper in Edelstein who's never seen without his smile. While he often makes offhand remarks, there's a sharp edge hidden in his words that makes them hard to ignore.\r\nPerhaps he's truly devoted to metropolitan cleanliness, because he seems to appear every time I eat a snack, watching me closely. Since I can't write unless I have something in my mouth, I've often caught Brighton standing behind me with his strange smile. Thankfully, he doesn't seem interested in the notes I'm taking in my journal, but I still find it rather unsettling.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc:
An ordinary kid from Edelstein. It seems her real name is different from the name she goes by here. She treasures the balloon given to her by Checky, the teddy bear mascot, and just looking at it seems to make her heart swell with joy.
I once had a lovely dream of riding a balloon to the top of a mountain made of cakes. Strawberries, chocolate, whipped cream--every kind of cake you could imagine was there. Even just writing about it makes me hungry. Perhaps I should go buy another snack.
This kid looks hungry too, so I'll buy her one as well. I don't have many Mesos left, but it should be fine. It's just a snack for a kid, after all...
                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: An ordinary kid from Edelstein. He seems smarter than his peers, but at the end of the day, he's still a kid. When I offered to take he and Cutie to a dessert shop, he shook his head, saying that it was dangerous to follow strangers. I asked if buying him a snack would make me not-a-stranger, and he immediately agreed to that.\r\nStill, buying two snacks does stretch my daily snack budget. I'll have to gather more Mesos by doing a bit of street performing or something. Is this finally the moment I'll live up to my name? It's time to show what I can really do.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc:
Edelstein's teddy bear--or rather, a part-time worker in a teddy bear costume. Despite taking on the responsibility of giving hopes and dreams to children, the person inside the suit seems rational and realistic.
When I observed him, I had this odd sense of familiarity, as though he may have worked part-time at Fantasy Theme World as well. Apparently, he's constantly pestered by people who want to see the face behind the bear head. When it comes to that sort of thing, bribing him with food works best, or so I've heard.
I can't help but wonder if I ought to see if it works. Be advised, though; good adventurer probably ought not follow my example.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: A boy from Edelstein with a striking silhouette. He likes balloons and tries to act cool, but he's still very much a kid, deep down.\r\nOn one occasion, he got upset after failing to get one of Checky's balloons and ran out of town in a huff. After that, he ended up crying his eyes out on the road when snakes showed up, yet even then he still tried to keep up a brave, cool facade. It's kind of cute, honestly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: An ordinary kid from Edelstein who loves to eat and always seems to be munching on something. I figured that since we had that in common, we were sure to get along well. \r\nHowever, it turns out the kid just likes sweets. His palette isn't developed enough to have well-rounded tastes yet. Then again, how much culinary discernment can one really expect from a child? Still, he crossed a line when I saw him sprinkle sugar over those tomato slices. Absolutely unforgivable!\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: The Council President of Edelstein. While the position originally belonged to Albert, it was forcibly handed over to Anthony after the Black Wings occupied Edelstein. Even the mansion was seized.\r\nThere are five things in this world one should never mess with. Another person's spouse, their car, their dog, their home, and of course their food. Taking someone's home is a truly unforgivable act, committed by truly despicable people. Rumors say the one responsible steals credit for other adventurers' achievements, embezzles funds, and even sells things like light bulbs to line his own pockets. As expected, my instincts were right on the money. You needn't look far: he's a Black Wing through and through.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: A mysterious gentleman accompanied by a dog named Coco. He stands between Anthony and Bavan, giving rise to suspicions that he may be affiliated with the Black Wings. While he does not seem particularly dangerous, his unreadable nature makes it difficult to let down one's guard around him.\r\n\r\Coco is incredibly ferocious; his barking is bad enough, but he's also constantly eyeing my emergency rations: a special pork sausage sourced from Utah's pig farm. I can see it in his eyes, plotting and scheming how to snatch it from me. As if I'd let my prized meat be snatched away by some dog! What kind of owner fails to keep their pet in check like that?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc:
A Black Wings Watchman who is always eating something. When I ask for even a single bite, he ignores me completely. That itself is evidence of his personal failings.
I overheard a story from an adventurer who was running an errand for Albert. Albert had been sending clothes and food to his daughter through Bavan, but apparently, this man pocketed all the money inside and got rid of everything else.
Perhaps I was too gentle, remarking on his personal failings. He's a fiendish devil of whom demons might say, "At least I'm not like THAT!" You just don't mess with someone's food.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc:
The former council president of Edelstein. Records indicate he stepped down from his position after the Black Wings took control of the city.
I've heard he has a daughter, but she's nowhere to be seen. Judging by the worry etched on his face, it seems she may have left home. According to a passing adventurer, she was taken prisoner by the Black Wings. How could this be? Not satisfied with taking homes, they resort to separating families as well? 
Wherever one goes, a fundamental truth is that one must eat. But with the Black Wings having demonstrated such a capacity for cruelty, would they even feed her properly? I find myself worried for her safety as well.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc:
A timid child from Edelstein, holding his dog tightly in his arms.
Jun has a younger brother named Von who, unlike him, seems to be fearless. The two brothers couldn't be more different. Jun waits for Von, who ran away from home saying he was going to save someone.
He seems to have headed toward the mines, but with so many monsters in the area, I do hope he'll be all right.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc:
A bold child from Edelstein, and a self-proclaimed neighborhood boss. I was told I ought to show some goodwill if I didn't want to get on her bad side, so I tried winning her over with an offering of snacks.
Thanks to that, I earned Ulrika's trust. She says Doctor Claudine is her older sister, and while the two resemble each other in some ways, in others they are exceptionally different.
Like any child her age, she's always getting into some sort of mischief here and there. Still...putting a snake in a Checky doll costume does sound rather amusing.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

15.desc:
A rather suspicious Black Wings Watchman. While he appears blunt and cold, he doesn't seem to be a heartless individual in truth. 
According to Ulrika, he's a traitor and should be avoided. But could the eyes of a traitor really show an expression so full of longing? It's clear to me from observing him that he yearns for something. 
He seems weighed down with a story he can't bring himself to tell. ...A sudden idea just came to mind, but I feel that to pry any deeper would be inappropriate.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

16.desc: Edelstein's storage keeper. He looks after the belongings of adventurers whose bags are filled to the brim, storing everything from weapons and armor to fresh fruit.\r\nThough his overly servile smile makes him seem somewhat untrustworthy, there have been no major incidents reported so far. While he once charged storage fees, these days, it's difficult to tell how he makes ends meet.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

17.desc: Edelstein's hairstylist. Those who wish for a new look can visit him to change their hairstyle. He takes great pride in his work and is said to be constantly developing new perm techniques.\r\nAt one point, he spent a large sum to bring in Firebombs, but they were all wiped out after Bavan mistakenly believed they were making explosives and put out a request to eliminate them. I heard he demanded compensation for the loss, but whether he was ever repaid is anyone's guess.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

18.desc:
A short-tempered old man from Edelstein who once worked in the mines in his younger days.
Though he seems like little more than an odd and eccentric old man, for some reason, the Black Wings appear to be keeping a watchful eye on him. He also seems to be quite good at making money. Seeing so many goods changing hands, I can't help but wonder if taxes have something to do with it.
Huh... Why is Surl speaking with him...? I'm pretty sure he said he was going to take a nap when I spoke to him earlier.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

19.desc:
Edelstein's weapon and armor seller. Despite his fierce appearance, he is in truth quite kind. Perhaps because of his years collecting armaments, his knowledge of weapons is exceptionally deep.
Ever since the Black Wings took over the town, he has struggled to acquire quality weapons, leaving him with many worries. The oak barrel he sits on appears to be a bomb at first glance, but is actually just a replica.
From what I've heard, it's a fairly famous type of bomb in the munitions industry. It sounded like he acquired in the hopes of avoiding interference from the Black Wings.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

20.desc:
Edelstein's general goods merchant who can always be seen promoting his wares, megaphone in hand.
Surprisingly, he seems to sell the same items as general stores elsewhere, suggesting that the Black Wings do not meddle with stores of certain types. Or perhaps what I saw was after the inspection has been performed.
To be honest, I really want that megaphone. I think it would have an amazing effect if I could sing into it. But after already buying three snacks, I was out of pocket money, so I decided to give up on that dream...for now.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

21.desc:
Edelstein's dermatologist. The skin around her eyes is a different color, perhaps because she tans while wearing goggles. 
It may look like Mel Nomie provides the treatments herself, but in reality, a skincare specialist named Nami handles them instead.
She has teeth so strong they practically shine and claims the secret to putting a real glint in your smile is avoiding sweet foods, which seems sensible as far as dental advice goes.
                                       - Chronicler Harper

22.desc: The director of Edelstein Plastic Surgery, able to give clients the appearance they desire. It seems she used to perform the procedures herself, but these days, she brings in Plastic Roy instead.\r\nThat being the case, it does lead one to wonder why she even has an assistant, but I chose to overlook that, assuming there must be a reason. She's always staring at a mirror, though it's hard to tell whether she's looking at her own reflection or something she sees behind her in the glass.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

23.desc: An ordinary citizen of Edelstein. She deeply loves the city where she was born and raised, but says things haven't been the same since the Black Wings took over. She hopes that her hometown goes back to the way it used to be as soon as possible.\r\nPerhaps all the people of Edelstein feel the same way. I, too, find myself hoping the cruel Black Wings will pack up and leave sooner rather than later.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

24.desc:
A Black Wings Watchman who indulges in luxury and vanity. Like other watchman, her main duty is analyzing patrol robots.
Rumor has it she's being hounded by debt collectors due to money she borrowed to maintain her life of luxury.
Since joining the Black Wings, she's become untouchable by those same debt collectors, and one can make the sensible conclusion that it would be wise to avoid getting involved with her in matters of money.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

25.desc:
A doctor at the Edelstein Medical Center. Though she appears cold and composed, she's actually a warm and caring person, always concerned about the health and safety of Edelstein's citizens.
Perhaps because of her younger sister Ulrika, she shows a particular kindness toward children.
She seems to make frequent house calls, as the hospital is often left unattended.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

26.desc: A pilot at Edelstein Temporary Airport. Through Ace, you can travel to Victoria Island and Orbis.\r\nPerhaps because pilots frequently interact with the outside world, the Black Wings seem to keep a close eye on him. I heard that on one occasion, he accidentally threw a diamond ring out with the trash. If that's true, he may be more careless than he appears.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

27.desc: The instructor and leader of the Resistance, a secret organization formed to liberate Edelstein. Her role as a doctor was merely an identity she assumed as cover. Even with a mask concealing her eyes, her charisma and care for her fellow Resistance members remains unmistakable.\r\nSome people occasionally refer to her mask as a sleep aid, but under no circumstances should you say #e'Your sleep mask looks great.'#n within earshot of her.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

28.desc:
The Mechanic instructor of the Resistance, a secret organization formed to liberate Edelstein. His job as a teddy bear mascot was merely an identity assumed as cover, though he continues to wear the bear costume.
According to passing Resistance members, he still uses it as a disguise during missions. While the costume may be cute on the outside, the man inside it is said to be a cold, city-raised mechanic.
Though his demeanor is typically rational, he displays a curious tendency toward self-praise. Perhaps it's a cultivated part of his mysterious persona. Unlike the other four instructors, who appear to share close personal ties, he seems slightly out of place.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

29.desc:
The Wild Hunter instructor of the Resistance, a secret organization formed to liberate Edelstein. Her role as a police officer was merely an identity she assumed as cover--the timid officer persona is nowhere to be seen. She is in truth a bold and straightforward heroine through and through.
That said, the part about hating bugs was no act. She mistook the earthworm jelly I was eating for a real worm and panicked... Her slap was so fierce that my back still stings. Strength aside, the fact that she tamed and rides a ferocious jaguar into battle makes it clear that she's a highly skilled fighter.
Belle and the other Resistance members will often head out together somewhere on days when the weather is good. If you say #e'Nice weather today.'#n to her, she just might take you along.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

30.desc:
A black jaguar ridden by Belle. It's rumored that Belle tamed it through sheer strength, and the cat is said to possess the mysterious ability to tell when someone is lying.
Its sharp fangs and powerful claws provide a clear deterrent, warning others to stay away. Some claim to have heard it utter human speech, but as far as I've observed, it's done nothing but growl at me.
Surely it's not eyeing my special sausage too, right?
                                      - Chronicler Harper

31.desc: The Blaster instructor of the Resistance, a secret organization formed to liberate Edelstein. His role as a kindergarten teacher was merely an identity he assumed as cover. The sight of him wearing an Arm Cannon gives the man an imposing presence.\r\nStill, his delicate side seems unchanged from his time posing as a kindergarten teacher. I've spotted him collecting cute dolls, though he takes precautions to keep it from being known.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

32.desc:
The Battle Mage instructor of the Resistance, a secret organization formed to liberate Edelstein. His role as streetsweeper was merely an identity he assumed as cover.
Unlike his blithe streetsweeper persona, not a hint of a smile can be detected on his face. He claims to be a boring person, but when he's around his fellow instructors, he seems to joke around quite freely.
I heard a few rumors of some sort of relationship between he and Belle, but I wasn't able to dig up anything concrete. Honestly, the less it has to do with food, the less interested I am in chasing a lead.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

33.desc: The Basic Training Instructor of the Resistance, a secret organization formed to liberate Edelstein. He oversees Resistance training at the entrance to the Training Rooms.\r\nHis role as the headmaster was merely an identity he assumed as cover. Judging by his strong, dignified presence, he seems like someone who was quite renowned in his prime. Perhaps that's why the people of Edelstein continue to place their trust in him.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

34.desc:
The Treatment Specialist of the Resistance, a secret organization formed to liberate Edelstein. If you are injured, you can go to her for medical assistance.
As a city resident, she works as a plastic surgery assistant. 
She provides treatment free of charge to members of the Resistance and, upon further investigation, also appears to offer free treatment even to those who aren't part of the Resistance, claiming it's simply the duty of a medical professional. She's quite skilled with her hands, able to prepare medicines in no time at all.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

35.desc:
A Black Wings Watchman who values money above all else. He's rumored to have betrayed his hometown and joined the Black Wings purely for profit.
Though he's shown a willingness to do just about anything to scrape together more wealth, no one knows what he plans to do with it all. Between he and Anthony, one begins to wonder whether skimming off supplies is standard procedure among Black Wings Watchman.
Well, considering you can obtain a Black Wings hat from him, it's not entirely bad. Still, the whole thing leaves a bad taste in my mouth.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

36.desc: The administrator of the secret portal known as the 'Black Portal,' created for the Black Wings Boss. By using a Black Wings Token received from Harry Lion, one can ride the Black Portal to reach Six Path Crossway.\r\nHe looks like a rigid stickler for rules and principles, but is surprisingly soft-hearted and easily swayed by emotional appeals. I discovered that he absolutely detests Big Boulder Munchers, but when I tried to probe into why, I was enthusiastically beaten with a baton and had to beat a hasty retreat. For a small rabbit, he packs quite a punch.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

37.desc:
A kid plotting how he might get into the mine. He tried charging in head-on with a Rock Shield and failed.
Since the brute-force approach didn't work, he seems to have gone back to the drawing board to figure out another plan of action. It's fortunate that the gatekeeper giant at the mine entrance is a fool. Had it been a different member of the Black Wings, who knows what might have happened?
He might've been captured and used as a test subject, or something worse... It would be safer if he went home as soon as possible, but this kid seems stubborn to a fault.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

38.desc: A Black Wings gatekeeper stationed at the mine entrance. With such an enormous build, anyone who picks a fight recklessly isn't likely to walk away in one piece. And that one there... For a rabbit, he's impressively huge.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

54.regionDesc: A massive mine located on the outskirts of Edelstein. Occupied by the Black Wings, subordinates of the Black Mage, this mine is where they extract a mineral called 'Rue' and use its energy as part of their plan for the Black Mage's resurrection.

0.desc: Security robots that are deployed when the power plant's crime prevention system is tampered with. As emergency-use guard robots, they seem weaker than the base model, Guard Robot L. \r\nThese units are not normally active, and can only be encountered in the intruder search area that becomes accessible after triggering the power plant security's crime prevention system.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: Robots tasked with guarding the Edelstein Mine. Armed with a baton, they seem to be the most basic model of Edelstein's guard robot series.\r\nGuard robots are produced on demand by an automated system, so instead of performing repair work, damaged units are simply destroyed and replaced. It feels wasteful, but in a way, it does seem very in-keeping with the Black Wings' way of doing things.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: Raccoon monsters that live in the mine. Judging by their appearance, they are unmistakably raccoons of some sort, and I couldn't help but notice that their plump tails do look undeniably appetizing.\r\nSurl finds these creatures extremely annoying, mentioning that he always had a hard time dealing with them in his younger days, when he worked in the mines. Perhaps because they are among the most gentle raccoons, they are sometimes put to work as laborers.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: Raccoon monsters that live in the mine. Judging by their appearance, they are unmistakably raccoons of some sort, and I couldn't help but notice that their plump tails do look undeniably appetizing.\r\nUnlike the Racoco, they carry a rock instead of a shovel. The fact that they're able to do work in the mine using only stones suggests they possess considerable strength. That brawn seems to have come at the cost of their hair, though.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: Raccoon monsters that live in the mine. Judging by their appearance, they are unmistakably raccoons of some sort, and I couldn't help but notice that their plump tails do look undeniably appetizing.\r\nWith age, these monsters have learned to skillfully handle ore. Unfortunately for them, that wisdom has done nothing to help overcome their hair loss.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: Large spider monster that dwell in tunnels. They weave their webs wherever they please, causing no end of trouble for the miners.\r\nGetting one's feet tangled in the strands of their webs is a given, and their habit of piling up bedrock fragments serves to block straightforward progress into the mine The fuzzy hairs on their bodies and their antennae give them a look that calls to mind bees more than spiders.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: Teddy bear monsters that ride around in carts. I heard that Black Wing officers Chang and Wong enjoy eating their meat. Judging by their appearance, the meat from their well-developed arms looks like it would make an especially prime cut.\r\nThere have been many theories as to why they use carts to move around rather than simply using their legs, but the simplest explanation is that their lower bodies get stuck in the carts and they were unable to extricate themselves. The age at which this happens is apparently quite early, leading to them simply... rolling with it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: A robot assigned to guard the Edelstein Mine. As their name suggests, they are an upgraded version of the units seen at the entrance to the mine.\r\nWith larger, bulkier builds and the electric rackets they're equipped with, the threat they present is immediately clear even to the most clueless of onlookers. \r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: Androids found in the Android Research Lab. Most of the androids commonly encountered in Edelstein are the AF-type Android.\r\nIt seems they are easier to mass-produce, perhaps because they're a newer model than the DF Android. As a hostile construct, the AF Androids have a notably sharp and intimidating gaze. They don't hesitate to fire the gas gun they carry, so those intending to approach them should exercise caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc:
Androids found tucked away in a corner of the Android Research Lab. As their name suggests, they are a broken, failed model.
What remains of them seems to have been left uncovered in corners, awaiting disposal. Their loosely fastened screws appear ready to fall out at the slightest touch.
Their primary method of attack is firing electric rounds from their hands, so those vulnerable to shock should not approach them without taking the necessary precautions.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: Mechanical constructs found in the Gelimer Research Lab. They serve as laboratory security robots and appear to be powered by the ore mounted on their heads. For reasons unknown, they carry keycards that grant access to certain research labs.\r\nLike other guard robots, they are believed to be produced on-demand by an automated system.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc:
Mechanical constructs found in the Gelimer Research Lab, representing a more powerful version of the laboratory security robot.
They appear to be powered by the ore mounted on their heads and, just like the standard guard robots, are produced on-demand by an automated system.
Judging by the power capacity on their gauges, they seems capable of operating at a higher output level than standard security systems. 
                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc:
Monsters that appear deep within the mine, in the lowest tunnels. As their name suggests, their diet consists mainly of rocks and stone, and they are said to produce Rue Ore, which they cherish.
Rabbits that appear to be completely unhinged ride on their backs, mercilessly abusing them.
These monsters are also one of Gelimer's research targets. A strange rumor has also circulated that a photograph of an unidentified young girl was once found in the possession of one of these monsters.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

0.desc:
A secretary who works with the Black Wings. Her job is described as 'assisting the Black Wings' Boss,' which in reality boils down to handling a bunch of menial yet necessary tasks the boss couldn't be bothered to do.
Sources have indicated that the Black Wings offer good pay, so it's likely she took the job out of necessity. Given her unreadable personality, though, it's possible she has other motives.
At first glance, she seems kind, but there's something sharp and a bit intimidating about her personality. It feels like she's always one step ahead of me. When she smiles at me in that gentle way, it feels like she already knows something. Could it be? Did she find out I smuggled in Gusto's hot dog?
                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc:
A Black Wing in the form of a rabbit. He is tasked with keeping watch so that the captive Gabrielle can't escape.
He seems strict and rigid, a real stickler for rules and principles, so it would be best not to let your guard down around him.
Don't ever look down on him just because he's a rabbit or you may end up sorely regretting it.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: The daughter of Albert, the former Council President of Edelstein. Having being taken captive, she is now kept under the watch of Buck Teeth.\r\nHer lack of resistance might seem like resignation, but in truth, she remains compliant to protect the citizens of Edelstein from further harm.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc:
A Black Wing Boss. Unlike most of the other bosses, he appears to have plenty of free time. It's said that he can only display his true power when he combines with Chang.
Because of this, they are constantly training to combine, and as a result, the walls of the Baroq Room never survive intact. According to Chang, he doesn't talk much.
He appears to enjoy eating bear meat...but aren't they themselves pandas?
                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc:
A Black Wing Boss. Unlike most of the other bosses, he appears to have plenty of free time. It's said that he can only display his true power when he combines with Wong.
Because of this, they are constantly training to combine, and as a result, the walls of the Baroq Room never survive intact. He seems to sleep a lot, and is often seen dozing off. 
He appears to enjoy eating bear meat...but aren't they themselves pandas?
                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: An android guarding the Power Plant Security. As an AF Android, it appears to lack emotion.\r\nIt is said to have two younger siblings, if androids can be said to have such things. Not all AF Androids seem to be related, so perhaps they were produced on the same line. The criteria remain unclear.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc:
A Black Wings Watchman stationed inside the mine. He is tasked with keeping watch to prevent the researchers from escaping.
At first glance, it seems like an easy post, but from what I hear, quite a few researchers managed to escape in the early days. He dislikes robots and androids, referring to them as "mechanical dolls."
He finds it distasteful to treat emotionless androids like people, and has even had his patrol routes changed to avoid them.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: An AF Android stationed in First Square. One of Muscat-2000's two younger siblings. Being a newer model, it feels gentler and more natural than Muscat-2000, but an android is still an android.\r\nIt's said to operate by draining the energy of others and converting it into bio-energy, which is a bit scary. ...And no, that's not why I left the area! I just had some work to catch up on.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc:
A research intern who seems to have been captured along with the other researchers. He was originally studying Rue.
At the power plant, his job is to stop intruders. All the actual research is dne only on Second Square, so being stationed in First Square leaves him extremely bored. There are rumors that he enjoys strange games, which tend to leave afflicted with certain conditions.
Curses, weakness, and the like. Let me emphasize, I am not avoiding him out of fear. I just have chronicling to do.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: One of the researchers forcibly conscripted into the Black Wings' experiments. Perhaps because he is obsessed with his work, he doesn't seem to harbor much resentment or resistance.\r\nHe uses raccoons as test subjects. In response, the Raco are said to frequently steal his research notes. At this rate, the raccoons might end up staging a full-scale uprising...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc:
The lead researcher of the Verne Mine. He's also one of the scientists who was forcibly conscripted into the Black Wings' experiments, and one of the few genuinely decent people at the Gelimer Research Lab.
His research involved finding ways to generate energy using Rue, but after being warned that it posed a danger to the villagers, he seems to have been drawn into the Black Wings' research.
Though he harbors doubts, he continues to remain at the mine. It may be the case that he was promised something by the Black Wings, but there's no telling how things will turn out.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc: A scientist of the Black Wings. Cruel, mad, and utterly devoid of human compassion, he has created many atrocities, including the Black Wings' rabbit subordinates.\r\nHe shows no hesitation in extinguishing lives for the sake of his research, and once a subject has served its purpose, he discards it without mercy. Being discarded is the better outcome, as he often tears them apart and repurposes them for further experiments instead. From his heart to his gut, he's inhuman in every sense.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc:
An AF Android found in the Android Research Lab, she is the middle child between Muscat-2000 and the younger Zechtok-2000. Unlike the other two, she is a combat-type android.
While she is formidable, her efficiency is poor, so it's said she would be the first android Gelimer would dispose of if and when fuel becomes scarce.
She has been showing troubling behavior lately, as if she is nearing the end of her operational lifespan and knows it.
All three siblings have names that sound like drinks. I kind of like that.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc:
A ghost sighted in a corner of the mine. It's said to be blind, unable to see us at all.
According to rumors, there was once a miner who was forcibly taken by the Black Wings to collect Rue Ore. He was made to work day and night, without even proper meals.
Then one day, after a sudden earthquake sealed off one of the mine entrances, he disappeared without a trace. There are also rumors that he had a daughter, but I've had no luck in verifying that.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc:
A skeleton found deep within the mine, in a remote corner of a deep tunnel. Its identity is still unknown. It is said that no one has dared retrieve it, for fear of bringing bad luck upon themselves.
Judging by the safety helmet found alongside it, the remains likely belong to a miner. Unsettlingly, however, the skeleton is missing its lower jaw, and its upper teeth are severely damaged.
The upper teeth appear to have been worn down from biting something hard. It must have had a hard time eating anything...
                                      - Chronicler Harper

55.regionDesc: A wasteland beyond Verne Mine. It is a graveyard of machines, with mountains of abandoned technology. \r\nIt serves as a refuge for robots who've been marked for destruction.

0.desc: A modified DF Android with a red body. It wears a strange blindfold. As the name implies, the Modded Scaredroid fidgets constantly, and does not attack directly.\r\nAs its presence in the Scrapyard suggests, this one is also a failed model marked for disposal.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: A unit modified from a broken DF Android. It's unclear whether it was meant to be made useful somehow or if it was intended as a prototype for something else.\r\nAn antenna has been attached to its head, and it now wears a strange blindfold. Still a failed model, it continues to wander the Scrapyard.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: A red Chaseroid carrying a gun. Its glowing red eyes are quite intimidating. Because of that, although it is weaker than the blue unit, it feels like a more dangerous monster.\r\nIt travels together with the Hunterizer Red. They seem to communicate via the red antennae on their heads.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: A red Hunterizer. It travels together with the Chaseroid Red. They appear to communicate via the red antennae on their heads.\r\nIt has a reckless and aggressive nature, and it even packs a gun in its mouth, so unless you're confident in your strength, it's best not to approach.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: A blue Chaseroid carrying a gun. It's stronger than the red unit, but for some reason, this one feels slightly less threatening.\r\nIt travels together with the Hunterizer Blue. They appear to communicate via the blue antennae on their heads.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: A blue Hunterizer. It travels together with the Chaseroid Blue. They appear to communicate via the blue antennae on their heads.\r\nIt has a reckless and aggressive nature, and it even packs a gun in its mouth, so unless you're confident in your strength, it's best not to approach.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: This red bomb drone flies through Skyline, as well as both the interior and exterior of Black Heaven. It seems designed to track and attack any living thing it sees.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: This blue bomb flies through Skyline, as well as both the interior and exterior of Black Heaven. It seems designed to track and attack any living thing it sees.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: This yellow bomb drone flies through Skyline, as well as both the interior and exterior of Black Heaven. It seems designed to track and attack any living thing it sees.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: This green bomb drone flies through Skyline, as well as both the interior and exterior of Black Heaven. It seems designed to track and attack any living thing it sees.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: An android that fires missiles from a back-mounted launcher.\r\nJudging by its resemblance to the Chaseroid Red, it appears to be an upgraded model.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc: A transport vehicle used to carry modified androids. Currently, the androids it's carrying are all shut down.\r\nHowever, if the Deliverbot is destroyed, the androids inside will be forcibly activated. Be careful not to destroy it recklessly, or its cargo might come alive and hurt you.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc: A modified DF Android with a blue body. Like the other modified DF Androids, it's equipped with an antenna and a blindfold.\r\nTrue to its name, it has an arm-mounted laser cannon.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc: A Repairoid that helps maintain Black Heaven. Cosidering it can also be found in the Skyline, it doesn't seem to be limited to repairing Black Heaven alone.\r\nIts small size allows it to access even the tightest and most hard-to-reach areas.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc: Androids that hide inside the head of another, bigger android. When the Buffroid is defeated, the androids hidden inside burst out.\r\nLike the Deliverbot, these are variations on Modded Laseroids, Scaredroids, and Broken Androids.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

15.desc: An android that fires missiles from a back-mounted launcher. Judging by its resemblance to the Chaseroid Blue, it appears to be an upgraded model.\r\nIt delivers more powerful attacks than the Salvoroid Red, so proceed with caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

16.desc: A guard robot that monitors the exterior of Black Heaven. It appears to be a modified version of the guard robots from Verne Mine. Being designed for outdoor use, the siren light on its head is extra bright, and its alarm is extremely loud.\r\nIt uses electrical attacks, with remarkably long range, so be careful when approaching.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

17.desc: A massive heated icebreaker created by the Black Wings. Designed not only for breaking ice but also for combat, it boasts top-tier performance as a weapon.\r\nIts destructive power is said to be beyond imagination. That said, the Demolishizer's true strength varies greatly depending on the skill of its operator.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

18.desc: A Xenoroid made from relatively inexpensive scrap metal. Its appearance closely resembles that of a certain blue Xenoroid.\r\nJudging by its use of an energy sword, it seems to be either a mass-produced unit or a prototype.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

19.desc: A guard robot that monitors the interior of Black Heaven. It appears to be a modified version of the guard robots from Verne Mine. Being designed for indoor use, the siren light on its head is only moderately bright, and its alarm is relatively quiet.\r\nIt uses electrical attacks, and its range is remarkably long, so be careful when approaching.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

20.desc: A Xenoroid made from relatively inexpensive scrap metal. Its appearance closely resembles that of a certain pink Xenoroid.\r\nJudging by its use of a specialized mechanical scythe, it seems to be either a mass-produced unit or a prototype.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

21.desc: A Xenoroid made of steel. Its dark-toned body and glowing red eyes give off a deeply unsettling feeling.\r\nIts appearance, and use of a mechanical scythe, strongly resemble that of a certain pink Xenoroid.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

22.desc: A Xenoroid made of steel. Its dark-toned body and glowing red eyes give off a deeply unsettling feeling.\r\nIts appearance, and use of an energy sword, strongly resemble that of a certain blue Xenoroid.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

23.desc:
The only android to be found in Black Heaven's interior. True to its name, it is indeed enormous.
It's orders of magnitude stronger than the androids on the exterior, so be very cautious if you choose to face it 
Befitting its massive size, the red bulb set in its eye is overwhelmingly large.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

24.desc: A Xenoroid made from high-grade alloys. It's the most powerful Xenoroid in Black Heaven.\r\nIts appearance, and use of a mechanical scythe, closely resemble that of a certain pink Xenoroid.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

25.desc: A Xenoroid made from high-grade alloys. It's the most powerful Xenoroid in Black Heaven.\r\nIts appearance, and use of an energy sword, closely resemble that of a certain blue Xenoroid.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

26.desc:
One of the Black Mage's commanders. According to records, she was originally a Spirit of Darkness, but the White Mage gave her a human body.
Afterwards, she committed cruel acts throughout Maple World, and is even said to have assassinated Empress Aria, the former ruler.
However, her rampage did not last long. She ultimately met her end at the hands of the hero 'Phantom.'
It's said that Orchid, her twin sister and fellow commander, founded an organization called the Black Wings, and recruited Gelimer, in an attempt to revive her.
However, due to Gelimer's betrayal, Lotus became his puppet, leading to what is now known as the Black Heaven incident. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: A scout android found throughout Haven. It stands guard to protect the village from external threats.\r\nA telescope has been attached to its damaged eye, allowing it to observe distant areas. From what I hear, since these units are considered living beings, they seem to work in shifts.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

1.desc: An injured DF Android, with another DF Android tending to it.\r\nThey seem to be waiting patiently for the injured unit's replacement parts to arrive.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

2.desc: A blue DF Android holding a flower. It wants to smell the fragrance. Adding an olfactory sensor might be a good idea, but it's unclear whether it would be compatible with a DF Android's motherboard. \r\nIt's searching for a strange heart-shaped object, which can be obtained inside Black Heaven. If you happen to find one, be sure to bring it back.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

3.desc: A Storage Keeper robot in Haven. One-Eye must have come up with its name.\r\nBecause it holds red potions and blue potions, one might mistake it for a general goods merchant. Being a robot, it seems like it would take good care of anything entrusted to it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

4.desc: A pink android with three arms. It originally had four, but one broke.\r\nIt exchanges AbsoLab Coins for weapons. It's also in a loving relationship with fellow android One-Eye.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

5.desc: This DF Android appears to be waiting for parts to repair its damaged arm.\r\nFrom the look of things, it will take some time. Getting the parts does not seem to be going smoothly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

6.desc: This green DF Android's head antenna has been torn off, and it appears to be waiting for replacement parts.\r\nIts visual circuits also seem to be damaged, as it can't see very well. Peculiarly, this android appears to feel pain, as if it has a sense of touch.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

7.desc: A green DF Android playing with a dog. It's using a wrench as a tug toy.\r\nThe dog seems quite strong. It mentioned a young lady, who seems to have been the android's owner. How did it end up being marked for disposal?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

8.desc: The adopted daughter of One-Eye and Three-Hands. True to her name, she seems perpetually displeased. She also does not appear to get along well with the other androids.\r\nShe seems full of complaints, but she hasn't left Haven, so she must have SOME attachment to the place.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

9.desc: A blue DF Android playing a drum. It looks like a handmade instrument built from mechanical parts, probably a djembe.\r\nWho says androids have no souls? This one has soul to spare.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

10.desc: A green DF Android. It claps in admiration of Drumma's impressive drumming skills. I found myself clapping along too.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

11.desc: An ordinary green DF Android. The fact that it resides in the scrapyard means it's a failed model destined for disposal.\r\nIt seems to get along well with the other androids and live a peaceful existence, though.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

12.desc: A blue DF Android. It claps in admiration of Vocalroid's impressive singing. I joined in and clapped along too.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

13.desc: A singing DF Android. It wears a bouquet of flowers on its head.\r\nIts instrument appears to be broken, but it doesn't seem to mind, showing off remarkable singing skills even without any accompaniment.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

14.desc: This one-eyed android holds a position similar to that of Haven's village chief. It has a rather unusual sense for naming things.\r\nThis android is married to Three-Hands. Android or not they're an adorable couple, overflowing with affection and warmth.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

15.desc: A scout android found at the scrapyard. It can be seen at Scrapyard Hill, Skyline, and Black Heaven. One of its eyes is damaged, and a telescope appears to be attached in its place for long-range recon.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Harper

16.desc:
An android found at the scrapyard. Unlike the others, it has a somewhat dim-witted look about it. 
Part of its head has been torn away, leaving exposed wiring, which makes it easy to recognize.
I've heard that its story is quite sad.
                                      - Chronicler Harper

56.regionDesc: A mysterious island floating in the sky, and the home base of Empress Cygnus and her Knights. Long protected by a sacred aura, this island is where the Cygnus Knights gather, swearing their vows to safeguard the peace of Maple World. An air of elegance and nobility breezes over the entire island. Under the Empress's rule, the Knights devote themselves to training for the sake of peace. \r\nIt's said that all Knights born on this island are destined to fight against the forces of darkness.

0.desc: A small bird-like monster commonly found in Ereve's Training Forest. It's been modified for training purposes, so it isn't dangerous. \r\nIt's kind of cute that they're so tiny and still so grumpy. I hear some Knights smuggle out food for them or keep them as pets.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc: A small bird-like monster commonly found in Ereve's Training Forest. It's been modified for training purposes, so it isn't dangerous. \r\nIts feathers have not fully grown yet, leaving it covered in soft down. It flaps its wings as if practicing flight, but it still has a long way to go before it can actually fly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc: A small bird-like monster commonly found in Ereve's Training Forest. It's been modified for training purposes, so it isn't dangerous. \r\nAlthough it can't fly yet, its feathers have grown in well enough that it can leap quite far. Some knights get confused, but the things sticking up on its head are feathers, not ears.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc: A bird-like monster commonly found in Ereve's Training Forest. It's been modified for training purposes, and it's not dangerous. \r\nIt's grown quite a bit now, with a larger body and a properly formed beak. But it still looks as grumpy as ever.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: A small bird-like monster commonly found in Ereve's Training Forest. It's been modified for training purposes, so it isn't dangerous.\r\nNow fully grown, it wanders about with confidence. Its feathers grew so long they covered its eyes, so they've been tied back with a string.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

0.desc:
Her Majesty, who leads Maple World and stands at the heart of the Cygnus Knights. She is always kind, gentle, elegant, eloquent, and well, perfect really.
I once happened to greet her while she was out on a walk, and to my amazement, she called me by name. The fact that she even knows the name of an ordinary knight like me means she must have memorized the names of every single knight.
If I ever have the chance to meet her up close, I will be sure to express my #eloving devotion#n.
                                      - Chronicler Q

1.desc:
Shinsoo, the guardian of Ereve, the island of the Empress of Maple World, and protector of Her Majesty herself. 
Shinsoo astonished me the first time I saw her. She takes the form of a magnificent feathered beast. I once witnessed her take flight, and words cannot describe the awe I felt in that moment. 
May Shinsoo continue to protect Her Majesty forever.
                                      - Chronicler Q

2.desc:
The chief tactician of Her Majesty Cygnus, Empress of Maple World, and the leader of the Cygnus Knights. 
He's incredibly busy, handling everything from gathering info across Maple World to maintaining the Knights and keeping Ereve flying steady. Because of all that, a lot of Knights say it's hard to approach him, even when they need to report something. It probably doesn't help that he's known for his sharp tongue. 
But I don't mind. I finally have a chance to talk to him myself, and I'm not going to pass that up!
Still, just the thought of walking up to Neinheart makes me tremble a little...
                                      - Chronicler Q

3.desc:
Oz serves as the Chief Knight of Fire among the Cygnus Knights' five leaders. 
In everyday life, she is kind and adorable, but when she enters battle, she wields powerful fire magic. I once saw her completely scorch an entire hill during a monster extermination mission. 
She also seems to be on friendly terms with Chief Knight Irena.
                                      - Chronicler Q

4.desc: Hawkeye serves as the Chief Knight of Lightning among the Cygnus Knights' five leaders.\r\nAccording to a friend in the Thunder Breaker unit, he has a down-to-earth personality and treats the Thunder Breakers as friends. However, when he enters battle, he becomes a completely different person, sweeping away enemies with the power of the sea and lightning, earning everyone's respect.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

5.desc:
Irena serves as the Chief Knight of Wind among the Cygnus Knights' five leaders. 
She always leads her members with calm composure, showing a knightly demeanor that is cold toward enemies and kind toward allies. In a way, she can be called the spiritual pillar of us Wind Archers. 
After I took her advice and changed the way I held my bow, my accuracy improved significantly. She really is the best!
                                      - Chronicler Q

6.desc: Mihile serves as the Chief Knight of Light among the Cygnus Knights' five leaders. \r\nHe originally served as Her Majesty's personal guard, but these days, he seems to travel throughout Maple World more often. When he's away, the Dawn Warriors work hard to fill the gap in his absence.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

7.desc:
Eckhart serves as the Chief Knight of Darkness among the Cygnus Knights' five leaders. 
He often wears a mask, as his covert knights known as Night Walkers do. 
He seems difficult to approach, so I've never even heard his voice, but among the Chief Knights themselves, they appear to interact with one another quite casually and amicably.
                                      - Chronicler Q

8.desc: Kidan serves as a trainer of the Cygnus Knights. He is most often found in the Knights' Chamber. \r\nIn his younger days, he focused on martial training and strict physical discipline. These days, however, he focuses more on teaching proper conduct and mental discipline befitting a knight.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

9.desc: One of the Cygnus Knights' informants. I hear she mainly gathers information around Victoria Island, but recently, she seems to have been dispatched to other regions as well. \r\nShe appears to be even busier than the Knights themselves, which always makes me feel grateful.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

10.desc: The Cygnus Knights' Storage Keeper. He looks after the knights' personal belongings and unused weapons. \r\nHe's got a laid-back personality, to the point where he's always dozing in the sunlight of Ereve, but I hear he's never lost a single item.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

11.desc: A general goods merchant who helps out the Cygnus Knights. \r\nBecause the knights and soldiers use large amounts of potions during training, he's always busy trying to keep them on the shelves. But he's good at that. He's got a keen eye for business.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

12.desc: He sells weapons and armor for the Cygnus Knights. As befits, his station he is extremely strict about the care and upkeep of one's gear. \r\nIf you treat it carelessly and show up with a rusted shield or a dented helmet, he will scold you until you acquiesce. Stoic as he seems, he's quite passionate about that.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

13.desc: A crewman of the Cygnus Knights. He operates the ship that travels between Ereve and Orbis. \r\nWith his chatty personality, time flies while you're talking with him, and before you know it, you look around and you're in Orbis Station already.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

14.desc: A crewman of the Cygnus Knights. He operates the ship that travels between Ereve and Victoria Island. \r\nHe has a gregarious personality, and could tell you all about the towns of Victoria Island...if you had the time to listen to him. He talks really, really slowly.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

15.desc: Kiku serves as a trainer for the Cygnus Knights. He runs the courses in the Training Forest. \r\nWhen I first became a knight, Kiku was my trainer too. I still remember how he patiently trained me, step by step, when I rushed ahead, all too eager to become stronger.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

16.desc: Kiridu serves as the Cygnus Knights' mount trainer. He is stationed at the hatchery around the clock, always taking care of the birds. \r\nHis gentle disposition makes you feel at ease whenever you're around him. It's always nice for a knight to stop by the hatchery now and then to greet him and lend a hand.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Q

57.regionDesc: A tower rising from the seabed at the northernmost edge of Maple World. Alicia, the Transcendent of Life, created this space so that the beings of the Maple World could survive even the end of the world.

0.desc: This ancient slime inhabits the 1st Floor of the Tower of Oz. Though no longer seen in Maple World, it is said to have once flourished just as widely as Orange Mushrooms. \r\nCompared to the slimes found on Victoria Island, it is order of magnitude larger.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: This ancient slime inhabits the 1st Floor of the Tower of Oz. Though no longer seen in Maple World, it is said to have once flourished just as widely as Orange Mushrooms. \r\nCompared to the slimes found on Victoria Island, it is order of magnitude larger.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
An ancient King Slime that inhabits the 1st Floor of the Tower of Oz. Ancient slimes are already enormous, but as its title suggests, the Ancient King Slime is even larger. 
The massive flower attached to its head and bell suggests that it once lived outdoors, surrounded by nature. 
Like other slimes, it primarily attacks by jumping and slamming down. However, its immense size makes those slams harder, so stay cautious.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
A wolf-like monster found on the 2nd Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. Its entire body is covered in coarse fur, suited for enduring the cold.
When attacked, it uses magic to send a clone charging forward, so if it starts to growl, you should quickly move back. 
The fact that its appearance has remained nearly unchanged throughout the years suggests that the El Nath region has always been as cold as it is now.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
A wolf-like monster found on the 2nd Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in the present-day Maple World. Its entire body is covered in coarse fur to withstand the cold.
