The White Fang is harder to spot than the Hector due to its white fur, to say nothing of its greater attack power. Being far more accustomed to the cold, Ice-attribute attacks are not very effective against it. 
The fact that its appearance has remained nearly unchanged throughout the years suggests that the El Nath region has always been as cold as it is now.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: A turtle-shaped monster found on the 3rd Floor of the Tower of Oz. Its orange shell is quite distinctive. No longer seen in Maple World, it is believed to have once lived in the habitats near Brexton in the Minar Forest.\r\nAncient Turtles are extremely docile and are known for never attacking first, which makes the Minar Forest a surprising choice for their habitat. For reference, Alicia's Soul claims that the eggs they produce are truly delicious.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
A turtle-shaped monster found on the 3rd Floor of the Tower of Oz. Its bright blue shell is quite distinctive. No longer seen in Maple World, it is believed to have once lived in the habitats near Brexton in the Minar Forest.
Ancient Turtles are extremely docile and are known for never attacking first, which makes the Minar Forest a surprising choice for their habitat. For reference, Alicia's Soul claims that the eggs they produce are truly delicious.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
A reptilian monster found on the 4th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. 
There have been many theories, over the years, about this monster's origins, but according to the research of one brave scholar, it was determined to be a reptile rather than a cat.
However, its eyes do look feline, so much more research is clearly still needed. No definitive results have been reached so far.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc: Found on the 6th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. It's surprising that this species has existed unchanged for so long. \r\nAccording to the Ellinia Ecology Report, some ancient slimes eventually became ordinary slimes. It seems that some specimens may have adapted and changed rapidly depending on their environment.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc:
Found on the 6th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. It's surprising that this species has existed unchanged for so long.
It shares similar traits with the current King Slime, but I heard an interesting story from Alicia, the master of the tower. 
According to her, a King Slime is simply a mass formed by slimes clumping together. This would surely come as a shock to slime scholars.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc: An insect monster found on the 8th Floor of the Tower of Oz. It appears to be the same species that once inhabited Perion, back when the terrain was volcanic, but it disappeared from the region when its environment changed.\r\nApparently, it draws its energy from volcanic heat.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc: An insect monster found on the 8th Floor of the Tower of Oz. It appears to be the same species that once inhabited Perion, back when the terrain was volcanic, but it disappeared from the region when its environment changed.\r\nApparently, it draws its energy from volcanic heat.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc:
A massive spider-type monster found on the 10th Floor of the Tower of Oz. It resembles a species that once lived outside the Tower, but our researchers have had trouble confirming that, as its aggressive nature keeps them from getting too close. 
If it creates cocoons and produces spiderlings, they can multiply to overwhelming numbers, so it's wise to destroy any cocoons as quickly as possible. 
For reference, when it wraps its body in webs, it becomes extremely durable and deflects all attacks. Attacking it carelessly may result in injury instead, so proceed with caution.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc: A golem-type monster found on the 11th Floor of the Tower of Oz. Moss and flowers grow on its body. \r\nIt's believed to have lived in a dense, humid forest environment. Considering these traits, it is suspected to have once inhabited the area near Ellin Forest.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

14.desc: A golem-type monster found on the 11th Floor of the Tower of Oz. Moss and flowers grow on its body. \r\nIt's believed to have lived in a dense, humid forest environment. Considering these traits, it is suspected to have once inhabited the area near Ellin Forest.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc: A monster, closely resembling a cow, found on the 13th Floor of the Tower of Oz.\r\nPerhaps because it's still wild and undomesticated, its massive horns are extremely threatening. One other distinctive feature is the flower growing from its body.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

16.desc: A monster, closely resembling a cow, found on the 13th Floor of the Tower of Oz.\r\nPerhaps because it's still wild and undomesticated, its massive horns are extremely threatening. One other distinctive feature is the flower growing from its body.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

17.desc:
This monster, found on the 13th Floor of the Tower of Oz, closely resembles a bear. 
There was once a fairy tale about Thorny Bears living in El Nath, so seeing one in such a humid environment feels odd.
Still, the Transcendent of Life would not make such a mistake, so perhaps this is simply a highly adaptable specimen.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

18.desc:
This monster, found on the 13th Floor of the Tower of Oz, closely resembles a bear. 
There was once a fairy tale about Thorny Bears living in El Nath, so seeing one in such a humid environment feels odd.
Still, the Transcendent of Life would not make such a mistake, so perhaps this is simply a highly adaptable specimen.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

19.desc: A winged mushroom-like monster found on the 14th Floor of the Tower of Oz. This species is no longer found anywhere else in Maple World. \r\nIts tiny wings, which seem comically small for its size, are its main charm. Judging by the moss growing on its head, it's believed to have lived in a humid environment.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

20.desc: A winged mushroom-like monster found on the 14th Floor of the Tower of Oz. This species is no longer found anywhere else in Maple World. \r\nIts tiny wings, which seem comically small for its size, are its main charm. Judging by the moss growing on its head, it's believed to have lived in a humid environment.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

21.desc: A crocodile-like monster found on the 16th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. \r\nIt's surprising that this species has existed unchanged for so long. Though small in size, it's faster than an Ligator and possesses strong jaws, along with tough, resilient hide.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

22.desc: A crocodile-like monster found on the 16th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. \r\nWith a sleepy expression, it slowly crawls along the swamp floor. Its attacks are powerful, but it is slow-moving and weak against fire-attribute attacks.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

23.desc:
A crab-like monster found on the 18th and 19th Floors of the Tower of Oz. Long ago, the same species could be seen in Maple World, but it has since disappeared.
Its native environment is in sandy seashores. With extremely quick movement and relatively high physical and magical defense, it can be difficult to deal with. 
Because it lives near water, it is very weak to electricity, so try attacking it with Lightning-attribute magic.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

24.desc:
A crab-like monster found on the 18th and 19th Floors of the Tower of Oz. Long ago, the same species could be seen in Maple World, but it has since disappeared.
Its native environment is in sandy seashores. In terms of movement speed, physical defense, and magical defense, it surpasses the Lorang in every regard. 
However, like tge Lorang, it lives near water and is extremely weak to electricity, so attacking it with lightning-attribute magic is recommended.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

25.desc:
A turtle-like monster found on the 19th Floor of the Tower of Oz. Until relatively recently, this same species could also be found in the wilds of Maple World. 
It primarily inhabited sandy areas near the coast. Despite its sluggish appearance, it moves surprisingly fast and can spit poisonous liquid. 
With high physical and magical defense and no particular weaknesses, it is considered one of the more difficult monsters to defeat.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

26.desc:
A being created by Alicia's Soul to guard and manage the tower. It once carried out those duties, but over time, it gradually outgrew its intended purpose. 
The Tin Woodman moves slowly, making its attacks easy to avoid, but failing to dodge them can be fatal. Since its body is made of tin, it requires occasional oiling. When this happens, Dorothy summons an illusion to apply the oil. 
Be advised, if the oiling is successful, it becomes extremely powerful.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

27.desc: A monster found on the 21st Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species still found in present-day Maple World, this full grown Jr. Lioner is also often spotted in Orbis. \r\nThe mature Lioner draws strength from static in the air and uses the horn on its head to attack. As you might think, his monster is highly resistant to lightning-attribute attacks. Ice-attribute attacks, however, can be quite effective.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

28.desc: A monster found on the 21st Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species still found in present-day Maple World, this full grown Jr. Grupin is also often spotted in Orbis. \r\nThe mature Grupin, which changes from purple to green, draws strength from cold air and uses the horn on its head to attack. As you might think, his monster is highly resistant to ice-attribute attacks. Fire-attribute attacks, however, can be quite effective.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

29.desc: A monster found on the 21st Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species still found in present-day Maple World, this full grown Jr. Cellion is also often spotted in Orbis. \r\nThe mature Cellion draws strength from hot air and uses the horn on its head to attack. As you might think, his monster is highly resistant to fire-attribute attacks. Ice-attribute attacks, however, can be quite effective.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

30.desc:
Found on the 21st Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. An ancient creature that's been dormant for a long period of time. 
They say Eliza used to be the beloved pet of a Goddess and ruled over Orbis. Unfortunately, the Pixies kidnapped the Goddess while Eliza was asleep, taking over Eliza's nesting place. 
The angry Eliza exploded in fury and created numerous doppelgangers as an expression of its rage. Perhaps this is one of those clones.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

31.desc: Found on the 26th Floor of the Tower of Oz. While most slimes are generally bouncy, this one is distinguished by its extremely sticky texture. \r\nIf you are wearing expensive clothes, I recommend you change before making contact.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

32.desc: A snake-like monster found on the 28th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. A type of Necki that lives only in the desert. \r\nNot only can it see far with its two huge eyes, but it can also lure adventurers exploring at night with the jingling bell tied to the ribbon around its neck. But don't worry! This monster is not venomous.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

33.desc: A lizard-like monster found on the 28th Floor of the Tower of Oz. This desert-dwelilng species can still be found in present-day Maple World.\r\nIt's characterized by its perpetually heat-weary expression. Its appearance is somewhat unrefined, and that trait becomes especially noticeable when it runs around.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

34.desc: A fairy monster found on the 29th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. It looks just like the Desert Dwarf, only darker. \r\nIt is infamous for its ferocity, as well as its knack for discovering jewels. It carries around the flames of the desert.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

35.desc:
A being created by Alicia's Soul to guard and manage the tower. It once carried out those duties, but over time, it gradually outgrew its intended purpose. r

It's timid, and often runs away or hides, but occasionally it drinks a Courage Potion and lets out a powerful roar. The more courage the lion has, the stronger its attacks become, so if it becomes too much to handle, it may be wise to think of a way to reduce that courage.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

36.desc: An insectivore slime found on the 31st Floor of the Tower of Oz. Long ago, the same species could be seen in Maple World, but it has since disappeared. Rather than a typical slime, it's a mutated variant. \r\nIn person, it looks cuter than expected, but don't be deceived by its appearance. Judging by its habitat, it's believed to have lived near Ellin Forest in the distant past.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

37.desc: An insectivore slime found on the 31st Floor of the Tower of Oz. Long ago, the same species could be seen in Maple World, but it has since disappeared. Rather than a typical slime, it's a mutated variant. \r\nIn person, it looks cuter than expected, but don't be deceived by its appearance. Judging by its habitat, it's believed to have lived near Ellin Forest in the distant past.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

38.desc: A fairy found on the 31st Floor of the Tower of Oz. Fairies can still be seen in Maple World today, but those in the Tower of Oz have a slightly different appearance. \r\nThey are likely a species known as Ancient Fairies, as described in old records.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

39.desc:
A Blue Ancient Slime found on the 32nd Floor of the Tower of Oz. Long ago, the same species could be seen in Maple World, but it has since disappeared. 
Like other ancient slimes, it likely once flourished just as widely as did Orange Mushrooms. 
As expected, it boasts a much larger size compared to those slimes found on Victoria Island.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

40.desc:
A cow-like monster found on the 34th Floor of the Tower of Oz. Long ago, the same species could be seen in Maple World, but it has since disappeared. 
Grass grows across the upper part of its body, as if nature itself has taken root there. At a glance, it may not even look like a cow, but defeating one and examining its hide will reveal that it is unmistakably bovine. 
The hide is thin and lightweight, yet remarkably durable. If this creature still existed in the wider world today, it would be a valuable commodity.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

41.desc:
A cow-like monster found on the 34th Floor of the Tower of Oz. Long ago, the same species could be seen in Maple World, but it has since disappeared. 
Grass grows across the upper part of its body, as if nature itself has taken root there. At a glance, it may not even look like a cow, but defeating one and examining its hide will reveal that it is unmistakably bovine. 
The hide is thin and lightweight, yet remarkably durable. If this creature still existed in the wider world today, it would be a valuable commodity.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

42.desc:
A scorpion-type monster found on the 37th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. 
Although it has a poisonous sting on its tail, the sting is rarely used to attack; only a very few people have been stung in such a way. 
Russellon, who lost an eye to a Scorpion, is one of those rare unfortunates.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

43.desc: An eagle-like monster found on the 37th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. \r\nPerhaps due to the strong sun, it has few feathers on top of its head, somewhat resembling a baldheaded old man.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

44.desc: A mole-like monster found on the 37th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. \r\nIt hunts for food under the sand, and has a good rapport with the Sand Dwarves, so it is frequently seen carrying a small Sand Dwarf on its head.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

45.desc: This type of meerkat lives only in the desert. It has the tendency to whip out its telescope whenever it hears a noise.\r\nAlthough it looks nothing like a cat, it drops Cat's Eyes, as if it is trying to prove its feline heritage. Not that its eyes actually look like those of a cat or anything.\r\n                                          - Chronicler J.K.

46.desc:
A monster found on the 38th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. This monkey feeds on peaches at the Peach Farm, which gives its fur a pinkish color.
Appearances aside, these monkeys rival, if not surpass, the intelligence level of humans.
At first, the Peach Monkeys helped spread the seeds to expand the Peach Farm, but because of the gradual growth of their population, they have actually begun to hinder the farm's growth instead.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

47.desc:
A monster found on the 38th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in the present-day Maple World. This type of bear lives near Mu Lung. 
Although it's only a bear, it has a heartfelt desire to become a virtuous master, which is why it devotes so much of its energy in training. 
Despite the dignity and aristry of its training, it sometimes fails to suppress its animalistic instinct and attacks passersby.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

48.desc:
A monster found on the 38th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. This type of bear lives near Mu Lung. 
Although it's only a bear, it has a heartfelt desire to become a virtuous master, which is why it devotes so much of its energy in training. 
It looks similar to the people of Mu Lung, but it is unclear whether this is an inherent trait of the bear or a sign of its training.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

49.desc: A being created by Alicia's Soul to guard and manage the tower. It once carried out those duties, but over time, it gradually outgrew its intended purpose. \r\nDespite its scarecrow-like appearance, it possesses intelligence, making it difficult to deal with using ordinary methods. However, since it's made of straw, using fire should be effective.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

50.desc: A beetle-like monster found on the 42nd Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. \r\nIt thrives in habitats with leafy trees. A thick outer shell protects it from external impacts, and the sizable horn it sports on its head can toss any threatening enemy far away.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

51.desc: A beetle-like monster found on the 42nd Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World.\r\nIt's said to have once been a Beetle, but through molting, it gained a new silver shell as hard as steel. With attacks more powerful than those of a Beetle, it poses an even greater threat to its enemies.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

52.desc: A bird-like monster with a long tail found on the 42nd Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. \r\nIt has a ravishing blue tail and a lovely voice that complements its beauty; however, it charms people in order to lower their Accuracy, putting them in danger.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

53.desc: A bird-like monster with a long tail found on the 42nd Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World.\r\nIt has a ravishing red tail, charming appearance, and lovely voice, all of which make it more dangerous to its prey.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

54.desc: A monster found on the 46th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. A ferocious dragon that lives in the Dragon Canyon, usually nesting between the valleys. \r\nIt has a huge pair of reddish wings, which can generate a powerful gust of wind. Despite its lack of front legs, it's extremely fast, not to mention intelligent and capable of fire breath.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

55.desc: A monster found on the 46th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. A ferocious dragon that lives in the Dragon Canyon, usually nesting between the valleys. \r\nIt has a huge pair of blue wings, which can generate a powerful gust of wind. Despite its lack of front legs, it's extremely fast, not to mention intelligent and capable of ice breath.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

56.desc: A monster found on the 46th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The same species can still be found in present-day Maple World. A ferocious dragon that lives in the Dragon Canyon, usually nesting between the valleys. \r\nIt has a huge pair of dark wings, which can generate a powerful gust of wind. Despite its lack of front legs, it's extremely fast, not to mention intelligent and capable of casting curses with its very breath.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

57.desc: A beetle-like monster found on the 48th Floor of the Tower of Oz, and only the Tower of Oz. There are no wild specimens in Maple World anymore. \r\nIts most distinctive feature is its massive purple horn, which it uses to gather energy and unleash lightning attribute attacks. Excercise all appropriate caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

58.desc: A beetle-like monster found on the 48th Floor of the Tower of Oz, and only the Tower of Oz. There are no wild specimens in Maple World anymore. \r\nIts most distinctive feature is its massive purple horn, which it uses to gather energy and unleash lightning attribute attacks. Excercise all appropriate caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

59.desc:
A being created by Alicia's Soul to guard and manage the tower. It once carried out those duties, but over time it outgrew that purpose, and now even recognizes Alicia's Soul as an enemy.
In order to block outside intrusions, it freely tears apart the interior of the tower, leaving Alicia's Soul at a loss.
It's said that even Alicia's Soul is not confident she could win a battle against Dorothy. Be wary of Dorothy's magic, her clones, and her pet dog.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: The soul left behind by Alicia, the Transcendent of Life, to guard the Tower of Oz. Alicia's Soul claims that it has no knowledge of the original body's activities after its creation. \r\nWhether this reflects the original Alicia's personality or is a trait unique to souls is unclear. In any case, despite the title 'Mother of All Life,' its selfish behavior and blunt manner of speech feel oddly unsettling.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: A woman who sells various items at the Tower of Oz. She is has wavy blonde hair and is often seen wearing a blue dress. \r\nShe claimed to be a witch from the south, though her pure and gentle appearance hardly seem witch-like. Despite this, she insists that she truly is a witch.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: A rookie adventurer found in the basement of the Tower of Oz. Judging by appearance and ability, they're not much for combat, but they do possess keen observational skills. \r\nIf you need time to think, or you're unsure how to proceed, try talking to them. They may not give a straight answer, but they might be able to point you in the right direction.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc: An adventurer found on the 38th Floor of the Tower of Oz. They have a knack for sniffing out dark energy. \r\nSince dark energy is what's making the monsters aggressive in the Tower of Oz, this ability will be extremely useful. If you ever need to detect traces of dark energy, try speaking with them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc: An explorer found on the 39th Floor of the Tower of Oz. The fact that they've survived up there that long is proof of their strength.\r\nNot only that, but they've eliminated all surrounding monsters and taken over the floor. If you face a trial there, it'll come from them, so do not let your guard down.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: One of the adventurers found inside the Tower of Oz. They wear leather clothing suited for mobility, and carry mysterious artifacts that help them traverse each floor with ease. \r\nBetween their mannerisms, attire, and motley collection of weapons and artifacts, they appear to be a Thief.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: Alicia's Soul created this clone of Dorothy to guard and manage the tower.\r\nOn the 49th Floor of the Tower is a test, set up to judge whether you are worthy to face her. Clone though she is, facing her may bring an abrupt end to all your efforts, so plan accordingly.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Ritt

1000.regionDesc: This land west of Zipangu is dominated by a hill filled with maple trees and a large castle. This is where the Sengoku Warriors first arrived in Maple World after being warped from Hinomaru. On these grounds, the Sengoku Warriors waged a pitched battle against the tyrant, Oda Nobunaga.

0.desc: Oda Scout. They specialize in daggers and throwing stars, nimbly outmaneuvering their foes. They're never seen without their masks.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

1.desc: Elite Oda Scout. They wear masks like the regular scouts, but they have more intense eyes and sharper daggers. Their headbands are decorated with a crude Oda emblem.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

2.desc: Oda Foot Soldier. Typically armed with a simple katana. Banners featuring the Oda Clan crest are attached to their backs.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

3.desc: Oda's warriors tote long, sharp spears, and their armor puts the typical foot soldier's armor to shame. The warriors at this rank all ditch the banner for these shiny ornamental helmets. It seems they think the helmets look cool.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

4.desc:
Oda's wife is utterly loyal to Nobunaga. He put her in charge of the Four Heavenly Kings, which includes her retainers, warriors, and a massive goldfish Shikigami. She also wields powerful Eight Trigrams magic.
She tried to brainwash the Sengoku Warriors into helping with her husband's Demon King ritual, but Ayame foiled her before they could pull it off.

                                      - Chronicler Red

0.desc:
Matsuyama Sakuno is the leader of the Sengoku Warrior. As the head of the Matsuyama Clan, she stood against the evil forces of Oda Nobunaga in her homeworld of Hinomaru. Ever since the Sengoku Warriors and the Oda army were transported to Zipangu, she has continued to lead her allies with wisdom and courage.
She has all the grace and dignity you'd expect of a princess, and the Sengoku Warriors serve her with respect and loyalty. And is it any wonder? She would never ask her retainers to make any sacrifice that she herself wouldn't make.
The Maple Alliance was impressed by the princess's resolve and sincerity, and joined forces to help her hunt down Oda Nobunaga. In return, the Sengoku Warriors pledged themselves to aid Maple World.
It is only thanks to Princess Sakuno's leadership that the Sengoku Warriors have managed to overcome the obstacles before them. If I ever have the opportunity, I'd like to pay my respects to the princess by telling her, #e'the Sengoku Warriors are a gift to the Alliance.'#n

                                      - Chronicler Red

1.desc:
The great Spirit Walker of the Sengoku Warriors has a striking look to him. His calm expression and his moonlight-colored hair make him all the more mysterious. Wherever he goes, he's followed by his fox Shikigami companion.
His title is well earned, too. He taught Princess Sakuno and Kanna their skills as Spirit Walkers. Seeing as one of his students became one of the Sengoku Warriors' greatest heroes, and another became one of its most formidable allies, it's clear he knows his craft.
The man holds many secrets we're yet to uncover. It seems like he always knows the hidden truth behind things, including the strange events that dragged the Sengoku Warriors to Maple World. I wonder...has he figured me out yet?

                                      - Chronicler Red

2.desc:
The head of the Mouri Clan and one of the founding members of the Sengoku Warriors. He's known for his mastery of tactics and strategy, and he even advised Princess Sakuno's father, Matsuyama Kanetsugu, during early victories agaisnt Oda Nobunaga.
He can instantly switch between directing detailed battle plans and viewing the big picture, and he's never one to miss out on exploiting the enemy's carlessness and mistakes. In some ways, he's the glue that hold the faction together, often playing peacemaker between Kenshin and Shingen.
It's a good thing we have the Mouri Clan as an ally, even if he does have a...disgruntled look. You would be disgruntled, too, if you had to deal with Kenshin and Shingen all day.

                                      - Chronicler Red

3.desc: The eldest son of Mouri Motonari. He's got a softer look than his father, Motonari, and he's always preferred academics to martial arts. Thanks to his keen sense for numbers, he's been placed in charge of the Sengoku Warriors' general supplies.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

4.desc: The middle son of Mouri Motonari. Unlike his older brother, Takamoto, he carries himself with the formidable air of a warrior. He is in charge of the Sengoku Warriors' weapons and logistics.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

5.desc:
The youngest son of Mouri Motonari. He's got the best of his father and his two brothers in him, being both a sharp mind and a fierce warrior. Out of the three brothers, he has the strongest resemblance to their father.
He also manages part of the Sengoku Warrior armory, and will exchange special weapons for Marks of the Silver Wolf.

                                      - Chronicler Red

6.desc:
This samurai is known by his Sengoku Warrior allies as the Mirror of Loyalty, and there are few in this world more trustworthy than him. The Sengoku Warriors often send him out into the field to scout out suspicious situations, so he's already explored his fair share of Maple World.
Does he work alone because of the kinds of missions he takes? Or does he take those missions so he can be alone? I have a feeling that scar on his face holds the answer.

                                      - Chronicler Red

7.desc:
She served Princess Sakuno's father, Matsuyama Nobukane, and is still close to the princess to this day. With her fiery eyes, her expertise with firearms, and her top aim, she's a force to be reckoned with.
In another life, she was the leader of a musket-wielding mercenary group, but she infiltrated the Oda army as a spy at Nobukane's suggestion.

                                      - Chronicler Red

8.desc:
The head of Sengoku Warrior's greatest clan, the Uesugi Clan! Her titles are well earned from her feats in battle and include the Greatest Samurai, the God of War, and the Dragon of Echigo.
Of course, her best title is certainly the Incarnation of Bishamonten! The flash of her sword as she calls upon Bishamonten's power, slashing her enemies to bits, makes her seem unbeatable.
She may seem cold at first, but she's a chivalrous warrior who values loyalty and integrity above all else. Because she cares about honesty so much, she can be a little...blunt. I wonder what she's said about me?

                                      - Chronicler Red

9.desc:
Uesugi Kenshin's retainer and student. Just like Kenshin, he deeply values loyalty and love. He's even added the character for love to his helmet.
He's usually pretty reserved, but when it comes to Kenshin, he can help but gush. He's constantly bickering with Shingen's retainer, Sanada Yukimura. If you spend any time with them, try not to get dragged into their arguments.

                                      - Chronicler Red

10.desc:
The head of the Takeda Clan is known as the Tiger Daimyou for his bravery in battle. With flame-red hair and armor, he's a striking figure when leading his cavalry, the Red Corps. When he charges into battle, it's like watching a wildfire sweep through the enemy.
From his rough voice, you might think he's a brute who's always eager to jump into battle, but he's a sharp leader who makes his decision based on logic.
Have those tiger eyes of his figured me out?

                                      - Chronicler Red

11.desc:
A warrior under Takeda Shingen and the vanguard of Shingen's cavalry. Yukimura is Shingen's right-hand man. Just like their lords, Yukimura and Naoe Kanetsugu are constantly bickering over whose master is better.
Ever since he arrived in Maple World, Shingen has sent him on many scouting missions throughout the land. I've seen him beyond the borders of Honnou-ji several times now. I was especially impressed when he infultrated the Dead Mine in El Nath by himself.

                                      - Chronicler Red

1001.regionDesc: This floating island at the heart of Zipangu was the first place from another world to appear in Maple World. Nestuled in a beautiful forest of cherry blossom trees, the Mushroom Shrine is dedicated to Daidarabotchi, guardian of Ziapngu.\r\nFrom the mysterious great tree Kamuna at the center of the island to the nearby Grieving Grotto to the Hunting Lodge of the dark forest to the shrine itself, each place has a unique story. If you find yourself passing through, sit a while and listen to the stories of the humans, the yokai, and those who are something in between.

0.desc: These mechanical warriors of the Oda army wield with large laser-katana in each hand. Expect no mercy from these killing machines.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

1.desc: These mechanical warriors of the Oda army attack with hidden throwing stars. It is said that their computerized brains focus on their mission and nothing else.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

2.desc:
These mysterious wander the dark forests of Mushroom Shrine. They carry unfurled scrolls to hide their presence.
Unfortunately for them, their bamboo swords and large hats stick out from behind the scrolls, making the camouflage pretty ineffective. Well, the forests are dark, so maybe they can try sticking to the shadows.

                                      - Chronicler Red

3.desc: A ghost shrouded in dark cloth. It is said to be born from the shadows, but it's possible that they're just ordinary ghosts. In either case, caution is advised.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

4.desc: These mechanical Oda army warriors carry high-tech, state-of-the-art muskets. Their reload speed and accuracy put other muskets to shame.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

5.desc: These mushrooms are commonly found around the Mushroom Shrine. They're similar to Victoria Island's Orange Mushrooms, but they have a cherry blossom pattern on their caps. They're adorable when they bounce around, and they smell nice, too.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

6.desc: A raccoon yokai that carries a bundle of firewood on its back. Legend has it that the first of these yokai went to the forest to gather firewood, and a human lit the bundle of firewood on its back as a prank. To this day, it's still wandering, terrified and angry over a bit of innocent arson.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

7.desc: A fox yokai wandering around Mushroom Shrine. It has a cloud-like tail and a leaf on its forehead, which it uses to shapeshift and play pranks on passersby.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

8.desc: A fox yokai wandering around Mushroom Shrine. It was once an ordinary fox, but it passed away and absorbed dark magic, reviving as the yokai we see today. It can use the leaf on its head to shapeshift.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

9.desc:
These mysterious yokai sometimes appear in abandoned houses in the forest near Mushroom Shrine. They resemble red rag dolls that drift aimlessly through the air.
They may look like dolls, but they're anything but friendly. There are other similar yokai that come in different colors in the area. It's unknown if they're related.

                                      - Chronicler Red

10.desc: A large blue mushroom monster that sometimes appears at the Lonely House near Mushroom Shrine. Unlike the Cherry Blossom Mushrooms there, its cap has a standard spotted pattern. The locals call it a Mushdad. Is it related to the Mushmoms of Victoria Island?\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

11.desc: These crows move in murders in the dark forests east of Mushroom Shrine. It's quite annoying to be strolling through the forest and find yourself under their shadow.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

12.desc: A lantern ghost with a grudge. It's said that this lantern was carried by a passerby who was attacked while traveling through the forest. The local kami have possessed the lantern and brought it to life.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

13.desc:
These mysterious yokai sometimes appear in abandoned houses in the forest near Mushroom Shrine. They resemble blue rag dolls that drift aimlessly through the air.
They may look like dolls, but they're anything but friendly. There are other similar yokai that come in different colors in the area. It's unknown if they're related.

                                      - Chronicler Red

14.desc: A yokai with red skin, small white wings, a chiseled face, and a big noise. It is said that martial artists who seek a shortcut to power without fortifying their mind transform into these. Be careful, as they tend to attack on sight.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

15.desc: These are the spirits of people who died by the rivers of Mushroom Shrine and were unable to let go of their regrets. Now they are doomed to wander, lost, as though being chased by something.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

16.desc:
These mysterious yokai sometimes appear in abandoned houses in the forest near Mushroom Shrine. They resemble black rag dolls that drift aimlessly through the air.
They may look like dolls, but they're anything but friendly. There are other similar yokai that come in different colors in the area. It's unknown if they're related.

                                      - Chronicler Red

17.desc: A ghost wandering the Hunting Lodge near Mushroom Shrine. In life, they were sacrificed to a god of the land long ago. Their resentment at being sacrificed has prevented them from moving on, and in the ages since they were cursed, they have forgotten what it was like to be human.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

18.desc:
The yokai native to the river that flows through Mushroom Shrine. After humans started polluting their once-pristine waters, they began to attack humans on sight.
They've even taken to using their favorite food, cucumbers, as weapons against anyone who passes by.

                                      - Chronicler Red

19.desc:
These mysterious yokai sometimes appear in abandoned houses in the forest near Mushroom Shrine. They resemble green rag dolls that drift aimlessly through the air.
They may look like dolls, but they're anything but friendly. There are other similar yokai that come in different colors in the area. It's unknown if they're related.

                                      - Chronicler Red

20.desc: This is the true form of Tengu, the crow yokai. As a guardian of the Wood Element, it possesses immense power: its talons are sharper than a predator's fangs, and every flap of its wings creates a storm.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

21.desc:
Formerly one of Oda Nobunaga's Four Heavenly Kings, this samurai is a master swordsman who wields a katana that's taller than he is.
Under Oda's command, he committed countless atrocities, including nearly wiping out the Matsuyama Clan and kidnapping Princess Sakuno for Oda's Demon King ritual.
However, on the night of the ritual, he betrayed Oda. As a result, both Oda's forces and the Sengoku Warriors were transported to Maple World.
Afterward, he helped the Sengoku Warriors defeat Oda at Fort Asura, only to betray THEM and play both sides against each other. Since then, he has been sowing chaos throughout Maple World and making enemies everywhere he goes.
It's said that he was disullisioned by Oda for failing to end the war after claiming victory in Hinomaru. It's said that he is an enemy to anyone who starts a war. However, his tendency to betray everyone, his cruel disdsain for the weak, and his incredible arrogance hardly makes him a sympathetic figure. He's a true lone wolf--do not let your guard down around him.

                                      - Chronicler Red

0.desc:
The head shrine maiden of Mushroom Shrine. She's diligent and keeps a tidy shrine. She also knows all about Maple World, having tended to the shrine since it appeared in Zipangu.
When the Sengoku Warriors first arrived, she was the one who helped them understand where they were.
She also constantly sings a cute little song while she sweeps. Unfortunately, she's forgotten all of the lyrics except for the words 'Mushroom Shrine.'

                                      - Chronicler Red

1.desc:
A shrine maiden of Mushroom Shrine and the younger sister of Takeno Konoko. She's half-yokai, which has led to her being sickly for most of her youth.
There's nothing she wants more than for humans and yokai to coexist peacefully. Even though she was nearly killed by a powerful yokai, Genkou, she insists that the experience actually helped make her healthier and heartier.
A young yokai named Nue has a crush on her, but she doesn't seem to be aware. If you ask her, #e'How have you been since then?'#n, she might tell you what's been going on.

                                      - Chronicler Red

2.desc:
A fox yokai that can shapeshift into a human. He's the head of the Mushroom Shrine foxes and the guardian of the Earth Element. Despite his adorable appearance, he possesses immense power that befits his title of guardian. However, he feared his own power so much that he hid himself away in a cave for 5 years.
His fellow fox yokai, Izuna, is a childhood friend--who maybe wants to be something more. But he's completely oblivious, and so Izuna has no choice but to sulk.
In spite of all this, he's slowly grown into a leader for the fox yokai in their struggle against the people of Showa Town.
Whenever he's in a bad mood, Izuna gives him dango to cheer him up.

                                      - Chronicler Red

3.desc:
A fox yokai that can shapeshift into a human. She was close to Takeno Konoko since they were young. She asked Takeno Konoko for help after her childhood friend, Kurama, was chosen to lead the fox yokai--and instead decided to hide in a cave for 5 years.
Kurama eventually accepted his role as leader and got over his fear of his own power, but she's unhappy that Kurama is oblivious to the hints that she wants to be more than friends.
I hear she likes flowers. Want to tell Kurama about it?

                                      - Chronicler Red

4.desc:
As a talkative young Kappa yokai, Yorozu can transform into a child. She serves Tengu, and you need Tengu's permission to even talk to her.
Judging from her book and toolbag, she seems to have an interest in machines and alchemy.

                                      - Chronicler Red

5.desc:
A weasel yokai with a large scythe. Ah, but don't call him a weasel to his face--Maitachi hates that. He's known Ibaraki for a while now. Surprisingly enough, he's actually the older of the two.
He can hold his own in a fight and seems to be searching for an item to protect Zipangu. Since he has power over wind, he floats instead of walking.

                                      - Chronicler Red

6.desc:
He calls himself 'an oni who lives with humans,' but he seems more human than yokai. He's got a sophisticated sense of fashion with his white coat, dual pistols, and intimidating red oni mask.
It's been a long time since he went back to his hometown, but he played a big role in a battle against a frenzied oni and taking back the Metal Element. Sadly, it was his brother Gyuki who lost control while trying to absorb the Metal Element, and he had to watch his brother take his last breath at the end of the battle.
Still, he says he was grateful to even be able to have one last conversation with his brother. He moved to Mushroom Shrine shortly after that. He may be an oni on the outside, but inside, he's deeply human.

                                      - Chronicler Red

7.desc:
This yokai was Nue's right-hand woman when he led his cult in the Grieving Grotto. Even though the cult is finished, she still holds a grudge against Kamaitachi.
Even though both Kubinashi and Kamaitachi have settled down in Mushroom Shrine, they seem to be coexisting without attacking each other. She's constantly talking about dueling Kamaitachi, but Kamaitachi has yet to accept.
She has a soft spot for swords.

                                      - Chronicler Red

8.desc:
This kid somehow managed to start a guild in the Grieving Grotto to the west of Mushroom Shrine. He made up a fake doctrine and convinced a bunch of ghosts and skeletons to worship him, but that all went away when it was revealed that he was just a young boy.
Since then, he moved into Mushroom Shrine. It seems he developed a crush on Takeno Konoko when he saw her exorcise the spirits near the Grieving Grotto. To have any chance with her, he'll need to avoid Kino Konoko's watchful gaze.
He won't admit it, but he loves sweet desserts.

                                      - Chronicler Red

9.desc:
This crow yokai has known Takeno Konoko for a long time. When he takes on human form, he appears as a long-haired monk. He's the guardian of the Wood Element, keeping it safe from those whose hearts are filled with anguish and ambition. It is for this reason that he made a test to ensure that only the truly worthy could claim the Wood Element.
The most difficult part of the test is a battle against Tengu in his true from. It goes without saying that he commands amazing power.

                                      - Chronicler Red

10.desc:
The chef of Mushroom Shrine sells food and other items. He has looked after the Konoko sisters for a long time.
He specializes in local dishes, and his cooking is said to be so good that it shocks yokai and bewitches foxes. I tried everything on his menu, and I have to say the rumors are true.
Eating all this delicious food was part of my investigation. I swear.

                                      - Chronicler Red

11.desc:
This mysterious woman resides beneath Kamuna, the sacred tree that stands at the heart of Zipangu. As the guardian of Zipangu, she has had many names throughout history, though the shrine maidens of Mushroom Shrine know her as Daidarabotchi. When Takeno Konoko was nearly killed by Genkou, it was she who used the power of the Five Elements to revive the shrine maiden.
She's known as the protector of ALL of Zipangu, not just Mushroom Shrine, and you can see signs of her influence throughout the regions. I have a feeling that she may be a being even greater than Daidarabotchi.

                                      - Chronicler Red

12.desc:
If you need to travel around Zipangu, this pelican can help you out. Hop into its huge bill and it will fly you to wherever you need to go. It can even take you from Zipangu all the way to the Six Path Crossway Tree Platform.
It promises it would never eat any of its passengers. Still, I think I'd rather walk than hop into its bill...

                                      - Chronicler Red

1002.regionDesc: This mysterious looms large in western Zipangu, filled with bizarre mazes and deadly traps. What's actually inside this castle? What's going on in there? Rumor has it that the castle was actually made as a testing ground to hone someone's combat skills.

0.desc: These Sakura Genin trained in Ninja Town. They're technically not at the level of Chunin or Jonin yet, but their blades are just as sharp.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

1.desc: This soldier fights for Ninja Castle to defend a Daimyo who doesn't actually exist. He doesn't seem to be very comfortable with the spear he's using.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

2.desc: A ninja who has graduated from Genin to Chunin rank. They specialize in blowgun assassination, so watch your back when going into dark places.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

3.desc: A lady ninja of Ninja Town. I once asked a Kunoichi how she became a ninja, and she told me she was once an ordinary woman. A yokai murdered her fiancee, and she trained so she could get her revenge. They specialize in stealth missions, but in Ninja Castle, they have no issue fighting out in the open.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

4.desc: A highly-ranked ninja who has mastered much of the ninja arts. I once asked a Sakura Jonin why he wrapped his entire body in bandages. He told me it's because he had severe frostbite from an ice attack during training.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

5.desc: Leader of the ninjas. According to ninja lore, you can only become a Sakura Ninto when you have walked the line between life and death. It's unclear which side of that line these ninjas end up on.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

6.desc: A soldier who died in battle long ago within Ninja Castle. The grudge they felt at the moment of death lives on, and now they remain to swing their sword at anything they see.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

7.desc: An ancient toad yokai who's learned how to shapeshift into a person. It drove out and replaced the original daimyo of Ninja Castle, and now it acts like it owns the place.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

8.desc: The true form of the toad yokai who is impersonating the daimyo, having been pushed into a corner. However, the whereabouts of the true daimyo are still unknown. When the toad gets angry enough, it unleashes a poison that engulfs the entire castle.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

0.desc: A merchant selling weapons outside Ninja Castle. He has a large weapon rack showing off most of his goods, but some of his stock isn't on display.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

1.desc: A merchant selling armor outside Ninja Castle. Despite his bright, confident smile, his armor selection is pretty limited.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

2.desc: A child playing with a top outside Ninja Castle. Look at him play without a care in the world. Is he the only person in Ninja Castle who's actually happy?\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

3.desc: Akai's father. He once was a simple cloth merchant, but he somehow got dragged into supplying poison to the daimyo of Ninja Castle at some point.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

4.desc: Hamadaya's daughter. She's looking for people to help her father, who was an ordinary cloth merchant who became embroiled in the daimyo's schemes. She's sad that her once kind father has changed so much.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

5.desc: One of the soldiers guarding the gate of Ninja Castle. Unlike his fellow guard, Sasuke, he is a disciplined and upstanding fellow.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

6.desc: One of the soldiers guarding the gate of Ninja Castle. Unlike his fellow guard, Daisuke, he's annoyed at his job and he doesn't care who knows it.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

7.desc: Someone hired this man to investigate Ninja Castle. He seems to be working with the falconer sitting at the top of the castle.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

8.desc: An unidentified figure below Ninja Castle's gate. He wears a unique mask and a blue hood. He doesn't answer no matter how much you try to talk to him, so he must be on some sort of stealth mission.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

9.desc: An elegant lady in a pink kimono. She asked Nobuo and the falconer to investigate Ninja Castle. She's searching for her father, the true daimyo of Ninja Castle, and fighting back against the yokai who replaced him.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

10.desc: An unknown man in a fox mask clinging to Ninja Castle's wall. He looks just like Sai in Ninja Castle, but he doesn't answer if you try to say hello. Is he on a secret mission?\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

11.desc: A man on top of Ninja Castle. He was hired to investigate the place. He seems to be working with Nobuo and using his falcon to scout inside the castle.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

12.desc: You might encounter this ninja in a fox mask if you go inside Ninja Castle. He can show you the way out if you're lost. What's his true identity? Is he also working with Princess Suzume?\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

1003.regionDesc: In this small town in eastern Zipangu, the sunset over the weathered rooftops is a sight to be seen. While it may seem like an ordinary town on the surface, rumor has it that Fire Raccoon Finance has a stranglehold over the town's criminal underbelly.

0.desc:
A gangster of Showa Town. I asked one why she joined the Yakuza, and she explained that Fire Raccoon Finance took her in as an orphan. They trained her up in the skills of the underworld.
Incidentally, this specific Yakuza has been seen meeting with Umi at the Showa Town grocer. Is there something going on between those two?

                                      - Chronicler Red

1.desc: A young Showa Town gangster. Rumor has it that Fire Raccoon Finance recruits promising young athletes who had to drop out from professional sports due to injuries or family hardship. That's not how you're supposed to use a baseball bat, son!\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

2.desc: These Showa Town gangsters are never seen without a brick in hand. If you miss a lone payment to Fire Raccoon Finance, one of these bricks might go flying through your window...and that's a best-case scenario.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

3.desc:
A common lowlife of Showa Town. I interviewed one of these gangsters. He was dedicated to kendo when he was a kid, but he hurt one of his opponents and had to drop out. But thanks to Fire Raccoon Finance, he can still practice his beloved kendo, even if his new opponents aren't so enthusiastic.

                                      - Chronicler Red

4.desc: One of the executives of Fire Raccoon Finance. He wields a katana and bears a scar from a past duel. He's also a snappy dresser.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

5.desc: One of the executives of Fire Raccoon Finance. He's an ace gunslinger, second to none when handling firearms. His talents for fashion, on the other hand, are not so great. What happened to his shirt?\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

6.desc: One of the executives of Fire Raccoon Finance. She actually knows that the Yakuza Boss is secretly a yokai, but she doesn't care.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

7.desc: A large black snake that lives in the Fire Raccoon Finance building. Why would they keep a snake like this? It is a security snake? A way of punishing gangsters who fail? Or is it just a pet? Whatever it is, this only proves that Fire Raccoon Finance is no ordinary company.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

8.desc: One of the executives of Fire Raccoon Finance. He's married to the Yakuza Underboss. He knows that the boss of their company is actually a yokai, but he doesn't seem to care.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

9.desc: The personal bodyguard of Fire Raccoon Finance's top boss. This muscular guy lives up to the image of a Yakzua Boss's protector, complete with an eye-catching tattoo. He's completely at ease punching and kicking in his suit. Anyone who wishes to challenge the Yakuza needs to get through him, first.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

10.desc: The personal bodyguard of Fire Raccoon Finance's top boss. His spiky blonde hair sets him apart. Unlike his more muscular partner, he prefers to attack enemies with firearms and rockets. You'll need to evade his rain of fire if you want to challenge the Yakuza of Fire Raccoon Finance.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

11.desc: The Yakuza Boss and owner of Fire Raccoon Finance. He may look like a stern old man, but he's actually an ancient raccoon yokai. His raccoon clan has long been at odds with humankind. After learning how to disguise himself as a human, he infiltrated the local criminal underworld and founded Fire Raccoon Finance to exploit the people of Showa Town.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

12.desc: These slimes inhabit the hidden hot springs under the Showa Town spa. The minerals in the water make them smoother and bouncier than other slimes. But why are they that murky color? Let's just...not think about it.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

0.desc:
A detective with the Showa Town police. He's looking into Fire Raccoon Finance, the front for the criminal organization that's got a chokehold on the town. It seems the other officers aren't too interested in helping him, as he's been getting help from adventurers.
He often sends people out to battle against Fire Raccoon Finance's gangsters. This raises an important question: where are all these gangsters coming from?!

                                      - Chronicler Red

1.desc: A girl in Showa Town. She's crying because Boss Kitty stole her favorite marble. It was a gift from her father, who's always away working in the city. No wonder she's so sad...\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

2.desc: A poor cat who's hiding and licking its wounds after being bullied by the other cats. Judging by its two tails, it's no ordinary critter. But why was it being bullied? Apparently it will teach anyone who helps it the language of cats.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

3.desc: A girl of Showa Town. If you listen to her request, she'll apparently give you a random marble. Where is she getting all these marbles? Sometimes she'll hand you one you've never seen before in your life.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

4.desc:
The owner of the Showa Town spa. The spa is open for everyone's use. She's been running the place for decades, but she still keeps it nice and pristine as the day she started.
She's a bit worried about all of the ghosts and yokai outside of town. It sounds like they've been an issue for quite some time, and she hopes someone can come along to defeat them.
Note: The spa has separate areas for men and women.

                                      - Chronicler Red

5.desc:
An employee of the Showa Town spa. She sells bathrobes and beverages to customers when they've finished their bath.
There's nothing quite like a cool glass of juice after a hot bath. I highly recommend you give it a try. Again, doing this was part of my job as a chronicler.

                                      - Chronicler Red

6.desc:
A child of Showa Town. A bold child, she's the first to rally her friends when they're in trouble. She's also the first to give away her least favorite sausages as a quest reward...

                                      - Chronicler Red

7.desc:
A middle-aged man who lives in Showa Town. He's always chewing gum.
He may look like one of the gangsters of Fire Raccoon Finance, but he's actually investigating their activities in secret. He's hoping to recruit some strong adventurers to defeat the Yakuza Boss.
It looks like he's been working alone to maintain his cover. That takes guts... He's more impressive than he looks.

                                      - Chronicler Red

8.desc: A fierce stray cat who bosses around all the other cats in Showa Town. Not only does it bully the other cats, but it even bullies the children. How can a kitty get so bad?\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

9.desc: As Showa Town's mailman, he also safekeeps items for the townsfolk. He still rides his bicycle to deliver the mail every day. You can use the mailbox next to him if you need to send a letter.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

10.desc: The director of Showa Town's hospital. He's distinguished by his thick, black mustache. He works closely with the nurse, Saeko, and puts a heavy emphasis on eye health.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

11.desc: The nurse of Showa Town's hospital. She works closely with Director Hikekuro and even does many procedures herself, though she seems pretty nervous when she does so. Most of their patients seek out the director's services instead, if they can manage it. If she wants to make a living at her career, she needs to learn to set her anxieties aside.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

12.desc: The barber of Showa Town. He's got pictures of all his customers on his wall, which appears to be almost everyone in town. He's got the look of a veteran haircutter.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

13.desc: The assistant and daughter of Tepei, the barber of Showa Town. She helps her father dye their customers' hair. Her own hair is a glossy brown--does her father handle her hair care?\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

14.desc:
The trolly driver of Showa Town. His passengers rarely see his face, as he's so focused on the dashboard.
His trolley goes all over town, even to the alleys. And he's always happy to take his passengers directly to their destination, and it's entirely free of charge! If you can explain how this trolley works, I'd love to hear it!

                                      - Chronicler Red

15.desc: A researcher in Showa Town who specializes in rare monsters. If you help him with his research, he'll give you an Orange Mushroom Piece and a Gray Piece. Mushrooms are common enough, but it's pretty impressive that he knows about the Grays of Omega Sector.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

16.desc:
The owner of Kusurio General Store in Showa Town. It's the only general store in town, but it's surprisingly big.
His store sells a unique cider which is quite popular. It's sweet and refreshing. I suggest you buy several bottles if you're ever in the area.


                                      - Chronicler Red

17.desc:
The grocer of Showa Town. Not only does she sell vegetables, but she's big into developing new products like health food or desserts made from cucumbers. She recently made quite a bit of money through a connection with Fire Raccoon Finance, and now she's worried her wallet is too small...
What a problem to have...

                                      - Chronicler Red

18.desc:
A Showa Town fishmonger. He leads a carefree lifestyle built around taking it easy and fishing.
He can also be a bit eccentric. I hear that he once sent someone to get a hat back from some kid. Apparently the kid had folded a page from his newspaper into a paper hat.

                                      - Chronicler Red

19.desc:
The owner of Kotobuki Pawnshop in Showa Town. He sells weapons that have been given to him as collateral. It seems that he's married to Hanako.
He looks like a wandering swordsman, but he sells all kinds of weapons, including baseball bats, bricks, and even fish.
Some of those weapons are decent, at least...

                                      - Chronicler Red

20.desc: Shinta's wife sells refurbished armor at Kotobuki Pawnshop. Most of the armor there can also be found in other towns, but there are some unique throwing weapons, like Paper Planes and Oranges.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

21.desc:
This mysterious gentleman resides in Showa Town. If you bring him large quantities of items you found laying around town, he will reward you based on their quality. He's very picky, though.
He loves fried eggs for breakfast.

                                      - Chronicler Red

22.desc: Showa Town's most famous actress. She works with the film director Furano and is completely obsessed with her looks. She particularly loves fox fur coats... Given the nature of the local foxes, she should be careful not to make any enemies.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

23.desc:
An actress in Showa Town. She appears in Furano's films with Mariwaka. Her hat and tailcoat combo is quite striking, but maybe that's just the costume for her next movie? She doesn't just act, but sings, also. She usually sings the theme songs for the movies she's in.

                                      - Chronicler Red

24.desc: Showa Town's resident movie director. He often works with Mariwaka and Skai. You can see posters for his movies on the theater walls.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

25.desc: This man struts around Showa Town with his eyes wide open, swearing that laser beams are shooting from them. And yes, that is strange. But he also helps recruit adventurers to fight back against Fire Raccoon Finance, so he can't be all bad, can he?\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Red

1004.regionDesc: Xuanshan is a great mountain in southern Jianghu. The shore at the foot of the mountains is rocky and the current is strong, so only experienced sailors can even navigate there.\r\nThe port town of Hejin offers safer passage to and from the rest of Jianghu. Because of that, the town is always bustling with martial artists and merchants.\r\nThe Xuanshan School is deep in the mountains, but access is restricted to anyone who is not part of the school.

0.desc:
Can you believe folks used to keep these critters as pets? Oh, sure, they seemed cute and cuddly at the time, but something's got their ears in a twist, I tell you.
The other day, one of 'em hopped right up to me and smashed my favorite begging bowl! Blasted rabbits! If I ever get my hands on one of 'em, I'll be having rabbit stew.
What's going on in this town to make these bunnies so unfriendly, anyway?


                                      - Chronicler Dust

1.desc:
These antlered rabbits are a Xuanshan specialty. Used to be they'd use these antlers to protect themselves, but they wouldn't harm a fly otherwise.
Not anymore. Just like all the other beasties in Xuanshan, these little critters have got it in their heads that it's time to mash all the towsnsfolk. And trust me, those antlers are good for mashing.
Hmm. I wonder if they taste like rabbit or like venison? I'd try it out for myself, but you won't see me near those antlers, no sir.

                                      - Chronicler Dust

2.desc:
You'll find these creatures deep in Xuanshan. They find old bits of tree and wear 'em like armor. Then, if they're outmatched, they'll shed the wood and scamper off.
It's good wood, too. You can make a fence with it. Or maybe a bat.
Wish I had a bat. Then I could beat 'em away when they got too close.

                                      - Chronicler Dust

3.desc:
Most moshas are gentle, laid-back cuties that spend their days splashing around in the river. Not these fellas. They're called 'grumpy' for a reason.
Lately, they've started attacking anyone who tries to go fishing. I suppose that's how all the wild life in the area is nowadays.
Apparently their little flippers are good medicine. An old doctor asked if I could fetch one for him, and on the way I got it in my head that they might be good eatin', too.
Let me just say that I will never forget that taste as long as I live. Blech!

                                      - Chronicler Dust

4.desc:
Ooh, now these critters only appear where there's deep evil. That Feng--smart guy, Feng--says they're called 'shanbeasts.'
Their fur is soft, yeah, but even beggars know better than to use it for a cloak.
Now, hearing all that, you've gotta wonder... What're they doing so close to town?

                                      - Chronicler Dust

0.desc:
This kind lady keeps the biggest tavern in Xuanshan. Her somen is chewy and rich... My mouth's watering just thinking about it. I tried to get the recipe from her, but she wouldn't budge...
Everyone who's anyone stops here on their way through Xuanshan, which means all the gossip ends up here, too. She probably knows what's going on even better than the Beggar Guild.

                                      - Chronicler Dust

1.desc:
This guy was out gathering wood and got attacked by wild animals. Hurt his back running away. Can you believe it?
Good thing the Xuanshan School was around to help him out.

                                      - Chronicler Dust

2.desc:
If you're in Hejin, and you need potions, talk to Ju Ji. If you need braces for your martial arts, talk to Ju Ji. If you need fresh fruit, you talk to Ju Ji! She's got the freshest in town!
That's a weird thing, though. There aren't any fruit trees in town, so where's she getting fresh fruit from? Or is she just that good at bluffing? Makes you think, makes you think.

                                      - Chronicler Dust

3.desc:
Ah, our resident storage keeper. He keeps careful logs on every item that enters his care, and I assure you, the man's never lost a single thing. Rest easy knowing your stuff is safe while you're in Hejin.
Sometimes he forgets he put his brush behind his ear. So what does he write with when that happens, you ask? Well, that long beard isn't just for show!

                                      - Chronicler Dust

4.desc:
This doctor runs the biggest, and stinkiest, clinic in all of Hejin. The only place that rivals his smell is our own humble Beggar Guild, and the jury's out on which is worst.
I used to beg near the clinic, y'know. They'd give me licorice, saying it was the sweetest thing they got. Oh, I'd get so excited to have something to eat, but then I'd choke 'cause it was so dang bitter!
Still, the man knows his medicine. I don't think there's a poison in this world he can't cure, and I've even seen him work his craft on spirits.

                                      - Chronicler Dust

5.desc:
If you're looking to leave Hejin for the great wide world, this is the oarsman for you. It's a long journey, but he's never lost a passenger. How he manages in that tiny boat of his, I got no clue.
The passengers all come down with terrible seasickness, of course, but at least they're in one piece!

                                      - Chronicler Dust

6.desc:
Feng (this is not his real name) can be found around Hejin. If I, theoretically, had the privilege of knowing his true identity, I wouldn't tell you.
Feng commands seven birds, a privilege given to only the very highest-ranking members of the guild. On their swift wings, information flies--and there's no better informant in all of Xuanshan.
Don't believe me? Just go to him on a quiet day and ask #e'Feng, have any news for me?'#n.
                                      - Chronicler Dust

7.desc:
A member of the Xuanshan School, and daughter of a merchant leader. I've heard some talk among locals who say that she's nothing more than a rich, sheltered layabout, playacting at Jianghu, but even from a distance, I can tell that's nonsense. I, myself, witnessed her practicing her forms at the break of dawn.
She uses her father's connections to supply many basic necessities to Xuanshan School. Xiao Xiao's father's trading company has an agreement to supply all training dummies, wood, food, and many other resources to the school.
The merchant himself claims the school is an investment with great potential for growth, but his records tell a different story. His agreement with the school makes him pennies, if anything. The man clearly just loves his daughter. How sweet.
Xiao Xiao is righteous as well as strong. I spent some time begging in front of the Xuanshan School's doors. When others in the school yelled and tried to chase me off, she came to my rescue. She told them never to turn a blind eye to those in need--and even gave me a single precious dumpling.
Eating that dumpling, I felt myself change, deep in my soul. I must help others the way she helped me. And that's why my reports are late. I've spent much of my chronicling time chasing ferocious beasts away from her training grounds.
                                       - Chronicler Dust

1005.regionDesc: Here, stars are born and then return for their final rest--it is a planet at the crossroads of life and death. Here, stars born of new wishes have their first spark, and stars whose time is done have their final flicker.\r\nStar Guardian Sia Astelle bears witness to this cycle. She guides newborn stars to their full shine, and helps stars that are at their end pass on peacefully.

0.desc: An odd, globular creature that seems to have been carved from space itself. At the center of its head, a galaxy spins slowly. I could only look at it for a second--I felt as if I was being pulled in...\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

1.desc: An odd, globular creature that seems to have been carved from space itself. A meteor is trapped inside its head--maybe one that fell to Oort which it was particularly drawn to. But watching it move, I worry that it can't support the weight.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

2.desc: An odd, globular creature that seems to have been carved from space itself. If you look closely, you can see stars twinkling inside it--I believe that Seta captured some of the stars that floated into Oort's skies. \r\nThe subtle pink light that spreads from it may be escaping starlight, or simple bioluminescence. I haven't been able to tell.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

3.desc: A monster that takes the approximate shape of a human wearing a space helmet. It may be modeling itself after a former visitor to Oort. Some constellations told me that it was made of the memories of travelers who once frequented the land, but they may have just been trying to sound smart.\r\nIts body is made of stardust, and it can only maintain its shape for so long after forming. If left undisturbed, it will eventually disperse and blow away on the solar winds.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

4.desc: Okay, seriously, this thing is too cute, but don't let your guard down. Despite its short legs, it can move surprisingly quickly. If you see it wiggle its hindquarters in the air like a hunting cat, be especially careful--it's about to charge.\r\nI almost got bitten. Though that may be because I tried to pet it.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

5.desc: These creatures have a strong affinity for star flowers. Each one picks a live one and lets it grow on top of its head. When a group of them get together, the floral scent is overpowering. I wonder if they'd even taste like star flowers. Wait, that's a weird thing to write.\r\nRight, anyway, its body is made of stardust, and it can only maintain its shape for so long after forming. If left undisturbed, it will eventually disperse and blow away on the solar winds.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

6.desc: Its slow movements and blank expression might lead you to think this silly little creature is harmless, but that couldn't be further from the truth. Its secretions stunt the growth of star flowers and cause them to become diseased. If you were to grow a garden on Oort, this would be your main pest. \r\nObviously, it seems to really not like Flings, and vice versa.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

7.desc: She was once a constellation that could be seen in the Oort Cloud, but now shrouded in darkness. There is something almost mechanical about her transformed wings. Her movements remind me a bit of the butterflies that flit above the Arcane River.
