There's something striking about the way she looks, but there's nothing of the noble beauty I've heard about from stories of the old Bellatrix.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

8.desc: Once a Sider, now shrouded in darkness. In this form, it doesn't even wear a hat like the Sider does. Like it's lost interest in the things it used to like... There's nothing wrong with minimalism, but I think I prefer the other form.\r\n\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

9.desc: I hear this is a new addition to the ecology of Oort. I don't really like the look of it... Born of the eddying dark between planets, it looks pitch-black from far away. On closer inspection, you can see points of starlight embedded in its hide. If I were a star, I don't think I'd want my light to get stuck in there...\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

10.desc: This is another monster born of the eddying dark between planets, as if one weren't enough. It's easily confused for the Dark Aster except for the blue hue of its mane. It also exhibits more aggression than the Dark Aster, and is frequently seen baring its long, wickedly sharp teeth. Be careful of this one.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

0.desc: The constellation of shy shadows. No one has ever seen the face behind the mask, and therefore rumors abound about it.\r\nIzar is one of the hardest constellations to spot in the night sky, as he is extremely adept at hiding. Sirius told me that nothing in Oort is a greater challenge than getting Izar to speak. I'm not sure whether or not it was a joke.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

1.desc: The constellation of playful lies. According to Sirius, if you exclude the whole darkness incident, at least 80% of accidents in Oort's history are a result of Algol's pranks.\r\nEven with his reputation, he looks at you with such innocent eyes that you can't help falling for it anyway. Not that I'm speaking from experience. But if I were... Come on, who could resist that face?\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

2.desc: The constellation of cold truth. He seems to have decided it's his job to keep Algol in line... Or at least to scold him after a prank. When Sia Astelle is busiest, Vega is the strictest.\r\nOn the other hand, when Oort is quiet, he can be almost warm, bringing activity and excitement with him. Algol told me this is 'scarier than when he's mad.'\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

3.desc: The constellation of wanderers and adventure. He helps Sirius create meteor showers, guiding the starlight that Sirius scatters. Every time a meteor shower falls on the world, wishes are drawn to its light and gain the power to turn into stars.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

4.desc: The constellation of wariness and hesitation. He falls for Algol's lies more than anyone else. But even when Algol's not around, he spends most of his time running or hiding--I'm told that's just how he is.\r\nHe's undoubtedly one of the cutest constellations, and one of those who causes the most trouble, just like Algol--though unlike Algol, he doesn't seem to realize it.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

5.desc: The constellation of prayer and devotion. When Sirius and Canopus send out meteor showers, he takes responsibility for watching the wishes form around them.\r\nIf there is a problem, and wishes are not able to find the light, he uses his own light as a beacon, calling out to Sia Astelle.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

6.desc: The constellation of wisdom and secret knowledge. It seems whenever Sia Astelle is unsure of herself, she is ready with advice and reassurance.\r\nI found out for myself why she's called the wisest of the constellations. She's the only one who found out about my mapae.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

7.desc: The constellation of song and longing. He's known to be able to play any instrument, although I can't see how, since as a conch shell he doesn't have limbs, or breath, or any of the other things you usually need.\r\nWith Sirius's help, I did hear the song he sings any time a star is born or passes away. It lasted only a moment, but I'll never forget the sound.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

8.desc: The constellation of sweet oblivion. It's unclear to me what time means to the constellations that exist outside of its usual flow, but they seem to have their own sense of it. This constellation signals when it's time for a star to move on.\r\nThey share the start of their name, 'Sadal', with Sadalmelik. I have a dictionary from Ariant, given to me by Schegerazade, which translates the syllable 'sad' as 'luck'.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

9.desc: The constellation of the rise and fall of glory. During their brief stay on the ground, their beautiful trophy-esque shape sparked a great deal of envy and enmity between two factions in Kerning City. Sia told me that things have calmed down after they returned to Oort, though.\r\nThey share the start of their name, 'Sadal', with Sadalmelik. I have a dictionary from Ariant, given to me by Schegerazade, which translates the syllable 'sad' as 'luck'.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

10.desc: The constellation of brilliant devotion. When she flaps her wings, motes of starlight float in the air like dust, a mesmerizing sight. Her beauty and her air of mystery often draw comparisons to Izar.\r\nSirius told me that during the trouble with darkness around Oort, Bellatrix was briefly corrupted while trying to protect Sia Astelle. After it was over, Sia's dearest wishes brought her back to the light.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

11.desc: The constellation of beloved light. He's Sia Astelle's closest companion, and helps her protect Oort's peace.\r\nHe frequently carries Sia on his back, and told me that sometimes, she even falls asleep while riding. Sirius has been my guide to Oort, and the reason I have been able to see as much as I have. I'll never forget his thoughtfulness and warm welcome to a stranger from a different dimension.\r\n                                       - Chronicler Maru

1006.regionDesc: A planet that bears the blessing of the Star Creator, the entity that created all the stars of Hielo. The Star Creator is said to rest in the Katanos Sanctum in central Helia.\r\nAt one time, the entire planet was surrounded by an impassible barrier to protect it from external threats. Five pillars of light gave the barrier its power. The barrier was destroyed, but the pillars of light still remain.\r\nThe differing light from each pillar results in distinct vegetation around each one, the basis of Helia's unique ecosystem.

0.desc: A monster with long antennae that lives in the Tres region.\r\nIts antennae glow, possibly an adaptation for living in dark areas. It feeds primarily on insects that are attracted to the light of its antennae. Which is nice, but I wish it didn't look so much like a huge bug itself...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

1.desc: A monster that lives in the Tres region. Its long tail has a glowing bulb, possibly an adaptation for living in dark areas. Since its legs and arms are so short, it is heavily dependent on its tail for movement and fighting.\r\nThe way its stubby little arms rest against its round belly is way too cute. I almost got attacked again...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

2.desc: A monster with a huge forehead that lives in the Tres region. Its horn and tail glow, possibly an adaptation for living in dark areas.\r\nI underestimated this creature. I expected it to charge into opponents horn-first, but it emits beams of light from its head and tail to attack.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

3.desc: A monster living in the Tessera region that seems to be made of glowing rock. Its arms are short, but threateningly sharp-looking.\r\nIt looks as if it's a transformed chip off an asteroid, but in actuality, nothing is known about where Kleps come from.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

4.desc: A monster living in the Tessera region that seems to be made of glowing rock. Superficially, it looks similar to a Rabah from the Pente region, but Rabah's body is made of crystal while Twino's body is made of a glowing stone.\r\nThe crystal is much harder, which may be why Rabah looks so much stronger.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

5.desc: A monster living in the Tessera region that seems to be made of glowing rock. Its body contains two holes positioned to look like eyes, but there's no evidence that it actually sees through them. Kleps, on the other hand, only have one, but seem to navigate just as well.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

6.desc: A floral monster that lives in the Duo region. This region is the warmest in Helia, and gets the most light, so its ecosystem can support more flora than anywhere else.\r\nWhile it is pretty, be cautious of approaching. It shoots spores of light when it feels threatened.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

7.desc: A fauna-type monster that lives in the Duo region. Duo, with its large amounts of plant growth, can support more organic life than any other region of Helia.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

8.desc: A monster that lives in the Duo region which looks like a conglomeration of rocks and earth. Its behavior suggests it is quite shy, as it hides underground whenever other creatures are around.\r\nIt's not very good at hiding, though. The flowers growing out of its head are always visible.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

9.desc: A monster that lives in the Pente region, covered all over in a hard, crystal-like skin. As cute as it is, with its big, sparkly eyes, watch out if it starts to crouch down. It's preparing to lunge. Have you ever been lunged at by something made of crystal? Ouch.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

10.desc: This monster from the Pente region is not actually its own species--it's another stage of life of the Ter. As seen by its advanced crystal growth, it's what a Ter becomes when it gets older.\r\nI guess it's supposed to look like that, but this thing reminds me of myself when I was a gangly teen. Though I was never so cute in middle school.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

11.desc: This monster from the Pente region is not actually its own species--it's the adult form of the Ter and the Nos. The crystals of a fully-grown one are said to be the hardest material in Helia. I'm not sure if that's true, but it's definitely the most powerful monster I encountered anywhere in Helia.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

0.desc: Second captain of the Argent Guard who protects Duo, the Pillar of Light. Local gossips told me that he didn't seem to like Erel much at first, but that he seems to have changed his mind sometime around when the barrier fell.\r\nOpinions are split between those who think this is because he gained faith in Erel's handling of that incident, and those who think he's just happy not to be the youngest captain any longer. Era and Wren have been captains longer, so there may be something to that...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

1.desc: Third captain of the Argent Guard who protects Tres, the Pillar of Light. She's responsible recordkeeping and preserving the history of Helia, which is stored in the Tres Archives. It's said this has been the responsibility of third captains for as long as anyone can remember.\r\nTo me, she seems like the calmest and most collected of the captains, which feels appropriate for someone steeped in history.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

2.desc: Fourth captain of the Argent Guard who protects Tessera, the Pillar of Light. He's been a member of the Guard longer than anyone except for the former head captain, Archon. It's rumored that he was offered the position of head captain, but turned it down, due to his guilt over being corrupted by darkness.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

3.desc: Member of the fifth squadron of the Argent Guard. He came up through the ranks alongside Erel. I've heard stories that after Erel became a captain, he had a hard time remembering to call them by their new title.\r\nBut even so, it's undeniable he has great respect for Erel, despite their youth. I certainly never heard them call him anything but 'Captain'.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

4.desc: Erel's youngest sister. To me, she looks more like Erel than her older sister Lennie does. Anyone who sees them together would know that they're family. She's even recently followed Erel's footsteps and joined the Argent Guard.\r\nWhen I asked her why, though, she said it was for her sister Lennie.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

5.desc: Rua's younger brother, and the cause of most of her stress, from what I can tell. He'll tell anyone about how cool Erel is--his sister says that ever since Erel rescued him from a dangerous trip to Katanos, he's idolized them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

6.desc: Rowan's older sister. Taking care of her younger brother seems to take a lot out of her. She told me she's been looking after him since they were little, which explains both her strong sense of responsibility and her mountains of stress.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

7.desc: A resident of Katanos who's devoted to her puppy, Cookie. They can be seen on walks together almost constantly.\r\nShe even used to leave town on their walks, but has stopped doing that recently. She didn't seem to want to talk about why.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

8.desc: A resident of Katanos. She's close friends with Yani, who manages the General Store.\r\nShe seems to like to dress up Yani a lot. She told me that she's responsible for Yani's current hairdo. When I asked why she doesn't tie up her own hair, she seemed to have absolutely no interest in the idea.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

9.desc: Sophie's puppy. Sophie heard that it was lucky to name dogs after food, and that it let them live longer, hence Cookie.\r\nHe seems to run away constantly, but he always comes back safe, so there may be something to that.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

10.desc: A young merchant that manages the General Store in Katanos. She's quite young to run a shop by herself--I believe she's not even 20 yet--but the store seems to be thriving, so she must be doing a good job.\r\nShe is a bit of a workaholic, but it seems like her friend Polly takes good care of her. Apparently, Polly even ties her hair up every morning.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

11.desc: The Katanos Storage Room's Storage Keeper. I made a bit of a faux pas when I first met them, because I didn't realize they were in charge. But in my defense, they are an adorable sheep. I'm still not sure how they manage the safe without thumbs, but they must be good at it. The residents all seem to trust them completely.\r\n\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

12.desc:
A member of the Argent Guard, protectors of Helia. They all seem to take their job quite seriously, and take great pride in keeping their home safe.
I may have 'borrowed' one of their uniforms for my investigation. They're stationed all over Helia, and everyone talks to them, so can you blame me? Plus, with the hood and everything, the uniform just feels right--it's so similar to what I used to wear. My nose still hurts from putting the goggles on over my glasses, though. Does every guard just have perfect vision?

                                      - Chronicler Maru

13.desc: A Temple Keeper who manages the Temple of Light, dedicated to the Star Creator. Among many other duties, they have to shush noisy visitors to keep a respectful atmosphere for worshippers.\r\nOr so I hear. I definitely didn't receive a warning, or anything...\r\n                                      - Chronicler Maru

2.worldDesc: The grand river where Erda, the source of the world's life, flows towards a single point. In this place where the walls of reality have fallen, the Dreaming City, Mysterious Forest, and Swamp of Memory emerge as Erda flows into the Origin Sea.\r\nThis mysterious river is the last barrier before the Black Mage--a barrier of his own making. Now, at last, the Adversary has arrived at the place where they will defy fate itself and battle for Maple World's future.

0.regionDesc: The place where the river of Erda first presents itself. In the Vanishing Journey all are destined to fade into nothingness.\r\nThose touched by the river's unstable Erda lose all memories of joy and happiness, and transform into nameless beings of oblivion.

0.desc:
A being of condensed Erda that now has its own power and can move on its own volition. 
The light blue parts bring to mind the joyful and pale blue memories hanging from the Tree of Memory. 
According to Legato, these are the happy memories of those living, those who have passed on, and those who will be born. 
Perhaps that's why looking into them makes one feel such overwhelming secondhand joy. What a blessing that the happiest memories are the ones that remain with us the longest. 
Fortunately, since the memories hanging in the village belonged to the former residents themselves, they have successfully persisted.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
Happy Erdas don't seem to actually attack. Instead, they jump up and down, presumably with joy. It seems that such a feeling is so urgent that they simply cannot keep it inside.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
A being of condensed Erda that now has its own power and can move on its own volition. 
According to Rona, raging memories should emit reddish light. But these Raging Erda don't take on that hue. 
Clearly these are raging, angry entities emboldened with fiery emotions, and yet they remain unrouged. Further investigation will be needed. 
While angry memories may not be pleasant, rage eventually fades. Perhaps, despite the fiery feelings, this memory was treasured all the same and hung upon the tree. 
Despite all that, its appearance reminds me of a particular hairstyle. I don't know if it's just my imagination, but I simply cannot unsee it.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
Look. It's always angry, so don't go near it. It's rage itself. Stay out of trouble.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc:
A being of condensed Erda that now has its own power and can move on its own volition. 
According to Rona, sad memories are supposed to emit melancholic yellow auras. But I can't seem to find any yellow on the Sad Erdas. 
But one thing is evident. When one gazes upon a Sad Erda, one feels, undeniably, the crushing sorrow of another. 
Most people wouldn't want to remember sadness, but even despair can house a cherished memory. After all, these Erdas are proof in themselves!
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
It's said that the projectiles launched by Sad Erdas are actually tears. But, I must say, they're pretty painful for only being tears!
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc:
A being of condensed Erda that now has its own power and can move on its own volition. 
According to Rona, joyful memories emit a green light. But just like the other Erdas, the Joyful Erda does not emit green light. 
But if one gazes closely upon a Joyful Erda, one will clearly feel the borrowed joy of another blossoming in their heart. 
Such feelings of elation are treasured by all, so they're probably even more precious to Erdas.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt
Paradoxically, it attacks by radiating overflowing joy. Perhaps it takes the form of a young child because our happiest memories stem from that short, sweet period.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc:
A being of condensed Erda that now has its own power and can move on its own volition. 
It takes the dual form of a rock with a crab, each part likely adapted to survive the searing flames of its habitat.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
Their claws are unbelievably hard. I can't believe how hard an Erda cluster is. At this point, chroniclers might have to call upon scholars and see if they've discovered a new substance. 
I wonder if even King Clang's claws would seem soft in comparison.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
A being of condensed Erda that now has its own power and can move on its own volition. 
Unlike Stone Erdas, it looks like this variety has embraced the flames of destruction themselves. If one struggles with differentiating between Erdas and scorching, destructive flames, remaining at a distance is strongly advised. 
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
The Blazing Erda was frozen with Frostprey's help, before collecting the matter inside. 
Upon examining the mass at room temperature, the inside of the Blazing Erda consisted of a sticky, oil-like substance. I think this sticky oil might be how it burns continuously. 
On a separate note, this investigation was a substantial challenge. It stemmed from personal curiosity, but I don't recommend this method to other chroniclers. As one may surmise, the Blazing Erda is capable of inflicting burns.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
A being of condensed Erda that now has its own power and can move on its own volition. 
It survived the flames of destruction by formidably cocooning itself to endure the heat. 
The scars left by the flames have not healed within the cocoon, but sheer determination keeps it maintaining its form.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
While struck with a bout of curiosity, I inspected the outer layer. I can confirm that after the inside of the Soulful Erda expires, its outside remains. 
If one selects the right shell, specifically one resembling a conch, one may find something truly useful. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
A being of condensed Erda that now has its own power and can move on its own volition. It appears to be holding a lantern, as if in mourning for someone. 
However, what they mourn may seem quite unusual because they grieve creatures that have ceased to exist. 
They're quite hostile towards ordinary beings, so approach with caution.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
If joyful memories emit green light as Rona says, then the Tranquil Erda might actually be holding a joyful memory in its lantern.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc: A lantern left behind by a Tranquil Erda. Surprisingly, it's even stronger than the Tranquil Erda itself. \r\nThe light of the lantern moves with an ominous and hostile glow.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc:
These Erdas that resemble green caterpillars can be found in the deepest parts of the Cave of Repose. 
They may have thrived and evolved in tandem with the giant caterpillars inside the cave. 
They're dangerous entities that spew suspicious substances from their sizable bodies, so take heed when approaching.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc:
An Erda taking the form of a giant caterpillar, habituating itself in the deepest parts of the Cave of Repose. 
It's as powerful as it is large, and is probably the apex predator of the Vanishing Journey region.
The Guardians of Time deployed to Vanishing Journey speculate that this being has already died once...and has come back to life! All to be a big bug...
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc:
A representative from the Temple of Time who is currently investigating Reverse City and Vanishing Journey. 
She occasionally returns to the temple so she won't forget it. 
However, Nina broke her arm in the meantime, so now she can't leave her post.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
A representative from the Temple of Time who is investigating Erda. She also invented the Erda Collector in order to further their Erda research. 
Unfortunately, her overwhelming curiosity drove her to jump into the Erda while Rona was away, resulting in a broken arm. 
Now Rona is stuck watching over Nina.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: A resident working as a Storage Keeper in Nameless Town. The reason they work as a Storage Keeper is because it's all they remember and it's the only thing they know how to do. \r\nAs they slowly begin to lose their memories, they decide their job is what matters most.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: A resident working as a merchant in Nameless Town. They don't remember the past, and they aren't even sure if the faint memories they have remaining are real. \r\nThey believe that exchanging junk that comes into town and forging relationships are the only ways to protect their existence.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: Said to be the first resident to open their eyes in Nameless Town. They've been serving as emotional support for the more vulnerable residents, but they seem to be vanishing too. \r\nThey're hoping that the residents feel even the smallest amount of happiness as they succumb to this hopeless situation. They appear to believe that this therapeutic service is their calling.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc:
A resident of Nameless Town. It's said they have been with Poco since the moment they opened their eyes. 
Neither remembers their relationship to each other, but they firmly believe that they have a history. In a way, they justify the other's existence. 
Molto spends most of their time staring at the Tree of Memory.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc:
A resident of Nameless Town. It's said they were with Molto ever since they first opened their eyes. 
They're always by Molto's side, but unlike Molto, they find staring at the Tree of Memory to be pointless. 
However, they would never say such a thing out loud for fear of hurting Molto's feelings.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: A resident of Nameless Town. He operates a boat that routinely crosses the Lake of Oblivion. \r\nEven the boat is growing fainter, but Kima's only joy is rowing his boat.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: A Flame Bird native to the Vanishing Journey region. It can't be mounted by most journeyers, seeing as it's covered in flames, but it can be temporarily tamed with a special method. \r\nIt's very sensitive, so travelers should take care not to scare or provoke it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: Blue clothing left on the cliff of Damp Falls, at the border where Vanishing Journey ends. They originally belonged to the priests that guarded the Temple of Time, but are naught but remnants of faint memories, abandoned in the mist. \r\nAll that remains is a quiet plea for success where others have failed. With that longing breath, one might hear, #e"We will make sure our dreams come true."#n\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.regionDesc: A city turned upside down at the edge of Vanishing Journey, right across the Erda river. It used to be part of a parallel world called "Friends World," but it was swept up in a giant sinkhole and carried into the Arcane River.\r\nThe skyscrapers hang from the sky due to the flipped gravity, and people live in the Subway Tunnel Refuge to avoid endlessly falling upward.

0.desc: Erdas taking the shape of mice. This isn't their original form, but they're said to have adopted the shape of sewer rats after coming into contact with them while living in the tunnels. \r\nUnlike regular mice, they roll up into balls to move throughout the world. They're a staple food for residents of the Subway Tunnel, and surprisingly taste like popping candy.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: Erdas taking the shape of mice. This isn't their original form, but they're said to have adopted the shape of sewer rats after coming into contact with them while living in the tunnels. \r\nUnlike regular mice, they roll up into balls to move throughout the world. They're a staple food for residents of the Subway Tunnel, and surprisingly taste like popping candy. Perhaps they're...grape flavored? I'm curious, but am unwilling to find out.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: Search drones that appeared in Reverse City after the world turned upside down. Contrary to their name, they do much more than search. Should they register an intruder as a threat, they fire focused attacks. Caution is advised.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: Search drones that appeared in Reverse City after the world turned upside down. While they're classified as Models A and B, they don't seem too different. \r\nThey may fire laser attacks at targets, requiring utmost caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: Combat drones that appeared in Reverse City after the world turned upside down. They were commissioned to prevent the Subway Tunnel residents from coming out to the surface. Their leg movements are repulsive, like those of spiders. \r\nThey fire powerful pointed attacks, requiring caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: Combat drones that appeared in Reverse City after the world turned upside down. They were commissioned to prevent the Subway Tunnel residents from coming out to the surface. Model B seems to be a newer make than Model A. \r\nThey fire powerful laser cannons, so caution is strongly advised.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc:
An exterminator combat drone that appeared in Reverse City after the world turned upside down. It's extremely dangerous. Its makers hailed it as "the ultimate evolution of drone technology."
However, it appears to have adopted a method of imprisoning a living creature, a "Monto," inside itself, as it could not independently resolve the challenges of locomotion in an environment with inverted gravity. 
The Monto within it remains completely motionless. It very well may be unable to move.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc:
An exterminator combat drone that appeared in Reverse City after the world turned upside down. It's extremely dangerous, being called the ultimate evolution of drone technology.
However, since it was unable to independently resolve the issue of walking in an environment with inverted gravity, it appears to have opted to confine an Erda Rat within it. 
The fact that the living being inside has no involvement in the drone's movements and is simply locked inside demonstrates this machine's cruelty.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc: An elderly man in the Subway Tunnel Refuge. Given that the residents of Reverse City are composed of Erda, it seems odd to call him elderly, but he is using a walker and enjoys complaining about "kids these days."\r\nAs the seemingly oldest person in the refuge, he naturally demands respect. He's been known to wander around, "entertaining" people with his rambling stories, but Rasol doesn't take any of them to heart.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
A young girl in the Subway Tunnel Refuge. She's managed to maintain her bright, bubbly personality in this dark, humid tunnel.
While every other resident is seemingly satisfied with the underground life, she hasn't lost the drive to make her way to the surface. It's shocking just how positive and chatty she is, though she doesn't seem to listen to others very well.
Rumor has it that Barr possesses a few early drafts of a hit book written in Reverse City. If an adventurer asks Rasol, #e"Do you know How to Survive in Reverse City?"#n, she might just show you too.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: A resident of the Subway Tunnel Refuge. Judging by their prominent hood and mask, they seem to be averse to being perceived. They also don't appear to talk much. \r\nHowever, that doesn't mean that they're not cooperative. They are known to quietly listen to what others have to say.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: A resident serving as a Storage Keeper in the Subway Tunnel Refuge. They tried to cook as many different dishes as possible, but there are only so many ways to dress up rat meat.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A resident serving as a Merchant in the Subway Tunnel Refuge. While they agree that the Subway Tunnel is awful, they nevertheless find it safer than the surface world. \r\nThey also believe that Rasol is a terrible listener.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: A resident of the Subway Tunnel Refuge. She's rather misunderstood, as there's no child in the stroller she constantly push around. It functions as a cart and item storage.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A resident of the Subway Tunnel Refuge. If they let go of the balloon they're holding, it falls toward the ceiling, whereas if they hold onto it, it floats down toward the floor. \r\nThis is normal in Reverse City, so there's no need to think too deeply about it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.regionDesc: A bizarre paradise full of primary colors. The Erdas of this place are all mutated creatures that have fused with the various foods and animals in the area. So, while bizarre and monstrous, it's a lively scene.\r\nMuto, the gargantuan rock giant that protects the village from the ravenous Gulla, has lost all will to fight and is blocking the path forward. \r\nWhy is it that Muto doesn't want to fight anymore?

0.desc:
Deer that reside in Five-Color Hill. The pine in front isn't Fine. It's Pine.
The natural inclination would be to eat the head, but apparently the hooves are the sweetest part. I find that rather difficult to believe. (However, I have not personally had the chance to verify if the head or hoof is tastier, so proceed at your own caution.)
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
As a fantastical maestro of Maple World's gourmet and grotesque foods, I could not help but to indulge myself in further investigation of the various ingredients that can be found on Chu Chu Island. (The following content was written with the advice of Chef Simia.)
The Pinedeer is as edible as it appears, with its hooves in particular boasting quite a high sweetness Brix level.
The best way to prepare the Sweet Hoof is by making a Fried Treat, a crispy fried dish that is gasp-worthy at first bite.
The strong, oily taste of being deep fried works perfectly with the sweetness of the deer's hoof.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc:
Deer that reside in Five-Color Hill. The pine in front isn't Fine. It's Pine. 
Compared to the Pinedeer, it has larger horns and looks like it has a worse temper. Maybe that's why they say its hooves are a bit spicy. Believe it or not, Simia has somehow figured out how to cook these up to taste like BREAD, of all things.r
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
Bighorn Pinedeers are also edible and, like the Pinedeer, the hooves are considered the acme of delicacies. The Bighorn Pinedeer's hooves have been named Spicy Hoof for their flavor and are best enjoyed cooked into the well-known dish, Fried Squish. While the name may sound suspect, it is the perfect amount of spice and warms the body from head to toe with just one bite. The highlight of the dish is that it is stir-fried with ingredients with a popping kick to them.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
Sheep that reside in Five-Color Hill, with the body of a banana and the head of a sheep. Ewenana is the female variety of this particular species.
Simia prefers to only use the peel of the banana in dishes, ignoring the meat entirely. Is it sheep? Or banana? Is it normal to eat the peel of a banana?
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
The edible part of the Ewenana is the peel. Surprisingly, it tastes quite greasy, hence the name, Greasy Peal.
I don't recommend eating it as-is, but instead cooking into a Savory Stir Fry. Simply julienne the Greasy Peal and stir-fry it with the correct ingredients and condiments to combat the greasiness.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
Sheep that reside in Five-Color Hill, with the body of a banana and the head of a sheep. Ramanana is the male variety of this particular species. The males tends to be more aggressive, so take caution while hutning them.
Simia still insists that one should only cook with the peel. I'm slowly beginning to wonder if I was always meant to eat a banana whole, peel and all.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
Just like the Ewenana, the edible part of Ramanana is the peel. Truly surprisingly, it tastes sour, hence the name, Sour Peel. While it is decent ENOUGH to eat fresh, that doesn't mean you should.
The dish Dumpling Delights will bring out the best flavor profile of these peels, but I don't particularly like it. It made me laugh, in a depressed, 'what has this world come to,' kind of laugh. Just imagine chewing on a warm, delicious dumpling, and then suddenly being hit in your taste buds with a sour candy. That's what it tastes like.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
A wolf that resides in Slurpy Forest. Of course, it isn't a normal wolf and looks like an unripe apple. 
One thing I can't understand no matter how hard I try is that it looks like an apple slice normally, but turns into a whole apple when attacking. 
Anyway, the point is that the soles of the feet taste good.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
The most delicious part of the Unripe Wolfruit is the soles of its feet, called the Soft Sole for its fluffy texture. It's surprisingly delicious even its raw form. A first, for the creatures of this island. I did quite enjoy it cooked into a Steamy Surprise as well. The steaming process makes the fluffy soles soak up the flavors of the other ingredients, creating an unaesthetic, but satisfying dish.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
A wolf that resides in Slurpy Forest. Unlike the Unripe Wolfruit, it looks nice and ripe. Do Unripe Wolfruit become Ripe Wolfruit when they get older? I'm curious, but there isn't enough time to investigate, so I may never know. 
Anyway, just like the Unripe Wolfruit, the soles taste good.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
The edible part of the Ripe Wolfruit is the soles, just like the Unripe Wolfruit. It's called Chewy Sole for its naturally chewy and spring texture.
The dish that makes its characteristics stand out best are Juicy Buns. This chewy bread makes you laugh the same, hallow laugh that Dumpling Delights do.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
A lion that resides in Slurpy Forest. ...Is it a lion? It does look like a lion... They say it's a lion, so I guess it's a lion.
Apparently, the mane is the best part to eat, but it's still considered meat. But it's a flower, so how is it not a vegetable?
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
It's hard to tell just from its appearance, but the Flyon is surprisingly edible. Its Fresh Mane IS fresh, but rather bland.
There isn't one particular dish that the Fresh Mane is used for, as it's closer to a condiment than an ingredient. I suppose its best used in a Berry Bouquet, but considering how that one tastes... Well, I'm sure some people enjoy it.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
A lion that lives in Slurpy Forest. It must be the more temperamental version of a Flyon, seeing as it's called Angry Flyon. But even when you pluck its mane, a Flyon won't turn into an Angry Flyon. So what does it take to make it that mad? I wish I had more time to find out.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
The Angry Flyon's Zesty Mane is both edible and zesty. It's superior to the Fresh Mane in that it's considered the main attraction of any dish it's cooked into.
It's popularly used in making Spicy Sausages. The flavor it adds really gives... Well, I'll simply say that I've never tried a dish that so accurately captures the highs and lows of existence.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc:
A type of fish that lives in the rapids that flow near Chu Chu Village. Just as its name implies, it's a fish with the face of a cat.
If one expected a more traditional fish with two whiskers, they have underestimated Chu Chu Village. It's sporting a bright green color that makes it easy to spot.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
The color may seem otherwise, but this Green Catfish is actually edible. Its Savory Fins should not be eaten raw, however, unless you enjoy snacks that cut up the inside of your mouth.
Stew the Savory Fins until it becomes soft enough to eat, and enjoy it as Nummy Noodles.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc:
A type of fish that lives in the rapids that flow near Chu Chu Village. Just as its name implies, it's a fish with the face of a cat.
This one seems to breathe through its mouth and nose instead of gills, but then how does it survive in the water? Chu Chu Island is full of mysteries.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
The Blue Catfish's Tart Fins are extremely sour and should not be eaten raw.
They're commonly used as an ingredient in Funky Pizza. If I had to describe it... It would be like putting tart pickles atop a perfectly good pizza.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc:
Is it a rhinoceros? Is a turtle? Well, according to the name, I guess it's both. It's commonly found around the rapids near Chu Chu Village. Pimi says that the shell is edible, but she and I have similar tastes, so I wouldn't necessarily trust that 
If you want a taste, try not to get impaled by its nose in the process.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
It's hard to tell just by its appearance, but the Rhyturtle's Crunchy Shell is edible. However, I would not recommend attempting to eat it raw, as its rough properties will likely cause your tongue to bleed.
Instead, it is a fantastic ingredient for Gamey Soup, which will add the necessary moisture to enjoy the shell. You need only cut the Crunchy Shell into small pieces and add it to your soup for a delicious, warm meal.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc:
The leader of the turtles that lives in the rapids near Chu Chu Village. It has a darker shell and an even meaner glare. 
What really differentiates it is its giant horn, which you should avoid getting hit by at all costs.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
Like the Rhyturtle, the Boss Rhyturtle is also edible. Funnily enough, its Soft Shell is the complete opposite: chewy and full of moisture.
The Soft Shell is best enjoyed in a Chewy Porridge, chopped up and added when the porridge is nearly finished. The flavor it adds is simply impeccable.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc:
A bird(?) that lives in Skywhale Mountain. For all intents and purposes, it is some type of crow, but with the head of a gorilla. Personally, I don't like either of them, so this is a nightmare in bird-form. It creates tornadoes with every flap of its ridiculously strong wings, so it's nearly impossible to get near one (which I didn't want to do anyway).
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
It's hard to tell just from its appearance, but the Crilia's feathers are apparently edible. I say 'apparently,' because I personally find it rather impossible to believe, but I've decided to trust Simia for the time being.
People enjoy making a Weird Wrap out of Slimy Feathers. Don't forget to add Fresh Mane and Savory Fins to your wrap, or the sliminess will be difficult to get past. Well, the appearance itself is difficult to get past, which is why I did not try it.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc:
The patriarch of the Crilia that reside in Skywhale Mountain. You can identify it by the red thorns and blue feathers around its head and neck.
No one knows where the blue feathers came from, though...
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
Like Crilia, Patriarch Crilia also has edible feathers. According to Simia, which I am again doubtfully trusting, its Sticky Feathers can be made into Yucky Pickles. I find the entire thing rather unsettling, but mixed together with some Tart Fins and Zesty Mane, it's said to make a sticky, tart, and zesty pickles.
I can do many things in this world, but trying this abomination of food is not one of them.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

14.desc:
A bird that resides in Skywhale Mountain. It flies through the sky so it's recorded as being a bird, but I'm not so sure anymore. At least, it can fly, so I'm recording it as a bird, but it's very questionable.
Pidol says to be careful because the Birdshark has sharp teeth and a strong jaw. He failed to mention the orca-shaped energy rays it shoots out as well, which I discovered when I met one.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
Another strange and edible monster, the Birdshark is best enjoyed by its Unpleasant Talons. At least, that's what Simia says. Why must one eat its stale claws when there is so much meat to be had? I could not tell you, and I don't believe I'd like to know, either.
The Unpleasant Talon is often used in Berry Bouquets, but honestly, the dish is just a medley of ingredients thrown together. One bite, and you'll be gasping for a glass of water, due its strange combination of flavors.
...I wouldn't have eaten it if I'd known what went in it. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc:
The patriarch of the Birdsharks that reside in Skywhale Mountain. It's easy to spot, as it's a different color entirely and wears a red ring of thorns around its waist. What stands out the most are its blue wings. Ah! I finally understand where the blue feathers on Patriarch Crilia came from.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
Just like the Birdshark, the Patriarch Birdshark has edible talons, known as Chewy Talons.
I really do wish I could be free of these strange dishes, but people apparently enjoy making Spicy Sausages out of them. Apparently the chewiness does resemble a sausage quite well, but after the Berry Bouquet, I believe I've quite had my fill of strange talons.
Simia has quite the...questionable taste in food. I'm rather craving a nice, homecooked meal from Henesys now.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc: The village's self-proclaimed best cook, but when compared to Maple World as a whole, the dishes are...far from traditional. Still, the villagers seem to enjoy the dishes, so the reputation IS earned. There's no accounting for taste, I guess. Please don't repeat my words in front of the cook himself, however.\r\nIf you approach him and politely say #e"I would like one of your recipes."#n, he very well may teach you. However, it'll likely be insane, so proceed at your own caution.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
The village elder. A true leader who claims to be a mere philanthropist. He's strangely boisterous, but based on his frequent meowing, he's a proper resident of Chu Chu Island. 
He has a tendency to resort to physical solutions, so one should not let their guard down around him.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
He wears a cape with a rather familiar emblem, along with his trademark friendly expression. Many in Chu Chu Chu Village appear to be chimeras of sorts, so what does that make Lyon...? No, it can't be.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc: The merchant of Chu Chu Island. The most fiscal-minded individual in the village. After years of collecting knick-knacks, she's become the de-facto speculator of Chu Chu Village. \r\nShe never gives discounts, so don't try to haggle.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: The Storage Keeper of Chu Chu Island. As his beaver-like appearance would indicate, his giant storage facility was originally a pile of tree branches he collected to build his house. When it ended up bigger than expected, he pivoted his plans entirely. \r\nHis residence may be made of wood, but wooden structures are what beavers do best. So one can be assured their items will be safe under his care.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: The youngest of the baby chick siblings, who were banished to their lonely corner of the village because of their strange tastes. He's a bit touched in the head, but can pull out a biting remark or two when the situation calls for it.\r\nIt's hard to tell for certain if he's actually crazy or not, but I believe it's all an act.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: The second oldest of the baby chick siblings, who were banished to their lonely corner of the village because of their strange tastes. She seems to be the most normal of the three. However, it was because Pimi made fun of Master Lyck's palate and accused everyone in the village of being tasteless that the three were banished in the first place. So maybe 'normal' is subjective. If there were a leader between the siblings, it would be her.                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: The youngest of the baby chick siblings, who were banished to their lonely corner of the village because of their strange tastes. The embodiment of macho with muscles up to the brain. Yet he can't say a thing to Pimi. \r\nHe claims to be the strongest creature across Chu Chu, but without much merit.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: The highly energetic monkey girl who serves as Master Lyck's sous chef. The only Chu Chu Village resident that has any amount of common sense and a good cook to boot. However, the residents of Chu Chu Village don't seem to think so. She experiences everything those with common sense suffer through when surrounded by those without any.                                      - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: A massive Erda that blocks Arcane River. He is the only entity that can stop the other massive Erda on Chu Chu Island, Gulla, from attacking Chu Chu Chu Village. Seeing as how he's always been able to eat all of Master Lyck's terrible food without complaint, he likely has a very understanding personality.\r\nHe seems to think he's playing with Gulla, but no one else, including Gulla, shares his sentiment.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.regionDesc: The hidden shadow to Chu Chu Island's bright colors that serves as a strange laboratory filled with unique Erdas.\r\nMutants, having taken strange forms that are something between creature and object, find shelter here. There are traces of creation left behind by an unknown person.

0.desc: It looks like a monkey, but one with horns and wings. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Balrog and Lupin. It will attack on sight.\r\nAll those who awaken on Yum Yum Island have only faint memories of where they came from, along with an uncontrollable desire for chaos. Caster claims that his sense of control is what sets him apart from the others.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: Something that looks like a mushroom, but with ears. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Mushmom and Moon Bunny. Upon closer inspection, it even has whiskers. \r\nThe glint in its eyes makes it very clear that it's not your average bunny-mushroom.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: Something that looks like a cow, but with a body of rock and wood. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Lyka and Golem. \r\nI believe the boundaries of what is considered a 'creature' are getting rather blurred at this point. But I also believe that such ponderings aren't much use on Yum Yum Island.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc:
Something that looks like a huge tree, but mixed with stone. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Stumpy and Golem.
It's rather reminiscent of bonsai, and the butterflies are a charming touch.
It prefers to attack with its branches, rather than the rock on the bottom. I assure you it's equally as painful, however.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc:
Something that looks like a spider that was carved out of stone. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Zakum and Big Spider. It's a wonder how it even ended up like this. 
It's particularly noteworthy that it has six spider legs. Even Zakum has eight arms, so why does a spider have six...?

                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: Something that looks like a squirrel, but with four horns, and wings on its back. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Manon and a squirrel.\r\nIt is the cutest creature in the creepy Fungos Forest. I wonder what its Acorn Breath smells like... Regardless, it's very painful to be hit by it, and its creepy eyes suggest that petting one would be a very bad idea.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: Something that looks like a bee, but with fins instead of wings. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Pianus and Hornet. The scar on its forehead is a dead giveaway.\r\nA flying Pianus... The Hornet isn't at all tame, so when the two together is a hostile combination.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: Something that looks like a bee, but with fins instead of wings. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Pianus and Hornet.\r\nUpon tracking down what could be its origins, I discovered groups of them bursting out from flowers. It would be best to give them a wide berth.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc: Something that looks like a bee, but with fins instead of wings. It's theorized to be the combination of Erda from Maple World's Pianus and Hornet.\r\nUnlike other Piabee, it has a purple coloration. Perhaps it's because it contains the Erda of a Poison Hornet, instead of a regular one?\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc: Mrs. Piggy claims she was born from a flower with the feeling that she once served a powerfully charismatic queen, all while wearing a fancy dress. There has never been queens in Yum Yum Island, or dresses for that matter, however. She wandered about aimlessly for quite some time, until Caster recommended she take on the role of storage keeper.\r\nShe seems to enjoy Yum Yum Village, with the oddly familiar Caster, Bappy, and Treecat.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc:
A three-headed dog born from a flower on Yum Yum Island. Its name reminds one of the (once) terrifying dragon of Maple Island, but in person, its charm is tripled, just like its heads.

Puptail did try asking it a question, out of a sense of kinship, but the three heads only licked his hand.

                                      - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc:
Caster says the first thing he saw upon waking from the flower was a familiar rising sun. Since he has no other way to prove his existence, Caster hopes that the sun will illuminate his path forward.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
A chameleon and chicken... It reminds me of the Guardians that attack Root Abyss from Maple World. Upon further thought, that chicken-like Guardian was named Von Bon. There were chameleons in the garden that Von Bon was protecting, so it could be a mix of the two.

                                      - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc:
A parrot born from a flower on Yum Yum Island. It looks so much like Bappy that it seems impossible that they both exist.
Just like Bappy, it's unsophisticated and speaks only of parties, which makes it difficult to discern the difference between the two. Besides the fact that Muppy is blue, and Bappy is red.
When I asked #e"What do you have there?"#n it told me that it picked up a note that was tossed on the ground. It doesn't appear to know how to read, however.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc:
A parrot born from a flower on Yum Yum Island. It claims to have been aware of its incompleteness the moment it opened its eyes, as it did not have its fated partner with them.
It seems to be constantly battling the compulsion to hold parties, has a great need for a partner, and is doing its best to not give into the instinct to sow chaos.

                                      - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: Treecat remembers flashing lights, clowns, and a wonderful tea party. It can't remember what it looked like at the time, but it care much.\r\nWhat it does know is that it's cute, and that's all that seems to matter. Mostly because Treecat learned very quickly that being cute can lead to money.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.regionDesc: A city with an eternal fireworks display under a purple night sky. The Erda of this place takes shape in the form of a grand festival and an unending masquerade, creating a dangerous city that makes the onlooker lose their minds with saccharine temptations.\r\nResidents in glamorous masks dance in the eternal loop of joy, but on the other side lies a horrendous nightmare that prevents people from ever waking up from that dream as they lose all sense of self.

0.desc: A chicken that has fun jumping around the Night Market, where the food fight happens. Or should be it just be called poultry?\r\nEither way it's full of energy. The tomatoes it throws hurt quite a bit.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: A chicken that has fun jumping around the Night Market, where the food fight happens. It could be a turkey, but that doesn't matter.\r\nIt smells quite delicious and could even be taken in as a pet.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc: A plate that Pie Mask earned by winning a food fight competition. He earned so many that Victory Plate Street was filled with them.\r\nThe sound it makes when broken is quite pleasant. After all, the true value of a plate is when it shatters.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: A plate that Pie Mask earned by winning a food fight competition. He earned so many that Victory Plate Street was filled with them.\r\nOnly the color of the decoration separates it from the Angry Victory Plate. The sound it makes when shattered is also the same. Why it's even called a Crooked Victory Plate is a mystery. Should this be investigated more?\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: The lower-floor citizens who, failing to find proper masks, have donned paper bags on their heads.\r\nThey focus on stealing masks, so they can participate in the festival. The masks may be the actual faces of other citizens, but they don't care.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: The lower-floor citizens who, failing to find proper masks, have donned wood plans on their heads.\r\nThey focus on stealing masks, so they can participate in the festival. Has anyone ever successfully stole a mask and been able to participate? If so... did they find happiness?\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc:
A Lachelein resident that couldn't wake up from the dream. Even while enjoying the festival, when they enter the masquerade, their deepest violent nature comes to light.

They are dangerous entities that have a twisted greed seeking to steal masks that they envy even if it means killing the original wearer.

                                      - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: A Lachelein resident who is trapped in the dream. The festival is no longer a place to dance and sing, but one to destroy the opponent. This has come about, not due to greed or anger, but because the residents h ave been consumed by madness.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: Lucid's influence in Lachelein has loosened, and so her followers have weakened.\r\nWith the Awakened Ones already out, they have no more options for survival. Not even Lucid can save them, so it would be merciful to give them a painless end.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc:
Red Dancing Shoes that dance even if no one is wearing them. They may be your size, but if you put them on, you'll yourself dancing for the rest of your days.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
While I was listening to Chronicler J.K., a pair of these stomped on my pinky toe. It was so painful, I fainted for a period of times. This record is both a warning and a question... Where in the world did they go?

                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc: Lucid's underlings who ensure that the dream of Lachelein remains undisturbed. Those who wake up are taken by the Dreamkeepers and extinguished. However, just like the other residents of Lachelein, Lucid can eliminate them as she sees fit.\r\nBoth the residents of Lachelein and the Dreamkeepers are Lucid's creations.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc:
A statue that guards the Clocktower.
The blue flame burning within it makes its eyes glow a radiant blue. Any who wish to enter the Clocktower must first defeat this stone statue.

                                      - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: A statue that guards the Clocktower. \r\nThe blue flame burning within it makes its eyes glow a radiant blue. Any who wish to enter the Clocktower must first defeat this stone statue.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc:
A loyal elf of Elluel. She was born with the ability to control dreams and fragments of fantasy. She once trained in combat alongside Athena Pierce.
She looked up to the elven queen, Mercedes, but resented the queen for, in her eyes, favoring Athena Pierce. The self-perceived inadequacy drove her to bitterness and solitude.
Due to her powers, when the elves of Elluel were cursed and trapped in ice, Lucid remained conscious in her dreams. She slowly lost her mind in the endless cycle of dreams and nightmares. Therefore, when the Black Mage approached her, she easily fell victim to his promise of power. As his commander, she unleashed her power of dreams upon the world.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

0.desc: The Storage Keeper on Lachelein Main Street. I've never seen a Storage Keeper so lavishly dressed, but he must have his reasons. He's worried his fine mask and glamorous outfit will get dirtied by the raucous festivities.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc: The merchant of Lachelein Main Street. Unlike Stylish Gentleman Mask, he's enjoying the festival to the fullest.\r\nHe never seems to stop drinking, to the point that I'm quite curious where all that liquid goes. Despite his inebriated state, he's never miscalculated a single transaction.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc:
A resident who seems to be enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Main Street.
At some point, he became aware that Lachelein was just a shell of a world created by Lucid, but Shrimp Mask continued to play their part as if their life hung in the balance.
Later, he was rescued by the Adversary from the eternal play.
                                     - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: A member of the Lachelein resistance who aims to gather Awakened Ones from around town. After learning that the residents of Lachelein are mere Erdas, she were was into bouts of existential dread.\r\nHowever, she continues to do all she can to save everyone she can. If one were to ask, #e"Can you take off that mask?"#n she would happily oblige. And when she does, it's easy to see that she is a good person both inside and out.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A resident of Lachelein that keeps the party going with his flute. His brother is Piper Mask.\r\nSince he's too busy playing his instrument, he doesn't have much to say. His skill in playing his instrument is impressive.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc: A resident of Lachelein that keeps the party going with his flute. His brother is Flutist Mask. Contrary to his plain clothing, he's quite sensitive to dress codes.\r\nI personally prefer Flutist Mask's playing to his brother's.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc: A perfectly content resident of Lachelein. \r\nA childhood friend of Rabbit Mask, although he doesn't know where Rabbit Mask is from, or how the two even met. He just insists that the two were childhood friends, and that the party is so, so much fun.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc:
A perfectly content resident of Lachelein. 
A childhood friend of Cat Mask, although he doesn't know where Cat Mask if from, or how the two even met. He just insists that the two were childhood friends, and that the party is so, so much fun.
Do these two even know each other?
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: A perfectly content resident of Lachelein. \r\nShe's happily singing songs and enjoying the festival, as if she hadn't a care in the world. She looks happy to be sure, but her vague humming gives Lachelein and the endless festival a creepy atmosphere.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc:
A perfectly content resident of Lachelein. 
She sings that eating is bliss, and that continuously eating is a source of unending happiness. Yet, she isn't eating anything.
Seeing as how Beauty Mask can be found in the Night Market as well, she really is making the most of the festival.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: A resident who has realized that Lachelein is all a part of Lucid's machinations. He, along with Protective Mask, is gathering Awakened Ones in a back alley. \r\nHe calls himself Gray Mask, but he doesn't seem to be quite so old as he presents himself. However, it's to be expected that nothing is as it seems in Lachelein.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: A perfectly content resident of Lachelein. \r\nWith a wreath of flowers on their head, they're enjoying their time in the festival with a nice cocktail. Don't waste your time trying to talk to them.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc: A chef and judge of the food fight competition, which has now been held 65,535 times.\r\nSeeing as there has never been a single complaint about the food across 65,535 competitions, no one can doubt his skills in the kitchen.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc:
A perfectly content resident of Lachelein, who's currently participating in a food fight. 
The eternal rival of Pie Mask, who's lost against Pie Mask in food fight 65,535 times now. 
Note: there are only ever two competitors.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc: A resident who seems to be enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Night Market. \r\nIt seems he was aware that something was strange in Lachelein, but played his part perfectly. With the help of the Adversary, he manages to escape the eternal play.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

15.desc: A resident who is enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Night Market.\r\nIt's impossible to understand what he's saying. His esoteric manner of speaking could possibly only be topped by Circus Mask. He seems to enjoy Balloon Mask's pizza a lot.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

16.desc: Circus Mask's pet chicken, but based on its size, it's closer to a turkey. \r\nIt has no feathers, no venom, and is just not important when garlic is being tossed around.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

17.desc: A resident who is enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Night Market. \r\nHe's practically incomprehensible, but it's clear that he truly loves his pet chicken, Elizabeth. Elizabeth is his love and dream, his moonlight. I feel a bit weird about writing that down on paper.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

18.desc:
A resident who seems to be enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Ballroom. 
At some point, he became aware that Lachelein was just a shell of a world created by Lucid. His cynical personality fits his name, Dark Mask. He danced among the residents in their hazy state of bliss to hide that he had awoken.
Later, he managed to escape with the Adversary's help.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

19.desc:
A resident who is enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Ballroom. 
He claims to be happy, but it seems like something was stolen from him by a Insane Masquerade Citizen. He keeps claiming that they need more education. It must be true based on how he claims they need more education.
Looking closely into his eyes, there's an eerie emptiness to them.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

20.desc: A resident who is enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Ballroom.\r\nShe's seriously enjoying the dance. She has fire-red hair and is wearing crimson dress. She claims to have seen someone from Maple World in her dream...\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

21.desc: A resident who is enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Ballroom.\r\nShe is accompanying Noblewoman Mask, but they don't seem to know much about each other. That is to be expected of people who come to a party wearing masks. To them, what people look under the mask is unimportant.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

22.desc: A resident who is enjoying the festival in the Lachelein Ballroom.\r\nShe is accompanying Bird Beak Mask, but they don't seem to know much about each other. Or perhaps they're just pretending not to know each other. As long as the masks stay on, it's only polite to pretend to not know their identity.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.regionDesc: This mystical forest is home to countless spirits basking in moonlight. The Erda of this place forms spirits of water, wind, sun, and plants, living in harmony to maintain what may be the purest ecosystem in all of the Arcane River.\r\nHowever, after an unknown evil energy swept through this peaceful forest, the Spirit Tree that maintained the forest's life began to rot, and the once harmonious songs of nature have been silenced. This peaceful place now holds danger in every shadow.

0.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Water Spirits.
Their domain, water, is one of the three basic elements that nourishes a forest. These ones have turned violent because of the evil energy that has consumed their home.
If you squint, they look a bit like a jellyfish. Or maybe some kind of squid. Something that lives underwater, is the point.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Sun Spirits.
Their domain, sun, is one of the three basic elements that nourishes a forest. These ones have turned violent because of the evil energy that has consumed their home.
I don't understand the shape of this one. It doesn't look like the sun at all. Strange creature.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Earth Spirits.
Their domain, earth, is one of the three basic elements that nourishes a forest. These ones have turned violent because of the evil energy that has consumed their home.
I don't need to put in writing what this reminds me of, do I? A big, steaming pile of... Well, you know.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Snow Cloud Spirits.
These were once simple cloud spirits, but the influence of the forest's evil energy imbued them with a bitter cold.
The presence of one of these spirits causes such a temperature differential in the surroundings that they're constantly followed by strong winds.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Thunder Cloud Spirits.
These were once simple cloud spirits, but the influence of the forest's evil energy imbued them with crackling electricity. They look quite similar to the Snow Cloud Spirits due to their shared origin.
I think these things would look right at home among the aliens of the Omega Sector. Something about the shapes and the colors...
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Toxic Spirits.
They were once Sun Spirits, but corruption has transformed them utterly into a much more dangerous form. If you get too close, just breathing in their powerful venom seems to paralyze your sense of smell.
You'll know this thing is coming before it gets too close because of its terrible scream. People say that even fallen trees stand up straight when they hear it...but then again, people say a lot of silly things.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Volatile Spirits. 
They were once Earth Spirits, but corruption has transformed them utterly into a much more dangerous form. For some reason, they've also developed a most unpleasant stink. Almost like...no, it can't be.
You'll know this thing is coming before it gets too close because of its explosive scream. People say that it's loud enough to make fallen trees fall again... But honestly, I have no idea what that's supposed to mean.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc:
These Befuddled Spirits live beneath Arcana. 
They are created from the evil energy that has intertwined with the roots of the Spirit Tree. The influence of these spirits slowly corrupted the forest's Spirit of Harmony, turning it around and around to make it lose its physical and metaphorical way.
It's bad news, but it's still pretty cute... It must be so confusing to have two heads.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc:
These Mournful Spirits live beneath Arcana. 
They are created from the evil energy that has intertwined with the roots of the Spirit Tree. The influence of these spirits slowly corrupted the forest's Spirit of Harmony, causing it overwhelming sadness.
What about this thing is mournful? The spikes? The angry expression? To me, it just seems vicious.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc:
These Anguished Spirits live beneath Arcana. 
They are created from the evil energy that has intertwined with the roots of the Spirit Tree. The influence of these spirits slowly corrupted the forest's Spirit of Harmony, causing it overwhelming pain.
One of the more aggressive of the spirits. It'll attack anyone in range. It's certainly caused this chronicler some anguish...
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc:
These Discordant Spirits live beneath Arcana. 
They are created from the evil energy that has intertwined with the roots of the Spirit Tree. The influence of these spirits slowly corrupted the forest's Spirit of Harmony, like a moldy potato causing the rest of the food in your cupboard to go bad.
Actually, if you left a potato in the back of your cupboard for long enough to grow mushrooms, it might look a bit like these things. And smell like them, too.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc:
A Spirit of Harmony that has been corrupted by evil energy.
It was once brightly colored and transparent, but that form has been lost, along with all emotion in its eyes. It's also grown out of proportion, as if it's struggling to contain the evil energy.
This creature needs help to regain its original form. Someone ought to do something.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc:
This sort of Spirit Debris can be found all across Arcana. 
No one truly knows where it comes from. I've heard it theorized that this debris is shed from dying or wounded spirits, that it's naturally-occurring Erda that has yet to take form, and all sorts of other stories.
If given enough time, this debris may one day form into a true spirit of its own.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc:
This spirit can be found selling its wares under the Spirit Tree. 
It looks strikingly similar to the Small Spirit. Are they related? The same species, or from the same family? Not enough is known about spirits to understand one way or another.
Though its eyes are closed, it's not sleeping. So don't try anything.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
This spirit can be found under the Spirit Tree, and will hold onto items for you. 
This spirit looks quite similar to the Small Spirit, but not as much as the Industrious Spirit does. Still unsure what this signifies about their relationships. Its key seems to be a part of its body. There's no corresponding safe anywhere I can see. I am not sure where, exactly, it puts the items it holds.
I've never heard a story about it losing items, but still, I'm not giving it my prized possessions.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Rock Spirits.
They's often seen stacked on top of one another in a cairn. They seem to prefer travelling in a pack. I don't know what good these things are, but they are extremely cute, so that's something.
They have a lot of energy and a rather childlike manner. When many of them gather in one spot, the resulting scene can be...overwhelming.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc:
