The spirit that dwells inside great tree at the very center of Arcana. 
As large as it is, I didn't expect it to be so shy. It seems to enjoy the company of the other spirits, but it never says a word to them. Perhaps it's taking all its courage just to be here.
This spirit is a true hero who tried to contain all the evil that once plagued this forest. I asked, #e"Are you getting along with the other spirits?"#n and got a bashful smile in return. It's good to see it happy.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc:
This spirit's small and quite prone to crying.
It tried to save its forest, but it really wasn't strong enough to accomplish much of anything.
It's unclear what type of spirit this is, exactly. The best theory I've heard is that it's a Dew Spirit, because of its tearful nature and how it can be found everywhere in the forest.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc:
These are Arcana's resident Tree Spirits. 
They didn't previously move about in groups like this, but ever since one of them went missing, they gather together warily whenever an outsider comes near.
They were the only witnesses to Tana's passage through the forest.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.regionDesc: The foggy swamp Morass was created as the river of Erda hit a bend, creating a stagnant pool that reflects the nature of those who visit it. Physical manifestations of Fragments of Time can be found here, and the violent afterimages of the fallen kingdom Kritias hold on tenaciously.\r\nThe Adversary learns the sad story of a mysterious girl named Tana in the midst of the phantoms created by the Swamp of Memory. Then, they must shake themselves free of the swamp's temptations and attempts to subsume their memories, uncover the truth that lies beneath, and open the path to the Origin Sea.

0.desc: The population of stray Coastal Cats has exploded in the back alleys. The fact that no one's taking care of them is a sure sign of Hekaton's neglect of the country. \r\nThey're stronger than they look and can do some damage if one is not careful. In my opinion, they're just as much of a symptom of Kritias's fall as the widespread gangsters.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
You wouldn't think a Xenoroid would do well in the ocean, but this one seems fine. More than fine, even--it's adapted enough that a local starfish has apparently taken up residence on its head. It's clear that Morass is not reality, in the strictest sense, but still. This is ridiculous.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
In speaking with the temple keepers, I have learned that Morass was created by Erda in response to someone's memories. Does that mean that the Xenoroid, too, is taken from a memory? Perhaps the Adversary, who passed through here on their travels, knows the truth.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
You wouldn't think a Xenoroid would do well in the ocean, but this one seems fine. The coral growing out of it seems to be flourishing, too.
Upon further observation, it's become clear that these so-called Xenoroids are actually conglomerations of Erda.
Can't something just be what it looks like? I'm getting a little tired of the Arcane River.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc: You wouldn't think a Xenoroid would do well in the ocean, but this one seems fine. It seems this one has befriended a local jellyfish. Further observation has revealed that the jellyfish, as well as the Xenoroid itself, are both just byproducts of Erda. Strange, but I myself saw the Erda scattering when one disappears.                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc:
Violent gangs, like the ones these individuals belong to, grew like weeds while Hekaton focused on his research at the expense of everything else, including the basic well-being of his kingdom.
They've carved out a large chunk of Kritias for their territory, and harass and extort the citizens unfortunate enough to live there.
They show no fear of the guards, but always seem to steer clear Kritias defense force and temple keepers.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc:
Violent gangs, like the ones this man leads, grew like weeds while Hekaton focused on his research at the expense of everything else, including the basic well-being of his kingdom.
You'll want to stay away, if you know what's good for you. He's stronger than the Powerful Gangsters and not afraid of any kind of guard.
If the defense force and the temple keepers both stepped in, they might be able to handle him, but I doubt that will happen.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc:
Nothing definitive is known about the shadows that haunt the halls underneath Kritias. Researchers responded to my questions with only silence. But my professional pride as a chronicler won't let me leave it at that. What follows is mainly based on hearsay and my own personal deductions, but it is all I could find.
It's whispered that there were two magician's rebellions in Kritias. But Hekaton crushed both utterly--without leaving a single magician alive. No official record of either remains, but they seem to have taken place around the same time as Hekaton rose to the position of the most powerful magician of the kingdom. Curious.
The halo that adorns the Blue Shadow's shoulders is said to be a common accessory found on battle mages in Kritias at that time.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc:
Nothing definitive is known about the shadows that haunt the halls underneath Kritias. Researchers responded to my questions with only silence. But my professional pride as a chronicler won't let me leave it at that. What follows is mainly based on hearsay and my own personal deductions, but it is all I could find.
It's whispered that there were two magician's rebellions in Kritias. But Hekaton crushed both utterly--without leaving a single magician alive. No official record of either remains, but they seem to have taken place around the same time as Hekaton rose to the position of the most powerful magician of the kingdom. Curious.
The staff that the Red Shadow wields is notably similar to the records I found of those that Kritias's arch mages once wielded.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc:
Remnants of Hekaton's failed immortality rituals.
I haven't been able to find anything about what, exactly, these experiments consisted of. Maybe that's for the best. What is certain is that each time an experiment failed, more and more of these experiments gone wrong spread across Kritias itself. The objects take on almost humanoid shapes, and roam the city in packs.
They act almost as if they have souls themselves, but if they do, that implies that the rituals... I don't want to even write it.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc:
Remnants of Hekaton's failed immortality rituals.
I haven't been able to find anything about what, exactly, these experiments consisted of. Maybe that's for the best. What is certain is that each time an experiment failed, more and more of these experiments gone wrong spread across Kritias itself. In time, the Underground Prison was full of these monsters.
Hekaton, the fool, only made matters worse by walling off part of the Underground Prison instead of calling a stop to his experiments.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: This being, once a royal guard, was transformed into a monster when Hekaton's immortality ritual failed. \r\nIt has been stripped of its mind, and even its body is now unstable. While still capable of some movement, I would theorize that a being in this state will surely one day disappear.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc: This being, once a royal warhammer knight, was transformed into a monster when Hekaton's immortality ritual failed. \r\nIt has been stripped of its mind, and even its body will one day disappear. I cannot stop thinking about its fate. What will be left of it, once its vessel is gone? I am reminded of the remains of the experiments in the Underground Prison... Will these beings one day fuse to whatever object is to hand, and be subjected to that torment?\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

12.desc:
This being, once a royal wizard, was transformed into a monster when Hekaton's immortality ritual failed.
This creature has no body at all--there is nothing behind the mask it wears.
I'm afraid its current form may be the results of a spirit joining with nearby objects, much like the Experiment Remnants.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

13.desc: This being, once a royal archer, was transformed into a monster when Hekaton's immortality ritual failed.\r\nLike the wizard, there is no body at all beneath its mask. I can't help but wonder what the experience is like of this creature, a mere bundle of clothes with a spirit attached. How does it see itself and its place in the world? Does it know that it is dead?\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

14.desc:
These pigeons are commonplace in Trueffet, to the dismay of many.
I've heard numerous complaints about the excrement rusting buildings, the spread of disease, parasites...the list goes on. The merchants that sell their wares in the plaza are particularly vehement in their dislike.
They may appear rather cute, but I believe a traveler would be wise to follow the locals' advice and stay away.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc: Floating Maces such as this one are hazards found around Trueffet. Their habit of flying at around head height makes them particularly dangerous. I would advise my readers, if they should visit, to always remain aware of their surroundings.\r\nIt was originally assumed that these are inanimate objects made to move with magic, but while reading the reports of other chroniclers, I have begun to wonder if that is not the case.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

16.desc:
Some sort of remnant of Hekaton's ill-fated bid for immortality.
Alas, it is a distinct possibility that it is animated not by simple magic, but because the spirit of a victim of the experiments is trapped inside. If so...it is impossible to even imagine that poor soul's fate.
I have a plea for all researchers of conscience: please, seek a way to lay them to rest, to put an end to this tragedy.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc:
A professor at Kritias's Magic School. 
I've heard she's a strict and demanding teacher, and most students seem to fear her. But her skills as a magician speak for themselves, and she's well aware of both the promise and danger of magic. She was walking in Trueffet Square just before the incident.
I met her once when Kritias appeared in Minar Forest, but she was somewhat different than I expected. And once again, I am reminded that the Arcane River is a creation of the Black Mage.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

1.desc:
A member of Kritias's guard. 
Since Hekaton decided to spend the nation's resources exclusively on researching immortality, the guards have struggled to keep the peace. They don't have the resources or equipment to keep up with the ever-growing number of gangsters, and they've lost the trust of the citizens, too.
And in the middle of all that, they suddenly appeared in Minar Forest? I can understand their confusion.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

2.desc:
A magic researcher from Kritias. 
Kritias's Magic School produces many of these, and they mostly go on to join the royal magic laboratory. Recently, their efforts have gone exclusively to Hekaton's obsession with creating a spell of immortality.
I wonder... Could Kritias's appearance in Minar Forest be related somehow to the immortality experiments? It's hard to know. The king has made every effort to keep the experiments a secret, including disappearing some of the researchers--presumably, those were the ones who couldn't keep quiet.
Anyway, the remaining researchers are understandably a bit tightly wound. If you were to go up to them and say something like, #e"She will kill us all!"#n I expect they'd panic.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

3.desc:
A self-proclaimed thief and master of darkness.
Born and raised in Kritias, he makes his living stealing from outsiders. He has big dreams of getting out of town one day and making his fortune somewhere else.
Will his dream come true? He hasn't been seen since Kritias appeared in Minar Forest, so it's possible that he's already left town.
One day, I saw him scribbling something in a notebook and grinning. I asked him, #e"What are you drawing?"#n but he refused to show me. I'm a professional, though, so I managed to acquire the document anyway. It is attached to this report.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

4.desc: A researcher Kritias's magical laboratory who reports directly to the king. \r\nTheir research has to do with changing the anti-magic properties of darkness into light magic through the use of the Ranheim Rod. However, they're lacking an essential component of their research--someone who can use the pillar's power. I wonder if there's anyone out there who could help.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

5.desc:
A merchant from Kritias.
It seems he's head over heels for Nita, the storage keeper, but he hasn't gotten up the nerve to say anything. He told me that he's practicing magic for the day he finally tells her how he feels.
Despite the upheaval when Kritias appeared in Minar Forest, he hasn't changed a thing. I wonder if he'll ever say anything...
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

6.desc:
Kritias's storage keeper.
She's the daughter of the local blacksmith, Dostov. Her dream is to follow in her father's footsteps, but her father hasn't agreed.
Dostov sees the weapons he creates as tools of destruction, and he wants better for his daughter.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

7.desc: She works in Trueffet Square selling capes for wizards.\r\nKritias has quite strict laws about the distribution of magical technology to outsiders, so she won't sell to anyone who isn't local. It's a shame. The cape she's wearing herself looks to be of incredible quality.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc: This merchant works in Trueffet Square, selling ceramics.\r\nShe's suffered recently due to the outbreak of crime in Kritias, with some thugs even wandering through and breaking her ceramics. When I asked if she could go to the guards for help, she just laughed. Her complete lack of faith in them seems to be representative of the opinion of most citizens.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

9.desc: The royal chef of Kritias. \r\nI met him after Kritias appeared in Minar Forest. He's the head of a sizeable kitchen, but he still goes to the markets himself to pick out ingredients. He told me there's no one else he can trust to do it right.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

10.desc: A merchant selling fruit in Trueffet Square. \r\nAs lawlessness has increased in Kritias, he's had a hard time. He has plenty of stories of being threatened and extorted by gangsters. Whenever he can, he tells Michelin what the people are thinking, but it doesn't seem like it ever reaches Hekaton.\r\n                                      - Chronicler J.K.

11.desc:
All the cats in this neighborhood look alike. I can't tell them apart.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.
Cats are a good judge of character. I was able to lure one to me with food, and... Hm, there's something in its fur that looks like gem dust? Odd. But the fact remains that this little cat is exceedingly cute.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.regionDesc: Esfera, called the Origin Sea, is the endpoint for the flow of Erda, and the ultimate destination of all life. It is a mystical space made only of pure light and silent waves, where barrier between reality and fantasy crumbles. \r\nHowever, under its peaceful surface lies a vicious ritual that will determine the fate of the world...

0.desc:
A monster that appears where Esfera's pure Erda gathers. 
It has taken the form of a turtle due to the influence of oceanic terrain. It is most recognizable for the plant life growing on its shell.
It grazes on the energy of the Erda scattered across the sea of Esfera to survive, but it seems that this creature will eat anything in front of it, Erda or not.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: A monster that appears where Esfera's pure Erda gathers. \r\nIt is not truly a unique creature, but another stage in the life of an Ahtuin. If an Ahtuin lives long enough for the plants on its back to grow to the size of a tree, it is considered an Atus. It grazes on the energy of the Erda scattered across the sea of Esfera to survive.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: A monster that appears where Esfera's pure Erda gathers.\r\nIt has taken the form of a seahorse due to the influence of oceanic terrain. Its semitransparent body has the unique property of showing portions of the creature's bones. It is more aggressive than the Ahtuin and Atus, perhaps due to its higher density of Erda.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: A monster that appears where Esfera's pure Erda gathers.\r\nIt has taken the form of a seahorse due to the influence of oceanic terrain. Its semitransparent body has the unique property of showing portions of the creature's bones. Unlike Bellalion, it has powerful horns it can use in a fight. It is an aggressive Erda monster with an intimidating mien.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc:
This spider monster is a creation of Commander Will. 
The power of the mirror world allows it to appear in any place, at any time. It attacks by shooting venomous webs from its mouth. Despite its typically land-dwelling form, it's capable of moving freely in the ocean. This is typical of its overall adaptability.
If you encounter these creatures, take special care not to be surrounded. They are capable of closing distance to their prey at great speeds.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: This spider monster is a creation of Commander Will. \r\nThe power of the mirror world allows it to appear in any place, at any time. It attacks by shooting venomous webs from its mouth. It has a stronger venom than the Aranya.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc:
This strange temple keeper assists the Grandisian Transcendent of Light. 
According to Ollie's notes on his time in Esfera, Keepers are lower-ranking attendants. The Keeper of Light, as the name suggests, serves the power of light, just one of the powers of the Transcendent of Light.
The temple keepers that appear in Esfera have been transformed by the influence that the Transcendent Tana had over the pure Erda. As projections of her subconscious while she faced danger, they attack any that get close.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: This strange temple keeper assists the Grandisian Transcendent of Light. This keeper, as the name suggests, serves the power of darkness. \r\nThe temple keepers that appear in Esfera have been transformed by the influence that the Transcendent Tana had over the pure Erda. As projections of her subconscious while she faced danger, they attack any that get close.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc:
A mysterious being that serves the Transcendent of Light in the Grandisian Temple of Light. 
These executors have surrendered their names and bodies to wait upon the birth of a Transcendent. They serve different aspects. The Light Executor, as the name suggests, is pledged to the power of light.
The executors that appear in Esfera are shaped from phantoms drawn out of Tana's subconscious by Commander Will, using the power of the mirror world. These phantoms then were given physical form by Erda.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc:
A mysterious being that serves the Transcendent of Light in the Grandisian Temple of Light. 
These executors have surrendered their names and bodies to wait upon the birth of a Transcendent. They serve different aspects. The Dark Executor, as the name suggests, is pledged to the power of darkness.
The executors that appear in Esfera are shaped from phantoms drawn out of Tana's subconscious by Commander Will, using the power of the mirror world. These phantoms then were given physical form by Erda.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

10.desc:
A conglomeration of pure Erda that takes the form of an orb.
It defends Esfera, the Origin Sea, and attacks anything that was not born in the region.
It seems this creature wishes to return everything to pure Erda, like itself.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

11.desc:
A conglomeration of pure Erda that takes the form of an orb.
It defends Esfera, the Origin Sea, and attacks anything that was not born in the region.
It seems this creature wishes to return everything to pure Erda, like itself.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

12.desc: Something mixed with the pure Erda of Esfera when Commander Will materialized the Temple of Light in the Mirror World, and this is the result.\r\nLike the pure Erda it was formed from, it seeks to attack anything that isn't from the temple.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

13.desc:
Will was a human scholar from the Nihal Desert of Magatia. Even as a child, he immersed himself in books, learning all he could. He was especially interested in the Transcendents and their powers.
After the revival of the Black Mage, Will became one of his commanders not through any effort of coercion or persuasion, but out of pure curiosity, an insatiable need to know what the Black Mage would create.
Will quickly proved to be one of the Black Mage's most powerful commanders, thanks to his ability to create his own dimension, a mixture of reality and its reflections, confounding all he faces.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

0.desc:
This grizzled veteran, a Blaster from the Resistance, was chosen as an Alliance scout to the Arcane River. 
He's specialized in mechanics and uses a gauntlet and numerous other machines. His laid-back and easygoing manner hides a deep darkness within him, which took root after losing past comrades. However, his current friendships with his new allies seems to be healing some of these wounds.
He was a member of Edelstein's unit of divers before the Resistance was formed. When asked, #e"What did you look like in those days?"#n he showed me a photo that seems to mean a lot to him.

                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc:
She is a member of the Cygnus Knights and trained scout affiliated with the Thunder Breakers. Although born to everyday farmers, she has trained day and night since joining the Cygnus Knights, and her work was rewarded when she was chosen as a part of the Arcane River vanguard. While she cannot truly be said to be the best in any particular skill, her hard work and tenacity set her apart.
Don't be fooled into thinking she's all work all the time. She has a playful side, as well. Apparently, she tries hitting anything mechanical that doesn't work, and she wanted to be a magical girl as a child.
When I asked, #e"Why do you use a sword?"#n (unusual for a Thunder Breaker) she launched into a detailed explanation of the knights' organizational structure, and I was unable to extricate myself for some time. Ask at your own risk.

                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc:
A Guardian of Time dispatched to the Arcane River.
He's investigating dense collection of Commander Will's Erda traces that were left in Esfera. For one so young, he's been recognized for his talent and skills, and thus assigned to the Arcane River.
His serious personality, which makes him seem older than he is, gets him into frequent arguments with Dimo.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc:
A Guardian of Time dispatched to the Arcane River.
He's investigating dense collection of Commander Will's Erda traces that were left in Esfera. He's got a strong sense of mischief, and seems to derive a lot of joy from playing pranks on Kanto.
He's instantly recognizable from the unusual curls in his hair.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc:
Full name: Melangioruiana. A unusual-seeming magician who wields a large staff. No one I've spoken to has ever seen the eye that's covered by his somewhat sloppily mended hat.
I could not find even basic demographic information about him, and cannot report his race, age, or place of birth. I do know that he is a pupil of the Grandisian Great Enchanter, but no one of the alliance knows more of his past than that one detail.
Based on what has been seen already of his use of rune magic and his ability to create dimensional gates, Melange's magical prowess is unquestionable. Rumor says that he loves sleeping so much that he is frequently sleepwalking when he's seen out and about.
                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.regionDesc: In the depths under Esfera, the Origin Sea--a place where not even a beam of light can find purchase--this is Sellas, Where the Stars Rest.\r\nDespite the dark and the pressure, the Erda of this place shines like constellations. Swimming here is like swimming through space itself. \r\n

0.desc: An Erda monster that has materialized in Sellas, Esfera's deepest depths. The environment around it caused it to take the form of a deep-sea jellyfish.\r\nAny part of its body can discharge an electric shock. It stuns any creature that gets too close and then makes its escape.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

1.desc: An Erda monster that has taken the form of a deep sea anemone. The resemblance is superficial, though. This creature can gather energy in its head and fire it as a laser.\r\nIt does have some similarity to the aliens of the Omega Sector.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

2.desc: An Erda monster that has taken the form of a deep sea salamander. It spits out explosive bubbles. Of all the Erda monsters, this one is inarguably one of the most adorable.\r\nI would caution against getting too close, though. It takes advantage of an opponent's distraction to begin producing bubbles.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

3.desc: An Erda monster that has taken the form of a deep sea fish. It lives deep in Sellas. Its transparent skin, which almost seems to be made of liquid, allows one to see its skeleton inside.\r\nIt's hypothesized that it took on this form as a reflection of the fear of the members of the vanguard who first visited the region. It attacks by spitting a liquid with many of the same properties as its skin.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

4.desc: An Erda monster that has taken the form of a deep sea squid. It lives so deep in Sellas that no light reaches it, so it has developed a faint bioluminescent glow.\r\nIts skin is transparent, but it's full of dark ink that it's hard to differentiate it from its surroundings. In this way, it's possible to become surrounded by Denebola without seeing them approach. It attacks by spitting explosive ink, and then quickly detonating it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

5.desc: An Erda monster that has taken the form of a stingray. It lives at the very bottom of Sellas. It moves quite gracefully, as if it is gliding effortlessly through the water.\r\nDespite looking like a stingray, it has the internal structure of an invertebrate, to better survive the intense pressure of its home.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

6.desc: A mysterious Erda monster that lives in the deepest parts of Sellas. This deep, it formed without ever being noticed by people. Therefore, it did not take its form from a familiar sea creature, like many of the others.\r\nIts respiratory system is particularly strong, letting it create forceful jets of water even under such pressure.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

7.desc: An Erda monster that has been sighted in Sellas which takes the form of a jellyfish. It drifts freely through the sea even so deep.\r\nIt's not too aggressive, but it's still an Erda monster. It's not advisable to attempt to touch it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

8.desc: An Erda monster that has been sighted in Sellas which takes the form of a jellyfish. It drifts freely through the sea even so deep.\r\nIt's not too aggressive, but it's still an Erda monster. It's not advisable to attempt to touch it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.desc: An Erda monster that has been sighted in Sellas which takes the form of a jellyfish. It drifts freely through the sea even so deep.\r\nIt's not too aggressive, but it's still an Erda monster. It's not advisable to attempt to touch it.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ael

9.regionDesc: Moonbridge, revealed at last to be the final approach to the black sun.\r\nThis is the great barrier that links the edge of the Arcane River to the Black Mage. Here, the Maple Alliance and the White Spear take to the battlefield with the very fate of the world hanging in the balance.\r\nIn the midst of obscuring thunderstorms and fog, the Adversary and the Alliance engage in a battle with unseen enemies.

0.desc:
A bizarre entity that an unwary traveler may encounter in Moonbridge. The longer one looks at one, the darker it seems. This led the Guardians of Time to call it the Soot Beast. 
According to the Guardians of Time, there is a high possibility that Tenebris is the materialization of a certain being's subconscious. Who, you may ask? It is unknown, but only one possibility comes to mind...
I can confirm that the place has a tremendous effect on us, even as outsiders prepared for a journey into the unknown. My skin prickles, as if I were facing pure chaos.
Thankfully, the Soot Beasts are smaller than anticipated. Their attacks are all relatively close range, which one may take advantage of.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc:
A bizarre entity that an unwary traveler may encounter in Moonbridge. The Guardian of Time named it the Soot Talon due to its curved shape and destructive mien.
Since we arrived, they have continuously attacked our ship and cannon, trying to destroy both. If they are able, I have no doubt they would try to destroy us next. It seems a basic instinct for them.
The Soot Talons have a longer reach than the Soot Beasts, and move faster. It should be noted for the record that they are very dangerous foes.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
A strange being that can be found in the Mysterious Fog.
It takes advantage of low visibility in the area to creep up silently on its prey. In behavior, it reminds me of the silence of a hunting snake, in the moments before it chokes its next meal. It is hard not to fear that an attack can come at any time, from any place. This fear is reflected in the name: the Soot Slug.
If you can, keep your distance from this creature. It can attack at range by shooting some sort of energy. Of course, avoiding it is only possible if you can spot it through the fog.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
A strange being that can be found in the Mysterious Fog.
If, while lost in the fog, you feel a gaze upon you, but cannot see anything, this creature is a likely culprit. The red glow it emits gives the appearance of eyes in the fog, and also lends the creature its name, the Soot Core.
If you do encounter one, do your best not to look at it directly while you fight. The sight of those red eyes may freeze you in fear.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
An anomalous entity that one might find in the Void Current.
While it might look like a broken-off chunk of a golem, its composition is fundamentally different. If you were to pick up one of the many fragments that make it up, you would feel the force of its powerful thoughts. If you, unwisely, decided to keep holding it, you'd quickly find your mind falling into the abyss of its gravity. Its name, the Crushing Glare, comes from this effect.
While its unknowable thoughts might arouse your curiosity, you'd be wise to avoid its pull. The moment you give in, you will be lost to the darkness.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
An anomalous entity that one might find in the Void Current.
Its body appears to be made of a coil of wound-up chains. It seems like it may be a smaller version of the Gloom, but the resemblance may just be superficial. Like the Crushing Glare, if you approach it, you can feel the force of its powerful thoughts.
Its twilight hues put one in the mind of an approaching end. If it is true that Tenebris was created from someone's subconscious, then it's clear that person is preoccupied with the end of the very world.
We are here to stop the end from coming.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc: An uncanny being that you may see anywhere in Moonbridge. \r\nIf a small Gloom ever took flight, it might look like this. Its movements seem to be aimless, so it has been named the Wandering Soot Glare. It's impossible to know if it has some strange purpose, or if it truly is simply a wanderer. We can only be careful that we don't let it lead us astray.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc: A gigantic monster that can appear from the fog of Tenebris. According to Edea, it was created by the Black Mage, and is the manifestation of his dark emotions.\r\nMost who see it, even from a distance, do not even have the will to fight, perhaps due to the force of those emotions, or due to its sheer, intimidating size. I have never before seen a creature with the ability to induce such a feeling of powerlessness.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc: A soldier of Ereve who has arrived in Tenebris on a dangerous mission.\r\nI can only imagine the fear these soldiers must be experiencing. Not only do they face the natural dangers of the Arcane River, they must also look ahead to the mission's ultimate goal--a confrontation with the Black Mage. I say that I can only imagine, though, as these soldiers remain loyal to their cause and steadfast at their stations. They have not backed down at all.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
The long-time advisor to the Empress is now taking on that same role for the whole of the alliance.
This is the first time I have seen him take the field himself. His habit is generally to issue orders from Ereve. But it seems this operation at Tenebris is unlike any I have seen before.
Every time I have glimpsed the man he has been in a state of deep thought, as if his every waking moment is spent ensuring that each step is planned out exactly. While I don't personally enjoy his company, I must admit he is truly worthy of his reputation as a tactician.
I don't believe he's any sort of combatant, and yet I haven't seen him show fear for his personal safety. He must have great trust in his soldiers to keep him safe.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
Cygnus hardly needs an introduction, famed as the esteemed Empress of Maple World and the leader of the Cygnus Knights. 
Once, when the Alliance was first being formed, I thought she was rather meek, and had my doubts that she was fit carry such a responsibility. I am pleased to see my doubts were entirely incorrect. She is a fine commander, and leads the soldiers from the front line with her stalwart example. I am certain that she has her own fears, though she never shows them. I only hope she has someone to confide in.
The task of defeating the Black Mage won't be an easy one... Yet I believe the Alliance can accomplish that goal.
I know Chronicler Q would have loved to be here to write this entry. Alas, as a member of the Cygnus Knights, he lacked the distance necessary, and I was chosen instead.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc: A priest that was dispatched to Tenebris from the Temple of Time.\r\nThe priests of the Temple of Time usually specialize in healing and injury recovery, but it seems they're committed to helping investigate the unusual properties of Tenebris as well. They are constantly out and about collecting research materials for scholarly pursuits.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.regionDesc: The Labyrinth of Suffering, where the endless coil of darkness twists into a maddening trial.\r\nThe Erda manifestations here feed on accumulated sorrow and deep-rooted fear. They've thrived in a despairing space that distorts the memories of all who enter by ceaselessly reopening their deepest wounds.\r\nCountless Alliance soldiers have lost themselves after falling into this maze, writhing in eternal agony under Commander Hilla's reaping of souls.

0.desc:
A strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, it resembles a horrific jumble of flint and tree branches.
If it's truly made up of broken fragments, one must conclude that it's made of the labyrinth itself. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc:
A strange being that can be found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, it resembles sentient and broken labyrinth fragments moving on their own volition.
If it's a monster created from endlessly breaking and regenerating labyrinth fragments, isn't it...also part of the labyrinth? It's chilling to ponder that the labyrinth itself might be alive.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
A unique being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
At first glance, one might mistake it for a giant insect.
However, a closer inspection reveals that instead of wings, it seems to propel itself with a blood-like energy. Furthermore, its body is composed of skeletal remains. Clearly, it's considerably more terrible than a giant insect.
Those who have seen it have been so terrified that they've nicknamed this monstrosity the "flying fear." 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
A giant golem found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
It appears to be made of animated pieces of the labyrinth.
Through the branches of the tree wrapped in stone bricks, one can spot a blue flame resembling Goblin Fire. Survivors are generally so overwhelmed by the golem's sheer size that their instincts drive them to flee in fear. 
Unfortunately, no one has ever battled this being, so there is a dearth of information. Is such a monster even capable of being defeated? 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
An enchanted being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, it initially appeared to be an array of strangely arranged stones, orbiting and floating in the air. It looks as if it were in the process of becoming a Golem, but was unable to complete its task, earning it the title of "Dark Miscreation."
However, chroniclers remain unsure if this being actually exists. As travelers repeatedly encountered this "being" within the stone maze, they were led to believe that this could possibly be a manifestation of the labyrinth itself. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
An enchanted being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, it initially appeared to be an array of strangely arranged stones, orbiting and floating in the air. Enveloped by the darkness, these beings often went undetected until the moment they attacked, earning them the name "Dark Construct."
Like the Dark Miscreation, one cannot conclusively verify their existence. There's always the disturbing possibility that stricken people, lost inside the endless, dark maze, were seeing illusions. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
A strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, it is as dark as a shadow and it floats in the air with giant wings.
It doesn't appear to be a living organism, so it's presumed to be a Necro. Nevertheless, if the reader is to believe that the Necro existed in this labyrinth before the Alliance was established... Then how... Oh dear. This raises so many questions...
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
A strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, its giant wings and eerie floating make it appear quite demonic.
Knocking it down causes it to disappear, but it will leave behind a burning fragment. However, one must take heed! Picking up that trinket will make a traveler feel as though their very soul is burning beneath their skin. One cannot help but instinctively toss it to the side, only to find that the mysterious piece immediately vanishes. What, precisely, do these wicked beings leave in their wake?
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

8.desc:
A strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, it resembles a giant insect composed of skeletal fragments.
It is a ghastly sight, with notable empty eye sockets and magic pulsating near its exposed ribs. It has a habit of flying towards people's heads. When travelers instinctively attempt to swat this monstrosity away, it's known to explode instantly.
Wise explorers must know to stay as far away as possible from this wretched creature. Take heed and only attack from a distance.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

9.desc:
A strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, it resembles a Cygnus Knight soldier.
Because of this resemblance, some tortured souls thought that these beings were the animated corpses of recently-deceased comrades.
Such a horror is almost beyond the realms of the imagination. To think, deep inside the labyrinth, throwing arms against the corpse of a dead friend... How much torment can a soul bear?
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

10.desc:
A strange being that can be found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
According to survivor accounts, it resembles a Resistance soldier.
Because of this, some people mistook it for a reanimated corpse.
What a terrifying thought! Imagine being inside the labyrinth, and thinking that the ghost of one's dead comrade is attacking. It's enough to drive one to madness!
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

11.desc:
A strange being native to the Labyrinth of Suffering.
Survivors lucky enough to walk away from a row with it say that it resembles an armored Nova Soldier.
Since it doesn't resemble any of the other monsters in the Labyrinth of Suffering, many warriors approached it, thinking they were greeting a fellow Alliance member.
Unfortunately, none of the encounters ended peacefully...
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

12.desc:
A strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
Witness accounts consistently describe this being as "a giant rat with horns and wings." Keep in mind that rats are well known for carrying and spreading disease. Maybe the Silent Watchman does the same?
If a traveler is bitten by one of these wretched creatures, they should disinfect the area immediately and ensure that their drinking water is not contaminated.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

13.desc:
A strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.

Those unlucky enough to encounter such a creature describe it as a giant rat with horns and wings, much like the Silent Watchman. However, astute Chroniclers will notice that its body is a bit darker in hue and its horns are a different color.

Additionally, it's said that the Silent Watchman and Silent Assassin emit sounds similar to a lion's roar. Frankly, it's hard to understand why such creatures are called "silent." Neither is quiet, so listen carefully and avoid them if possible.

                                      - Chronicler Ritt

14.desc:
A uniquely strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
One can't help but notice that it resembles a giant insect seemingly constructed from skeletal bones.
It doesn't have a signature attack, but it flies very quickly in the darkness, making it unavoidable once it sets its eyes upon an unlucky traveler. It's also noted for having a saliva-like gland capable of dealing immense pain, so avoid being pricked!
That's a tough wound to recover from, so one must take care of this monster before it ambushes them from the shadows.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

15.desc:
A bizarre being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
Eyewitnesses claim that it has significant structural similarities to the Blackheart that's always at Commander Hilla's side. Note the similar horns, wings, tail, and the distinct hind legs.
All this indicates that the Labyrinth of Suffering was once Commander Hilla's domain. However, the Blackheart Negative is much bigger than the standard Blackheart. It also has two heads, making it at least twice as threatening. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

16.desc:
A strange being found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
Witnesses reported that, from a distance, the creature only resembles a dimly-lit green flame. However, upon closer inspection, they saw that this was a monster covered in bones.
Some say that when it swings its arms, bones emerge from the ground, dealing devastating attacks. Attacks using bones... I can't imagine! How would one even classify such an art? Ossiomancy? To make matters worse, the creature emits a blood-curdling scream as it perishes, sounding almost human... 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

17.desc:
A bizarre creature found in the Labyrinth of Suffering.
Witnesses report that, from a distance, the creature is easily mistaken for a dimly-lit purple flame.
However, upon closer inspection, it shows itself to be an eerie creature covered in bones. Soldiers report that, due to its humanoid shape and man-like death screams, many thought they were vanquishing a fellow soldier. All in all, this is one of the most traumatizing and nightmarish monsters one can encounter.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

18.desc:
Head shamaness of the collapsed Azwan, as well as one of the Black Mage's Commanders. She is responsible for the destruction of Azwan, and is the keeper of the Labyrinth of Suffering.
While she was briefly spotted in Azwan, she quickly went back into hiding. Nevertheless, the hunt for Hilla continued.
But Hilla refused to surrender to authorities, instead choosing to relocate to the Labyrinth of Suffering.
Witnesses, including the Adversary, claim that her undeniable beauty, which she always sought to protect, had dramatically diminished to the point where she no longer appeared human.
She was ultimately defeated and time started to flow rapidly, causing her to dramatically age. It's said that she fled to hide her new appearance, and she is unlikely to ever appear in public again.
Whether she's alive or dead, one thing is certain... She will never be forgiven.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

11.regionDesc: The place where the last currents of the Arcane River subside. Here lies the last sanctuary where all causality ends.\r\nHere, where the Black Mage swallows the light and darkness of utopian dreams, is where the end and beginning of a world meet. Here, the dimension breaks and Erda spirals intersect.\r\nThe Alliance's "White Spear" fleet and the Adversary advance through the darkness, moving from the Giant's Heart toward the final battle that will decide the fate of Maple World.

0.desc:
An enchanted being found in Limina. Like all monsters in Limina, its true nature remains unknown. 
It has a geometric form that transcends cognition, making it appear otherworldly. Because it is always changing form, it's presumed to be some sort of higher-dimensional entity that transcends the limitations of physical objects. This earned it the name "Transcendion."
This being is known to intermittently spill out from Giant's Heart.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc:
An enchanted being found in Limina. Like all monsters in Limina, its true nature remains unknown. 
It appears in the form of a giant atomic structure, echoing the building blocks of our world. While gazing upon it, one cannot help but contemplate the origin and archetypes of all life, earning it the name "Ancestion."
It occasionally emerges from Giant's Heart, but it proves to be a formidable and baffling foe. With no head to speak of, an adventurer might wonder exactly what they should be targeting.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

2.desc:
An enchanted being found in Limina. Like all monsters in Limina, its true nature remains unknown. 
This tetrahedron-shaped being will dizzy anyone who gazes upon its form. Its constant movement makes one feel as if they've been transported to a multidimensional world. While the Turbion is rarely seen, it still sometimes comes out to interfere with the carefully-laid plans of tired travelers.
While catching one in the field is very rare, it is most likely to be found near Giant's Heart. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

3.desc:
An enchanted being found in Limina. Like all monsters in Limina, its true nature remains unknown. 
At first glance, it has a person's silhouette. However, since it is known to float silently with hardly any movement, it is clearly inhuman.
According to one account, it was found blocking the passage to some high point. Could that be why it earned the name "Ascendion"?
It occasionally appears around Giant's Heart. One must wonder what about Giant's Heart causes so many monsters like this to spill out from it. A humble chronicler does not know. Only the Adversary possessed the will to venture inside. 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

4.desc:
An enchanted being found in Limina. Like all monsters in Limina, its true nature remains unknown. 
It resembles the Turbion, but is oddly faint, making it more difficult to spot. Watching it move constantly, with wariness, could make one feel as if they're being pulled into a multidimensional world.
This rarely-seen but quite distracting entity has earned the name "Disturbion." 
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

5.desc:
An enchanted being found in Limina. Like all monsters in Limina, its true nature remains unknown.
As one gazes upon it, they are left unable to deny that it resembles a planet and an orbiting satellite. Why do majestic monsters like this appear in Limina?
Ultimately, the Foreberion is likely a Black Mage creation. Why did he forge such a monster? Experts remain baffled.
The Alliance decided to call this beast "Foreberion."
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

6.desc:
An enchanted being found in Limina. Like all monsters in Limina, its true nature remains unknown.
Hungry travelers may note that it resembles a giant donut. But if one looks more closely, they would find that particles of light gather at the center, in the form of a torus. It seems to signify the beginning of life or the primordial collection of atoms that begat life itself.
One can gaze upon it and ponder a meaning for hours. For this humble chronicler, it brings to mind something being reborn. The Alliance decided to call it "Embrion," connected to the word "embryo."
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

7.desc:
Knight Kellad, who was once the brightest sword of Sharenian. He was stripped of his title after trying to protect Prince Sharen IV from the maniacal king. Following that, he came to lead a problematic group of knights.
He received a proposal from his old student, the prince, to stage a coup to rescue the kingdom, but, torn between loyalty and compassion, Kellad responded with silence. His choice became the seed of an irreversible tragedy.
After the failure of the prince's coup, Kellad and his knights were trapped in the demon Ergoth's mirror world, where they fell under a terrible curse to spend hundreds of years in an endless cycle of death and combat. By the time he realized the futility of his existence, he had already taken the lives of his subordinates, who had gone mad.
Kellad's mind was shattered by guilt over failing to protect his student and the undeniable emptiness that followed. The White Mage appeared before him as he had fallen into despair, and proposed a twisted eternal pledge. 
The knight that was once the brightest light in the kingdom now has become its greatest darkness. His sword still serves a master, but Sharenian is nowhere in sight.
                                      - Chronicler J.K.

8.desc:
A mage who tried to save the world hundreds of years ago. 
He wanted to make people into more complete beings through "infinite knowledge existing beyond the horizon of perception." Ultimately, he concluded that the only constant was Ultimate Darkness, and not Ultimate Light. He fell and became the Black Mage, Transcendent of Light.
He and his commanders wrought chaos on the world and were eventually felled by brave heroes and sealed away. Freed from the seal hundreds of years later, he created the Arcane River and sought to bring destruction upon the world again, but eventually failed thanks to the Maple Alliance's Tenebris operation.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

0.desc:
A priest found on White Spear, sent from the Temple of Time. Based on her outfit, she appears to be a priest of the highest order.
When asked about her precise ranking, she is known to give kind chroniclers vague answers and deflections. Lorelai, who appears too mischievous to be a priest, was likely part of the defunct Temple of Time as well.
She's one of the few who witnessed the decisive battle in White Spear. If one exclaims #e"For Maple World!"#n, she might be inspired to share her memories of that heated day.
                                      - Chronicler Ritt

1.desc: A Resistance soldier found on the Resistance ship. While it is rousing to see him carrying out his tasks, it also proves to be worrisome.\r\nThe Alliance's operations have placed a tremendous burden on the Resistance. Such efforts must be lauded once the war is concluded.\r\n                                      - Chronicler Ritt
